Generated by `pnpm docs:generate` — do not edit by hand.
Every page of the docs site (apps/docs/content/docs) in sidebar order: title, description, source path, then the page body.


---

# Introduction

> TelamonJS is an admin framework for Next.js and React, with the auth, permissions, logging and queue packages around it

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/index.mdx

TelamonJS builds admin applications on Next.js and React. You describe a module once,
in a typed `CrudConfig`, and `<ListPage config={config} />` renders the list with
search, sorting, filters and export, plus the create, edit and view dialogs, all
backed by React Query.

## Start with the CLI

```bash
npx -p @telamonjs/cli create-telamonjs-app my-admin
cd my-admin
pnpm dev
```

You get a running Next.js admin: the `AdminShell` layout, NextAuth sign-in, a Prisma
database in Docker and a reference CRUD module. Then generate a module from one of
your Prisma models:

```bash
pnpm exec telamonjs generate crud products --model Product
```

The [CLI page](/docs/packages/cli) covers the options, the monorepo layout and the
other commands. To add TelamonJS to an app you already have, follow
[Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation).

## What a module looks like

```tsx title="app/admin/products/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { config } from './config'

export default function ProductsPage() {
  return <ListPage config={config} />
}
```

`config.tsx` holds the columns, the form sections, the Zod schema and the
`query`/`mutations` that call your API. [Quick Start](/docs/getting-started/quick-start)
walks through a generated one, and [CrudConfig](/docs/getting-started/crud-config)
documents every key.

## Packages

| Package | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`@telamonjs/ui`](/docs/components) | `CrudConfig` and `ListPage`, forms and fields, dialogs, detail views, the app shell, dashboards, charts, i18n |
| [`@telamonjs/data`](/docs/packages/data) | The server half of a list: the `ListPage` wire contract, sort and paging sanitizers, a Prisma adapter |
| [`@telamonjs/cli`](/docs/packages/cli) | Creates apps, generates CRUD modules from Prisma, lints modules against the conventions |
| [`@telamonjs/auth`](/docs/packages/auth) | One session token shared by a NextAuth v5 app and a NestJS API |
| [`@telamonjs/permissions`](/docs/packages/permissions) | RBAC materialized in the JWT, so a permission check is an array lookup |
| [`@telamonjs/logger`](/docs/packages/logger) | One logger API across browser, server and worker |
| [`@telamonjs/queue`](/docs/queue) | BullMQ jobs and schedules declared in config, with a dashboard |

The UI package supports Next.js 15 and 16 with React 18 or 19.

# Installation

> Start a new TelamonJS app with the CLI, or add @telamonjs/ui to an existing Next.js app

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/getting-started/installation.mdx

TelamonJS packages are published on the public npm registry under the
`@telamonjs` scope — no registry configuration or auth token needed.

You need **Node.js 22** or newer. pnpm is the recommended package manager.

---

## New app

The CLI scaffolds a complete Next.js admin: `AdminShell` with a typed menu,
NextAuth v5 sign-in, Prisma with a Docker Compose database, pt-BR/en/es messages,
and a reference CRUD module (`src/app/admin/usuarios/`).

```bash
npx -p @telamonjs/cli create-telamonjs-app my-admin
```

Unless you pass `--skip-install`, the CLI installs the dependencies, runs
`git init`, writes `.env`, starts the database with Docker Compose, migrates and
seeds it. If a step fails (no Docker, for example), it prints the manual steps
instead. In a terminal it also asks whether you want the monorepo layout.
Flags:

| Flag | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--provider <postgresql\|mysql>` | `postgresql` | Database provider for Prisma and Docker Compose |
| `--port <port>` | `3001` | Dev server port |
| `--monorepo` | off | pnpm monorepo instead of a single app: `apps/web`, `apps/api` (NestJS), `apps/jobs` (BullMQ), `packages/shared` (Prisma) |
| `--skip-install` / `--skip-git` | off | Skip `pnpm install` / `git init` |

Everything below this section is already done in a generated app. Continue with
the [Quick Start](/docs/getting-started/quick-start).

---

## Existing app

Adding `@telamonjs/ui` to a Next.js app you already have.

<Steps>

<Step>

### Install the package and its peers

```bash
pnpm add @telamonjs/ui
```

`@telamonjs/ui` brings its own UI dependencies (Radix, TanStack Table, Zustand,
Lucide, …). Your app provides the shared ones, so there is a single instance of
each:

<PeerDeps pkg="ui" />

The `jspdf` pair is optional: it only powers the PDF option of the export menu
every `ListPage` toolbar shows (Excel and CSV need nothing), and without it that
option shows an error naming the packages. `DashboardGrid` also needs `import 'react-grid-layout/css/styles.css'`.
Tailwind CSS 3 is a dev dependency of your app:

```bash
pnpm add -D tailwindcss@3 postcss autoprefixer
```

<Callout type='warn' title='React Query — one instance only'>
  `@tanstack/react-query` and `next-intl` are peers, never re-exported by the
  `@telamonjs/ui` barrel: import them directly from your app. Add
  `@telamonjs/ui` to `experimental.optimizePackageImports` in `next.config`.
  A second copy of react-query in the module graph shows up as
  "No QueryClient set". See [Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup).
</Callout>

</Step>

<Step>

### Configure Tailwind CSS

Extend the TelamonJS preset (theme tokens, `darkMode: 'class'`, animations) and
let Tailwind scan the package:

```typescript title="tailwind.config.ts"
import type { Config } from 'tailwindcss'
import telamonPreset from '@telamonjs/ui/tailwind-preset'

const config: Config = {
  presets: [telamonPreset],
  content: [
    './app/**/*.{ts,tsx,mdx}',
    './components/**/*.{ts,tsx,mdx}',
    './node_modules/@telamonjs/ui/dist/**/*.{js,mjs}',
  ],
}

export default config
```

Import the framework styles once, in your root layout. They include the
Tailwind directives and the CSS variables the preset reads:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import '@telamonjs/ui/styles'
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Wrap the app in the providers

`AppProviders` sets up React Query, the theme, the session, i18n and the Zod
error map in one component:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import { AppProviders } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import '@telamonjs/ui/styles'

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang='en' suppressHydrationWarning>
      <body>
        <AppProviders>{children}</AppProviders>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

[Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup) covers the full hierarchy:
passing your own `QueryClient`, messages and locale, and the `AdminShell` layout.

</Step>

<Step>

### Verify

```tsx title="app/test/page.tsx"
import { Button } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function TestPage() {
  return (
    <div className='p-8'>
      <Button>Click me</Button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

Run `pnpm dev` and open `/test`. A styled button means the package, the styles
and the preset are wired.

</Step>

</Steps>

---

## Troubleshooting

**Tailwind styles not applying.** The `content` array must include
`./node_modules/@telamonjs/ui/dist/**/*.{js,mjs}`, and `@telamonjs/ui/styles`
must be imported once in the root layout.

**Peer dependency warnings.** Install the missing peers from the table above;
pnpm names each one it could not resolve.

**"Cannot find package '@telamonjs/ui'".** Check that no `.npmrc` or
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` points the `@telamonjs` scope at another registry, then
`pnpm install --force`.

**"No QueryClient set".** Two copies of `@tanstack/react-query` are loaded.
Import it from your app (never through `@telamonjs/ui`), keep a single version in
the lockfile, and see [Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup).

# Quick Start

> Create an app with the CLI, generate a CRUD module from a Prisma model, and read its config

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/getting-started/quick-start.mdx

From an empty folder to a working **Products** module: list, search, create, edit,
view and delete, all in one route. You need Node.js 22+, pnpm and Docker (for the
database).

<Steps>

<Step>

### Create the app

```bash
npx -p @telamonjs/cli create-telamonjs-app my-admin
cd my-admin
pnpm dev
```

The CLI installs the dependencies, starts the database with Docker Compose,
migrates and seeds it (flags and the monorepo option are on
[Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation#new-app)). Open
`http://localhost:3001` and sign in as `admin@example.com` / `12345`.

The app ships one complete module, `src/app/admin/usuarios/`. It is the
reference for everything below, and `AGENTS.md` at the app root explains the
conventions to coding agents.

</Step>

<Step>

### Add a Prisma model

```prisma title="prisma/schema.prisma"
model Product {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  sku       String   @unique
  price     Decimal
  active    Boolean  @default(true)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  @@map("products")
}
```

```bash
pnpm db:migrate
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Generate the module

```bash
pnpm telamonjs generate crud products --model Product
```

The generator reads the model, maps each column to a field type, asks for the
module path (Enter accepts `src/app/admin/products`) and writes:

```
src/app/admin/products/
├── config.tsx                    # CrudConfig — the whole module
├── page.tsx                      # <ListPage config={productsConfig} />
└── _components/ProductDetail.tsx # body of the view dialog
src/lib/api/products-client.ts    # the only file that calls fetch()
src/app/api/products/route.ts     # GET list, POST create (Prisma)
src/app/api/products/[id]/route.ts# GET, PATCH, DELETE (Prisma)
```

It also adds a menu entry to `src/config/menu.ts` and the module's keys to
`messages/{pt-BR,en,es}.json`. Reload the app: **Products** is in the sidebar.

</Step>

<Step>

### Read the config

Data moves in one direction: Route Handler (Prisma) → `products-client.ts`
(`fetch`) → `config.tsx`. The config never touches Prisma or `fetch()`; it wires
the client into one `CrudConfig` object, and `page.tsx` renders it:

```tsx title="src/app/admin/products/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { productsConfig } from './config'

export default function ProductsPage() {
  return <ListPage config={productsConfig} />
}
```

`config.tsx` starts with `'use client'` (its queries and mutations run through
React Query hooks). Its key parts:

**`query`** loads the list. `queryFn` must resolve a `PaginatedResponse<T>`
(`data`, `page`, `total`, `totalPages`), not a bare array: the list is an
infinite, virtualized scroll that pages through it.

```tsx
query: { queryKey: ['products'], queryFn: productsApi.list, staleTime: 30_000 },
```

**`mutations`** write. Each `mutationFn` resolves `{ success, data? }`, so the
config adapts the client's raw entity; `invalidates` refreshes the list.
`getForEdit` and `getForView` fetch one record when a dialog opens — `getForEdit`
maps it to the form's shape:

```tsx
mutations: {
  create: {
    mutationFn: async (data) => ({ success: true, data: await productsApi.create(data) }),
    invalidates: [['products']],
  },
  // update and delete follow the same shape
  getForEdit: async (id) => {
    const item = await productsApi.getById(id)
    return { name: item.name, sku: item.sku, price: item.price, active: item.active }
  },
  getForView: productsApi.getById,
},
```

**`dialogs`** are where create, edit and view happen. Each one syncs to a URL
parameter (`?view=<id>`, `?edit=<id>`, `?create=1`), so it can be linked to and
Back closes it. The edit and create dialogs render `form.sections`; the view
dialog renders the detail component:

```tsx
dialogs: {
  view: {
    urlParam: 'view',
    title: msg('products.dialogs.view.title'),
    headerConfig,
    renderContent: (item) => <ProductDetail item={item} />,
  },
  edit: { urlParam: 'edit', title: msg('products.dialogs.edit.title'), headerConfig },
  create: { urlParam: 'create', title: msg('products.dialogs.create.title'), headerConfig },
},
```

**`actionsConfig`** adds the row buttons (view, edit, delete with a confirmation
dialog). **`form`** holds the field sections and the Zod schema shared by the
create and edit dialogs. Text slots use `msg('<key>')` so they follow the active
locale.

[CrudConfig](/docs/getting-started/crud-config) has the full annotated example
and every key.

</Step>

<Step>

### Check it

```bash
pnpm lint:telamonjs   # telamonjs lint src/app/admin
pnpm type-check
```

`telamonjs lint` checks modules against the list, dialog and hub conventions and
exits 1 on any error. A fresh module has no errors; it warns
(`i18n-untranslated`) about `en.json` and `es.json` keys that still hold the
pt-BR text, until you translate them.

</Step>

</Steps>

<Callout type='warn' title='No create, edit or detail routes'>
  A module is one route. Don't add `new/`, `[id]/` or `[id]/edit/` pages next to
  `config.tsx`: create, edit and view are the dialogs above, and delete is a row
  action. `telamonjs lint` fails on a `[id]/page.tsx` next to a `config.tsx`
  (`no-crud-pages`). For a form that genuinely needs its own page (a settings
  screen, a long wizard), see [Standalone form pages](/docs/patterns/edit-page).
</Callout>

## Next steps

- [CrudConfig](/docs/getting-started/crud-config) — the canonical example, key by key
- [Dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs) — rich headers, detail tabs, the portal view for large records

- [i18n](/docs/patterns/i18n) — `msg()`, `<Msg>` and the message files

# CLI

> Create a TelamonJS app, generate CRUD modules from Prisma, add admin-kit modules, and check modules against the conventions

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/packages/cli.mdx

`@telamonjs/cli` ships two binaries and no library code:

| Binary | What it runs |
| --- | --- |
| `create-telamonjs-app` | `telamonjs create` with the same arguments; with no arguments, the wizard |
| `telamonjs` | Every command on this page; with no arguments, the wizard |

It requires Node 22 or later.

---

## Create an app

```bash
npx -p @telamonjs/cli create-telamonjs-app my-admin
```

Or install the CLI globally and use `telamonjs`:

```bash
npm install -g @telamonjs/cli
telamonjs create my-admin
```

The single-app template is a Next.js admin wired to `@telamonjs/ui`: an
`AdminShell` layout with its menu, NextAuth v5, Prisma with a `docker-compose.yml`
database, a reference CRUD module (`usuarios`) whose create, edit and view open in
dialogs, database-backed roles and permissions (below), and `pt-BR`/`en`/`es`
messages. Unless you pass `--skip-install`, the CLI
installs dependencies and then sets the app up: it copies `.env`, starts the
database container, runs the migrations and the seed. Then:

```bash
cd my-admin
pnpm dev     # http://localhost:3001, sign in as admin@example.com / 12345
```

If the automatic setup fails (Docker not running, for example), the CLI prints
the manual steps: `docker compose up -d db`, `cp .env.example .env`,
`pnpm db:migrate`, `pnpm db:seed`.

### Roles and permissions in a new app

New apps ship RBAC from the database, built on
[`@telamonjs/permissions`](/docs/packages/permissions) and
[`@telamonjs/auth`](/docs/packages/auth):

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| `Role`, `Permission`, `RolePermission`, `UserRole` tables (the package's Prisma fragment); `User` has `roles`, `active`, `accessChangedAt`, `sessionsRevokedAt` | `prisma/schema.prisma` |
| The permission catalog (`users.read/write`, `roles.read/write`) and `loadAccess()` | `src/rbac.ts` |
| Catalog sync with `diffPermissionCatalog`, a built-in `admin` role holding every permission, the admin user with that role | `prisma/seed.ts` (idempotent: rerun it after adding a permission) |
| Roles and permission codes materialized into the JWT at sign-in; on every renewal `sessionState` signs out a deactivated or revoked user and recomputes the claims of a stale token | `src/auth.ts` |
| `requirePermission('users.write')` in every Route Handler | `src/lib/auth.ts`, `src/app/api/**` |
| `PermissionsProvider` around the `AdminShell`, menu items with `permission`, CrudConfigs with `permissions` | `LayoutProviders.tsx`, `src/config/menu.ts` |
| `/admin/papeis`: role CRUD and a `PermissionMatrix` tab (built-in roles locked); `/admin/usuarios`: multi-role assignment, activate/deactivate | `src/app/admin/**` |

Changing a role's permissions, renaming or deleting it, or changing a user's
roles stamps `accessChangedAt` on the affected users, so their next request
carries fresh claims without a new sign-in; deactivating a user or changing
their password stamps `sessionsRevokedAt` and ends their sessions. Granting has a
ceiling (`canGrant()` in `src/rbac.ts`): `users.write`, `roles.write` and
`invitations.write` only confer permissions the acting user already holds, only an
admin confers the built-in `admin` role, and a user with more access than yours
can't be edited; anything else is a 403. In the monorepo, `src/rbac.ts`
moves to `packages/shared` (`@<name>/shared/rbac`) and `apps/api` enforces the
same codes with `createPermissionsGuard` and `@Permissions(...)`.

### Options

```bash
telamonjs create [project-name] [options]   # alias: telamonjs new
```

| Option | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `-p, --provider <provider>` | `postgresql` | Database: `postgresql` or `mysql` |
| `--port <port>` | `3001` | Development server port |
| `--monorepo` | asked | Generate a pnpm monorepo instead of a single app (see below) |
| `--skip-install` | | Skip dependency installation and the automatic setup |
| `--skip-git` | | Skip `git init` |

Without `--monorepo`, `create` asks whether you want a monorepo when it runs in a
terminal, and creates a single app when it does not (CI, piped stdin).

```bash
telamonjs create my-admin --provider mysql --port 3005 --skip-git
```

### The wizard

`telamonjs` with no arguments, `telamonjs wizard` (alias `init`), or
`npx -p @telamonjs/cli create-telamonjs-app` with no arguments starts an
interactive setup. It asks for:

1. the project name
2. the database (PostgreSQL or MySQL)
3. the development server port (1024-65535, default 3001)
4. monorepo or single app
5. whether to install dependencies
6. whether to initialize git

It shows a summary, asks for confirmation, then runs `create` with those answers.

### `--monorepo`

```bash
npx -p @telamonjs/cli create-telamonjs-app my-admin --monorepo
```

```
apps/web/         Next.js + @telamonjs/ui, port <port>
apps/api/         NestJS API, prefix /v1, port <port> + 1000
apps/jobs/        BullMQ worker and scheduler on @telamonjs/queue
packages/shared/  Prisma schema and client, shared by web, api and jobs
```

`apps/web` starts from the single-app template, with Prisma, `src/rbac.ts` and
the Route Handlers of `usuarios` and `roles` moved out to `packages/shared` and
`apps/api`. The
monorepo uses pnpm through corepack and does not run the database setup for you:

```bash
cd my-admin
corepack enable pnpm        # once per machine
cp .env.example .env        # fill NEXTAUTH_SECRET (openssl rand -base64 32)
docker compose up -d        # postgres + redis
pnpm db:push
pnpm db:seed
pnpm dev                    # apps/web
pnpm dev:api                # apps/api
pnpm worker                 # apps/jobs
```

---

## generate crud

```bash
telamonjs generate crud [name] [options]   # alias: telamonjs g crud
```

Run it from the app root. It reads the Prisma schema, maps each model field
to a form field type and a column, and writes a module in the
[standard structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure). The schema is the
one `package.json#prisma.schema` names, else `prisma/schema.prisma` (also
`database/`, `src/prisma/` and a multi-file `prisma/schema/` folder); from a
monorepo's `apps/web` it finds `packages/shared/prisma` at the workspace root.
When the schema or the model is missing it stops and says where it looked, or
which models exist; `--no-prisma-schema` generates generic fields instead.

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `src/app/admin/<name>/config.tsx` | Zod schema, columns, form sections and the `CrudConfig`, with create, edit and view dialogs |
| `src/app/admin/<name>/page.tsx` | `<ListPage config={…} />`, the module's only route |
| `src/app/admin/<name>/_components/<Model>Detail.tsx` | The view dialog body |
| `src/lib/api/<name>-client.ts` | Typed REST client used by the config |
| `src/app/api/<name>/route.ts`, `[id]/route.ts` | Route Handlers backed by Prisma, gated by `requirePermission`: `<name>.read` on `GET`, `<name>.write` on `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` |

It also adds `<name>.read` and `<name>.write` to `PERMISSIONS` in `src/rbac.ts`
(`packages/shared/src/rbac.ts` from a monorepo's `apps/web`), adds the module
to the menu with `permission: '<name>.read'` and gives the `CrudConfig` the
same codes in `permissions`, writes the module's messages to
`messages/{pt-BR,en,es}.json` when the app has i18n, and formats the files with
Prettier when it is available. In an app whose `src/lib/auth.ts` has no
`requirePermission()` (one created before the template shipped RBAC), it stops
before writing anything and names the template files to add first.

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `[name]` | Module name, plural: folder, route and query key |
| `-m, --model <model>` | Prisma model to read (singular) |
| `-p, --path <path>` | Module path (default `src/app/admin/<name>`) |
| `--no-prisma-schema` | Skip Prisma detection and generate generic fields |
| `--no-update-menu` | Do not add the module to the menu |
| `-f, --force` | Overwrite the module's messages block if it already exists |

Missing arguments are asked interactively, including a pick list of the models
found in the schema.

```bash
telamonjs generate crud products --model Product
telamonjs g crud                                  # fully interactive
```

The output is a starting point. Fill in the `loadField` stubs for relationships
and review the validation schema: neither can be inferred from the schema. Run
`pnpm db:seed` so the admin role gets the new permissions, then grant them to
the other roles that need the module. Icons are resolved by name from
`src/lib/icons.ts`.

<Callout type='warn' title='Monorepo apps'>
  The generated Route Handlers import `@/lib/prisma`, which only exists in the single-app
  template. In a monorepo, the API belongs in `apps/api`: move the data access there and
  point the generated client at it.
</Callout>

---

## Admin kit: add admin

```bash
telamonjs add admin <module> [--dry-run] [--cwd <dir>]
```

Adds a ready-made admin module to an app generated by `telamonjs create`. It
detects the layout (single app, or a monorepo with `apps/api` and
`packages/shared/prisma`) and writes the module in the app's own patterns:
Prisma model, API with permission checks, permission codes, menu entry, i18n
messages and an admin page.

| Module | Prisma model | Permissions | Admin page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `audit` | `AuditLog`: user, impersonator, action, entity type and id, `changes` (JSON, secrets redacted), IP, user agent, method, path, status, date; indexed by entity, user and date | `audit.read` | `/admin/auditoria`: read-only list (when, who, action, entity, record), action filter, view dialog with `AuditChangesViewer` |
| `parameters` | `Parameter`: unique `key`, text `value` read through `type` (`STRING`, `NUMBER`, `BOOLEAN`, `JSON`), `description`, `group`, `public` | `parameters.read`, `parameters.write` | `/admin/parametros`: CRUD in dialogs, the value input follows the type |
| `invitations` | `Invitation`: `email`, `name`, `roleIds`, `tokenHash` (sha256 of the link's token, unique), `status` (`PENDING`, `ACCEPTED`, `REVOKED`; a pending one past `expiresAt` reads as `EXPIRED`), `expiresAt`, `acceptedAt`, `resendCount`, `invitedById`, `userId` | `invitations.read`, `invitations.write` | `/admin/convites`: list (email, roles, status, expiry, inviter), invite dialog with a roles multiselect, resend and revoke row actions; plus the public `/convite/<token>` accept page |

What each module writes besides the shared edits below:

| Module | Single app | Monorepo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit` | `src/lib/audit.ts` (`audit()`, built on `computeDiff` and `redactPayload`), `GET /api/audit` and `/api/audit/[id]`; the users and roles Route Handlers call `audit()` after each create, update, (de)activation, deletion, grant and revoke. The IP is the `X-Forwarded-For` entry your reverse proxy added: `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` from the right (default `1`; `0` when Next is reached directly, which records no IP) | `apps/api/src/modules/audit` (`GET /v1/audit`, `GET /v1/audit/:id`), and `createAuditInterceptor` registered as `APP_INTERCEPTOR`, so every successful, authenticated mutation is recorded |
| `parameters` | `src/lib/parameters.ts` (`getParameter(key, fallback)`), Route Handlers under `/api/parameters` | `apps/api/src/modules/parameters` (`ParametersService.get(key, fallback)`, exported by its module), wired into `AppModule` |
| `invitations` | `src/lib/invitations.ts`, `src/lib/mail.ts` (the mail port: `sendMail({ to, subject, html, text })`), Route Handlers under `/api/invitations` | `apps/api/src/modules/invitations` wired into `AppModule`, and `apps/api/src/modules/mail` (the mail port: the `MAIL_SENDER` token, a `MailSender` interface and `ConsoleMailSender`) |

The audit list takes the filters `entityType`, `entityId`, `userId`, `action`,
`from` and `to` (ISO dates), plus `search`. `GET /parameters/public?keys=a,b`
needs no session and answers `{ key: value }` for the requested parameters marked
`public`, typed; private and unknown keys are absent.

Invitations: `GET /invitations`, `POST /invitations`, `POST /invitations/:id/resend`
(a new link, the previous one stops working, a new 7-day expiry) and
`PUT /invitations/:id/revoke` check the permissions; `GET /invitations/by-token/:token`
and `POST /invitations/accept` need no session. The link carries a random 32-byte
token (`generateApiKey` from `@telamonjs/auth`) and the row keeps only its sha256
(`hashApiKey`). Inviting an email that already has a user or a pending invitation is
a 409; inviting with a role beyond your own access (the `canGrant` ceiling above) is a 403. Accepting creates the user (active, with the invited roles that still exist)
and marks the invitation accepted in one transaction; an unknown, used, revoked or
expired token gets the same 410. The accept page then signs in with the new
credentials. Mail goes through the port above, which only logs to the console:
replace it with your provider. The link is `NEXTAUTH_URL/convite/<token>`, never
the request's host, and the run notes it in `.env.example`.

Shared edits, all idempotent:

- `schema.prisma` gets a block between `// telamonjs:admin:<module>` markers;
  with a multi-file schema folder (`prisma/schema/`), the model goes in its own
  `<module>.prisma` file.
- The permission codes go into `PERMISSIONS` in `src/rbac.ts`
  (`packages/shared/src/rbac.ts` in the monorepo).
- A menu entry with its `permission` joins the Administration group of
  `src/config/menu.ts`.
- The module's keys are merged into `messages/{pt-BR,en,es}.json`; keys the app
  already has are never overwritten.
- `@telamonjs/data` is added to the dependencies when missing.

A second run changes nothing, and a module file that already exists is kept as
it is. `--dry-run` lists the files it would create or modify and writes nothing.
A code patch whose anchor is gone (a Route Handler you changed) is skipped with a
warning naming what to add by hand.

The command never touches the database. Afterwards:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm db:migrate --name add-audit   # monorepo: or pnpm db:push
pnpm db:seed                       # syncs the catalog; the admin role gets the new permissions
```

<Callout type='info' title='Apps not generated from the templates'>
  `add admin` refuses an app without `src/rbac.ts` and a `Role` model: it only edits code it
  knows. In an existing app, adopt the runtime pieces instead: `createAuditInterceptor` and
  `@SkipAudit` from `@telamonjs/data/nest`, `computeDiff` and `redactPayload` from
  `@telamonjs/data`, `AuditChangesViewer` and `PermissionMatrix` from `@telamonjs/ui`, and
  `diffPermissionCatalog` from `@telamonjs/permissions`.
</Callout>

---

## lint

```bash
telamonjs lint [dir] [--json]
```

Checks admin modules against the list, dialog and hub conventions. `dir` defaults
to `src/app/admin` when it exists, otherwise the current directory. Generated apps
have it as a script: `pnpm lint:telamonjs`.

Rules on `CrudConfig` run on every `config.tsx`; page rules run on every other
`.tsx`. A value the linter cannot resolve statically is never reported. The exit
code is 1 when there is at least one error, 0 otherwise, and 2 when the directory
does not exist. `--json` prints the report as JSON. Messages are printed in
Portuguese.

| Rule | Severity | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `list-infinite` | error | `list.infiniteScroll: false`: lists use infinite scroll, the default |
| `list-title-empty` | warning | `list.title` / `list.description` should be `''`: the shell breadcrumb names the page |
| `list-pagesize` | warning | `list.defaultPageSize` missing or below 50 (use 100 with infinite scroll) |
| `actions-icon-tooltip` | error | `actionsConfig.standard.view/edit/delete` needs `{ icon, tooltip }`, and `delete` also a `confirmDialog` |
| `view-header` | error / warning | `dialogs.view` without `headerConfig` or `renderHeader` (error); a `headerConfig` without `icon` or `title` (warning) |
| `view-content` | error | `dialogs.view` without `renderContent` or `portal` |
| `view-tabs` | error | The view dialog body imports raw `Tabs`/`TabsList`/`TabsTrigger`/`TabsContent` instead of `ContentTabs` |
| `dialog-height` | warning | A view dialog body with `ContentTabs` and no fixed height (`h-[min(600px,60vh)] overflow-y-auto`) |
| `portal-size` | warning | A view dialog body with more than 5 tabs: use `dialogs.view.portal` |
| `form-span` | error | A field `span` other than `'1'`, `'2'`, `'3'`, `'12'` or `'full'` |
| `no-fetch-in-config` | error | `fetch()` in `config.tsx`: only `src/lib/api/<module>-client.ts` calls `fetch` |
| `no-crud-pages` | error | `adicionar/page.tsx`, `[id]/page.tsx` or `[id]/editar/page.tsx` next to a `config.tsx`: CRUD happens in the list's dialogs |
| `icons-from-registry` | error | `config.tsx` imports from `lucide-react` instead of using `getIcon('Name')` from `@/lib/icons` |
| `no-raw-link` | error | A raw `<a>` or next/link `<Link>` for navigation instead of `<Button asChild><Link /></Button>` (external `target='_blank'`, downloads, `mailto:` and `tel:` are allowed) |
| `button-icon-size` | warning | An icon inside a `Button` whose `className` lacks `h-4 w-4` or `size-4` |
| `i18n-literal-in-config` | error | A pt-BR literal in `title`, `label`, `header`, `placeholder` or `description` in `config.tsx`, in an app with i18n: use `msg('<key>')` |
| `hub-tabs` | warning | A page with more than 5 tabs in `useTabUrlSync`: use `AdminPortal` |
| `i18n-untranslated` | warning | A key in `messages/en.json` or `es.json` whose value is identical to `pt-BR.json` |

To silence a deliberate exception, add a comment to the flagged file:

```tsx
// telamonjs-lint-disable-file no-crud-pages
```

List several rules separated by commas, or name none to disable every rule in that
file.

---

## link / unlink

```bash
telamonjs link [--ui <path>] [--package <path>]
telamonjs unlink [--package <path>]
```

Switch an app between the published `@telamonjs/ui` and a local TelamonJS
checkout, following the [link recipe](/docs/troubleshooting#consuming-the-packages-via-link):

- `link` sets `@telamonjs/ui` to an injected `file:` dependency on the checkout's
  `packages/ui` (`dependenciesMeta["@telamonjs/ui"].injected: true`) and adds a
  `pnpm.overrides` entry, a `link:` to its folder in `packages/`, for each package
  that `ui` declares as `workspace:^` (`@telamonjs/logger` and `@telamonjs/data`). The
  overrides go in the workspace root's `package.json`: the nearest directory
  with a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, or the app itself.
- `unlink` restores the range committed at `HEAD`, or `^` plus the latest
  published version when `HEAD` has none, never the checkout's own version, which
  may not be on npm yet. It removes the overrides and the `dependenciesMeta` entry.

| Option | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ui <path>` | `$TELAMONJS_UI`, else `../telamonjs/packages/ui` from the workspace root | The checkout's `packages/ui`; `packages/logger` and `packages/data` must sit next to it |
| `--package <path>` | `apps/web/package.json` when it exists, else `package.json` | The `package.json` that depends on `@telamonjs/ui` |

Neither command runs `pnpm install`: run it afterwards. A missing checkout, or a
`package.json` without `@telamonjs/ui`, exits 1 without writing anything.

In a monorepo generated with `--monorepo`, the root scripts `pnpm telamonjs:link`
and `pnpm telamonjs:unlink` run the command and then `pnpm install`. Its husky
hooks keep commits on the published range: `pre-commit` runs `telamonjs unlink`
and updates the lockfile (a failed update aborts the commit), and `post-commit`
runs `telamonjs link` again when `node_modules` still holds the checkout. For a
checkout outside the default location, export `TELAMONJS_UI` so the hook relinks
the same path.

---

## db

```bash
telamonjs db dump [name]   # database/dumps/<name>_<timestamp>.sql.gz
telamonjs db restore       # pick a dump from a list, confirm, restore
```

Both read `DATABASE_URL` from `.env` in the current directory and use `pg_dump`
and `psql`, so they need the PostgreSQL client tools on the `PATH` and work with
PostgreSQL only. Without a name, the dump is `dump_<timestamp>.sql.gz`.

---

## analyze

```bash
telamonjs analyze [--verbose] [--json]
```

Reads `package.json` in the current directory and reports the TelamonJS packages
installed, the database provider, NextAuth, Docker, and the recommended scripts
that are missing (`dev`, `build`, `db:migrate`, `db:seed`, and the `db:dump`
scripts for PostgreSQL), with a snippet to add them.

---

## stats

```bash
telamonjs stats [--verbose] [--json] [-p, --path <path>]
```

Git statistics for a repository (the current directory by default): lines added
and removed, commits, authors, activity by time of day, and lines per commit.

# Patterns

> The architectural patterns behind a TelamonJS app - CRUD modules, forms, dialogs, detail pages and the app shell

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/index.mdx

How TelamonJS apps are built. Read the relevant pattern **before** changing a CRUD module, a form,
a dialog, a detail page or a dashboard.

<Callout type='warn' title='Architecture'>
  Data flows Client → REST API in one hop (cookie auth), through **React Query**.
</Callout>

---

## Critical Rules

<Callout type='error' title='Dynamic Zustand selectors inside custom hooks loop forever'>
  A dynamic selector inside a custom hook causes an infinite loop (`getSnapshot should be
  cached`). Subscribe to the store and select locally. See
  [Zustand Selector Pattern](/docs/patterns/zustand-selector).
</Callout>

```ts
// ✅ CORRECT
const formState = useFormStore()
const data = formState.forms[formId]

// ❌ WRONG (inside a custom hook)
const data = useFormStore(state => state.forms[formId])
```

- `config.tsx` starts with `'use client'`.
- `query.queryFn` resolves `PaginatedResponse<T>`, and every `mutationFn` resolves
  `{ success, data? }` — adapt inside the `mutationFn`, not in the API client.
- There is no `'select'` field type: use `'relationship'` with `loadField`.

---

## CRUD Module

| Pattern | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| [Admin Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) | Where each file of a module lives, and `config.tsx` (`'use client'`) with the module's `CrudConfig` |
| [ListPage](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) | `<ListPage config={...} />`: infinite scroll (default), toolbar, filters, bulk actions, dialogs |
| [Data Layer (React Query)](/docs/patterns/react-query) | API client, `queryFn` → `PaginatedResponse<T>`, `mutationFn` → `{ success, data? }`, invalidation |
| [Form](/docs/patterns/form-pattern) | `AdminForm`/`CreateForm`/`EditForm`/`ZustandForm`: sections, grid, validation |
| [CRUD Field](/docs/patterns/crud-field) | `type: 'crud'` for 1:N / N:M lists inside a form (`create(data, { id: parentId })`) |
| [Nested Data](/docs/patterns/nested-data) | Nested records in forms with dot notation (`person.email`) |

## Dialogs, Detail Pages and Shell

| Pattern | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| [Dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs) | View, edit and create dialogs, rich headers, sizes |
| [Detail Page](/docs/patterns/detail-page) | A dedicated detail route with `DetailLayout`, `DetailCard`, `DetailField`... |
| [Standalone Form Pages](/docs/patterns/edit-page) | Create/edit routes with `CreatePage`/`EditPage`, when a dialog is not enough (dialogs are the default) |
| [Dashboard](/docs/patterns/dashboard) | `DashboardShell`, `ShellPage` + `AdminHeader` + `AdminTabs`, stat cards |
| [Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup) | `AppProviders`, the app's `QueryClient`, `AdminShell`, icon resolver |

## Cross-Cutting

| Pattern | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| [i18n](/docs/patterns/i18n) | UI text: `msg()` in configs, `useTranslations()`/`getTranslations()`, `useFormat()` |
| [Accessibility](/docs/patterns/accessibility) | `data-testid` conventions, ARIA attributes, `vitest-axe` tests |
| [Zustand Selector](/docs/patterns/zustand-selector) | Reading stores without render loops |
| [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting) | "No QueryClient set", linked packages, `getSnapshot should be cached` |

---

## A Complete CRUD Module

```
app/admin/users/
├── config.tsx          'use client' — CrudConfig (module config + data layer)
├── page.tsx            <ListPage config={config} />
└── [id]/
    └── page.tsx        Detail Page (optional — the view dialog covers most cases)

lib/api/
└── users-client.ts     list / get / create / update / delete against the API
```

```tsx title="config.tsx"
'use client'
import { type CrudConfig } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { usersApi } from '@/lib/api/users-client'

export const config: CrudConfig<User, UserFormData> = {
  module: { name: 'users', title: 'Users', description: 'Manage system users', route: '/admin/users' },
  list: { title: 'Users', description: 'Registered users', columns, searchPlaceholder: 'Search...' },
  form: { sections, validation: validationSchema },
  // queryFn resolves PaginatedResponse<User> ({ data, total, page, pageSize, totalPages })
  query: { queryKey: ['users'], queryFn: usersApi.list },
  mutations: {
    // mutationFn resolves { success, data? } — shape it here, not in the API client
    create: {
      mutationFn: async data => ({ success: true, data: await usersApi.create(data) }),
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
    update: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id, data }) => ({ success: true, data: await usersApi.update(id, data) }),
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
    delete: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id }) => {
        await usersApi.delete(id)
        return { success: true }
      },
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
  },
}
```

```tsx title="page.tsx"
import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { config } from './config'

export default function UsersPage() {
  return <ListPage config={config} />
}
```

---

## Anti-Patterns

- ❌ A dynamic Zustand selector inside a custom hook (see above)
- ❌ `type: 'select'` — use `'relationship'` with `loadField`
- ❌ Server Actions, `actions.ts` or `unstable_cache` as the data layer
- ❌ `className: 'w-full'` on a form field — the grid ignores it; use `span`
- ❌ `any` — use `unknown` or the real type
- ❌ `redirect()` inside `try`/`catch` — the `NEXT_REDIRECT` error is caught; redirect outside the block
- ❌ Looking for React Query hooks in `@telamonjs/ui` — they are not re-exported; import `@tanstack/react-query` directly

---

## Next Steps

1. [Admin Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) - What goes in `config.tsx`
2. [ListPage](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) - Everything `ListPage` does with the config
3. [Data Layer (React Query)](/docs/patterns/react-query) - API client, mutations and invalidation
4. [Form Pattern](/docs/patterns/form-pattern) - Sections, grid and validation
5. [Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup) - App shell + providers

# CrudConfig

> The central concept of TelamonJS — one object that drives an entire CRUD module

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/getting-started/crud-config.mdx

`CrudConfig<T, TFormData>` is the **central concept** of TelamonJS. One object
holds everything a CRUD module needs — module metadata, list columns, form
sections, data fetching, mutations, row actions and dialogs — and `ListPage`
reads it all from a single prop.

```tsx
<ListPage config={config} />
```

<Callout type='warn' title="'use client' is required">
  The `config.tsx` file MUST start with `'use client'`: `query` and
  `mutations` are wired to React Query hooks, which only run client-side.
</Callout>

---

## Anatomy

| Key | Type | Required | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `module` | `ModuleMetadata` | Yes | Identification: `name`, `title`, `description`, `route` (all required) |
| `list` | `ListConfig<T>` | Yes | `title`, `description` (required), columns, search placeholder, sorting, page size, toolbar |
| `form` | `FormConfig` | No | Form `sections` + Zod `validation` (optional), shared by the create and edit dialogs. Omit it for a read-only list |
| `query` | `QueryConfig<T>` | Yes | React Query: `queryKey`, `queryFn`, `staleTime?`, `refetchInterval?` |
| `mutations` | `MutationsConfig<T, TFormData>` | Yes | `create`/`update`/`delete` (each a `MutationConfig`) with declarative `invalidates`, plus `getForEdit`/`getForView` |
| `actionsConfig` | `DataTableActionsConfig<T> \| false` | No | Row action buttons: `standard: { view, edit, delete }` + custom actions |
| `dialogs` | `DialogsConfig<T>` | No | View/edit/create dialogs: rich headers, the view body, deep links via `urlParam` |
| `pages` | `PagesConfig<T>` | No | Dedicated pages instead of dialogs (see [Standalone form pages](/docs/patterns/edit-page)) |
| `permissions` | `CrudPermissions` | No | Who may create, edit, delete, view and export (see [Permissions](#permissions)) |

`create`, `update` and `delete` are each optional: an omitted one resolves
`{ success: false }` instead of throwing, so a read-only module needs no stub
mutations.

A read-only list also needs no form: without `form`, `ListPage` offers no "New"
button and no create or edit dialog, even if `dialogs.create` / `dialogs.edit`
are set. The view dialog keeps working.

### Permissions

`permissions` names the permission each operation needs (a string, or an array
meaning any of them). An operation without one stays allowed:

```tsx
import { createPermissionChecker } from '@telamonjs/permissions'
import type { AuthUser } from '@telamonjs/auth'

const checker = createPermissionChecker({ bypassRoles: ['superadmin'] })

export function usuariosConfigFor(user: AuthUser): CrudConfig<Usuario, UsuarioFormData> {
  return {
    ...usuariosConfig,
    permissions: {
      can: perm => checker.can(user, perm),
      create: 'usuarios.create',
      edit: 'usuarios.update',
      delete: 'usuarios.delete',
      view: 'usuarios.read',
    },
  }
}
```

| Operation | Gates |
| --- | --- |
| `create` | the "New" button and the create dialog (`?create=1` included) |
| `edit` | the row edit, the view dialog's Edit, the edit dialog and `dialogs.view.portal.onSaveSection` |
| `delete` | the row delete and the view dialog's Delete |
| `view` | the row view and the view dialog (row click included) |
| `export` | the toolbar export menu (`list.enableExport` / `list.onExport`) |

The checker is `can` when set, so bypass roles and wildcards work as your
checker defines them. Without `can`, the names are looked up in
`actionsConfig.userPermissions`; without either, the `can` of a
[`PermissionsProvider`](#one-checker-for-the-whole-app) above the list decides.
The row view/edit/delete inherit the operation's permission unless their own
`ActionConfig` declares a `permission`, and the same checker decides the
`permission` of custom actions (`permissions.can` becomes `actionsConfig.can`).

With no checker at all, everything is allowed: the gate is
fail-open, so a config that forgot the checker shows every write button. In
development the list warns once per config when that happens. Set
`failClosed: true` (same meaning as in `@telamonjs/permissions`) to deny every
declared operation and every action `permission` until a checker exists — for
example while the session that feeds `can` is still loading:

```tsx
permissions: {
  failClosed: true,
  can: session ? perm => checker.can(session.user, perm) : undefined,
  create: 'usuarios.create',
},
```

#### One checker for the whole app

Instead of injecting `can` into every config, give it once to a
`PermissionsProvider` where the session is readable (inside the app's
`SessionProvider`, around the `AdminShell`). Every `ListPage` below uses it for
`permissions.*` and action `permission`s, and `AdminShell` filters the menu with
it. A config then only names its permissions:

```tsx title="components/providers/LayoutProviders.tsx"
'use client'

import { useCallback } from 'react'
import { useSession } from 'next-auth/react'
import { AdminShell, PermissionsProvider } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function LayoutProviders({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const { data: session } = useSession()
  const can = useCallback((perm: string) => checker.can(session?.user, perm), [session])
  return (
    <PermissionsProvider can={can}>
      <AdminShell menuConfig={menuConfig}>{children}</AdminShell>
    </PermissionsProvider>
  )
}
```

```tsx title="config.tsx"
permissions: { create: 'usuarios.create', edit: 'usuarios.update', export: 'usuarios.export' },
```

A checker the config declares itself (`permissions.can`, `actionsConfig.can` or
`actionsConfig.userPermissions`) wins over the provider's, and so does
`AdminShell`'s own `can` for the menu. Without a provider, nothing changes.

---

## Canonical example

This is the reference module every generated app ships
(`src/app/admin/usuarios/config.tsx`). It is compiled in CI, so it always matches
the current API. Other pages show excerpts of it and link here.

```tsx title="src/app/admin/usuarios/config.tsx"
'use client'

import { z } from 'zod'
import {
  Badge,
  type CrudColumnDef,
  type CrudConfig,
  type DialogHeaderConfig,
  type FormSection,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { msg, Msg } from '@telamonjs/ui/i18n'
import { getIcon } from '@/lib/icons'
import { usuariosApi, type Usuario } from '@/lib/api/usuarios-client'
import { rolesApi } from '@/lib/api/roles-client'
import { formatDate } from '@/lib/utils'
import UsuarioDetail from './_components/UsuarioDetail'

// ============================================================================
// 1. VALIDATION SCHEMA
// ============================================================================
export const validationSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1),
  email: z.string().email(),
  // Required on create, optional on edit (blank keeps the current password) --
  // enforced server-side in the API route, not here.
  password: z.string().min(5).optional().or(z.literal('')),
  // Multi-role: the user holds the union of the roles' permissions
  roleIds: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
  // AdminForm's FormData submit path serializes booleans as the literal
  // strings 'true'/'false' -- z.coerce.boolean() would treat ANY non-empty
  // string (including 'false') as true, so coerce explicitly instead.
  active: z.preprocess((v) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v === 'true' : v), z.boolean()).default(true),
})

export type UsuarioFormData = z.infer<typeof validationSchema>

// ============================================================================
// 2. HEADER CONFIG (view/edit/create dialogs)
// ============================================================================
const headerConfig: DialogHeaderConfig<Usuario> = {
  icon: 'User',
  iconColor: 'blue',
  title: (u) => u.name ?? u.email,
  subtitle: (u) => u.email,
  gradient: 'from-blue-50 to-indigo-50',
  badge: {
    field: 'active',
    variants: { true: 'default', false: 'secondary' },
    labels: { true: msg('usuarios.statusActive'), false: msg('usuarios.statusInactive') },
  },
}

// ============================================================================
// 3. COLUMNS
// ============================================================================
export const columns: CrudColumnDef<Usuario>[] = [
  {
    header: msg('usuarios.columns.name'),
    accessorKey: 'name',
    enableGlobalFilter: true,
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <div>
        <div className='font-medium'>{row.original.name || <Msg k='usuarios.noName' />}</div>
        <div className='text-xs text-muted-foreground'>{row.original.email}</div>
      </div>
    ),
  },
  {
    header: msg('usuarios.columns.roles'),
    id: 'roles',
    enableSorting: false,
    cell: ({ row }) =>
      row.original.roles.length ? (
        <div className='flex flex-wrap gap-1'>
          {row.original.roles.map((role) => (
            <Badge key={role.id} variant='outline'>
              {role.name}
            </Badge>
          ))}
        </div>
      ) : (
        <span className='text-sm text-muted-foreground'>
          <Msg k='usuarios.noRoles' />
        </span>
      ),
  },
  {
    header: msg('usuarios.columns.status'),
    accessorKey: 'active',
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <Badge variant={row.original.active ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>
        <Msg k={row.original.active ? 'usuarios.statusActive' : 'usuarios.statusInactive'} />
      </Badge>
    ),
  },
  {
    header: msg('usuarios.columns.createdAt'),
    accessorKey: 'createdAt',
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <span className='text-sm text-muted-foreground'>{formatDate(row.original.createdAt)}</span>
    ),
  },
]

// ============================================================================
// 4. FORM SECTIONS (rendered inside the create/edit dialogs)
// ============================================================================
export const formSections: FormSection[] = [
  {
    label: msg('usuarios.sections.personal.label'),
    description: msg('usuarios.sections.personal.description'),
    grid: '2',
    fields: [
      {
        name: 'name',
        label: msg('usuarios.fields.name'),
        type: 'text',
        placeholder: msg('usuarios.fields.namePlaceholder'),
        required: true,
        focus: true,
      },
      {
        name: 'email',
        label: msg('usuarios.fields.email'),
        type: 'email',
        placeholder: msg('usuarios.fields.emailPlaceholder'),
        required: true,
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: msg('usuarios.sections.access.label'),
    description: msg('usuarios.sections.access.description'),
    grid: '2',
    fields: [
      {
        name: 'password',
        label: msg('usuarios.fields.password'),
        type: 'password',
        placeholder: msg('usuarios.fields.passwordPlaceholder'),
        description: msg('usuarios.fields.passwordDescription'),
      },
      {
        name: 'roleIds',
        label: msg('usuarios.fields.roles'),
        type: 'multiselect',
        description: msg('usuarios.fields.rolesDescription'),
        // Options are domain data (role names), not chrome text.
        loadField: async () => {
          const { data } = await rolesApi.list({ page: 1, pageSize: 100 })
          return data.map((role) => ({ value: role.id, label: role.name }))
        },
      },
      {
        name: 'active',
        label: msg('usuarios.fields.active'),
        type: 'boolean',
        description: msg('usuarios.fields.activeDescription'),
        // span = section grid -> full width (className 'w-full' is a no-op: CSS Grid)
        span: '2',
      },
    ],
  },
]

// ============================================================================
// 5. CRUD CONFIG
// ============================================================================
export const usuariosConfig: CrudConfig<Usuario, UsuarioFormData> = {
  module: {
    name: 'usuarios',
    title: msg('usuarios.title'),
    description: msg('usuarios.description'),
    route: '/admin/usuarios',
  },

  // Checked with the PermissionsProvider's `can` (LayoutProviders): a denied
  // operation loses its button, row action and dialog deep link. The Route
  // Handlers enforce the same codes.
  permissions: {
    view: 'users.read',
    create: 'users.write',
    edit: 'users.write',
  },

  list: {
    // Empty: the shell breadcrumb already names the page; the list is content, not a header.
    title: '',
    description: '',
    searchPlaceholder: msg('usuarios.searchPlaceholder'),
    columns,
    defaultSortBy: 'name',
    defaultSortOrder: 'asc',
    serverSidePagination: true,
    infiniteScroll: true,
    defaultPageSize: 100,
    // ICU plural: the message takes `{count}` (messages/*.json)
    toolbar: { counterLabel: msg('usuarios.counter') },
  },

  form: { sections: formSections, validation: validationSchema },

  query: { queryKey: ['usuarios'], queryFn: usuariosApi.list, staleTime: 30_000 },

  mutations: {
    // mutationFn must resolve to { success, data? } -- usuariosApi.* returns
    // the raw entity, so we shape the result here rather than in the client.
    create: {
      mutationFn: async (data) => ({ success: true, data: await usuariosApi.create(data) }),
      invalidates: [['usuarios']],
    },
    update: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id, data }) => {
        // Blank password means "keep the current one" -- don't send it.
        const { password, ...rest } = data
        return { success: true, data: await usuariosApi.update(id, password ? data : rest) }
      },
      invalidates: [['usuarios']],
    },
    // No delete: users are deactivated (row action below), never removed.
    getForEdit: async (id) => {
      const u = await usuariosApi.getById(id)
      return {
        name: u.name ?? '',
        email: u.email,
        password: '',
        roleIds: u.roles.map((role) => role.id),
        active: u.active,
      }
    },
    getForView: usuariosApi.getById,
  },

  actionsConfig: {
    standard: {
      view: { icon: getIcon('Eye'), tooltip: msg('usuarios.actions.view') },
      edit: { icon: getIcon('Pencil'), tooltip: msg('usuarios.actions.edit') },
    },
    // The list refetches after a custom handler succeeds.
    custom: [
      {
        id: 'deactivate',
        icon: getIcon('UserX'),
        tooltip: msg('usuarios.actions.deactivate'),
        permission: 'users.write',
        visible: (row) => row.active,
        handler: (row) => usuariosApi.update(row.id, { active: false }),
        successMessage: msg('usuarios.actions.deactivated'),
        confirmDialog: {
          title: (row) => msg('usuarios.confirmDeactivate.title', { name: row.name ?? row.email }),
          description: msg('usuarios.confirmDeactivate.description'),
          confirmText: msg('usuarios.confirmDeactivate.confirmText'),
          cancelText: msg('usuarios.confirmDeactivate.cancelText'),
          variant: 'destructive',
        },
      },
      {
        id: 'activate',
        icon: getIcon('UserCheck'),
        tooltip: msg('usuarios.actions.activate'),
        permission: 'users.write',
        visible: (row) => !row.active,
        handler: (row) => usuariosApi.update(row.id, { active: true }),
        successMessage: msg('usuarios.actions.activated'),
      },
    ],
  },

  dialogs: {
    view: {
      urlParam: 'view',
      title: msg('usuarios.dialogs.view.title'),
      headerConfig,
      renderContent: (item) => <UsuarioDetail usuario={item} />,
    },
    edit: {
      urlParam: 'edit',
      title: msg('usuarios.dialogs.edit.title'),
      description: msg('usuarios.dialogs.edit.description'),
      headerConfig,
    },
    create: {
      urlParam: 'create',
      title: msg('usuarios.dialogs.create.title'),
      description: msg('usuarios.dialogs.create.description'),
      headerConfig: {
        ...headerConfig,
        title: msg('usuarios.dialogs.create.title'),
        subtitle: undefined,
        badge: undefined,
      },
      defaultValues: { active: true, roleIds: [] },
    },
  },
}
```

The page stays a one-liner:

```tsx title="src/app/admin/usuarios/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { usuariosConfig } from './config'

// All CRUD (view/create/edit/delete) happens in dialogs on this list —
// there are no adicionar/ or [id]/ routes.
export default function UsuariosPage() {
  return <ListPage config={usuariosConfig} />
}
```

What to notice:

- **`query.queryFn`** resolves `PaginatedResponse<T>` (`data`, `page`, `total`,
  `totalPages`). The list is an infinite, virtualized scroll by default and needs
  that metadata to page.
- **Every `mutationFn`** resolves `{ success, data? }`. The API client returns
  the raw entity; the config shapes it, not the client.
- **`getForEdit`** maps the record to the form's shape (here it blanks the
  password and turns `roles` into `roleIds`); **`getForView`** passes the record
  to the view dialog as is.
- **`permissions`** names the code each operation needs; the app's
  `PermissionsProvider` checks them, and the Route Handlers enforce the same
  codes. There is no `delete`: users are deactivated by a custom row action, and
  the list refetches after its `handler` succeeds.
- **`dialogs`** replace create, edit and detail routes. `urlParam` makes each one
  linkable (`?view=<id>`, `?edit=<id>`, `?create=1`), and Back closes it.
- **Text slots** take `msg('<key>')` (from `@telamonjs/ui/i18n`) so they follow
  the active locale. Text rendered inside a `cell` uses `<Msg k='<key>' />`.
- **Icons** are strings resolved through the app's registry (`getIcon('Eye')`),
  never Lucide components imported into the config.
- **`relationship`** and **`multiselect`** (the roles here) load their options
  with `loadField`. There is no `'select'` field type and no `options` prop.

---

## Data flow

The generated app has one direction: Route Handler (Prisma) →
`<module>-client.ts` (`fetch`) → `config.tsx`. In the monorepo layout the
client calls the NestJS API instead. Either way, React Query manages it:

- `query.queryFn` loads the list, cached under `query.queryKey`.
- `mutations.*.mutationFn` calls the API client.
- `invalidates` declares which query keys to refresh on success — it must match
  `query.queryKey` for the list to update.

---

## Related types

All exported from `@telamonjs/ui`:

- `CrudConfig<T, TFormData>` — the main interface
- `ModuleMetadata`, `ListConfig<T>`, `FormConfig`
- `QueryConfig<T>`, `MutationConfig<TInput, TOutput>`, `MutationsConfig<T, TFormData>`
- `DialogConfig<T>`, `DialogsConfig<T>`, `PagesConfig<T>`
- `CrudPermissions` — the `permissions` key
- `CrudConfigWithAnyForm<T>` — alias for `CrudConfig<T, any>` when a context must accept any config (`TFormData` is invariant)

---

- [Quick Start](/docs/getting-started/quick-start) — generate a module like this one from a Prisma model
- [ListPage Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) — everything `ListPage` does with your config
- [Dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs) — headers, detail tabs, the portal view
- [Form Pattern](/docs/patterns/form-pattern) — sections, validation and field types

# Module Structure

> The files of a CRUD admin module, what goes in config.tsx, and how data flows from the list to the database

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure.mdx

A TelamonJS admin module is one `config.tsx` that declares everything (schema,
columns, form sections and the `CrudConfig` with its data layer), a one-line
`page.tsx` that renders `<ListPage config={config} />`, a typed API client, and
the REST Route Handlers behind it. Create, view, edit and delete open in dialogs
on the list, so the list is the module's only route.

This is the shape `telamonjs create` gives the reference module of a new app and
the shape [`telamonjs generate crud`](/docs/packages/cli#generate-crud) writes
from a Prisma model.

<Callout type='info' title='Nested data?'>
  If the module edits nested relations (e.g. `person.name`), read [Nested
  Data](/docs/patterns/nested-data) first.
</Callout>

---

## Files

```
src/
├── app/
│   ├── admin/users/
│   │   ├── config.tsx              # 'use client': schema, columns, form sections, CrudConfig
│   │   ├── page.tsx                # <ListPage config={config} />, the only route
│   │   └── _components/
│   │       └── UserDetail.tsx      # view dialog body, custom cells
│   └── api/users/
│       ├── route.ts                # GET (list) + POST (create)
│       └── [id]/route.ts           # GET + PATCH + DELETE
└── lib/api/
    └── users-client.ts             # the only file that calls fetch() for this module
```

| Concern | File | Runs on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Configuration | `config.tsx` | Client |
| Page | `page.tsx` | Client |
| API client | `lib/api/<module>-client.ts` | Client |
| HTTP API | `app/api/<module>/route.ts`, `[id]/route.ts` | Server |

Data flows in one direction:

```
ListPage (list + create/edit/view dialogs)
        │  React Query: queryKey + queryFn / mutationFn
        ▼
lib/api/users-client.ts      ← typed fetch client
        │  HTTP (credentials: 'include')
        ▼
app/api/users/route.ts       ← Route Handler: auth + Zod + Prisma
        ▼
      Prisma
```

The page never touches Prisma, and the Route Handlers never know about React
Query. The API client is the seam between the two.

---

## What goes in config.tsx

1. **`validationSchema`** (Zod) and the form-data type inferred from it
2. **`columns`**: `CrudColumnDef<Entity>[]`
3. **`formSections`**: `FormSection[]`
4. **`config`**: `CrudConfig<Entity, EntityFormData>` with `module`, `list`, `form`,
   `query`, `mutations`, `actionsConfig` and `dialogs`

Everything is a **named export**, so pages, dialogs and tests import exactly what
they use.

<Callout type='warn' title="'use client' is required">
  `ListPage` turns `query`/`mutations` into React Query hooks, and the config holds
  React components (cells, icons) and functions (`loadField`, `mutationFn`). Next.js
  cannot pass those from a Server Component, so the whole file is a Client Component.
</Callout>

```tsx title="app/admin/users/config.tsx"
'use client'

import { z } from 'zod'
import type { CrudColumnDef, CrudConfig, DialogHeaderConfig, FormSection } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { getIcon } from '@/lib/icons'
import { usersApi, type User } from '@/lib/api/users-client'
import { UserDetail } from './_components/UserDetail'

// 1. Validation schema: one schema, also the source of the form-data type
export const validationSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1, 'Name is required'),
  email: z.string().email('Invalid email'),
  role: z.enum(['USER', 'ADMIN']),
  active: z.boolean().default(true),
})

export type UserFormData = z.infer<typeof validationSchema>

// 2. Table columns
export const columns: CrudColumnDef<User>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
  { accessorKey: 'email', header: 'Email' },
  { accessorKey: 'role', header: 'Role' },
]

// 3. Form sections: `label`, not `title`; BaseForm is a CSS grid, widths come from `span`
export const formSections: FormSection[] = [
  {
    label: 'User',
    grid: '2',
    fields: [
      { name: 'name', label: 'Name', type: 'text', required: true, focus: true },
      { name: 'email', label: 'Email', type: 'email', required: true },
      {
        name: 'role',
        label: 'Role',
        type: 'relationship', // there is no 'select' type; options come from loadField
        required: true,
        loadField: async () => [
          { value: 'USER', label: 'User' },
          { value: 'ADMIN', label: 'Admin' },
        ],
      },
      { name: 'active', label: 'Active', type: 'boolean', span: '2' }, // full width = section grid
    ],
  },
]

const headerConfig: DialogHeaderConfig<User> = {
  icon: 'User',
  iconColor: 'blue',
  title: user => user.name,
  subtitle: user => user.email,
  gradient: 'from-blue-50 to-indigo-50',
}

// 4. CrudConfig: the object ListPage reads
export const config: CrudConfig<User, UserFormData> = {
  module: { name: 'users', title: 'Users', description: 'Manage system users', route: '/admin/users' },

  list: {
    title: '', // the shell breadcrumb already names the page
    description: '',
    searchPlaceholder: 'Search...',
    columns,
    defaultPageSize: 100, // infinite scroll (the default) fetches large pages
    enableExport: true,
  },

  form: { sections: formSections, validation: validationSchema },

  // queryFn resolves PaginatedResponse<User> ({ data, total, page, pageSize, totalPages })
  query: { queryKey: ['users'], queryFn: usersApi.list },

  mutations: {
    // mutationFn resolves { success, data? }; the client returns the raw entity, so adapt here
    create: {
      mutationFn: async data => ({ success: true, data: await usersApi.create(data) }),
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
    update: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id, data }) => ({ success: true, data: await usersApi.update(id, data) }),
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
    delete: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id }) => {
        await usersApi.delete(id)
        return { success: true }
      },
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
    getForEdit: usersApi.getById, // loads the record when the edit dialog opens
    getForView: usersApi.getById, // loads the record when the view dialog opens
  },

  actionsConfig: {
    standard: {
      view: { icon: getIcon('Eye'), tooltip: 'View' },
      edit: { icon: getIcon('Pencil'), tooltip: 'Edit' },
      delete: {
        icon: getIcon('Trash2'),
        tooltip: 'Delete',
        confirmDialog: {
          title: row => `Delete ${row.name}?`,
          description: 'This action cannot be undone.',
          confirmText: 'Delete',
          variant: 'destructive',
        },
      },
    },
  },

  dialogs: {
    view: { urlParam: 'view', title: 'User', headerConfig, renderContent: user => <UserDetail user={user} /> },
    edit: { urlParam: 'edit', title: 'Edit user', headerConfig },
    create: { urlParam: 'create', title: 'New user', defaultValues: { active: true, role: 'USER' } },
  },
}
```

```tsx title="app/admin/users/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { config } from './config'

export default function UsersPage() {
  return <ListPage config={config} />
}
```

Every key is documented in [CrudConfig](/docs/getting-started/crud-config). What
`ListPage` does with the config (search, filters, sorting, toolbar) is in
[List pages](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern), the dialogs in
[Dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs), and the `query`/`mutations` contract in
[Data layer](/docs/patterns/react-query).

<Callout type='info' title='Keep config.tsx declarative'>
  Move larger pieces (the view dialog body, custom cells) to `_components/` and keep
  business rules in the API, not in the config. In an app with i18n set up, text slots
  take `msg('<key>')` instead of literals; see [i18n](/docs/patterns/i18n).
</Callout>

---

## Route Handlers

The module owns a small REST API under `app/api/<module>/`. Every handler does
three things in order: **authorize, validate, execute**. `requirePermission()`
answers 401 without a session and 403 without the permission; a signed-in user
is not enough.

```ts title="app/api/users/route.ts"
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import { z } from 'zod'
import { prisma } from '@/lib/prisma'
import { requirePermission } from '@/lib/auth'

const createSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1),
  email: z.string().email(),
  role: z.enum(['ADMIN', 'USER']).default('USER'),
  active: z.boolean().default(true),
})

// Whitelist sortable fields: never interpolate user input into orderBy
const SORTABLE_FIELDS = new Set(['name', 'email', 'role', 'active', 'createdAt'])

export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  const currentUser = await requirePermission('users.read')
  if (currentUser instanceof NextResponse) return currentUser

  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url)
  const page = Number(searchParams.get('page') ?? '1')
  const pageSize = Number(searchParams.get('pageSize') ?? '10')
  const search = searchParams.get('search') || undefined
  const sortByParam = searchParams.get('sortBy')
  const sortBy = sortByParam && SORTABLE_FIELDS.has(sortByParam) ? sortByParam : 'createdAt'
  const sortOrder = searchParams.get('sortOrder') === 'asc' ? 'asc' : 'desc'

  const where = search
    ? {
        OR: [
          { name: { contains: search, mode: 'insensitive' as const } },
          { email: { contains: search, mode: 'insensitive' as const } },
        ],
      }
    : undefined

  const [data, total] = await Promise.all([
    prisma.user.findMany({ where, orderBy: { [sortBy]: sortOrder }, skip: (page - 1) * pageSize, take: pageSize }),
    prisma.user.count({ where }),
  ])

  return NextResponse.json({ data, total, page, pageSize, totalPages: Math.ceil(total / pageSize) })
}

export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
  const currentUser = await requirePermission('users.write')
  if (currentUser instanceof NextResponse) return currentUser

  const parsed = createSchema.safeParse(await request.json())
  if (!parsed.success) {
    return NextResponse.json({ message: parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? 'Invalid data' }, { status: 400 })
  }

  const user = await prisma.user.create({ data: parsed.data })
  return NextResponse.json(user, { status: 201 })
}
```

The `[id]/route.ts` sibling implements `GET` (one record), `PATCH` (partial update,
every field optional) and `DELETE`. Route params are async:
`const { id } = await params`.

Conventions:

- **GET list** returns the `PaginatedResponse` shape (`data`, `total`, `page`,
  `pageSize`, `totalPages`) that `ListPage` expects.
- **Errors** are `{ message }` with the right status: 400 validation, 401
  unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not found, 409 conflict.
- **Server-side rules stay server-side**: password hashing, uniqueness checks,
  "you cannot deactivate yourself". The client schema is UX; the route schema is the law.
- **Never serialize secrets**: strip `password` before returning entities.

---

## API client

One file per module wraps the REST API in typed functions. The `query` and
`mutations` of the config consume it:

```ts title="lib/api/users-client.ts"
import type { PaginatedResponse, PaginationParams } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import type { UserFormData } from '@/app/admin/users/config'

export interface User {
  id: string
  name: string
  email: string
  role: 'ADMIN' | 'USER'
  active: boolean
  createdAt: string
}

const BASE_URL = '/api/users'

async function parse<T>(res: Response, errorMessage: string): Promise<T> {
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.json().catch(() => null)
    throw new Error(body?.message ?? errorMessage)
  }
  return res.json()
}

const json = (method: string, data: unknown): RequestInit => ({
  method,
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  credentials: 'include',
  body: JSON.stringify(data),
})

export const usersApi = {
  list: (params: PaginationParams): Promise<PaginatedResponse<User>> => {
    const query = new URLSearchParams({ page: String(params.page), pageSize: String(params.pageSize) })
    if (params.search) query.set('search', params.search)
    if (typeof params.sortBy === 'string' && params.sortBy) query.set('sortBy', params.sortBy)
    if (params.sortOrder) query.set('sortOrder', params.sortOrder)
    return fetch(`${BASE_URL}?${query}`, { credentials: 'include' }).then(res => parse(res, 'Failed to load users'))
  },
  getById: (id: string): Promise<User> =>
    fetch(`${BASE_URL}/${id}`, { credentials: 'include' }).then(res => parse(res, 'User not found')),
  create: (data: UserFormData): Promise<User> =>
    fetch(BASE_URL, json('POST', data)).then(res => parse(res, 'Failed to create user')),
  update: (id: string, data: Partial<UserFormData>): Promise<User> =>
    fetch(`${BASE_URL}/${id}`, json('PATCH', data)).then(res => parse(res, 'Failed to update user')),
  delete: (id: string): Promise<void> =>
    fetch(`${BASE_URL}/${id}`, { method: 'DELETE', credentials: 'include' }).then(res => {
      if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Failed to delete user')
    }),
}
```

Rules of the seam:

- **`credentials: 'include'`** on every call: the session cookie is the auth.
- **Throw `Error` with the server's `message`** on non-OK responses; React Query
  surfaces it and the dialogs toast it.
- **The entity interface lives here**, typed as it travels over JSON (dates are
  strings), and is imported by the config and the components.
- **Query keys** are `['users']` for the list and `['users', id]` for one record.
  Mutations invalidate the list key.

---

## Dedicated pages (not the default)

Dialogs cover create, edit and view for most modules. When a form or a detail view
outgrows a dialog, the standalone pages are documented in
[Standalone form pages](/docs/patterns/edit-page) and
[Detail views](/docs/patterns/detail-page); they reuse the same `formSections` and
schema. For six or more detail sections, prefer `dialogs.view.portal` over a route.

`telamonjs lint` reports `adicionar/page.tsx`, `[id]/page.tsx` and
`[id]/editar/page.tsx` next to a `config.tsx` as `no-crud-pages` errors. Silence it
per file with `// telamonjs-lint-disable-file no-crud-pages` when the page is
deliberate. See the [rule table](/docs/packages/cli#lint).

---

## Naming

| Item | Convention | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Module folder | kebab-case, plural | `users`, `order-items` |
| API route | mirrors the module name | `app/api/users/` |
| API client file | `<module>-client.ts` | `lib/api/users-client.ts` |
| API client object | `<module>Api` | `usersApi` |
| Entity interface | PascalCase singular | `User` |
| Form data type | `<Entity>FormData` | `UserFormData` |
| Query keys | `[module]` / `[module, id]` | `['users']`, `['users', id]` |
| Components | PascalCase, module-prefixed, in `_components/` | `_components/UserDetail.tsx` |

---

## Testing the config

Everything is a named export, so the declarations are testable without rendering:

```ts title="config.test.ts"
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { columns, validationSchema } from './config'

describe('users config', () => {
  it('accepts a valid record', () => {
    expect(validationSchema.safeParse({ name: 'Ada', email: 'ada@example.com', role: 'USER' }).success).toBe(true)
  })

  it('has the expected columns', () => {
    expect(columns.map(c => c.header)).toEqual(['Name', 'Email', 'Role'])
  })
})
```

---

## FAQ

**A module without CRUD (a report)?** It doesn't need a `CrudConfig`. Keep its
filters and metadata in `config.tsx` as named exports and render your own
component from the page.

**Custom toolbar buttons (import, sync)?** Use the `ListPage` props
`headerActions`, `toolbarPrepend` and `toolbarContent`. Export comes from
`list.enableExport` (loaded rows), `list.exportAll` (every page) or `list.onExport`
(your backend); see [exporting every row](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern#exporting-every-row-or-exporting-on-the-server).

**Auto-filling a field from another?** `form.onFieldChange` receives
`{ field, value, values, setValue }` on every change.

---

## Checklist

- [ ] `config.tsx` starts with `'use client'` and has named exports only
- [ ] `EntityFormData` is inferred from `validationSchema`
- [ ] `columns` are typed `CrudColumnDef<Entity>[]`, with no hand-written actions column (`ListPage` builds it from `actionsConfig`)
- [ ] `query.queryFn` resolves `PaginatedResponse<Entity>`, not an array
- [ ] Every `mutationFn` resolves `{ success, data? }` and every `invalidates` includes the list's `queryKey`
- [ ] `lib/api/<module>-client.ts` is the only place with `fetch()`
- [ ] `page.tsx` renders `<ListPage config={config} />`; create, edit and view are `dialogs`
- [ ] `telamonjs lint` reports no errors
- [ ] No `any`

---

- [CrudConfig](/docs/getting-started/crud-config): every key of the config object
