# Data Layer (React Query)

> API client, query, mutations and cache invalidation behind every CrudConfig module

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/react-query.mdx

The browser talks to your REST API directly, in one hop, and React Query owns the cache. A
module's data layer has three parts:

| Part | Where | Job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API client | `lib/api/[entity]-client.ts` | The only file that calls `fetch()` for the entity. Returns raw entities, throws on errors |
| `query` | `CrudConfig.query` in `config.tsx` | Loads the list: resolves `PaginatedResponse<T>` |
| `mutations` | `CrudConfig.mutations` in `config.tsx` | Adapts the client to the `{ success, message?, data? }` contract and declares what to invalidate |

`config.tsx` starts with `'use client'`: `ListPage` turns `query` and `mutations` into React
Query hooks. The app's `QueryClient` and providers are covered in
[Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup); a complete client is in the
[Quick Start](/docs/getting-started/quick-start).

<Callout type='warn' title='Server Actions are not a data layer'>
  `query` and `mutations` are required on `CrudConfig`: the data layer is React Query talking to
  your REST API, not Server Actions or `unstable_cache`.
</Callout>

---

## The API Client

Keep the client thin: build the URL, send cookies, parse the response, and throw when the
response is not OK. Do not shape results for the UI here; that happens in `mutationFn`.

```ts title="lib/api/orders-client.ts"
import type { PaginatedResponse, PaginationParams } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const BASE_URL = `${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/orders`

async function parse<T>(res: Response, fallback: string): Promise<T> {
  if (!res.ok) {
    const body = await res.json().catch(() => null)
    throw new Error(body?.message ?? fallback) // this message reaches the error toast
  }
  return res.status === 204 ? (undefined as T) : res.json()
}

export const ordersApi = {
  list: (params: PaginationParams): Promise<PaginatedResponse<Order>> => {
    const qs = new URLSearchParams({ page: String(params.page), pageSize: String(params.pageSize) })
    if (params.search) qs.set('search', params.search)
    if (typeof params.sortBy === 'string') qs.set('sortBy', params.sortBy)
    if (params.sortOrder) qs.set('sortOrder', params.sortOrder)
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(params.filters ?? {})) {
      if (value !== undefined && value !== null && value !== '') qs.set(key, String(value))
    }
    return fetch(`${BASE_URL}?${qs}`, { credentials: 'include' }).then(res => parse(res, 'Failed to load orders'))
  },
  get: (id: string): Promise<Order> =>
    fetch(`${BASE_URL}/${id}`, { credentials: 'include' }).then(res => parse(res, 'Order not found')),
  // create / update / delete follow the same shape and return the raw entity (or nothing)
}
```

- `credentials: 'include'` sends the session cookie; the API validates it (see
  [Auth](/docs/packages/auth) for the NestJS guard).
- The library reads the error message from `Error.message`, a NestJS body
  `{ message: string | string[] }`, an axios-style `response.data.message`, or
  `errors: Record<string, string[]>`. Throw something that carries the backend's message and the
  toast shows it.
- The list endpoint pages, searches, sorts and filters on the server. The browser never imports
  Prisma.

---

## `query`

```ts
query: {
  queryKey: ['orders'],
  queryFn: ordersApi.list,
  staleTime: 30_000, // default: 5_000
},
```

| Key | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `queryKey` | Base key. `ListPage` appends the current page, search, sort and filters to it |
| `queryFn` | Receives `ListQueryParams` (`page`, `pageSize`, `search?`, `sortBy?`, `sortOrder?`, `filters?`) and resolves `PaginatedResponse<T>` |
| `staleTime` | Milliseconds before a cached page is refetched. Default `5_000` |
| `refetchInterval` | Polling interval, or `false`. Paginated table only |
| `options` | Extra `useQuery` options. Paginated table only |

<Callout type='warn' title='Infinite scroll ignores refetchInterval and options'>
  The default infinite list only reads `queryKey`, `queryFn` and `staleTime`. For a polling list,
  set `list.infiniteScroll: false`, or invalidate the key yourself on an interval.
</Callout>

`ListPage` always sends `sortBy` as a single column name (a string), so `ListQueryParams` is
`PaginationParams` with `sortBy?: string`. A client whose own params type says
`sortBy?: string`, `page?: number` or extra optional filter keys is a `queryFn` as is — no wrapper,
no cast:

```ts
query: { queryKey: ['orders'], queryFn: ordersApi.list },
```

`asQueryFn` (an unchecked cast) is only left for a client that still does not fit, such as one
whose result is typed differently from `PaginatedResponse<T>`.

### An endpoint that answers a plain array

For a short list whose endpoint does not page (sub-lists, queues, lookups), wrap the fetch in
`arrayQueryFn` instead of hand-building a one-page `PaginatedResponse`. It fetches the array and
does the search, filters, sort and paging in memory:

```ts
import { arrayQueryFn } from '@telamonjs/ui'

query: {
  queryKey: ['members', teamId],
  queryFn: arrayQueryFn(() => teamsApi.members(teamId), {
    searchFields: ['name', 'email'], // default: the row's top-level string/number values
  }),
},
```

- **Search**: case- and accent-insensitive substring over `searchFields` (dotted paths work).
- **Filters**: equality per key, compared as strings (toolbar values are strings, so `'true'`
  matches `true`); empty values are skipped, and the toolbar's "all" choice never reaches a
  `queryFn`. A key that `fetchAll` consumes itself (a parent id in `filters`) and the rows do not
  carry: list the keys that should filter in `filterFields` (`[]` for none).
- **Sort**: by `sortBy` — numbers, dates and booleans by value, text with `localeCompare`, empty
  values last. A nested column needs `list.sortParam: 'path'` so `sortBy` is the dotted path.
- `fetchAll` receives the `ListQueryParams`, so it can still forward a scope or a search the
  endpoint understands.

There is no cache: every page request calls `fetchAll` again. With the infinite list's default
page size most such lists load in one request; a list that outgrows that wants server paging.

### What `sortBy` carries

`list.sortParam` picks what a column's sort looks like on the wire. It applies everywhere the list
sends its sort: `queryFn`, `exportAll`, `list.onExport`, `toolbarContent` and the URL (`urlSync`).

| Column | `sortParam: 'id'` (default) | `sortParam: 'path'` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accessorKey: 'name'` | `name` | `name` |
| `accessorKey: 'created_at'` | `created_at` | `created_at` |
| `accessorKey: 'customer.name'` | `customer_name` | `customer.name` |
| `accessorKey: '_count.items'` | `_count_items` | `_count.items` |
| `id: 'owner', accessorKey: 'owner.name'` | `owner` | `owner.name` |
| `id: 'total', accessorFn` (no `accessorKey`) | `total` | `total` |

In `'id'` mode the field is TanStack's column id: a dotted `accessorKey` arrives with every `.`
turned into `_`, so a backend cannot tell `customer_name` (nested) from `created_at` (snake_case).
`'path'` sends the data path itself. Saved views and `defaultSortBy` may hold either form in both
modes (`defaultSortBy: 'customer.name'` highlights the right header).

```ts
list: { columns, sortParam: 'path' }, // opt in per list; the default in the next major
```

<Callout type='info' title="Before turning on 'path'">
  Check that the endpoint accepts the dotted form. A backend that whitelists `customer_name` will
  silently fall back to its default order for `customer.name`: add the dotted key next to the old
  one (`customer.name` and `customer_name`) and keep both while old clients are around. Order by a
  relation count with `{ items: { _count: 'asc' } }` for `_count.items`.
</Callout>

### Server helpers

`createPaginatedResponse(data, total, page, pageSize)` builds the response.
`buildPrismaOrderBy(sortBy, sortOrder, sortableFields?)` and
`buildPrismaOrderByMulti(sortFields, sortableFields?)` turn either wire form into a Prisma
`orderBy`:

- A value with a dot is a data path, used as-is: `customer.name` → `{ customer: { name } }`,
  `order_item.created_at` → `{ order_item: { created_at } }`.
- `_count.items` → `{ items: { _count: 'asc' } }` (also `customer._count.orders`), in either form.
- A value listed in `sortableFields` is used as-is, so `created_at` stays a column.
- Any other underscored value is decoded as a legacy column id (`customer_name` →
  `customer.name`); with `sortableFields`, only when the decoded path is listed. Without
  `sortableFields`, `created_at` becomes `created.at`: pass the list when you have snake_case
  fields.

`createPaginationContext(...).createPaginatedService(config)` accepts any `sortBy` the client sends
unless you set `sortableFields: ['name', 'customer.name', 'created_at']` (data paths). A legacy id
passes when its dotted form is listed (`customer_name` for `customer.name`), so one whitelist serves
both modes; anything else falls back to `defaultOrderBy`. An invalid `sortOrder` always falls back
to `defaultOrderDirection`.

---

## `mutations`

Each `mutationFn` resolves a fixed shape. The API client returns raw entities, so adapt inside
the `mutationFn`:

```ts
mutations: {
  create: {
    mutationFn: async data => ({ success: true, message: 'Order created', data: await ordersApi.create(data) }),
    invalidates: [['orders']],
  },
  update: {
    mutationFn: async ({ id, data }) => ({ success: true, data: await ordersApi.update(id, data) }),
    invalidates: [['orders'], id => ['orders', id]],
  },
  delete: {
    mutationFn: async ({ id }) => {
      await ordersApi.delete(id)
      return { success: true }
    },
    invalidates: [['orders']],
  },
  getForEdit: ordersApi.get,
  getForView: ordersApi.get,
},
```

| Key | Receives | Resolves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create.mutationFn` | the form values | `{ success, message?, data? }`: `data` is the entity |
| `update.mutationFn` | `{ id, data }` | `{ success, message?, data? }`: `data` is the entity |
| `delete.mutationFn` | `{ id }` | `{ success, message? }` |
| `getForEdit` | `id` | the record the edit form needs (nested relations included): the form data or the entity itself (`TFormData \| T`) |
| `getForView` | `id` | the record the view dialog shows |

When your actions answer something other than the entity in `data` (`{ id }`, or nothing in
particular), say so once in the config's third type argument, and `onSuccess` gets that type:

```ts
export const ordersConfig: CrudConfig<Order, OrderFormData, { id: string }> = {
  // ...
  mutations: {
    create: { mutationFn: ordersApi.create, invalidates: [['orders']] }, // resolves { success, data?: { id } }
  },
}
```

Use `unknown` when the actions return various shapes. A component or helper that takes any of
your configs types it as `CrudConfigWithAnyForm<T>` (what `ListPage` takes), not `CrudConfig<T, F>`,
which expects the entity in `data`.

What the library does around each mutation:

- **On success** it invalidates every key in `invalidates`, calls your `onSuccess(result, variables)`,
  shows a success toast when the result has a `message`, and waits for the list's first refetch
  attempt before resolving (see [Cache Invalidation](#cache-invalidation)).
- **On error** (the `mutationFn` throws) it calls your `onError(error, variables)` and shows an error
  toast with the error's message.
- A result with `success: false` keeps the form open and shows its `message` as a toast and an
  inline error.
- Resolving the raw entity, without `success`, leaves the dialog open with no feedback, even
  though the record was saved.

Every mutation is optional. Leave out `create` (or `update`, `delete`) and the matching button is
not rendered.

---

## Cache Invalidation

`invalidates` lists query keys, or functions that receive the mutated record's `id` and return a
key (`update` and `delete` pass the id; `create` passes `undefined`).

- **Include the list's `queryKey`.** Because `ListPage` appends the params to it, invalidating
  `['orders']` refreshes every cached page, search and filter of that list. A key that doesn't
  match leaves the list stale after a save.
- **Use hierarchical keys** for everything about one entity: `['orders']` for lists,
  `['orders', id]` for a detail, `['orders', 'stats']` for aggregates. Invalidating `['orders']`
  then reaches all of them.
- **The dialog closes over a fresh list.** The mutation resolves once each invalidated query that
  is on screen finished its first refetch attempt, so the saved row is already in the list when
  the dialog closes. A failing refetch never turns the save into an error and never holds the
  dialog through its retries: the mutation resolves on the first failure and React Query keeps
  retrying in the background.

The list also refreshes on its own after a successful custom row action (`actionsConfig.custom`)
or bulk action; return `{ success: false }` from the handler to skip that. Other queries (a
dashboard, another module, a detail page) need an explicit invalidation:

```tsx
'use client'
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function OrdersPage() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  return (
    <ListPage
      config={config}
      // runs after every list refresh, including the one after an action
      onRefreshAction={async () => {
        await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['dashboard', 'orders'] })
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

Import `useQueryClient`, `useQuery` and the rest from `@tanstack/react-query` directly. The
library does not re-export React Query, on purpose: a second copy causes "No QueryClient set".

---

## Errors

| Where it fails | What handles it |
| --- | --- |
| The list query | `ListPage` renders an error state with a retry button |
| A CRUD mutation | The library toasts the message; add `onError` only for extra behavior |
| Rendering (a cell, dialog content) | `ListPage` wraps itself in an error boundary (`errorBoundary`, default `true`; `errorFallback` customizes it) |
| An automatic background refresh | Logged, never toasted. Refresh on window focus is opt-in: `disableAutoRefresh={false}` |
| A button you wire yourself | `try`/`catch`, a loading state that disables the button, and a toast for success and failure |

Every query and mutation the library runs carries `meta: { skipErrorToast: true }`. If the app's
`QueryClient` has a global `onError` toast, skip those or users see the error twice: see
[Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup).

---

## Testing

Everything in `config.tsx` is a named export, so the data layer can be tested without rendering:
mock the API client and call the adapters directly.

```ts title="config.test.ts"
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'
import { config, validationSchema } from './config'

vi.mock('@/lib/api/orders-client', () => ({
  ordersApi: { create: vi.fn(async (data: unknown) => ({ id: '1', ...(data as object) })) },
}))

describe('orders config', () => {
  it('create resolves the mutation contract, not the raw entity', async () => {
    const result = await config.mutations.create?.mutationFn({ customer: 'ACME', total: 10 })
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ success: true, data: { id: '1' } })
  })

  it('rejects an order without a customer', () => {
    expect(validationSchema.safeParse({ total: 10 }).success).toBe(false)
  })
})
```

To render `ListPage` in a test, wrap it in the same providers the app uses (see
[Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup)), with a `QueryClient` that does not retry.

---

## Checklist

- [ ] `config.tsx` starts with `'use client'`
- [ ] The API client is the only `fetch()` for the entity, sends `credentials: 'include'` and throws with the backend's message
- [ ] `queryFn` resolves `PaginatedResponse<T>`, not an array
- [ ] Every `mutationFn` resolves `{ success, message?, data? }`
- [ ] Every `invalidates` includes the list's `queryKey`
- [ ] React Query is imported from `@tanstack/react-query`, never through the library

---

- [CrudConfig](/docs/getting-started/crud-config) - The full config object

# ListPage Pattern

> Config-driven list pages with React Query, infinite scroll or pagination, search, filters and row actions

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern.mdx

A list page is one `CrudConfig` plus one `<ListPage config={config} />`. The config declares
columns, form, data fetching (`query`) and mutations; `ListPage` renders the table (or the
infinite list), search, filters, row actions and the create/view/edit dialogs from it.

```
app/admin/users/
├── config.tsx   # 'use client' — CrudConfig (columns, form, query, mutations)
└── page.tsx     # <ListPage config={config} />
lib/api/
└── users-client.ts  # REST client: the one hop from the browser to your API
```

<Callout type='warn' title="config.tsx must start with 'use client'">
  `query` and `mutations` run through React Query hooks, which only exist on the client.
</Callout>

---

## 1. The API Client

The browser calls your API directly; React Query owns caching. The list call must resolve
`PaginatedResponse<T>`:

```tsx title="lib/api/users-client.ts"
import type { PaginatedResponse, PaginationParams } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export const usersApi = {
  async list(params: PaginationParams): Promise<PaginatedResponse<User>> {
    const qs = new URLSearchParams({
      page: String(params.page),
      pageSize: String(params.pageSize),
      ...(params.search ? { search: params.search } : {}),
      ...(typeof params.sortBy === 'string' ? { sortBy: params.sortBy, sortOrder: params.sortOrder ?? 'asc' } : {}),
      ...params.filters, // toolbar/column/URL filters, keyed by filter key
    })
    const res = await fetch(`/api/users?${qs}`, { credentials: 'include' })
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Failed to load users')
    return res.json() // { data, total, page, pageSize, totalPages }
  },
  // create / update / delete / get return the raw entity (or nothing)
}
```

Error messages and the server-side helpers are in
[Data Layer (React Query)](/docs/patterns/react-query). By default `sortBy` is the column id
(`customer_name` for `accessorKey: 'customer.name'`); `list.sortParam: 'path'` sends the data path
instead — see [what `sortBy` carries](/docs/patterns/react-query#what-sortby-carries).

---

## 2. config.tsx

```tsx title="app/admin/users/config.tsx"
'use client'

import { z } from 'zod'
import type { CrudColumnDef, CrudConfig, FormSection } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { usersApi } from '@/lib/api/users-client'

export const validationSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1, 'Name is required'),
  email: z.string().email('Invalid email'),
  role: z.enum(['USER', 'ADMIN']),
})
export type UserFormData = z.infer<typeof validationSchema>

const columns: CrudColumnDef<User>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
  { accessorKey: 'email', header: 'Email' },
  { accessorKey: 'role', header: 'Role' },
]

const formSections: FormSection[] = [
  {
    label: 'User',
    fields: [
      { name: 'name', label: 'Name', type: 'text', required: true },
      { name: 'email', label: 'Email', type: 'email', required: true },
      {
        name: 'role',
        label: 'Role',
        type: 'relationship', // there is no 'select' field type
        required: true,
        loadField: async () => [
          { value: 'USER', label: 'User' },
          { value: 'ADMIN', label: 'Admin' },
        ],
      },
    ],
  },
]

export const config: CrudConfig<User, UserFormData> = {
  module: { name: 'users', title: 'Users', description: 'Manage system users', route: '/admin/users' },
  list: { title: 'Users', description: 'Registered users', columns, searchPlaceholder: 'Search users...' },
  form: { sections: formSections, validation: validationSchema },

  // queryFn receives { page, pageSize, search, sortBy, sortOrder, filters }
  // and must resolve PaginatedResponse<User>
  query: { queryKey: ['users'], queryFn: usersApi.list },

  mutations: {
    // mutationFn must resolve { success, data? } — adapt the raw API response here
    create: {
      mutationFn: async data => ({ success: true, data: await usersApi.create(data) }),
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
    update: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id, data }) => ({ success: true, data: await usersApi.update(id, data) }),
      invalidates: [['users'], id => ['users', id]],
    },
    delete: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id }) => {
        await usersApi.delete(id)
        return { success: true }
      },
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
    getForEdit: usersApi.get,
    getForView: usersApi.get,
  },

  actionsConfig: { standard: { view: true, edit: true, delete: true } },

  dialogs: {
    view: { title: 'User', urlParam: 'view', renderContent: user => <UserDetail user={user} /> },
    edit: { title: 'Edit user', urlParam: 'edit' },
    create: { title: 'New user', urlParam: 'create', defaultValues: { role: 'USER' } },
  },
}
```

`invalidates` must include the list's `query.queryKey`, or the list will not refresh after a
mutation. Each mutation is optional: omit `create` for a read-only module and the create
button is not wired. The full mutation contract (toasts, `onSuccess`/`onError`, invalidation
rules) is in [Data Layer (React Query)](/docs/patterns/react-query).

---

## 3. page.tsx

```tsx title="app/admin/users/page.tsx"
import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { config } from './config'

export default function UsersPage() {
  return <ListPage config={config} />
}
```

### ListPage props

| Prop | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config` | `CrudConfig<T, TFormData>` | **Required.** Everything about the module |
| `tableId` | `string` | Key of the table state in the Zustand store. Default: `config.module.route` |
| `urlSync` | `boolean` | Keeps page, page size, sort and search in the query params; a link carrying them opens the list there, and Back/Forward or a link to the same page update the list. With infinite scroll (the default) only sort and search: every load starts at page 1 |
| `urlFilters` | `Record<string, 'string' \| 'number'>` | Extra filters read from the URL (with `urlSync`) and passed to `queryFn` |
| `filterOptions` / `loadFilterOptions` | `ColumnFilterConfig` / `() => Promise<ColumnFilterConfig>` | Column filter options, static or loaded on mount |
| `enableBulkActions` / `bulkActions` | `boolean` / `BulkAction<T>[]` | Checkbox column and toolbar for selected rows |
| `headerActions` | `{ label, icon?, onClick, variant?, loading? }[]` | Extra toolbar buttons |
| `toolbarPrepend` / `toolbarContent` | `ReactNode` | Custom toolbar content before search / after filters |
| `filtersPanel`, `activeFilters`, `onClearFilters`, `footerContent` | | Second toolbar level (see below) |
| `cardComponent` | `ComponentType<{ data; onClick? }>` | Custom card for the mobile view of the paginated table (the infinite list has no mobile cards) |
| `embedded` | `boolean` | Render inside a container that owns the toolbar (e.g. a tab) |
| `header` | `ReactNode` | Bars, alerts or status panels above the toolbar, inside the list (see [Content above the list](#content-above-the-list)) |
| `dialogUrlSync` | `boolean` | Set `false` for a ListPage inside another ListPage's dialog (see [Dialogs](#dialogs)) |
| `onRefreshAction` | `() => Promise<void \| { success }>` | Runs after every list refresh (see [Refreshing](#refreshing)) |
| `disableAutoRefresh` | `boolean` | Default `true`. Set `false` to refetch when the window regains focus |
| `errorBoundary`, `errorFallback`, `className` | | Error boundary (on by default) and styling |

---

## Infinite Scroll vs Pagination

`ListPage` renders a virtualized infinite list by default. It stops fetching using `page`,
`totalPages` and `total` from the `PaginatedResponse` — a `queryFn` resolving a bare array
misbehaves silently. Set `list.infiniteScroll: false` for the classic paginated table.

```tsx
interface PaginationParams {
  page: number
  pageSize: number
  search?: string
  sortBy?: string | SortField[]
  sortOrder?: 'asc' | 'desc'
  filters?: Record<string, any>
}

interface PaginatedResponse<T> {
  data: T[]
  total: number
  page: number
  pageSize: number
  totalPages: number
}
```

`queryFn` receives `ListQueryParams`: the same fields with `sortBy` already a single column
(a string). `createPaginatedResponse(data, total, page, pageSize)` builds the response when you
page a local array.

Keep the paginated table when the backend cannot return `page`/`totalPages` (cursor
pagination, for example), when users need "jump to page N", or for short lists.

The infinite list requests `list.defaultPageSize` rows per page (50 when unset). In a standalone
page it fills its parent and scrolls inside itself, not the window, so the parent (normally the
`AdminShell` main area) must give it a height.

---

## Dialogs

With `dialogs.view`, `dialogs.edit` and `dialogs.create` set, every CRUD step happens in dialogs
on top of the list: view and edit rows open their dialog, the toolbar's create button opens
the create dialog, and the edit form submits through `mutations.update`. Dialog content, rich
headers and sizes are covered in [Dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs).

### Deep links (`urlParam`)

Give a dialog a query-param name and it becomes linkable:

```tsx
dialogs: {
  view: { title: 'User', urlParam: 'view', renderContent },  // ?view=<id>
  edit: { title: 'Edit user', urlParam: 'edit' },             // ?edit=<id>
  create: { title: 'New user', urlParam: 'create' },          // ?create=1 (no id)
},
```

`ListPage` keeps the dialog and the URL in sync both ways:

| Event | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Page load, client navigation, browser Back/Forward | The dialog opens or closes to match the URL |
| The user opens a dialog | `router.push`, so the browser's Back button closes it |
| The user closes it (X, Esc) | `router.replace`, with no extra history entry |

- Other params (`?tab`, `?page`, `?sort`, filters) are kept, so `/admin/registry?tab=assets&view=42`
  works.
- If several dialog params are present, only one dialog opens: `edit` wins over `view`, which
  wins over `create`.
- Several lists mounted on one route (keep-alive tabs) can share the same param name: only the
  visible list opens its dialog from the URL.
- A ListPage rendered **inside another ListPage's dialog** (for example, tabs of a record opened
  with the parent's `?view=<id>`) must get `dialogUrlSync={false}`. Otherwise it reads the
  parent's id as its own and opens a dialog for a record that does not exist.

`urlParam` is optional; a dialog without it is not driven by the URL.

---

## Row Actions

`actionsConfig.standard` turns on view/edit/delete (`true` or an `ActionConfig`); view and
edit open the dialogs, delete asks for confirmation and runs `mutations.delete`. Pass an
`ActionConfig` to change the icon, tooltip or confirmation text:

```tsx
actionsConfig: {
  standard: {
    view: true,
    edit: true,
    delete: {
      tooltip: 'Deactivate user',
      confirmDialog: {
        title: row => `Deactivate ${row.name}?`,
        description: 'This cannot be undone.',
        confirmText: 'Deactivate',
        variant: 'destructive',
      },
    },
  },
  custom: [
    {
      id: 'publish',
      label: 'Publish',
      icon: Upload,
      handler: row => processesApi.publish(row.id),
      confirmDialog: {
        title: row => `Publish process ${row.number}?`,
        confirmText: 'Publish',
      },
      visible: row => row.status === 'DRAFT',
    },
  ],
},
```

`actionsConfig.custom` adds actions beyond CRUD. After a custom `handler` succeeds, the list
refetches by itself; resolve `{ success: false }` to skip that. Set `actionsConfig: false` to
hide the actions column.

`ActionConfig` also takes `href`, `onClick`, `enabled`, `tooltip`, `variant`, `permission`,
`successMessage` and `errorMessage`.

`confirmDialog.inputs` asks for values before confirming (a reason, a note); they reach the
handler as `(row, { inputs })`. The dialog stays open while the action runs and after a
failure — see [ConfirmActionDialog](/docs/components/confirm-action-dialog), which is also
available for your own buttons.

`permission` is checked against `actionsConfig.userPermissions` by exact name. Set
`actionsConfig.can` (or `config.permissions.can`, or once for the app a `PermissionsProvider`,
see [Permissions](/docs/getting-started/crud-config#permissions)) to decide it with your own
checker instead, so a bypass role with no listed permissions still sees the actions.

---

## Bulk Actions

`enableBulkActions` adds a checkbox column and a toolbar for the selected rows, in both the
infinite list and the paginated table:

```tsx
const bulkActions: BulkAction<Order>[] = [
  {
    id: 'approve',
    label: 'Approve selected',
    confirmDialog: {
      title: rows => `Approve ${rows.length} orders?`,
      description: 'Each order is approved individually.',
    },
    handler: async rows => {
      await ordersApi.approveMany(rows.map(r => r.id))
      return { success: true, message: `${rows.length} approved` }
    },
  },
]

<ListPage config={config} enableBulkActions bulkActions={bulkActions} />
```

- In the infinite list, the header checkbox selects every row **already loaded**. Rows not yet
  fetched are never part of the selection, and the status bar says "N selected of M loaded".
- Selection is kept by row `id`; it is cleared after a successful action, and the list refetches.
- The ids `delete` and `export` render as direct buttons; other actions go into a "more" menu.

---

## Search and Filters

### Global Search

The search box value reaches `queryFn` as `params.search`; filter on the API side.
`list.searchPlaceholder` sets the placeholder, and `list.toolbar.showSearch: false` hides it.

### Toolbar Filters

Declare filters in `list.toolbar.filters`. Each selection reaches `queryFn` as
`params.filters[key]`; the values `'all'` and `''` mean "no filter" and are dropped.

```tsx
list: {
  title: 'Users',
  description: 'Registered users',
  columns,
  toolbar: {
    filters: [
      {
        key: 'status',
        label: 'Status',
        options: [
          { value: 'all', label: 'All' },
          { value: 'ACTIVE', label: 'Active', dot: 'bg-green-500' },
          { value: 'INACTIVE', label: 'Inactive', dot: 'bg-gray-400' },
        ],
        displayMode: 'buttons', // or 'select' for a compact dropdown
      },
    ],
  },
},
```

By default the first option is the "all" choice: in `buttons` mode it is not rendered, and
`defaultValue` only applies when it is not the first option. Set `allValue` to name the "no
filter" value explicitly instead — the first option becomes an ordinary option, `defaultValue`
always applies, and `'all'`/`'todos'` are ordinary values:

```tsx
{
  key: 'status',
  label: 'Status',
  allValue: 'ANY',
  defaultValue: 'ACTIVE', // applied on load even though it is the first option
  options: [
    { value: 'ACTIVE', label: 'Active' },
    { value: 'INACTIVE', label: 'Inactive' },
    { value: 'ANY', label: 'All' },
  ],
}
```

### Active / inactive preset

For a boolean "active" column, `activeFilter(key = 'active', overrides?)` returns that filter
ready-made: All / Active / Inactive, labelled by the library messages (every locale), with
`allValue: 'all'`. "Active" sends `?<key>=true`, "Inactive" `?<key>=false` and "All" sends
nothing, which is what a `'boolean'` filter of
[`@telamonjs/data`](/docs/packages/data) parses. The overrides are `label`, `defaultValue`,
`displayMode` and `className`:

```tsx
import { activeFilter } from '@telamonjs/ui'

toolbar: {
  filters: [activeFilter('ativo', { defaultValue: 'true' })], // opens on the active rows
},
```

### Filters in the URL

With `urlSync`, a toolbar filter whose `key` is also in `urlFilters` round-trips with the URL:

```tsx
<ListPage config={config} urlSync urlFilters={{ status: 'string' }} />
```

- Opening `?status=ACTIVE` filters the data **and** selects "Active" in the toolbar.
- Changing the filter writes `?status=`; going back to "All" removes the param.
- Toolbar filters not listed in `urlFilters` stay in memory only. Keys in `urlFilters` that are
  not toolbar filters are read from the URL (on mount, and again on Back/Forward or a link to the
  same page) and passed to `queryFn`.

For a "Filters" panel with selectors, date ranges and text fields that stays in sync with the
URL — reload, Back and shared links keep it — use [`useUrlFilters`](/docs/hooks/use-url-filters).
It returns `filtersPanel`, `activeFilters` and `onClearFilters` for `ListPage`, plus the active
`values`:

```tsx
const { values, filtersPanel, activeFilters, onClearFilters } = useUrlFilters(FILTERS)
// values reach the data through config.query, memoized on them
const config = useMemo(
  () => ({
    ...ordersConfig,
    query: {
      ...ordersConfig.query,
      queryKey: [...ordersConfig.query.queryKey, values],
      queryFn: (params: ListQueryParams) =>
        ordersConfig.query.queryFn({ ...params, filters: { ...params.filters, ...values } }),
    },
  }),
  [values]
)

<ListPage config={config} filtersPanel={filtersPanel} activeFilters={activeFilters} onClearFilters={onClearFilters} />
```

- **Do not put the hook's params in `urlFilters`.** `urlFilters` is read once on mount and its
  sync writes those keys back with the mount values, undoing every change made in the panel.
- `values` is a stable object (same identity until a filter changes), so it can key the
  config's `useMemo` and the query.

### Toolbar levels

A crowded toolbar can move secondary controls into a second level. All of these are opt-in:

| Option | Where | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filtersPanel` | `ListPage` prop | Content of a "Filters" popover (selects of client, period...) |
| `activeFilters` | `ListPage` prop | `ActiveFilterChip[]` (`key`, `label`, `onRemove`) shown as removable chips under the toolbar |
| `onClearFilters` | `ListPage` prop | "Clear filters" next to the chips |
| `more: true` | filter option | The option leaves the toolbar buttons and appears in the "Filters" panel, as a chip when active |
| `toolbar.actionsMenu` | `list.toolbar` | Export and Refresh in one "⋯" menu instead of two buttons |

`footerContent` adds content to the list status bar, after "N of M" (infinite scroll), such as the
totals of the current filter.

### Content above the list

A bar, alert or status panel that sits above an embedded list (a tab, a panel) goes in `header`,
not next to the `ListPage`:

```tsx
<ListPage
  config={config}
  embedded
  header={<Alert>Results are preliminary until the deadline.</Alert>}
/>
```

`header` renders inside the list's root, before the toolbar. In the flex-column layouts (embedded
or infinite scroll) it keeps its own height and the table fills the rest of the panel, so the
footer stays at the bottom without extra scroll. No wrapper is needed: a sibling above the
`ListPage` either leaves the list without a height (footer mid-screen) or adds to its 100%
height (footer below the viewport). In the paginated standalone layout it is the page's first
block.

### Your own button with the list's query

`toolbarContent` also takes a function. It receives the list's current query
(`ListQueryState`) and re-renders when it changes, so an export or PDF button fetches exactly
what the list shows:

```tsx
<ListPage
  config={ordersConfig}
  toolbarContent={({ params }) => (
    <Button
      variant='outline'
      size='sm'
      onClick={() => ordersApi.downloadPdf({ ...params, page: 1, pageSize: 10_000 })}
    >
      PDF
    </Button>
  )}
/>
```

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `search` | the search box value, as typed |
| `filters` | every active filter: toolbar filters (resets dropped), column filters, `urlFilters` |
| `sorting` | the current sort (`SortField[]`) |
| `params` | the `ListQueryParams` the list passes to `query.queryFn` (debounced search, current page, `sortBy` as the first sort column) |

`toolbarContent` renders in the list toolbar: infinite scroll (the default) and `embedded`.

### Exporting every row, or exporting on the server

`list.enableExport` puts an Excel/CSV/PDF menu in the toolbar. Its "All" exports the rows already
loaded in the browser. With infinite scroll (the default) that is only the pages scrolled so far,
so a 2 000-row list with `defaultPageSize: 100` exports 100 rows. Two opt-ins change that:

```tsx
list: {
  enableExport: true,
  // 1. Fetch every matching row through query.queryFn before generating the file
  exportAll: true, // or { pageSize: 200, maxRows: 5_000 }
},
```

```tsx
list: {
  // 2. Hand the export to your backend: the menu lists the formats and calls you
  exportFormats: ['excel', 'csv'],
  onExport: async ({ params }, format) => {
    await ordersApi.export({ ...params, format }) // e.g. downloads a file or queues a job
  },
},
```

| | `exportAll` | `onExport` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who builds the file | the browser, with the list columns | your backend |
| Query | current search, filters and sort, page by page through `query.queryFn` | `ListQueryState`, the same object `toolbarContent` gets |
| Size | up to `maxRows` (10 000); past it the file holds the first rows and a warning says so | whatever your backend handles |
| UX | progress toast with Cancel; "Current page" still exports the loaded rows | formats only; the trigger shows a spinner until your promise settles |
| Cost | one request per page, sequential, so the backend sees the same load as scrolling | one request |

`exportAll` requests use `exportAll.pageSize`, else `defaultPageSize` (50 when unset): a size
your backend already accepts. Choose `onExport` when exports grow past a few thousand rows,
need columns the table does not show, or must be audited on the server. `onExport` shows the
menu even without `enableExport`; throw from it to show the export error toast. Announcing
success (or a queued job) is up to you. Both options apply to the paginated list
(`infiniteScroll: false`) as well.

### Columns only in the export

`meta.exportOnly` keeps a column out of the table and in the CSV/Excel/PDF export, so a table that
merges fields into one cell does not lose data in the spreadsheet:

```tsx
columns: [
  { accessorKey: 'client', header: 'Client', cell: ({ row }) => <ClientCell client={row.original} /> },
  { accessorKey: 'taxId', header: 'Tax ID', meta: { exportOnly: true } },
]
```

---

## Lists Scoped to a Parent

A child list inside a parent record (a customer's contacts tab, for example) reuses the child
module's config through `withScope`:

```tsx
import { ListPage, withScope } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const customerContacts = withScope(contactsConfig, {
  filters: { customerId },           // merged into params.filters and the queryKey
  locked: { customerId },            // hidden from form, columns and filters; injected on create
  invalidates: [['customers', customerId]],
})

<ListPage config={customerContacts} embedded />
```

`defaults` adds editable create defaults. `withScope` returns a new config and never mutates the
original. It replaces an inline [CRUD field](/docs/patterns/crud-field) when the child list is
large or needs search, filters and paging.

---

## Refreshing

React Query is the cache. Mutations refresh the list through `invalidates`; the toolbar's
refresh button and successful row or bulk actions refetch the query. Two optional hooks:

- **`AppProviders` `config.revalidateAction`** runs first, with the current pathname, to clear the
  app's Server Component cache. Use `revalidatePathAction` from `@telamonjs/ui/server`.
- **`onRefreshAction`** (`ListPage` prop) runs after the refetch, for example to invalidate other
  modules that show the same data:

```tsx
'use client'
import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function CustomersPage() {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  return (
    <ListPage
      config={customersConfig}
      onRefreshAction={async () => {
        await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['orders'] })
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Checklist

- [ ] `config.tsx` starts with `'use client'`
- [ ] `query.queryFn` resolves `PaginatedResponse<T>` (`data`, `total`, `page`, `pageSize`, `totalPages`)
- [ ] Every `mutationFn` resolves `{ success, data? }`
- [ ] Every mutation's `invalidates` includes the list's `queryKey`
- [ ] Columns are typed `CrudColumnDef<T>[]`, and the form-data type is inferred from the Zod schema
- [ ] Dropdowns use `type: 'relationship'` with `loadField`
- [ ] `page.tsx` renders `<ListPage config={config} />`

---

## Troubleshooting

### The list never stops loading, or only shows the first page

`queryFn` returns a bare array or a response without `page`/`totalPages`. Return
`PaginatedResponse<T>`, or set `list.infiniteScroll: false`.

### The record was saved, but the dialog stays open

The `mutationFn` resolves the raw entity instead of `{ success, data? }`. Adapt inside the
`mutationFn`: `async data => ({ success: true, data: await api.create(data) })`.

### The list does not update after create/edit/delete

The mutation's `invalidates` does not match `query.queryKey`.

### "No QueryClient set"

`config.tsx` is missing `'use client'`, the app has no `QueryClientProvider`, or two copies of
`@tanstack/react-query` are installed. See [Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup).

### Search or filters do nothing

The API ignores `params.search` / `params.filters`. Log the params your `queryFn` receives.

### A list inside a dialog opens a dialog for the wrong record

It reads the parent's `?view=<id>`. Pass `dialogUrlSync={false}` to the inner `ListPage`.

---

- [Admin Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) - What goes in `config.tsx`
- [Form Pattern](/docs/patterns/form-pattern) - Forms used by the dialogs
- [Dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs) - View, edit and create dialogs
- [Field Types](/docs/reference/field-types) - All field types

# Dialogs

> Create, edit and view dialogs declared in CrudConfig.dialogs — rich headers, tabs, deep links, portal views, and the standalone components

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/dialogs.mdx

TelamonJS has three record dialogs. You declare them under `CrudConfig.dialogs` and
`ListPage` renders, opens and closes them — no `useState`, no handlers:

| Dialog | Opens from | Content | Loads the record with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Create** | The "New" button | `form.sections` → `CreateForm` | nothing (only `defaultValues`) |
| **Edit** | The edit row action | `form.sections` → `EditForm` | `mutations.getForEdit(id)` |
| **View** | The view row action / row click | `renderContent` or a `portal` | `mutations.getForView ?? getForEdit` |

The form inside the create and edit dialogs is the module's form: `form.sections` and
`form.validation`. `dialogs.*` only describes the dialog around it.

---

## Wiring

```tsx title="config.tsx"
'use client'

import { type CrudConfig } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export const customersConfig: CrudConfig<Customer, CustomerFormData> = {
  // ...module/list/query...
  form: { sections: customerSections, validation: customerSchema },

  mutations: {
    // mutationFn must resolve { success, message?, data? }
    create: {
      mutationFn: async data => ({ success: true, data: await customersApi.create(data) }),
      invalidates: [['customers']],
    },
    update: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id, data }) => ({ success: true, data: await customersApi.update(id, data) }),
      invalidates: [['customers']],
    },
    getForEdit: customersApi.getById, // the full record the form needs
  },

  actionsConfig: { standard: { view: true, edit: true, delete: true } },

  dialogs: {
    create: { title: 'New customer', urlParam: 'create', defaultValues: { active: true } },
    edit: { title: c => `Edit ${c.name}`, urlParam: 'edit' },
    view: {
      title: c => c.name,
      urlParam: 'view',
      renderContent: c => <CustomerDetail customer={c} />,
    },
  },
}
```

```tsx title="page.tsx"
import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { customersConfig } from './config'

export default function CustomersPage() {
  return <ListPage config={customersConfig} />
}
```

`ListPage` has no per-dialog props — everything comes from `config`.
Submitting calls `mutations.create` / `mutations.update` with the typed form values; the
list refreshes through `invalidates` (no `router.refresh()`). The dialogs are loaded on
first open, so a list that never opens one never pays for the form code.

<Callout type='warn' title='Not dialog options'>
  `sections`, `validation` and `submitText` are **not** keys of `dialogs.*` — the form
  always comes from `form`, and the submit labels come from the library's i18n
  messages. To show a different set of fields per dialog, use `editOnly` on sections
  (below) or `lockedFields`.
</Callout>

### `dialogs.*` options

| Option | Applies to | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | all | `I18nText` or `(item) => string`. Used when there is no rich header |
| `description` | all | Subtitle under the default title |
| `headerConfig` | all | Declarative rich header — see [Rich headers](#rich-headers) |
| `renderHeader` | all | Custom header JSX; wins over `headerConfig` |
| `size` | all | `'sm' \| 'md' \| 'lg' \| 'xl' \| 'full' \| 'auto'` |
| `dialogHeight` | all | `'auto'` (default) or `'full'` |
| `dialogClassName` | all | Extra classes, merged **over** the `size` preset |
| `urlParam` | all | Deep link query param — see [Deep links](#deep-links) |
| `useTabs` | create, edit | Force tabs on or off (default: automatic) |
| `defaultValues` | create | Initial form values; keys outside `T` (form-only fields such as `categoryId`) are accepted |
| `lockedFields` | edit | Fields shown read-only on edit (e.g. the record's parent); create keeps them editable |
| `renderContent` | view | The dialog body |
| `portal` | view | Grid launcher + rail instead of `renderContent` — see [Portal view](#portal-view-6-sections) |

---

## Shared behavior

### Size and height

`size` picks a width preset: `sm` (`max-w-md`), `md` (`max-w-2xl`), `lg` (`max-w-4xl`),
`xl` (`max-w-6xl`), `full` (`max-w-[95vw]`). The default for create/edit is `'auto'`,
computed from the form: ≤ 4 fields in one section → `md`, ≤ 10 fields in ≤ 3 sections → `lg`,
otherwise `xl`. The view dialog defaults to `full`.

```tsx
dialogs: {
  edit: {
    title: 'Edit order',
    size: 'xl',
    dialogHeight: 'full',         // h-[min(800px,85vh)], the body scrolls inside
    dialogClassName: 'max-w-7xl', // merged over the preset; your class wins conflicts
  },
}
```

- `dialogHeight: 'auto'` sizes to the content, capped at 90vh. Use `'full'` instead of
  hand-written `h-[90vh]`-style classes when the height must stay fixed.
- `dialogClassName` also reaches the mobile Sheet, minus width/height utilities.

### Desktop and mobile

Create and edit render a centered `Dialog` on desktop and a bottom `Sheet` (90vh, slide-up)
below the Tailwind `md` breakpoint (768px, via `useIsMobile()`). The config-driven view
dialog always stays a centered dialog.

### Tabs and the form footer

With more than one section, create/edit switch to tabs automatically when the form has
**more than 20 fields**; shorter forms render as one page (`useTabs` overrides this). A
one-page form in a wide dialog (`xl`/`full`) gives sections without an explicit `grid` 3
columns instead of 2.

The tabbed form generates its own footer:

```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|  < Previous | Next >      [.====....]      | Cancel | Save       |
|  tab navigation           progress dots      action buttons      |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

- **Previous / Next** move between sections and disable at the ends.
- **Progress dots**: one per section, the active one wider; clickable.
- On mobile only the action buttons remain — the tabs themselves are clickable.

### Unsaved changes

Closing a create or edit dialog with a dirty form — Cancel, ESC, click outside, the X — asks
"discard changes?" first. A successful save never triggers it. The same guard is exported as
`useUnsavedChangesGuard` (wired to `AdminForm`'s `onDirtyChange`) for custom screens.

### Deep links

`urlParam` keeps the dialog and the URL in sync in both directions:

- view/edit carry the id (`?view=42`, `?edit=42`); create uses `?create=1`.
- Opening pushes a history entry, so the browser **Back** button closes the dialog; closing
  with X/ESC replaces the entry instead.
- Other params (`?tab`, `?page`, `?sort`, filters) are preserved.
- If several are present, `edit` wins over `view`, which wins over `create`.

---

## Rich headers

A rich header replaces the default title with an icon, a gradient, a status badge and —
on the view dialog — stats cards. When one is set, the form inside create/edit switches to
**flush** mode automatically: no rounded border or shadow around the form, tabs glued to the
header, footer integrated with the dialog.

### `headerConfig` (declarative)

Prefer `headerConfig`: one object, same shape for all three dialogs.

```tsx
headerConfig: {
  icon: 'Building2',            // icon name, resolved like menu icons
  iconColor: 'blue',
  title: c => c.name,
  subtitle: c => `#${c.code}`,  // I18nText or ReactNode, or a function returning either
  gradient: 'from-blue-50 to-indigo-50',
  badge: {
    field: 'active',
    variants: { true: 'default', false: 'secondary' },
    labels: { true: 'Active', false: 'Inactive' },
  },
  stats: {
    columns: 3,
    items: [
      { label: 'Orders', value: c => c._count?.orders ?? 0, icon: 'ShoppingCart', color: 'blue' },
      { label: 'Contacts', value: c => c.contacts.length, icon: 'Users', color: 'green' },
    ],
  },
}
```

`iconColor` and each stat's `color` take a preset (`blue`, `indigo`, `purple`, `violet`,
`green`, `emerald`, `teal`, `cyan`, `orange`, `amber`, `red`, `rose`, `pink`, `gray`, `slate`).
`iconColor` and `gradient` may also be functions of the record (`c => (c.active ? 'green' : 'gray')`);
without a record (the create dialog) they fall back to `gray` and the default gradient.
A stat can be hidden with `hidden` or turned into a link with `href`.

<Callout type='info' title='Stats are view-only'>
  Reuse the same `headerConfig` in `create`, `edit` and `view`: the form dialogs drop `stats`
  on their own — in a form they would repeat the fields being edited.
</Callout>

### `renderHeader` (custom JSX)

When the declarative shape is not enough, render the header yourself. Create gets no record;
edit and view get it:

| Dialog | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| Create | `() => ReactNode` |
| Edit, View | `(item: T) => ReactNode` |

```tsx
import { Badge, getIcon } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const BuildingIcon = getIcon('Building2')

renderHeader: customer => (
  <div className='border-b bg-gradient-to-r from-blue-50 to-indigo-50 px-6 py-4'>
    <div className='flex items-center gap-3'>
      <div className='flex h-12 w-12 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-blue-600'>
        <BuildingIcon className='h-6 w-6 text-white' />
      </div>
      <div className='min-w-0'>
        <div className='flex items-center gap-2'>
          <h2 className='truncate text-lg font-bold'>{customer.name}</h2>
          <Badge variant={customer.active ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>
            {customer.active ? 'Active' : 'Inactive'}
          </Badge>
        </div>
        <p className='text-sm text-muted-foreground'>#{customer.code}</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
),
```

`title` stays required as the fallback.

### Gradient convention

| Color | Gradient | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Blue** | `from-blue-50 to-indigo-50` | Main entities (customer, product) |
| **Green** | `from-green-50 to-emerald-50` | Financial entities (invoice, payment) |
| **Purple** | `from-purple-50 to-violet-50` | Settings (alert, parameter) |
| **Orange** | `from-orange-50 to-amber-50` | Operations (order, shipment) |

---

## Create dialog

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| [Icon] New customer                                     [X]  |  <- rich header
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| | General | | Address | | Contact |                          |  <- tabs (from the form)
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| Section description                                          |
| [ Field 1 * ]  [ Field 2 ]                                   |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| < Previous | Next >  [.====....]        | Cancel | Create    |  <- footer (auto)
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
```

- Nothing is fetched. Initial values come from `dialogs.create.defaultValues` and from each
  field's `default`.
- Sections with `editOnly: true` and fields of `type: 'crud'` are left out — nested rows
  need a parent id that does not exist yet.
- On success the dialog closes first; the list refresh runs in the background.

Give each section an `icon` and an optional `description` — they show up in the tabs:

```tsx title="form-sections.tsx"
import { getIcon, type FormSection } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const FileTextIcon = getIcon('FileText')
const MapPinIcon = getIcon('MapPin')

export const customerSections: FormSection[] = [
  {
    label: 'General',
    icon: <FileTextIcon className='h-4 w-4' />,
    description: 'Main customer data',
    grid: '2',
    fields: [
      { name: 'code', label: 'Code', type: 'text', required: true },
      { name: 'name', label: 'Name', type: 'text', required: true },
      { name: 'active', label: 'Active', type: 'boolean', default: true },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Address',
    icon: <MapPinIcon className='h-4 w-4' />,
    grid: '3',
    fields: [
      { name: 'street', label: 'Street', type: 'text', span: '2' },
      { name: 'city', label: 'City', type: 'text' },
    ],
  },
]
```

---

## Edit dialog

```
1. User clicks Edit (or opens ?edit=<id>)
2. The dialog opens with the row id (and the clicked row, for the header)
3. mutations.getForEdit(id) runs — loading state
4. EditForm renders with the fetched record
5. Submit → mutations.update.mutationFn({ id, data })
6. { success: true }  → invalidates refetch the list, the dialog closes
   { success: false, message } → the message is shown, the dialog stays open
```

**`getForEdit`** must return the **complete** record — every field the form needs, not
just the list columns — and **throw** when it does not exist (the dialog shows the error).
It may return nested data: a field named `customer.name` reads `{ customer: { name } }`
(see [Nested Data](/docs/patterns/nested-data)).

The dialog always does a fresh fetch on open: the list row is limited to its columns and may
be stale. That fetch costs one round-trip behind a loading state.

**The header before the fetch.** `ListPage` hands the clicked row to the dialog, merged
*under* the fetched record: the fetch wins on every key it returns, the row fills the rest.
So joined or denormalized display fields (a related entity's name that only the list
returns) still show in a rich header even though `getForEdit` does not return them.

**Edit-only sections.** Nested collections edited in place live in an `editOnly` section:

```tsx
{
  label: 'Contacts',
  icon: <UsersIcon className='h-4 w-4' />,
  editOnly: true, // hidden in the create dialog
  fields: [{ name: 'contacts', label: 'Contacts', type: 'crud' /* ... */ }],
}
```

See [CRUD Field](/docs/patterns/crud-field) for the field itself.

Errors: Zod errors from `form.validation` render per field before submit; a rejected
`mutationFn` or `{ success: false, message }` is shown inside the dialog.

---

## View dialog

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| [Icon] Record name [Badge]        | 17 Orders | 3 Contacts   |  <- rich header + stats
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| | Information | | Orders | | History |                       |  <- ContentTabs (flush)
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| [ Blue card        ]  [ Green card       ]                   |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| [Delete]                                  [Close] [Edit]     |  <- footer (auto)
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
```

- The body is `renderContent(item)`; the record comes from `mutations.getForView`, falling
  back to `getForEdit`.
- The footer is automatic and follows the row actions. **Edit** appears when `dialogs.edit`
  exists and `actionsConfig.standard.edit` is not `false`, and hands over to the edit dialog.
  **Delete** appears when `actionsConfig.standard.delete` is set and reuses its label, icon and
  confirmation. Both honor the action's `permission` (checked with `actionsConfig.can` or
  `config.permissions`, else against `userPermissions`) and its
  `visible`/`enabled` for the record — evaluated against the list row, or against the fetched
  record when the dialog opens from a deep link to a row outside the loaded page. A user who
  cannot edit or delete a row from the table does not get the button in the footer either.

### Tabbed detail content

For a detail with a few areas (up to ~5), return `ContentTabs` with `flush` so the tabs glue
to the header, and give each tab a **fixed height** so the dialog does not jump when
switching tabs:

```tsx title="_components/CustomerDetail.tsx"
'use client'

import { ContentTabs, SemanticCard, SemanticField, getIcon, type TabItem } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const UserIcon = getIcon('User')
const PhoneIcon = getIcon('Phone')

// 600px on large screens, 60% of the viewport on small ones; scroll inside
const tabBody = 'h-[min(600px,60vh)] overflow-y-auto p-6'

export function CustomerDetail({ customer }: { customer: Customer }) {
  const tabs: TabItem[] = [
    {
      value: 'info',
      label: 'Information',
      icon: 'Info',
      content: (
        <div className={tabBody}>
          <div className='grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-2'>
            <SemanticCard title='Identification' icon={UserIcon} color='blue'>
              <SemanticField label='Name' value={customer.name} />
              <SemanticField label='Tax ID' value={customer.taxId} mono />
            </SemanticCard>
            <SemanticCard title='Contact' icon={PhoneIcon} color='green'>
              <SemanticField label='Phone' value={customer.phone} icon={PhoneIcon} />
              <SemanticField label='E-mail' value={customer.email} />
            </SemanticCard>
          </div>
        </div>
      ),
    },
    {
      value: 'orders',
      label: 'Orders',
      icon: 'ShoppingCart',
      badge: customer._count?.orders,
      content: <div className={tabBody}><CustomerOrders customerId={customer.id} /></div>,
    },
  ]

  return <ContentTabs tabs={tabs} defaultValue='info' flush />
}
```

- Put the padding (`p-6`) on each tab's content, not on the tabs.
- Tune the height to the content: `min(400px,50vh)` for light tabs, `min(700px,70vh)` for heavy ones.
- `ContentTabs` also takes `variant` (`default`, `underline`, `pill`, `glass`, `gradient`),
  `compact` and a controlled `value`/`onValueChange`.

`SemanticCard` colors follow a convention: **blue** for identification, **green** for
contact, **purple** for location (address, coordinates), **orange** for metrics and status.

### Portal view (6+ sections)

With six or more sections a tab row turns into horizontal scrolling. Declare
`dialogs.view.portal` instead: a grid of section cards first, then the chosen section with a
side rail ("all sections" returns to the grid). Sections can be **edited inline**.

```tsx title="config.tsx (excerpt)"
const [generalSection] = customerSections // a FormSection works as a section's `edit`

dialogs: {
  view: {
    title: c => c.name,
    headerConfig: customerHeader,
    portal: {
      sections: c => [
        {
          value: 'general',
          label: 'Overview',
          icon: 'Info',
          color: 'blue',
          content: <CustomerOverview customer={c} />,
          edit: generalSection, // pencil → this section's form → "save section"
        },
        {
          value: 'orders',
          label: 'Orders',
          icon: 'ShoppingCart',
          color: 'purple',
          badge: c._count?.orders,
          content: <CustomerOrders customerId={c.id} />, // 1:N lists save on their own
          padded: false,
        },
      ],
      // receives ONLY this section's fields; ctx has the record id and item
      onSaveSection: async (values, _section, { id }) =>
        ({ success: true, data: await customersApi.update(id, values) }),
    },
  },
}
```

- Per-section validation is derived from `form.validation` — do not repeat it.
- `portal` and `renderContent` are mutually exclusive; with both, `portal` wins and a dev
  warning is logged.
- The portal has **no footer**: editing is per section, deleting lives in the row actions.
- With `config.permissions.edit` set, only users granted it get the section pencils
  (`onSaveSection` is dropped otherwise) — in `ListPage` and in `CrudViewDialog`.
- Leaving a dirty section (switching, back to the grid, closing) asks to discard first.
- Sections also accept `description` (shown on the grid card), `group` and `padded`
  (default `true`; pass `false` for lists and full-bleed content). `defaultSection` skips the
  grid; `columns` caps the grid columns.

<Callout type='warn' title='Record shape vs form shape'>
  A section's form is filled from the view record. A `relationship` field expects the
  **id**, while a view record often carries the populated object. Make `getForView` return
  the ids next to the objects, or the section will start empty.
</Callout>

### Opening a record from another screen

`CrudViewDialog` is the view dialog of a config, standalone — the same one `ListPage` opens
(portal or classic). Use it to open a record of another module in place instead of
navigating away:

```tsx
import { CrudViewDialog } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<CrudViewDialog config={productsConfig} id={productId} open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} />
```

It renders nothing when the config has no `dialogs.view`. The optional `footer` prop takes
the classic footer actions (`onEdit`, `onDelete`, `deleteLabel`, `deleteIcon`,
`deleteConfirmation`).

---

## Standalone dialogs

Outside a `ListPage`, render the components directly: `CreateDialog`, `EditDialog`,
`ViewDialog`, `ViewPortalDialog`. Their data props are plain async functions:

| Prop | Signature | On |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fetchAction` | `(id: string) => Promise<T>` | Edit, View, Portal |
| `onSubmitValues` | `(values) => Promise<FormActionResult<T> \| void>` | Create, Edit — **preferred**, typed values |
| `createAction` / `updateAction` | `(formData: FormData) => Promise<FormActionResult<T>>` | Create / Edit — FormData handler |
| `onSaveSection` | `(values, section, ctx) => Promise<FormActionResult>` | Portal |

`FormActionResult` is `{ success, message?, data? }`. On edit, `values` includes the record
`id`. The other props mirror the config options above (`sections`, `validation`, `title`,
`headerConfig`, `renderHeader`, `size`, `dialogHeight`, `dialogClassName`, `useTabs`,
`lockedFields`, `defaultValues`). `EditDialog` also takes `headerRow` (the row merged under the
fetch, as `ListPage` does) and `headerData` (replaces the fetched record for the header).

```tsx
'use client'

import { EditDialog } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'

export function EditProduct({ id, onClose }: { id: string | null; onClose: () => void }) {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  const update = useMutation({
    mutationFn: ({ id, ...data }: Record<string, unknown>) => productsApi.update(String(id), data),
    onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['products'] }),
  })

  return (
    <EditDialog
      id={id}
      open={id !== null}
      onOpenChange={open => !open && onClose()}
      fetchAction={productsApi.getById}
      onSubmitValues={async values => ({ success: true, data: await update.mutateAsync(values) })}
      sections={productSections}
      validation={productSchema}
      title='Edit product'
    />
  )
}
```

`ViewPortalDialog` has no `onEdit`/`onDelete`/`deleteConfirmation` — passing them does not
compile. Mounted standalone, it also loses what `dialogs.view.portal` gives for free (URL sync,
row click, the view action override), so prefer the config.

---

## Building a custom dialog

The library dialogs share one footer look. If you build your own around `AdminForm`, keep it:

- Footer: `border-t bg-muted/50 px-6 py-4`, full-bleed with `-mx-6 -mb-6` inside a `px-6` body.
- Put the form **directly** in the dialog body. A wrapper with its own padding (`px-4`)
  breaks the negative margins and leaves white gaps at the footer's edges.
- No bottom padding on the body (`pb-0`), or a gap appears under the footer.

---

## Checklist

- Form fields and validation live in `form`; `dialogs.*` only holds presentation options
- `getForEdit` returns the full record and throws when it is missing
- `mutationFn` resolves `{ success, data? }`; `invalidates` lists the list's query key
- `urlParam` set on dialogs worth linking to
- Rich header via `headerConfig` (stats only matter on view); `renderHeader` only when needed
- Sections have an `icon`; nested collections sit in `editOnly` sections
- View content: `ContentTabs` with `flush` and a fixed tab height up to ~5 areas, `portal` beyond
- ESC closes, focus is trapped, a dirty form asks before discarding; mobile shows a Sheet for create/edit

---

- [ListPage Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern)
- [Nested Data](/docs/patterns/nested-data)
- [CRUD Field](/docs/patterns/crud-field) — nested rows inside the edit dialog
- [Detail Page](/docs/patterns/detail-page) — full detail pages
