# Form Pattern

> The form components and when to use each - from simple CRUD to multi-step flows

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/form-pattern.mdx

Choose the right form component for your use case, and lay out its sections and fields.

<Callout type='info' title='Inside a CrudConfig module, you rarely need these'>
  `ListPage` already renders the create/edit dialogs from `config.form` and submits them
  through `config.mutations`. Reach for the components below for standalone pages and
  custom flows. The sections and field rules on this page apply to `config.form` too.
</Callout>

<Callout type='warn' title='Critical: Nested Data'>
  If your forms use nested data (e.g., `person.name`, `address.street`), read
  [Nested Data Pattern](/docs/patterns/nested-data) first!
</Callout>

---

## Available Form Components

`@telamonjs/ui` offers these form components:

1. **Form** (alias of **AdminForm**) - Base form component (generic)
2. **CreateForm** ⭐ - Semantic wrapper for creation (recommended for `/new`)
3. **EditForm** ⭐ - Semantic wrapper for editing (recommended for `/[id]/edit`)
4. **ZustandForm** - Form whose state lives in a store, readable by components outside the form
5. **ZustandFormServer** - Server Component wrapper that loads `ZustandForm` client-side

For a whole create or edit page (title, layout and form), `CreatePage` and `EditPage` wrap
`CreateForm`/`EditForm`: see [Standalone form pages](/docs/patterns/edit-page).

---

## Decision Tree: Which Form to Use?

```
Need a form?
│
├─ Is it a create page (/new)?
│  └─ Yes → CreateForm ⭐ (recommended)
│     • Filters sections/fields with editOnly: true, and CRUD fields
│     • Submit text: localized "Create" (default)
│     • Props: defaultValues (instead of data)
│
├─ Is it an edit page (/[id]/edit)?
│  └─ Yes → EditForm ⭐ (recommended)
│     • Requires id + data (TypeScript)
│     • Nested records work with dot-notation field names
│     • Submit text: localized "Save" (default)
│
├─ Is it a multi-step flow, or does a component outside the form need its values live?
│  └─ Yes → ZustandForm (ZustandFormServer from a Server Component)
│
└─ Anything else → Form / AdminForm
```

---

## Submitting: `onSubmitValues`

`Form`, `CreateForm` and `EditForm` share one submit contract. The default path is
`onSubmitValues`: it receives the validated values as a plain object (booleans and numbers
keep their types — no `FormData` parsing) and resolves a `FormActionResult`
(`{ success, data?, message?, errors? }`). Call your REST client or a React Query mutation there.

- `{ success: true }` → `onSuccess(result)` runs; without it, `cancelAction`; without either, the browser goes back.
- `{ success: false, message }` → the message is shown as a toast and as an inline error.
- A thrown error is caught and shown the same way.

`action` is the alternative for a Next.js Server Action: it receives `FormData`
(booleans become `'true'`/`'false'`, nested objects use dot-notation keys). Pass one or the
other, never both.

---

## Sections and Fields

### Grid and `span`

A section is a CSS grid with `grid` columns (default `'2'`). Each field takes one column unless
it sets `span`. **Width classes do nothing** — `className: 'w-full'` is ignored by the grid.

```tsx
const sections: FormSection[] = [
  {
    label: 'Product',
    // grid defaults to '2'
    fields: [
      { name: 'name', label: 'Name', type: 'text', required: true },        // 1 of 2 columns
      { name: 'price', label: 'Price', type: 'float', required: true },     // 1 of 2 columns
      { name: 'description', label: 'Description', type: 'textarea', span: '2' }, // full width
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Address',
    grid: '3',
    fields: [
      { name: 'street', label: 'Street', type: 'text', span: '2' },  // 2 of 3 columns
      { name: 'number', label: 'Number', type: 'text' },
      { name: 'notes', label: 'Notes', type: 'textarea', span: '3' }, // full width
    ],
  },
]
```

Rule of thumb: a full-width field sets `span` to the section's `grid` value. `fields` also
accepts rows (`FormField[][]`) when you need explicit line breaks.

Below Tailwind's `sm` breakpoint (640px) every section grid (and every row of up to six fields;
longer rows already wrap) collapses to a single column and
`span` is ignored, so fields stack on phones; from `sm` up the grid and spans apply as
declared. `grid` and `span` take `'1'`–`'12'` (and `span: 'full'`); every value is shipped as a
static class, so no Tailwind safelist is needed.

### Labels and help text

Fields use `label` and `description` (not `title` or `helperText`). `description` renders as help
text under the field and is wired to the field's `aria-describedby`; `boolean` and `checkbox`
fields show it inline next to the control instead.

### Choosing records

Use `type: 'relationship'` with an async `loadField` for a select — there is no `'select'` type
and no static `options` prop. `dependsOn` reloads a `loadField` when another field changes (a
cascade such as state → city). When each option needs detail, server-side search or depends on
another field, use `RichSelectorField` in a `type: 'component'` field: see
[RichSelector](/docs/components/rich-selector).

### Conditional visibility (`visibleWhen`)

To show or hide a field from the form's current values, use `visibleWhen`. On a section it hides
the whole group (only in the default layout; with `useTabs`, use it per field).

```tsx
const sections: FormSection[] = [
  {
    label: 'Discounts',
    fields: [
      { name: 'hasDiscount', label: 'Apply a discount?', type: 'boolean' },
      {
        name: 'discountPercent',
        label: 'Discount (%)',
        type: 'number',
        visibleWhen: values => values.hasDiscount === true,
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: 'Shipping',
    visibleWhen: values => values.requiresShipping === true,
    fields: [
      { name: 'carrier', label: 'Carrier', type: 'text' },
      { name: 'deadline', label: 'Deadline (days)', type: 'number' },
    ],
  },
]
```

- **Rendering:** only fields with `visibleWhen` subscribe to form changes; typing in one field
  never re-renders the others.
- **Validation:** a hidden field never blocks the submit, even when the Zod schema requires it.
  There is no need to mark it `.optional()`.
- **Submit:** a hidden field's value (typed before it was hidden, or a default) is left out of what
  `onSubmitValues`/`action` receive.

### Data that arrives after mount

When `data` reaches an already-mounted form (the fetch resolved after the first render), the
form applies it while it is still pristine. Once the user edits a field, late `data` no longer
overwrites it. There is no need to remount the form with a `key` to wait for data.

### Date fields

`date`, `masked-date`, `datetime` and `masked-datetime` take typing with a mask in the locale's
date order, or picking from a calendar opened by the icon inside the input. The form value is an
ISO string.

`date` fields take `minDate` and `maxDate`: a `Date`, an ISO string, `'today'`, another field
(`{ field, offsetDays? }`) or a function of the form values. The calendar disables the days
outside, and the form rejects a typed value outside with or without a schema rule. An empty field
opens the calendar on an allowed month.

```tsx
{ name: 'dueDate', label: 'Due date', type: 'date', minDate: { field: 'issueDate' }, maxDate: 'today' }
{ name: 'endDate', label: 'End', type: 'date', minDate: { field: 'startDate', offsetDays: 1 } } // strictly after
```

`{ field }` is that field's day, inclusive; `offsetDays` shifts it (negative too). While the other
field is empty there is no limit, and the calendar follows the other field as it changes.

### Reading other fields in a custom field

In a `type: 'component'` field, import `useWatch` and `useFormContext` from
`@telamonjs/ui`, not from `react-hook-form`. They come from the same copy the forms use;
with two copies installed, the app's copy cannot see the library's `FormProvider`.

```tsx
import { useWatch } from '@telamonjs/ui'

function Total() {
  const quantity = useWatch({ name: 'quantity' })
  return <span>{quantity}</span>
}
```

---

## 1. AdminForm (Generic)

### When to Use

✅ **USE when:**

- A form that is neither a plain create nor a plain edit page
- Zod schema validation
- You want full control over the props

❌ **DON'T USE when:**

- It is a multi-step flow, or a component outside the form needs its values live (use `ZustandForm`)

### Example

```tsx title="app/admin/jobs/new/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { Card, AdminForm, type FormActionResult } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { formSections, validationSchema, type JobFormData } from '../config'
import { jobsApi } from '@/lib/api/jobs-client'

export default function AddJobPage() {
  const router = useRouter()
  const queryClient = useQueryClient()
  const create = useMutation({
    mutationFn: jobsApi.create,
    onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['jobs'] }),
  })

  async function handleSubmit(values: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<FormActionResult<JobFormData>> {
    await create.mutateAsync(values as JobFormData)
    return { success: true }
  }

  return (
    <Card className='p-6'>
      <AdminForm<JobFormData>
        sections={formSections}
        validation={validationSchema}
        onSubmitValues={handleSubmit}
        data={{ active: true }} // Defaults
        submitText='Create Job'
        onSuccess={() => router.push('/admin/jobs')}
        cancelAction={() => router.push('/admin/jobs')}
      />
    </Card>
  )
}
```

### Props

```tsx
interface AdminFormProps<T> {
  // Fields (use sections OR fields, not both)
  sections?: FormSection[] // ⭐ Recommended
  fields?: FormField[] // Alternative

  // Submit (pass one)
  onSubmitValues?: (values: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<FormActionResult<T> | void>
  action?: (formData: FormData) => Promise<FormActionResult<T> | void>

  // Initial data
  data?: Partial<T>

  // Validation
  validation?: z.ZodType

  // UI
  submitText?: I18nText // Default: localized "Save"
  cancelAction?: () => void
  grid?: string // '1', '2', '3', '4'
  hideButtons?: boolean
  useTabs?: boolean // Use tabs for sections
  flush?: boolean // No border/shadow — inside a dialog

  // Mode
  id?: string // Entity ID (edit mode), added to the submitted values

  // Callbacks
  onSuccess?: (result: FormActionResult<T>) => void | Promise<void>
  onFieldChange?: (params: { field; value; values; setValue }) => void | Promise<void>
  onDirtyChange?: (isDirty: boolean) => void
}
```

---

## 2. CreateForm (Creation) ⭐ RECOMMENDED

### When to Use

✅ **USE when:**

- Creation page (`/new`, `/add`)
- Want semantic clarity in code
- Need to filter sections with `editOnly: true` automatically
- Default submit text "Create" is adequate

### Example

```tsx title="app/admin/users/new/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { CreateForm } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { formSections, validationSchema, type UserFormData } from '../config'
import { usersApi } from '@/lib/api/users-client'

export default function NewUserPage() {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <CreateForm
      sections={formSections}
      validation={validationSchema}
      onSubmitValues={async values => ({
        success: true,
        data: await usersApi.create(values as UserFormData),
      })}
      onSuccess={() => router.push('/admin/users')}
      defaultValues={{ active: true, role: 'USER' }}
      useTabs={true}
    />
  )
}
```

### CreateForm vs AdminForm

| Aspect                | CreateForm ⭐              | AdminForm        |
| --------------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------- |
| **Purpose**           | Create-specific            | Generic          |
| **Prop data**         | `defaultValues` (semantic) | `data`           |
| **Prop id**           | ❌ Not exposed             | Optional         |
| **Submit text**       | "Create" (default)         | "Save" (default) |
| **editOnly sections** | Filtered auto              | Included         |
| **CRUD fields**       | Filtered auto              | Included         |

---

## 3. EditForm (Editing) ⭐ RECOMMENDED

### When to Use

✅ **USE when:**

- Edit page (`/[id]/edit`)
- Want TypeScript forcing `id` + `data` required
- Default submit text "Save" is adequate

### Example

```tsx title="app/admin/users/[id]/edit/edit-user-form.tsx"
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { EditForm } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { formSections, validationSchema, type UserFormData } from '../../config'
import { usersApi } from '@/lib/api/users-client'

export function EditUserForm({ user }: { user: User }) {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <EditForm
      id={user.id} // ← Required
      data={user} // ← Required
      sections={formSections}
      validation={validationSchema}
      onSubmitValues={async values => ({
        success: true,
        data: await usersApi.update(user.id, values as Partial<UserFormData>),
      })}
      onSuccess={() => router.push(`/admin/users/${user.id}`)}
      useTabs={true}
    />
  )
}
```

### Nested Data

Pass the record as the API returns it — do not flatten it. Field names in dot notation are
resolved against the nested object by React Hook Form:

```tsx
// user = {
//   id: "1",
//   person: { name: "John", taxId: "123" },
//   views: [{ id: "v1", name: "View 1" }]
// }

{ name: 'person.name', label: 'Name', type: 'text' } // reads user.person.name
```

### EditForm vs AdminForm

| Aspect                | EditForm ⭐      | AdminForm        |
| --------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------- |
| **Purpose**           | Edit-specific    | Generic          |
| **Prop id**           | ✅ Required      | Optional         |
| **Prop data**         | ✅ Required      | Optional         |
| **Submit text**       | "Save" (default) | "Save" (default) |
| **TypeScript safety** | ✅ High          | ⚠️ Medium        |

---

## 4. ZustandForm (Centralized State)

### When to Use

✅ **USE when:**

- Real-time preview in another component, outside the form's tree
- Multiple components need to read the form's values at the same time
- A multi-step flow (you build the steps; every step reads and writes the same store)

❌ **DON'T USE when:**

- Simple form (unnecessary overhead)

`ZustandForm` submits through `onSubmit(data)` (typed values, the client-side path) or
`action(formData)` — see [ZustandForm](/docs/components/zustand-form). Each form needs a unique
`formId`; values of different forms live side by side in the store under their ids.

### Example: Real-Time Preview

The store keeps each form's values under its `formId`: read them with
`useFormStore(state => state.forms[formId])`, or imperatively with
`useFormStore.getState().forms[formId]`.

```tsx title="app/admin/processes/new/with-preview.tsx"
'use client'

import { Card, ZustandForm, useFormStore } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const FORM_ID = 'process-form'

function ProcessForm() {
  return (
    <div className='grid grid-cols-2 gap-6'>
      <ZustandForm formId={FORM_ID} sections={formSections} onSubmit={processesApi.create} />
      <ProcessPreview />
    </div>
  )
}

function ProcessPreview() {
  // Re-renders only when this form's values change
  const values = useFormStore(state => state.forms[FORM_ID])

  return (
    <Card className='p-6'>
      <h2 className='text-lg font-bold mb-4'>Preview</h2>
      <p>Title: {String(values?.title ?? '—')}</p>
      <p>Notice Number: {String(values?.noticeNumber ?? '—')}</p>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

<Callout type='warn' title='Selectors inside custom hooks'>
  A dynamic selector such as `useFormStore(state => state.forms[formId])` is fine in a component,
  but inside a custom hook it causes an infinite loop (`getSnapshot should be cached`). See
  [Zustand Selector Pattern](/docs/patterns/zustand-selector).
</Callout>

---

## 5. ZustandFormServer (Server Component Wrapper)

### When to Use

✅ **USE when:**

- The page is a Server Component and you want `ZustandForm` without a client wrapper file
- It takes the same props as `ZustandForm` and loads it client-side (`next/dynamic`) with a skeleton

Functions passed from a Server Component must be Server Actions, so here the submit
handler is `action` (receives `FormData`):

### Example

```tsx title="app/admin/processes/new/page.tsx"
import { ZustandFormServer } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { formSections } from './config'
import { createProcess } from './actions' // a 'use server' function

export default function NewProcessPage() {
  return <ZustandFormServer formId='process-complex' sections={formSections} action={createProcess} />
}
```

---

## Side-by-Side Comparison

| Aspect                | AdminForm ⭐            | ZustandForm                   | ZustandFormServer          |
| --------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| **Use cases**         | Most forms              | Outside preview, shared state | ZustandForm from an RSC    |
| **State**             | Local (React Hook Form) | Global (Zustand)              | Global (Zustand)           |
| **Typed submit**      | `onSubmitValues`        | `onSubmit`                    | — (`action` from an RSC)   |
| **FormData submit**   | `action`                | `action`                      | `action`                   |
| **Multi-step**        | ❌ No                   | ✅ You build the steps        | ✅ You build the steps     |
| **Real-time preview** | ❌ No                   | ✅ Yes                        | ✅ Yes                     |

---

## Best Practices

1. **Prefer semantic wrappers:** Use `CreateForm`/`EditForm` instead of generic `AdminForm`
2. **Submit with `onSubmitValues`:** typed values straight into your API client or mutation
3. **Lay out with `grid` and `span`**, never width classes
4. **Multi-step flows are `ZustandForm`**: every step shares the same store
5. **Validate with Zod:** one schema per form, inferred as the form-data type

---

## Related Patterns

- [Admin Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) - Where `config.tsx` and its form live
- [Nested Data Pattern](/docs/patterns/nested-data) - Handle nested data
- [CRUD Field Pattern](/docs/patterns/crud-field) - 1:N and N:M lists inside a form
- [Standalone form pages](/docs/patterns/edit-page) - `CreatePage` and `EditPage`
- [Field Types](/docs/reference/field-types) - Every field type

---

<Callout type='success' title='Final Recommendation'>
  **Default to CreateForm/EditForm** for semantic clarity, fall back to AdminForm for generic
  cases, and use ZustandForm for multi-step flows or when something outside the form needs
  its values.
</Callout>

---

# Detail Views

> Read-only views of one record, in the view dialog by default or on a dedicated page, built from the Detail components

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/detail-page.mdx

A detail view shows one record: grouped fields, status, stats and actions. In a
TelamonJS module it opens in the **view dialog** of the list by default. A
dedicated `[id]` page is the exception, for views that outgrow a dialog.

---

## Where a detail view lives

| Case | Use | Config |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Up to 5 sections (default) | A `<EntityDetail />` component in the view dialog, with `ContentTabs` for sections | `dialogs.view.renderContent` |
| 6 or more sections | A section launcher inside the dialog | `dialogs.view.portal` |
| A page with its own URL, dashboards or sub-resources | A dedicated `[id]/page.tsx` built on `DetailLayout` | none (see [Dedicated page](#dedicated-page)) |

The record comes from `mutations.getForView` when the dialog opens, so the
detail component receives a loaded entity and only renders it.

---

## The components

You own the JSX; the components give you the layout and the visual language. Each
one has its own page with the full props.

| Component | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [DetailLayout](/docs/components/detail-layout) | Page shell: title, header actions, alerts, 2/3/4-column layouts, footer |
| [DetailCard](/docs/components/detail-card) | Section card with title, icon, optional `headerBadge`; renders `fields` or children |
| [DetailCardHeader](/docs/components/detail-card-header) | The card header on its own, for custom cards |
| [DetailField](/docs/components/detail-field) | Label + value, optional icon |
| [DetailAvatar](/docs/components/detail-avatar) | Avatar with name/subtitle, initials fallback, optional zoom |
| [DetailStatsGrid](/docs/components/detail-stats-grid) | Grid of stat tiles |
| [DetailStatus](/docs/components/detail-status) | Status badge driven by a status → config map |
| [DetailAlert](/docs/components/detail-alert) | Inline danger/warning/info/success block |
| [DetailActions](/docs/components/detail-actions) | Card with a stack (or row) of action buttons |

All of them are exported by `@telamonjs/ui` and by the `@telamonjs/ui/detail`
entry point. Text props typed `I18nText` accept a plain string or a `msg()`
reference.

`DetailPage` is a declarative wrapper configured with a `fieldGroups` array. It
fits only flat field lists: it does not compose with `DetailCard`/`DetailField`
and has no custom footer.

---

## In the view dialog (default)

```tsx title="app/admin/orders/_components/OrderDetail.tsx"
'use client'

import { ContentTabs, DetailCard, DetailStatsGrid, DetailStatus, type TabItem } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { getIcon } from '@/lib/icons'
import { orderStatus } from '@/lib/order-status'
import type { Order } from '@/lib/api/orders-client'

const UserIcon = getIcon('User')
const MailIcon = getIcon('Mail')
const PackageIcon = getIcon('Package')

export function OrderDetail({ order }: { order: Order }) {
  // Fixed height: the dialog must not resize when switching tabs
  const tabHeight = 'h-[min(600px,60vh)] overflow-y-auto p-6'

  const tabs: TabItem[] = [
    {
      value: 'customer',
      label: 'Customer',
      icon: 'User',
      content: (
        <div className={tabHeight}>
          <DetailCard
            title='Customer'
            icon={UserIcon}
            headerBadge={<DetailStatus status={order.status} statusConfig={orderStatus} />}
            fieldLayout='2-col'
            fields={[
              { label: 'Name', value: order.customer.name },
              { label: 'Email', value: order.customer.email, icon: MailIcon },
            ]}
          />
        </div>
      ),
    },
    {
      value: 'items',
      label: 'Items',
      icon: 'Package',
      content: (
        <div className={tabHeight}>
          <DetailStatsGrid
            stats={[
              { label: 'Items', value: order.items.length, icon: PackageIcon },
              { label: 'Shipping', value: order.shippingStatus, color: 'info' },
            ]}
          />
        </div>
      ),
    },
  ]

  return <ContentTabs tabs={tabs} defaultValue='customer' flush />
}
```

```tsx title="app/admin/orders/config.tsx (excerpt)"
dialogs: {
  view: {
    urlParam: 'view',
    title: 'Order',
    headerConfig, // icon, iconColor, title, gradient, badge
    renderContent: order => <OrderDetail order={order} />,
  },
},
```

`telamonjs lint` checks this shape: the view dialog needs a `headerConfig` and a
`renderContent` (or `portal`), the detail component uses `ContentTabs` rather than
raw `Tabs`, each tab has a fixed height, and more than 5 tabs should become a
`portal`. See the [rule table](/docs/packages/cli#lint).

### Status maps

Keep the `DetailStatus` map in a file next to the module and pass it in:

```tsx title="lib/order-status.ts"
import type { StatusConfig } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { getIcon } from '@/lib/icons'

export const orderStatus: Record<string, StatusConfig> = {
  PENDING: { label: 'Pending', variant: 'secondary', icon: getIcon('Clock') },
  PAID: { label: 'Paid', variant: 'default', icon: getIcon('CheckCircle') },
  CANCELLED: { label: 'Cancelled', variant: 'destructive', icon: getIcon('XCircle') },
}
```

Helpers that derive a status from several fields (`paidAt`, `cancelledAt`) belong
in the same file, not inline in the component.

---

## Dedicated page

A dedicated `[id]/page.tsx` is a Client Component that loads the record through the
module's API client and lays it out with `DetailLayout`:

```tsx title="app/admin/orders/[id]/page.tsx"
'use client'
// telamonjs-lint-disable-file no-crud-pages

import { use } from 'react'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { DetailActions, DetailCard, DetailLayout, DetailStatus } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { getIcon } from '@/lib/icons'
import { ordersApi } from '@/lib/api/orders-client'
import { orderStatus } from '@/lib/order-status'

export default function OrderPage({ params }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
  const { id } = use(params) // route params are a Promise
  const { data: order, isLoading } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['orders', id],
    queryFn: () => ordersApi.getById(id),
  })

  if (isLoading) return <div className='p-8'>Loading...</div>
  if (!order) return <div className='p-8'>Order not found</div>

  return (
    <DetailLayout
      title={`Order #${order.number}`}
      alerts={
        order.status === 'PENDING'
          ? [{ variant: 'warning', title: 'Pending payment', message: 'This order is awaiting payment.' }]
          : []
      }
      leftColumn={
        <DetailCard
          title='Customer'
          icon={getIcon('User')}
          headerBadge={<DetailStatus status={order.status} statusConfig={orderStatus} />}
          fields={[
            { label: 'Name', value: order.customer.name },
            { label: 'Email', value: order.customer.email },
          ]}
        />
      }
      rightColumn={
        <DetailActions
          title='Actions'
          actions={[{ label: 'Print invoice', icon: getIcon('Printer'), href: `/admin/orders/${order.id}/invoice` }]}
        />
      }
    />
  )
}
```

- **`queryKey: ['orders', id]`** is the per-record key. Mutations elsewhere
  invalidate `['orders']`; after a mutation on this page, invalidate both.
- **Destructive actions** ask for confirmation, then invalidate the list key and
  navigate back to the list.

### Server Component + client child

A module that fetches on the server renders a client child, because a component
cannot be both `async` and `'use client'`:

```tsx title="[id]/page.tsx (Server Component)"
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
import { getOrder } from '@/services/orders'
import { OrderDetail } from './OrderDetail' // 'use client'

export default async function Page(props: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
  const { id } = await props.params
  const order = await getOrder(id)
  if (!order) notFound()
  return <OrderDetail order={order} />
}
```

<Callout type='warn' title='Only plain data crosses the server/client boundary'>
  - **Icons**: a Lucide icon is a React component. Passing `icon={User}` from the Server page
    throws `Only plain objects can be passed to Client Components`. Use icons only in the client
    child.
  - **Non-plain values**: Prisma `Decimal` (money, percentages) and other class instances fail
    the same way. Convert them on the server first (`Number(product.price)`, or a serializer).
</Callout>

---

## Best practices

- **Type the entity** with the interface from the module's API client instead of
  redeclaring it.
- **Render nested values, not objects**: `value={order.customer.name}`, never
  `value={order.customer}`.
- **Announce abnormal states**: an inactive or blocked record gets an alert
  (`DetailLayout`'s `alerts`, or a `DetailAlert`), not a buried badge.
- **Format through the app**: dates and money go through `useFormat()`, never a
  hardcoded locale.
- **Icons come from the app's registry** (`getIcon('Name')`) or are imported
  individually; `import * as Icons` breaks tree-shaking.

---

## Troubleshooting

**"Element type is invalid" on an icon.** The icon is undefined: a namespace
import, a typo in the registry name, or a name missing from the app's icon
registry.

**The detail shows stale data after editing.** The edit invalidated only the list
key. Invalidate the record key too:

```ts
await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['orders', id] })
await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['orders'] })
```

**The dialog jumps in height between tabs.** Give every tab body the same fixed
height (`h-[min(600px,60vh)] overflow-y-auto`).

---

## Related

- [Module structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure): where the detail component lives
- [Dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs): view dialog options, `headerConfig`, `portal`
- [Standalone form pages](/docs/patterns/edit-page): the edit page next to a dedicated detail page
- [List pages](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern): the list that opens the view dialog

---

# Provider Setup Pattern

> Correct provider hierarchy for TelamonJS apps (AdminShell + React Query)

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/provider-setup.mdx

How to mount the providers and the shell of a TelamonJS app: `AppProviders` at the root (with the
app's own `QueryClient`), `AdminShell` in the admin area's layout. Apps generated by the CLI
already start this way.

---

## File Structure

```
src/
├── app/
│   ├── layout.tsx                # Root: <html> + <body> + AppProviders
│   └── admin/
│       └── layout.tsx            # Server Component: auth() + redirect + LayoutProviders
├── components/
│   └── providers/
│       ├── providers.tsx         # 'use client': the app's QueryClient + AppProviders
│       └── LayoutProviders.tsx   # 'use client': AdminShell + Toaster
├── config/
│   └── menu.ts                   # Typed MenuItem[] (icons as strings)
└── lib/
    ├── auth.ts                   # NextAuth v5 (auth())
    └── icons.ts                  # Project-owned iconRegistry
```

The library's styles come from `@telamonjs/ui/styles` and its Tailwind preset from
`@telamonjs/ui/tailwind-preset`.

---

## 1. AppProviders

`AppProviders` mounts i18n, the theme (next-themes), the NextAuth session, the cache-revalidation
context, Google Maps and a React Query client. Everything it accepts goes through `config`
(`ProvidersConfig`): `queryClient`, `queryClientConfig`, `themeConfig`, `authConfig`, `session`,
`googleMapsApiKey`, `revalidateAction` and `i18n` (see [i18n](/docs/patterns/i18n)).

It does **not** mount a toaster. The library's toasts use [sonner](https://sonner.emilkowal.ski)
(a peer dependency), so render the `Sonner` toaster once yourself (see [AdminShell](#4-adminshell))
and call `toast` from `sonner` in app code.

It also mounts an instant tooltip: icon-only buttons and links show their `aria-label` or `title`
immediately on mouse hover. `data-tooltip="off"` opts an element out, and `data-tooltip-text` sets
explicit text, which also applies to buttons with a visible label. An app with its own global
tooltip for icon-only buttons must remove it, otherwise both run.

The root layout stays a Server Component; it only needs `<html suppressHydrationWarning>` and
`<body>` around the client providers component of the next section:

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import { Providers } from '@/components/providers/providers'

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang='en' suppressHydrationWarning>
      <body>
        <Providers>{children}</Providers>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

---

## 2. The app's QueryClient

Every module built on `CrudConfig` reads and writes through React Query. An app that has its own
`QueryClient` (global error toasts, 401 redirect) passes it to `AppProviders` in
`config.queryClient` **and** keeps its own `QueryClientProvider` outside, with the **same** client.
Neither half is enough on its own:

- **Only the outer provider:** with the published package there is a single copy of react-query,
  and the client `AppProviders` creates internally shadows the app's for the whole tree. The app's
  global `onError` handlers and the invalidations made on its client silently stop working.
- **Only `config.queryClient`:** the app's client also serves the library's queries and mutations,
  which already handle their own errors. Without the `meta` check below, users see each error twice.

```tsx title="components/providers/providers.tsx"
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import {
  MutationCache,
  QueryCache,
  QueryClient,
  QueryClientProvider,
} from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { AppProviders } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { revalidatePathAction } from '@telamonjs/ui/server'
import { handleApiError } from '@/lib/api/error-handler'

export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  // useState, never module scope: a module-level client would be shared
  // across requests (and users) on the server.
  const [queryClient] = useState(
    () =>
      new QueryClient({
        queryCache: new QueryCache({
          onError: (error, query) => {
            if (query.meta?.skipErrorToast) return
            handleApiError(error)
          },
        }),
        mutationCache: new MutationCache({
          onError: (error, _variables, _context, mutation) => {
            if (mutation.meta?.skipErrorToast) return
            handleApiError(error)
          },
        }),
        defaultOptions: { queries: { staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000, retry: 1 } },
      })
  )

  // Same client in both: AppProviders uses it for the whole tree. The outer
  // provider matters when the library is linked (see /docs/troubleshooting).
  return (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <AppProviders config={{ queryClient, revalidateAction: revalidatePathAction }}>
        {children}
      </AppProviders>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  )
}
```

- **`meta.skipErrorToast` contract:** every query and mutation the library runs (CRUD, lists, the
  queue dashboard) carries `meta: { skipErrorToast: true }`, because the library already shows its
  own error (a toast for mutations, an error state with a retry button for lists). The app's global
  handler must honor that key. The app can set the same key on its own queries that handle errors
  locally.
- With `config.queryClient`, `config.queryClientConfig` is ignored.
- A client from another copy of react-query (a linked library) is ignored with a
  development-only warning. See
  [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting#when-the-apps-client-comes-from-another-copy).
- Apps that mount providers by hand, without `AppProviders`, can use the library's
  `QueryClientProvider` (it accepts `client` or `config`).

<Callout type='warn' title='Single React Query instance'>
  Always import `QueryClient`, `QueryCache` and `MutationCache` from `@tanstack/react-query`
  (`@telamonjs/ui` never re-exports them) and configure
  `experimental.optimizePackageImports: ['@telamonjs/ui']` in `next.config`. Two instances of the
  react-query module cause `"No QueryClient set"`: see
  [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting#no-queryclient-set).
</Callout>

---

## 3. SystemConfigProvider (optional)

An app-wide configuration context read with `useSystemConfig()` (`{ config, updateConfig }`).
`AdminShell` does not depend on it; use it only when the app needs to read this configuration in
several places. `SystemConfig` has six required blocks:

| Block | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `identity` | `name`, `description`, `version`, `logo?`, `favicon?` |
| `layout` | `defaultSidebarState` (`'expanded' \| 'compact' \| 'hidden'`), `showBreadcrumb`, `showSearch`, `showNotifications`, `maxContentWidth?` |
| `menu` | `items: MenuItem[]`, `showIcons`, `showBadges`, `allowCollapse` |
| `theme` | `primaryColor`, `mode` (`'light' \| 'dark' \| 'system'`), `customCSS?` |
| `auth` | `enabled`, `redirectPath`, `sessionProvider` (`'nextauth' \| 'custom'`) |
| `links` | `home`, `support?`, `documentation?`, `github?` |

```tsx
import { SystemConfigProvider } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { systemConfig } from '@/config/system-config'

<SystemConfigProvider config={systemConfig}>{children}</SystemConfigProvider>
```

---

## 4. AdminShell

Composes `ModernSidebar` + `CommandPalette` (Cmd+K) + `ResponsiveBreadcrumb` + header. The admin
layout is a Server Component: it reads the session, redirects when there is none, and passes the
session down as a prop — `AdminShell` itself is `'use client'`.

```tsx title="app/admin/layout.tsx"
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
import { LayoutProviders } from '@/components/providers/LayoutProviders'

export default async function AdminLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  const session = await auth()
  if (!session) redirect('/sign-in')

  return <LayoutProviders session={session}>{children}</LayoutProviders>
}
```

```tsx title="components/providers/LayoutProviders.tsx"
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import type { Session } from 'next-auth'
import { AdminShell, Sonner as Toaster } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { menuConfig } from '@/config/menu'

export function LayoutProviders({
  children,
  session,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode
  session: Session
}) {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <>
      <AdminShell
        menuConfig={menuConfig}
        session={{
          user: {
            name: session.user?.name ?? undefined,
            email: session.user?.email ?? undefined,
          },
        }}
        systemName='My Admin'
        logoUrl='/logo.png'
        compactLogoUrl='/icon-compact.png'
        onSignOut={() => router.push('/sign-out')}
      >
        {children}
      </AdminShell>
      <Toaster />
    </>
  )
}
```

Main props: `menuConfig`, `session?`, `systemName?`, `logoUrl?`/`compactLogoUrl?` (plus
`logoHeight?`, `logoMaxWidth?` and their compact variants), `onSignOut?`, `onStopImpersonation?`,
`showImpersonationBanner?`, `headerActions?`, `commandActions?`, `breadcrumbProps?`,
`profileHref?`, `localeSwitcher?`. See [AdminShell](/docs/components/admin-shell) for the full list.

### Permissions (optional)

To gate menus, lists and actions with the session's permissions, wrap the shell in
`PermissionsProvider` with your checker. It lives here, not in `AppProviders`, because the
checker usually reads the session through a hook that only works inside `SessionProvider`:

```tsx
<PermissionsProvider can={can}>
  <AdminShell menuConfig={menuConfig}>{children}</AdminShell>
</PermissionsProvider>
```

See [One checker for the whole app](/docs/getting-started/crud-config#one-checker-for-the-whole-app).

---

## Provider Hierarchy

```
QueryClientProvider (the app's QueryClient)
  └── AppProviders (i18n, theme, session, same QueryClient, maps)
       └── app/admin/layout.tsx (Server Component: session + redirect)
            └── PermissionsProvider (optional: the session's `can`)
                 └── AdminShell (ModernSidebar + CommandPalette + Breadcrumb, 'use client')
                      └── {children}
```

---

## Typed menu (menuConfig)

`AdminShell` receives a typed menu with icons passed **as strings**, resolved via
`getIcon`/`setIconResolver` — never import the Lucide component directly in the menu.

```tsx title="src/config/menu.ts"
import type { MenuItem } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export const menuConfig: MenuItem[] = [
  {
    id: 'dashboard',
    type: 'single',
    title: 'Dashboard',
    href: '/admin',
    icon: 'LayoutDashboard', // STRING — resolved via getIcon()
  },
  {
    id: 'admin-group',
    type: 'group',
    title: 'Administration',
    icon: 'Settings',
    children: [
      { id: 'users', type: 'single', title: 'Users', href: '/admin/users', icon: 'Users' },
    ],
  },
]
```

### Icon Resolver (`setIconResolver`)

The `iconRegistry` (name → lucide component) belongs to **the project**, not to `@telamonjs/ui`; the
library only keeps a small curated fallback map. Domain-specific icons live in the project's
registry. Register a resolver once at boot (client side), for example at the top of the providers
component:

```tsx title="src/lib/icons.ts"
import { Home, Users, Settings, Receipt, type LucideIcon } from 'lucide-react'

export const iconRegistry: Record<string, LucideIcon> = {
  Home,
  Users,
  Settings,
  Receipt,
  // add entries here when using a new icon in a menu/tab/header
}
```

```tsx
'use client'
import { setIconResolver } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { iconRegistry } from '@/lib/icons'

// getIcon now looks up: the project's resolver → the library's curated map → Circle
setIconResolver(name => iconRegistry[name])
```

The same strings work everywhere an icon is accepted — menu items, `TabItem.icon`,
`AdminHeader.icon` and dashboard items all take `string | IconComponent`:

```tsx
const tabs: TabItem[] = [
  { value: 'usage', label: 'Usage', icon: 'Receipt', content: <UsageTab /> },
]
<AdminHeader title='Billing' icon='Receipt' />
```

Prefer strings over passing the Lucide component (`icon: Home as IconComponent`): strings work the
same everywhere, while a component can fail type-check when the library is linked (see
[Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting#consuming-the-packages-via-link)).
`setIconResolver(null)` clears the resolver (useful in tests).

---

## Best Practices

1. **Server session.** Fetch the session on the server and pass it down as a prop — never call
   `useSession()` inside a client component that renders `AdminShell`: it flashes content and
   causes hydration errors.
2. **One `QueryClient` per app**, created with `useState` in a client component and passed in
   `config.queryClient` (see [above](#2-the-apps-queryclient)).
3. **Separate config files:** `menu.ts` for navigation, `auth.ts` for authentication, and
   `system-config.ts` if you use `SystemConfigProvider`.
4. **Menu icons as strings**, resolved through the project's `iconRegistry` + `setIconResolver`.

---

## Troubleshooting

### Hydration Errors

**Symptom:** "Hydration failed" errors in console

**Solution:** Set `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` — next-themes changes its class before
hydration.

### Theme Not Persisting

**Symptom:** The theme resets on page reload.

**Solution:** `AppProviders` uses next-themes, which persists to `localStorage` on its own. Make
sure `suppressHydrationWarning` is set and there is no second theme provider.

### Global error handlers never fire

**Symptom:** The app's `QueryCache`/`MutationCache` `onError` (toast, 401 redirect) works in
development but not in production.

**Solution:** The app's client is not passed to `AppProviders`, so the library's internal client
shadows it. Pass it in `config.queryClient` (see [The app's QueryClient](#2-the-apps-queryclient)).

### "No QueryClient set"

Two copies of react-query: see [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting#no-queryclient-set).

### Menu Not Showing

**Symptom:** Sidebar empty or menu items missing

**Solution:** Verify `menuConfig` is passed to `AdminShell`, has the `MenuItem[]` shape
(`type: 'single' | 'group' | 'separator'`) and unique `id`s.

### Icon shows as a circle

**Symptom:** A menu/tab/header icon renders as a generic circle (`Circle`).

**Solution:** The icon name isn't registered in the project's `iconRegistry` — add it there,
not in `@telamonjs/ui`.

### Session Not Available

**Symptom:** `session` is `null` or `undefined`.

**Solution:** Make sure NextAuth is configured and the session is read on the server
(`const session = await auth()`) in the admin layout.

---

- [i18n](/docs/patterns/i18n) - Locale, messages and `config.i18n`
- [Admin Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) - Where each file of a CRUD module lives
- [Dashboard Pattern](/docs/patterns/dashboard) - Dashboard pages inside the shell

<Callout type='success' title='Result'>
  Correct provider hierarchy, theme persistence, a single React Query client shared by the app and
  the library, type-safe menu, server-side session.
</Callout>

# Theming & Dark Mode

> The CSS-variable tokens the shell, tabs and charts paint with, how dark mode switches them, and the ThemeToggle

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/theming.mdx

Every surface of the library paints with **shadcn-style CSS variables** declared in
`@telamonjs/ui/styles` (`:root` for light, `.dark` for dark) and exposed as Tailwind colors by
`@telamonjs/ui/tailwind-preset` (`bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`…).
Dark mode is the `dark` class on `<html>`, set by the next-themes provider inside `AppProviders`.

To restyle the app, redefine the variables in your own `globals.css`, for both modes. Never
override the library's classes: a token change reaches every component that uses it.

```css
@layer base {
  :root {
    --primary: 197 37% 24%;
    --muted: 210 40% 96.1%;
  }
  .dark {
    --primary: 173 58% 39%;
    --muted: 223 47% 11%;
  }
}
```

Values are bare HSL channels (`H S% L%`), with no `hsl()` wrapper: the preset adds it and
Tailwind's opacity modifiers (`bg-muted/30`) work on top.

---

## Tokens the shell uses

| Surface | Classes | Variables |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AdminShell` root | `bg-background` | `--background` |
| `AdminShell` content column | `bg-muted/30` | `--muted` |
| `AdminShell` sticky header | `bg-card/95`, `border-border/60` | `--card`, `--border` |
| Breadcrumb (mobile home link) | `text-muted-foreground`, `hover:bg-accent` | `--muted-foreground`, `--accent` |
| `PageContent` card | `border-border`, header/footer `border-border/50`, title `text-foreground`, description `text-muted-foreground` | `--border`, `--foreground`, `--muted-foreground` |
| `ContentTabs` / `AdminTabs` bar | `from-muted/40 to-muted/30`, `border-border`; idle tabs `text-muted-foreground` | `--muted`, `--border`, `--muted-foreground` |
| `ContentTabs` `pill` / `gradient` / `glass` lists | `bg-muted`; `glass` uses `bg-foreground/5`, `border-border/50` | `--muted`, `--foreground`, `--border` |
| `Tabs` primitive (`TabsList`) | `bg-border` | `--border` |
| Sidebar | `bg-sidebar`, `text-sidebar-foreground`… | `--sidebar-*` |

## Charts

`LineChart`, `AreaChart`, `BarChart`, `PieChart` and the dashboard `ChartWidget` route the
Recharts chrome through the same variables, so axes and tooltips stay readable in dark mode:

| Part | Color |
| --- | --- |
| Axis line and tick labels | `hsl(var(--muted-foreground))` |
| Grid lines | `hsl(var(--border))` |
| Tooltip | background `hsl(var(--background))`, border `hsl(var(--border))` |

Series colors are not theme tokens: they come from each chart's `colors` prop. Pass
`'hsl(var(--chart-1))'`…`'hsl(var(--chart-5))'` to make them follow the theme as well.

---

## ThemeToggle

A light/dark button for the header. It calls next-themes' `setTheme` (the same instance as the
exported `useTheme`), so the choice persists in `localStorage`, and it renders a Sun and a Moon
icon with `dark:hidden` / `dark:block`, so server and client HTML match without a mounted-state
placeholder.

In the shell, turn it on with one prop (off by default):

```tsx
<AdminShell menuConfig={menuConfig} themeToggle>
  {children}
</AdminShell>
```

Anywhere else:

```tsx
import { ThemeToggle } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<ThemeToggle className='ml-2' />
```

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` | Extra classes, merged into the ghost icon button |

Its label (`aria-label` and tooltip) is the `shell.toggleTheme` message (see [i18n](/docs/patterns/i18n)).
For a light / dark / system menu instead of a button, build it on `useTheme()`.

## Following the OS preference

`AppProviders` starts in `light`. To start from `prefers-color-scheme`, pass the whole
`themeConfig`:

```tsx
<AppProviders
  config={{
    themeConfig: { attribute: 'class', defaultTheme: 'system', enableSystem: true },
  }}
>
```

<Callout type='warn'>
  `themeConfig` replaces the default object as a whole: passing only `defaultTheme` leaves
  `attribute` undefined, next-themes falls back to `data-theme`, and the `dark` class (which the
  preset's `darkMode: 'class'` reads) never lands on `<html>`.
</Callout>

Set `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` (see
[Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup#theme-not-persisting)).

---

## See Also

- [AdminShell](/docs/components/admin-shell) - The `themeToggle` prop
- [Provider Setup Pattern](/docs/patterns/provider-setup) - `AppProviders` and `themeConfig`
- [Installation](/docs/getting-started/installation) - Styles and Tailwind preset

# Internationalization (i18n)

> Multi-language UI text with next-intl — msg() in configs, locale per user, formatting and zod messages

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/i18n.mdx

Every text the library emits (buttons, search, empty states, pagination, dialogs, validation,
queue dashboard) comes from translated messages in **`pt-BR` (default), `en` and `es`**, with a
locale per user and runtime switching. The engine is [next-intl](https://next-intl.dev), a
**required peer dependency**.

## The 3 rules

| Where | How |
| --- | --- |
| `config.tsx` (plain object, no hooks) | `title: msg('users.title')` |
| Client Component | `const t = useTranslations('users'); t('title')` |
| Server Component | `const t = await getTranslations('users'); t('title')` |

A new key goes into **all three** `messages/{pt-BR,en,es}.json` files of the app. Everything
i18n-related lives in the `@telamonjs/ui/i18n` entry point.

<Callout type='warn' title='Import next-intl directly'>
  The library never re-exports `next-intl`. With `optimizePackageImports` a re-export would
  create a second copy of the context — the same failure class as `"No QueryClient set"`.
</Callout>

## App setup

Apps generated by the CLI already start this way.

```ts title="src/i18n/config.ts"
export const locales = ['pt-BR', 'en', 'es'] as const
export type AppLocale = (typeof locales)[number]
export const defaultLocale: AppLocale = 'pt-BR'
export const timeZone = 'America/Sao_Paulo'
export const currency = 'BRL'
```

The locale is resolved per request: `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie → `Accept-Language` → default.
`pickLocale` below stands for that lookup; the CLI template ships a complete one.

```ts title="src/i18n/request.ts"
import { getRequestConfig } from 'next-intl/server'
import { cookies, headers } from 'next/headers'
import { telamonjsMessages } from '@telamonjs/ui/i18n'
import { timeZone } from './config'

export default getRequestConfig(async () => {
  const locale = pickLocale(
    (await cookies()).get('NEXT_LOCALE')?.value,
    (await headers()).get('accept-language')
  )
  const app = (await import(`../../messages/${locale}.json`)).default
  // Namespaces never collide (library = `telamonjs`, app = per module)
  return { locale, timeZone, messages: { ...telamonjsMessages[locale], ...app } }
})
```

Apps using the library's `AppProviders` pass everything through `config.i18n`:

```tsx
<AppProviders config={{ i18n: { locale, messages, timeZone, currency: 'BRL', onLocaleChange } }}>
  {children}
</AppProviders>
```

Without `config.i18n` the app runs in pt-BR with the library's own messages. Without
`messages`, only pt-BR is in the client bundle: en/es load on demand and the screen shows pt-BR
until they arrive, so an app in another locale should pass `messages` from the server
(`getMessages()`).

Apps mounting providers by hand wrap the tree once:

```tsx
import { NextIntlClientProvider } from 'next-intl'
import { TelamonjsI18nProvider, telamonjsMessages } from '@telamonjs/ui/i18n'

<NextIntlClientProvider locale='pt-BR' messages={telamonjsMessages['pt-BR']} timeZone='America/Sao_Paulo'>
  <TelamonjsI18nProvider>{children}</TelamonjsI18nProvider>
</NextIntlClientProvider>
```

An app that already has its own `NextIntlClientProvider` must merge `telamonjsMessages[locale]`
into its message tree, otherwise library text renders as raw keys (`telamonjs.common.save`).

**Typed keys:** the app declares next-intl's `AppConfig`, in a `global.d.ts`. The library does
not ship this augmentation, because it would win over the app's under `skipLibCheck`.

```ts title="global.d.ts"
import type { TelamonjsMessages } from '@telamonjs/ui/i18n'
import type { AppLocale } from './src/i18n/config'
import type ptBR from './messages/pt-BR.json'

declare module 'next-intl' {
  interface AppConfig {
    Locale: AppLocale
    Messages: TelamonjsMessages & typeof ptBR
  }
}
```

## Switching language at runtime

`<LocaleSwitcher />` writes the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie (1 year, `SameSite=Lax`), calls
`onLocaleChange?.(locale)` — use it to persist to the user's profile — and fires
`router.refresh()`: Server Components re-render in the new locale, with no reload and no client
locale state. `AdminShell` already shows it in the user menu when there is more than one locale
(turn it off with `localeSwitcher={false}`).

## Formatting

`useFormat()` returns functions bound to the provider's locale, `timeZone` and `currency`:

```tsx
const fmt = useFormat()
fmt.date(value)                        // 'short' (default), 'medium' or 'long'
fmt.date(value, 'long')
fmt.dateTime(value, { seconds: true })
fmt.time(value)
fmt.currency(1234.5)          // the provider's currency, not the language's
fmt.currency(1234.5, 'USD')
fmt.number(value)
fmt.percent(value)
fmt.relative(value)
```

Never call `toLocaleDateString('pt-BR')` in a component. For `react-day-picker`/`date-fns`, use
`useDateFnsLocale()`. Currency and time zone do **not** derive from the language.

## Validation (zod)

`setupZodLocale(locale)` installs an error map that translates common issues. Schemas without a
`message` come out translated; a custom `message` stays in control. Refinements tag the issue:

```ts
z.string().refine(isValidCpf, { params: { i18n: 'invalidCpf' } })
```

A key **without a dot** is relative to `telamonjs.validation` (the library's validators). A key
**with a dot** is absolute and resolves against the library's and the app's messages, passed as
the second argument:

```ts
setupZodLocale(locale, appMessages) // appMessages = the JSON of messages/<locale>.json
z.string().refine(isPlate, { params: { i18n: 'assets.validation.plate', values: { min: 7 } } })
```

## Config slots that accept `msg()`

Text slots are typed `I18nText = string | MessageRef`: literal strings keep working, and functions
of the item/row may return `msg()`.

| Slot | Note |
| --- | --- |
| `headerConfig.stats.items[].label/value` | `value: v => msg('assets.total', { count: v.n })` |
| `headerConfig.title/subtitle(item)` | |
| `confirmDialog.title/description` | static or `row => msg(...)`; `BulkAction` likewise with `rows` |
| `ActionConfig.successMessage/errorMessage` | |
| `list.toolbar.counterLabel` | a message using `{count}` receives it and drops the numeric prefix: `'{count, plural, one {# order} other {# orders}}'` |
| `IOption.label`, `StatusOption.label` | resolved when the options load |
| `AdminHeader.title/description`, `PageHeaderConfig`, `PortalItem.description` | |
| `crudConfig.title/description/emptyTitle/emptyDescription` | header and empty state of the sub-CRUD |
| `CrudColumnDef.meta.label` | the column name where a `header` function does not render (export, column selector, filters, mobile card) |

```tsx
columns: [
  {
    accessorKey: 'plate',
    header: () => <Msg k='assets.fields.plate' />,
    meta: { label: msg('assets.fields.plate') },
  },
]
```

## Traps

- `msg()` only in config objects. In a component, use `useTranslations()`.
- Code that **reads** a config text slot must resolve it first: `const text = useText()`, then
  `text(item.title)`. Otherwise a `msg()` renders as `[object Object]`.
- Do not translate domain identifiers, API keys, ids, persisted enum values or `data-testid`.
- Do not concatenate UI strings — use ICU: `{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}`.
- Date placeholders are day-first in every locale, because the mask parser is day-first.

## Related

- [Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup)
- [Form Pattern](/docs/patterns/form-pattern)

---

# Nested Data Pattern

> Handle nested data with React Hook Form + Zod - keep nested throughout

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/nested-data.mdx

Mandatory pattern for forms over nested records (e.g. a user with `person.name`) with React Hook
Form (RHF) + Zod.

<Callout type='error' title='Problem this solves'>
  **Symptom:** nested fields did not save on edit — the old value persisted in the database.
  **Root cause:** the record was flattened (`person.name` keys) before reaching the form, RHF then
  held BOTH shapes (flat + nested) in its state, and the submit picked the stale flat keys.
</Callout>

---

## Golden Rule: Keep Nested Throughout

**Never flatten a record before giving it to a form.** RHF maps dot-notation field names to
nested paths natively. `EditForm`, `EditPage` and the `ListPage` edit dialog pass `data` through
as is; don't flatten it first.

```tsx
// ❌ WRONG — creates duplicate flat + nested values in RHF state
<EditForm id={user.id} data={flatten(user)} sections={formSections} onSubmitValues={save} />

// ✅ CORRECT — pass the record as the API returns it
<EditForm id={user.id} data={user} sections={formSections} onSubmitValues={save} />
```

---

## Implementation Checklist

### 1. Zod schema — nested structure

```ts
// ❌ WRONG - flat keys
const schema = z.object({
  'person.name': z.string(),
  'person.taxId': z.string(),
})

// ✅ CORRECT - nested structure
const schema = z.object({
  person: z.object({
    name: z.string(),
    taxId: z.string(),
  }),
  email: z.string().email(),
})
```

### 2. FormSection — dot notation in field names

```ts
export const formSections: FormSection[] = [
  {
    label: 'Personal Data',
    fields: [
      { name: 'person.name', label: 'Name', type: 'text' }, // ← dot notation
      { name: 'person.taxId', label: 'Tax ID', type: 'masked' },
      { name: 'email', label: 'Email', type: 'email' },
    ],
  },
]
```

### 3. Loading — return the record nested

```tsx title="config.tsx"
mutations: {
  // the record exactly as the API sends it: { person: { name, taxId }, email, ... }
  getForEdit: usersApi.get,
  update: {
    // values arrive NESTED: { person: { name, taxId }, email }
    mutationFn: async ({ id, data }) => ({ success: true, data: await usersApi.update(id, data) }),
    invalidates: [['users']],
  },
},
```

The same holds for a standalone `<EditForm id={id} data={user} sections={formSections} onSubmitValues={...} />`.

### 4. Submit — what the handler receives

Forms have two submit modes:

| Mode | Prop | Receives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON (preferred; what `ListPage` uses) | `onSubmitValues` / `mutations.*.mutationFn` | the values **nested** (`{ person: { name } }`) and typed, plus `id` |
| FormData (Server Actions) | `action` | a `FormData` with **flat dot keys** (`'person.name'`), every value a string |

With `onSubmitValues` or a `mutationFn` there is nothing to rebuild: send the values to the API as
they are (the backend validates the nested DTO), or reshape them inside the `mutationFn` if the
endpoint wants another format. Only a `FormData` handler has to rebuild nested objects from the
dot keys itself.

---

## Data Flow

```
1. API (getForEdit)          { person: { name: 'John', taxId: '123' }, email: 'john@...' }
2. Form data prop            same object, no conversion
3. RHF defaultValues         same object
4. Field name="person.name"  → RHF path values.person.name
5. User edits                values.person.name = 'John Smith'
6. Zod (form.validation)     nested schema, client-side
7. onSubmitValues            { id, person: { name: 'John Smith', taxId: '123' }, email }
8. mutationFn({ id, data })  → PATCH /users/:id with the nested body
```

| Layer | Structure | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API / `getForEdit` | Nested | `{ person: { name, taxId } }` |
| Form `data` prop | Nested | Same as API |
| RHF `defaultValues` and state | Nested | `values.person.name` |
| FormSection fields | Dot notation | `name: 'person.name'` |
| Zod schema | Nested | `person: z.object({ ... })` |
| `onSubmitValues` / `mutationFn` | Nested | `{ person: { name, taxId } }` |
| `FormData` (`action`) | Flat | `'person.name': 'John'` |

---

## Common Pitfalls

### Pitfall 1: flat Zod schema with nested data

```ts
const schema = z.object({ 'person.name': z.string() }) // expects a flat key
schema.parse({ person: { name: 'John' } }) // ❌ Error: person.name is required
```

**Fix:** the schema mirrors the data structure (nested).

### Pitfall 2: flattening the record before the form

```ts
// RHF defaultValues: { 'person.name': 'John' } (flat)
// User edits field name="person.name" → RHF writes NESTED { person: { name: 'New' } }
// Result: BOTH shapes in state — the submit picks the stale flat value ❌
```

**Fix:** pass the nested record directly (no flattening).

### Pitfall 3: a FormData handler treating dot keys as nested

```ts
const data = Object.fromEntries(formData) // { 'person.name': 'John', ... } — flat, all strings
userSchema.parse(data) // ❌ nested schema rejects flat keys
```

**Fix:** submit with `onSubmitValues` (or `mutations.*` through `CrudConfig`), which receives
nested, typed values.

---

## Debugging Tips

```tsx
// Inside a component rendered in the form: look for duplicate flat/nested keys
import { useWatch } from '@telamonjs/ui'

function DebugFormState() {
  const values = useWatch()
  console.log({
    hasFlat: Object.keys(values).some(k => k.includes('.')),
    hasNested: Object.keys(values).some(k => typeof values[k] === 'object' && !Array.isArray(values[k])),
  })
  return null
}
```

A key containing a dot in the form state means something flattened the record on the way in.

---

## Checklist

- [ ] Zod schema is nested (no flat dot keys)
- [ ] No flattening before passing `data` to a form
- [ ] Submit via `onSubmitValues` / `mutations.*` (nested values), not a `FormData` `action`
- [ ] Test: edit a nested field → save → reopen → the value persisted

---

## Related

- [Form Pattern](/docs/patterns/form-pattern) — form components and field rules
- [CRUD Field Pattern](/docs/patterns/crud-field) — 1:N/N:M lists inside a form
- [Field Types](/docs/reference/field-types) — `'masked'`, `'crud'` and friends

# CRUD Field Pattern

> Manage nested 1:N and N:M relationships directly inside the parent form

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/crud-field.mdx

A `type: 'crud'` field manages a **child list inside the parent's form** — a table with add,
edit and delete, each in a small dialog — without leaving the page. Typical uses:

- **1:N** (one-to-many): Customer → Branches, Customer → Contacts
- **N:M** (many-to-many): User → Customers (with `manyToMany: true`)

The child list needs the parent's id, so it only exists once the parent is saved: CRUD fields
render in **edit** contexts (the edit dialog, `EditForm`, `EditPage`), and `CreateForm` filters
them out. Put them in a section with `editOnly: true`.

---

## When to Use

### ✅ USE when

- You need to create/edit/delete related entities in the same form
- The relationship is **tightly coupled** to the parent (e.g. a customer's branches)
- The user benefits from staying on the current page
- The number of related items is **small/medium** (&lt;100 items)

### ❌ Do NOT use when

- The relationship is **weak** or independent (use a `relationship` field instead)
- The child list is large or needs search, filters and paging — use an embedded `ListPage`
  scoped with `withScope` (see [Lists Scoped to a Parent](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern#lists-scoped-to-a-parent))
- The related entity has many complex fields (10+): give it its own dialog or page
- You need complex cross-entity validation

---

## Anatomy

Two formats configure the same component. **Prefer `crudConfig`**: it keeps the list, the form
and the operations together.

```tsx
{
  name: 'branches',
  label: 'Branches',
  type: 'crud',

  crudConfig: {
    title: 'Branches',                       // heading above the list (I18nText)
    columns: [{ header: 'Name', accessorKey: 'name' }],
    fields: [{ name: 'name', label: 'Branch name', type: 'text', required: true }],
    validation: branchSchema,                // Zod schema of the child form (optional)

    loadData: ({ id }) => branchesApi.listByCustomer(id),         // id = parent
    loadForEdit: (parentId, itemId) => branchesApi.get(itemId),
    create: async (data, { id }) => { await branchesApi.create(id, data); return true },
    update: async (data, { itemId }) => { await branchesApi.update(itemId, data); return true },
    delete: ({ id }) => branchesApi.delete(id),                   // 1:N: 2nd arg is { parentId }
  },

  // Optional, on the field itself
  manyToMany: false,   // true for N:M
  readOnly: false,     // true hides add/edit/delete
  Footer: BranchesFooter,
}
```

`crudConfig` also takes `description`, `emptyTitle` and `emptyDescription` for the copy around
the list.

---

## The Operations Contract

What the field calls at runtime:

| `crudConfig` | Field prop | Called with | Must resolve |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loadData` | `listingFn` | `({ id: parentId })` | the array of items |
| `loadForEdit` | `loadFn` | `loadForEdit(parentId, itemId)` / `loadFn(itemId, parentId)` | the item |
| `create` | `createFn` | `(values, { id: parentId })` | `true` or `{ status: 'success' \| 'error', description }` |
| `update` | `editFn` | `(values, { id: parentId, itemId })` | same as `create` |
| `delete` | `deleteFn` | 1:N `({ id }, { parentId })` · N:M `({ parentId, id })` | anything; a rejection shows an error |

<Callout type='warn' title='The data comes first, the ids second'>
  `create` and `update` receive the submitted values first and the ids second. The parent id is
  never inside the values (the field removes it), so read it from the second argument. The
  exported `CrudCreateFn`, `CrudEditFn` and `CrudDeleteFn` types describe exactly this order, for
  both formats.
</Callout>

- **Resolve `true`**, or `{ status: 'success', description }` to choose the success toast.
  Resolving the created entity is treated as a failure and shows a generic error, even though
  the record was saved: adapt inside the function.
- **Throw** (or resolve `{ status: 'error', description }`) to show a message in the child form,
  such as the API's validation error.
- Without `update`/`loadForEdit` the edit button is hidden; without `delete`, the delete button.

```ts
// ❌ WRONG — parent id first, entity returned
create: (parentId: string, values: unknown) => branchesApi.create(parentId, values)

// ✅ CORRECT — values first, { id: parentId } second, resolve true
create: async (values, { id }) => {
  await branchesApi.create(id, values)
  return true
}
```

---

## Complete Example: Customer → Branches

### 1. API client

```ts title="lib/api/branches-client.ts"
export const branchesApi = {
  listByCustomer: (customerId: string) => api.get<Branch[]>(`/customers/${customerId}/branches`),
  get: (id: string) => api.get<Branch>(`/branches/${id}`),
  create: (customerId: string, data: unknown) => api.post<Branch>(`/customers/${customerId}/branches`, data),
  update: (id: string, data: unknown) => api.patch<Branch>(`/branches/${id}`, data),
  delete: (id: string) => api.delete(`/branches/${id}`),
}
```

`api` stands for the app's fetch wrapper. The backend takes `customerId` from the route.

### 2. config.tsx

```tsx title="app/admin/customers/config.tsx (excerpt)"
'use client'

import type { CrudConfig, FormSection } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { customersApi } from '@/lib/api/customers-client'
import { branchesApi } from '@/lib/api/branches-client'

export const formSections: FormSection[] = [
  {
    label: 'General',
    fields: [{ name: 'name', label: 'Customer name', type: 'text', required: true }],
  },
  {
    label: 'Organization',
    editOnly: true, // the list needs the parent's id: edit only
    fields: [
      {
        name: 'branches',
        label: 'Branches',
        type: 'crud',
        crudConfig: {
          columns: [{ header: 'Name', accessorKey: 'name' }],
          fields: [{ name: 'name', label: 'Branch name', type: 'text', required: true, focus: true }],
          loadData: ({ id }) => branchesApi.listByCustomer(id),
          loadForEdit: (_parentId, itemId) => branchesApi.get(itemId),
          // the API returns the entity, so adapt here and resolve true
          create: async (data, { id }) => {
            await branchesApi.create(id, data)
            return true
          },
          update: async (data, { itemId }) => {
            await branchesApi.update(itemId, data)
            return true
          },
          delete: ({ id }) => branchesApi.delete(id),
        },
      },
    ],
  },
]

export const customersConfig: CrudConfig<Customer, CustomerFormData> = {
  // module, list, query...
  form: { sections: formSections, validation: customerSchema },
  mutations: {
    // create / update of the customer itself...
    getForEdit: customersApi.get,
  },
  dialogs: { edit: { title: 'Edit customer' }, create: { title: 'New customer' } },
}
```

The `ListPage` edit dialog passes the customer's `id` to the form, and the CRUD field uses it as
the parent. The field's operations do not go through the module's `mutations`: each one calls
the API directly, then reloads the child list and the record of the dialog that contains it.

---

## The Child Form

The add/edit dialog is an `AdminForm` in a two-column grid, filled with the item that
`loadForEdit` returns. Field names are relative to that item, so dot notation reaches its nested
relations (`person.name`) the same way as in any form — see the
[Nested Data Pattern](/docs/patterns/nested-data).

Child fields support `name`, `label`, `type`, `required`, `placeholder`, `readOnly`, `focus`,
`default`, `span`, `description`, `loadField`/`dependsOn`, `mask`/`maskType`, `rows`, `uploadFn`/`path`
and `Component`. Other field props (such as `visibleWhen` or date limits) are not applied inside
a CRUD field.

---

## Advanced Customization

### Custom footer

`Footer` renders under the list and receives `{ id, data, onRefresh }`:

```tsx
function BranchesFooter({ data }: { id?: string; data: unknown[]; onRefresh?: () => void }) {
  return <div className='mt-4 text-sm text-muted-foreground'>Total branches: {data.length}</div>
}
```

### Many-to-many (N:M)

```tsx
{
  name: 'customers',
  type: 'crud',
  manyToMany: true,
  crudConfig: {
    // ...
    // N:M: the parent id comes inside the first argument
    delete: ({ parentId, id }) => usersApi.unlinkCustomer(parentId!, id),
  },
}
```

Delete signatures: 1:N `({ id }, { parentId })`, N:M `({ parentId, id })`.

### Read-only

```tsx
{ name: 'branches', type: 'crud', readOnly: true, crudConfig: { /* ... */ } }
```

---

## Troubleshooting

### Saved in the backend, but the form shows an error

`create`/`update` resolved the entity instead of `true`. Adapt inside the function (see the
contract above).

### "parentId is undefined" / `values.id` is the parent's id

The parent comes in the second argument (`{ id }`), never inside the values:
`create: async (data, { id: parentId }) => { await api.create(parentId, data); return true }`.

### The list does not appear

The form has no `id` yet (create mode): `loadData` only runs once the parent exists. Put the
section under `editOnly: true`, or save the parent first.

---

## Related

- [Nested Data Pattern](/docs/patterns/nested-data) — dot notation for nested fields
- [Form Pattern](/docs/patterns/form-pattern) — general form configuration
- [ListPage Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) — embedded child lists with `withScope`
- [Field Types](/docs/reference/field-types) — the `'crud'` type in context
