# Dashboard Pattern

> Viewport-filling dashboards with auto-refresh, fullscreen, and stat cards

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/dashboard.mdx

Modern dashboard components with auto-refresh, fullscreen, and a glassmorphism aesthetic.

## Overview

`DashboardShell` is a viewport-filling container for dashboards with built-in auto-refresh, fullscreen mode, and status indicators. It orchestrates `DashboardHeader` and `DashboardFullscreen`.

**Key features:**

- **Two layout modes:** `fullHeight` (maps/real-time) vs scroll (grids/reports)
- **Auto-refresh** with configurable intervals and an on/off toggle in the header
- **Fullscreen mode** with ESC key support
- **Status indicators:** online/offline/loading/error with pulse animations
- Optional **search** input and custom header **actions**

### When to Use

| Scenario | Use DashboardShell? |
| --- | --- |
| Map dashboard (full-bleed) | ✅ Yes (`fullHeight={true}`) |
| Real-time monitoring | ✅ Yes (auto-refresh) |
| Executive dashboard (grids) | ✅ Yes (`fullHeight={false}`) |
| Dashboard with tabs | ❌ No — see below |
| CRUD pages | ❌ No — use `ListPage` |
| Forms | ❌ No — use `CreateForm`/`EditForm` |
| Detail pages | ❌ No — use `DetailLayout` |

For tabbed admin pages, prefer the composable shell: [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page) + [AdminHeader](/docs/components/admin-header) + [AdminTabs](/docs/components/admin-tabs).

---

## DashboardShell Modes

### fullHeight Mode (maps / real-time)

Use for maps (Google Maps, Mapbox, Leaflet), asset tracking, IoT dashboards, and full-screen visualizations.

- The shell fills its parent's height (`h-full`); the content area is
  `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-hidden`, with no default padding (full-bleed)
- Nested areas that must scroll get their own `overflow-auto`
- Great for 2-column layouts (map + sidebar)

```tsx
<DashboardShell fullHeight={true}>
  {/* Fixed container - no scroll */}
  <div className='grid grid-cols-2 gap-4 h-full p-4'>
    {/* Left: map (full-bleed) */}
    <div className='overflow-hidden rounded-lg border'>
      <MapComponent />
    </div>

    {/* Right: scrollable sidebar */}
    <div className='overflow-auto custom-scrollbar'>
      <StatsGrid />
      <AssetList />
    </div>
  </div>
</DashboardShell>
```

### Scroll Mode (grids / reports)

Use for executive dashboards with many widgets, report pages, and content taller than the viewport.
The content area is `overflow-visible` and the page scrolls naturally; add your own padding.

```tsx
<DashboardShell fullHeight={false}>
  {/* Natural page scroll */}
  <div className='p-6 space-y-6'>
    <StatsGrid />
    <ChartsGrid />
    <TablesGrid />
  </div>
</DashboardShell>
```

---

## Auto-Refresh Best Practices

### Typical intervals

| Dashboard type | Recommended interval | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Asset tracking (real-time) | 30s - 1min | Balance freshness vs API load |
| Monitoring dashboards | 1min - 2min | Reduce server load |
| Executive dashboards | 5min - 15min | Data changes infrequently |
| Report dashboards | Disabled (manual) | Data is static |

### How it behaves

- `autoRefresh` defaults to **`true`** and `autoRefreshInterval` to **30000 ms**. With an
  `onRefresh`, the shell calls it **once on mount**, then on every interval — a report page that
  should not poll must pass `autoRefresh={false}` (the manual refresh button still works).
- The header shows a refresh button, an auto-refresh toggle and the last update time whenever
  `onRefresh` is set. Pass `lastUpdate` to show your data's real timestamp instead of the time
  of the last call.
- `onRefresh` is kept in a ref, so an inline arrow function does not restart the interval;
  `useCallback` is not required.
- The interval keeps running while the browser tab is hidden.

### Wiring it to React Query

Pass the query's `refetch` — it resolves even when the request fails (the error lands in the
query state), so a failed refresh never breaks the interval:

```tsx
const { data, refetch, dataUpdatedAt } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['assets'], queryFn: assetsApi.list })

<DashboardShell
  title='Assets'
  onRefresh={refetch}
  lastUpdate={dataUpdatedAt ? new Date(dataUpdatedAt) : undefined}
  autoRefreshInterval={60_000}
>
```

If polling must stop while the tab is hidden, let React Query poll instead
(`refetchInterval`, which pauses in background tabs by default) and keep the shell's button
manual with `autoRefresh={false}`.

### Error handling

An `onRefresh` that throws is not caught by the shell. Handle errors inside it (React Query's
`refetch` already does), and surface them in the page — the `status='error'` indicator with a
`statusLabel` is the natural place.

---

## Fullscreen UX

`allowFullscreen` defaults to `true`. Keep it for maps, monitoring, and presentation mode;
**disable** it for simple stat grids, form-heavy dashboards, or mobile-only pages.

Built-in behavior:

- Without `fullscreenContent`, the shell itself expands to cover the viewport (`fixed inset-0 z-50`).
- With `fullscreenContent`, that content opens in a separate `DashboardFullscreen` overlay instead,
  with the same title, icon and status, and the page body stops scrolling while it is open.
- **ESC always closes** fullscreen, and so does the header button.

Use the `fullscreenContent` prop when the fullscreen version needs a different layout:

```tsx
<DashboardShell
  title='My Assets'
  fullscreenContent={<MapComponent zoom={12} />} // larger map in fullscreen
>
  <div className='grid grid-cols-2'>
    <MapComponent zoom={10} />
    <AssetList />
  </div>
</DashboardShell>
```

---

## Stat Card Patterns

### Color conventions

| Color | Use case | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Blue** | Default/neutral | Totals, revenue, general metrics |
| **Green** | Positive/online/success | Assets online, gains |
| **Yellow** | Warning/paused | Pending actions, attention needed |
| **Red** | Error/offline/critical | Assets offline, failures, losses |
| **Purple** | Special/featured | Premium users, VIP clients |
| **Orange** | Secondary highlight | Rates, conversion |
| **Gray** | Disabled/inactive | Archived items |

### Badges

- `success` → positive changes (+10%), goals met
- `warning` → attention needed, approaching limits
- `destructive` → critical alerts, negative changes

```tsx
<StatCard
  label='Monthly Revenue'
  value={125430}
  icon={DollarSign}
  color='blue'
  badge={{ text: '+12%', variant: 'success' }}
/>
```

### Numbers

`value` is formatted with the locale's separators unless `formatNumber={false}`. Pass a
pre-formatted string for currency and percentages (`fmt.currency(total)` from `useFormat()`).

### Animation

Enable `animate` for numeric values that change (counters, refresh transitions); disable for string values and performance-critical mobile dashboards. Default duration 500ms (`animationDuration`). Powered by [useAnimatedCounter](/docs/hooks/use-animated-counter).

### Interactive cards

Use `onClick` when a card links to a detail page, filters the dashboard, or opens a modal. The card renders inside a native `<button>`, so it is keyboard-reachable.

---

## Nested Scrolling Pattern

Content inside a fixed-height container will not scroll without the `min-h-0` trick:

```tsx
// ✅ Proper nested scrolling
<div className='h-[calc(100vh-7rem)] flex flex-col'>
  <DashboardHeader />

  {/* KEY: min-h-0 lets the flex child shrink below content size */}
  <div className='flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-auto'>{/* content scrolls here */}</div>
</div>
```

For multi-region scrolling (two independent columns), give each column `overflow-auto` inside a parent grid with `h-full`.

---

## Complete Example: Map Dashboard

```tsx
'use client'

import { useMemo } from 'react'
import { DashboardShell, StatCard } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Truck, Activity, Navigation } from 'lucide-react'

export default function AssetsPage() {
  const { assets, refetch } = useAssets()

  const stats = useMemo(
    () => ({
      online: assets.filter((v) => v.status === 'online').length,
      stopped: assets.filter((v) => v.status === 'stopped').length,
      offline: assets.filter((v) => v.status === 'offline').length,
    }),
    [assets]
  )

  return (
    <DashboardShell
      title='My Assets'
      description='Real-time monitoring'
      icon={Truck}
      status='online'
      statusLabel={`${stats.online} assets online`}
      autoRefresh
      autoRefreshInterval={120000} // 2 minutes
      onRefresh={refetch}
      fullHeight
      allowFullscreen
    >
      <div className='grid grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2 gap-4 h-full p-4'>
        <div className='rounded-lg border overflow-hidden'>
          <MapComponent assets={assets} />
        </div>

        <div className='flex flex-col gap-3 overflow-auto custom-scrollbar'>
          <div className='grid grid-cols-4 gap-2'>
            <StatCard variant='tinted' size='compact' label='Online' value={stats.online} icon={Activity} color='green' animate />
            <StatCard variant='tinted' size='compact' label='Stopped' value={stats.stopped} icon={Navigation} color='yellow' animate />
            <StatCard variant='tinted' size='compact' label='Offline' value={stats.offline} icon={Activity} color='red' animate />
            <StatCard variant='tinted' size='compact' label='Total' value={assets.length} icon={Truck} color='blue' animate />
          </div>

          <AssetList assets={assets} />
        </div>
      </div>
    </DashboardShell>
  )
}
```

---

## API Reference

### DashboardShell

```typescript
interface DashboardShellProps {
  // Identification
  title: I18nText
  description?: I18nText
  icon?: string | IconComponent // a string resolves through setIconResolver()

  // Status
  status?: 'online' | 'offline' | 'loading' | 'error' // default: 'online'
  statusLabel?: I18nText

  // Search
  searchPlaceholder?: I18nText
  searchValue?: string
  onSearchChange?: (value: string) => void

  // Auto-refresh
  autoRefresh?: boolean // default: true
  autoRefreshInterval?: number // ms, default: 30000
  onRefresh?: () => void | Promise<void>
  lastUpdate?: Date

  // Fullscreen
  allowFullscreen?: boolean // default: true
  fullscreenContent?: ReactNode

  // Edit mode (DashboardGrid integration)
  editable?: boolean
  onEditToggle?: (enabled: boolean) => void

  // Actions
  actions?: ReactNode

  // Layout
  fullHeight?: boolean // default: true
  className?: string
  contentClassName?: string
  children: ReactNode
}
```

### StatCard

Same component as [StatCard](/docs/components/stats-card): `label`, `value`, `icon` and `color` are
required; `variant` (`outlined` (default) | `tinted` | `accent`), `size` (`mini` | `compact` |
`default`), `subtitle`, `badge`, `formatNumber`, `animate`, `animationDuration`, `onClick`,
`highlight`, `pulse` and `wrapLabel` are optional.

Other pieces: `DashboardHeader` (status pulse, timestamp, compact actions), `DashboardFullscreen`
(overlay with ESC and body scroll lock). Both are exported for custom layouts.

---

## Performance Tips

1. **Memoize** derived stats with `useMemo`
2. **Debounce** search (`useDebounce(search, 300)`)
3. **Virtualize** long lists (`@tanstack/react-virtual`) inside scrollable sidebars

## Troubleshooting

- **Two requests on page open** → the shell calls `onRefresh` on mount, while the query's first
  load may still be in flight (`refetch` cancels and restarts it); pass `autoRefresh={false}` if
  that matters
- **A report page keeps polling** → `autoRefresh` defaults to `true`; pass `autoRefresh={false}`
- **Fullscreen doesn't cover everything** → z-index conflict; fullscreen uses `z-50`
- **Content doesn't scroll in fullHeight mode** → add `overflow-auto` to the nested container (see Nested Scrolling above)

---

## Related

- [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page) + [AdminTabs](/docs/components/admin-tabs) — composable shell for tabbed dashboards
- [useAnimatedCounter](/docs/hooks/use-animated-counter) — the counter animation hook
- [ListPage Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) — for CRUD list pages
- [Detail Page](/docs/patterns/detail-page) — for detail pages

---

# Standalone form pages

> When a module needs dedicated create/edit routes — EditPage and CreatePage with shared form sections, Zod validation and typed actions

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/edit-page.mdx

<Callout type='info' title='Dialogs are the default'>
  A `CrudConfig` module creates and edits records in **dialogs** that `ListPage` renders from
  `config.form`: no extra routes. That is what the CLI generates, and its `no-crud-pages` lint
  rule reports `adicionar/page.tsx`, `[id]/page.tsx` and `[id]/editar/page.tsx` next to a
  module's `config.tsx` as errors. Reach for a standalone page only when a form genuinely needs
  its own URL or a full-page layout (a long multi-section form, a flow linked from outside the
  list), and put `// telamonjs-lint-disable-file no-crud-pages` at the top of each such page.
  See [Dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs).
</Callout>

How to build dedicated create and edit pages (`adicionar/` and `[id]/editar/` below) using the
`EditPage` and `CreatePage` wrappers, sharing the `formSections` and Zod schema already defined in
the module's `config.tsx`.

---

## EditPage vs CreatePage

| Aspect        | `EditPage`                      | `CreatePage`                          |
| ------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Semantics     | Edit an existing entity         | Create a new one                      |
| Props         | `id`, `data`                    | `defaultValues` (no id)               |
| CRUD fields   | Rendered                        | **Auto-filtered** (need a parent row) |
| `editOnly` sections | Rendered                  | **Auto-filtered**                     |
| `useTabs` default | `true`                      | `false`                               |

Both wrap `PageContent` + the underlying form — use the bare
`EditForm`/`CreateForm` only when you already have a custom page layout.

<Callout type='info' title='Why CRUD fields are filtered on create'>
  A `type: 'crud'` field manages child rows of the entity (e.g. addresses of a
  client). Children can only exist after the parent does, so CreatePage strips
  those fields — and whole sections marked `editOnly: true` — automatically.
</Callout>

---

## File Structure

```
app/admin/usuarios/
├── config.tsx            # formSections + validationSchema (shared)
├── adicionar/
│   └── page.tsx          # CreatePage
└── [id]/
    └── editar/
        └── page.tsx      # EditPage
```

The form sections and the Zod schema are defined **once** in `config.tsx` and
imported by both pages. See
[Admin Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) for the full
config anatomy.

---

## Implementation (React Query)

### Edit

The page loads the entity through the module's API client, maps it to form
default values, and submits through a typed action:

```tsx title="app/admin/usuarios/[id]/editar/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { use } from 'react'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { EditPage, type FormActionResult } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { formSections, validationSchema, type UsuarioFormData } from '../../config'
import { usuariosApi } from '@/lib/api/usuarios-client'

export default function UsuarioEditPage({
  params,
}: {
  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
}) {
  const { id } = use(params)
  const router = useRouter()

  const { data: usuario, isLoading } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['usuarios', id],
    queryFn: () => usuariosApi.getById(id),
  })

  async function action(formData: FormData): Promise<FormActionResult<UsuarioFormData>> {
    const data = validationSchema.parse(Object.fromEntries(formData.entries()))
    // Blank password means "keep the current one" — don't send it.
    if (!data.password) delete data.password
    await usuariosApi.update(id, data)
    router.push(`/admin/usuarios/${id}`)
    return { success: true }
  }

  if (isLoading || !usuario) return null

  const defaultValues: Partial<UsuarioFormData> = {
    name: usuario.name ?? '',
    email: usuario.email,
    role: usuario.role,
    ativo: usuario.ativo,
  }

  return (
    <EditPage
      id={id}
      data={defaultValues}
      sections={formSections}
      validation={validationSchema}
      action={action}
      title={`Edit: ${usuario.name || usuario.email}`}
    />
  )
}
```

**Key points:**

1. **Explicit `defaultValues` mapping** — pick the editable fields from the
   entity instead of spreading it; the entity carries fields the form doesn't
   own (`id`, timestamps, computed data).
2. **The action receives `FormData`** — parse it with the same Zod schema the
   form validates with, then call the API client.
3. **Sensitive optional fields** — the blank-password-keeps-current rule is
   handled here (delete the key) and enforced again in the PATCH route.
4. **Return `{ success: true }`** — `EditPage` toasts success/failure from the
   `FormActionResult`; never call `toast` inside the action.

### Create

```tsx title="app/admin/usuarios/adicionar/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { CreatePage, type FormActionResult } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { formSections, validationSchema, type UsuarioFormData } from '../config'
import { usuariosApi } from '@/lib/api/usuarios-client'

export default function AdicionarUsuarioPage() {
  const router = useRouter()

  async function action(formData: FormData): Promise<FormActionResult<UsuarioFormData>> {
    const data = validationSchema.parse(Object.fromEntries(formData.entries()))
    await usuariosApi.create(data)
    router.push('/admin/usuarios')
    return { success: true }
  }

  return (
    <CreatePage
      sections={formSections}
      validation={validationSchema}
      action={action}
      title='New User'
      description='Register a new user in the system'
      defaultValues={{ ativo: true, role: 'USER' }}
    />
  )
}
```

No `id`, no data fetch — just `defaultValues` for the fields that should start
non-empty.

---

## Alternative: Server Component + Server Action

Modules on the Server Actions data layer fetch on the server and pass a
`'use server'` action:

```tsx title="[id]/editar/page.tsx (Server Component)"
import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'
import { EditPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { getUsuario } from '@/services/usuarios'
import { updateUsuarioAction } from '../../actions'
import { formSections, validationSchema } from '../../config'

export default async function Page(props: { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }) {
  const { id } = await props.params
  const usuario = await getUsuario(id)
  if (!usuario) notFound()

  return (
    <EditPage
      id={usuario.id}
      data={usuario}
      sections={formSections}
      action={updateUsuarioAction}
      validation={validationSchema}
      title={`Edit ${usuario.name}`}
    />
  )
}

export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'
```

The Server Action validates again, updates via the service, and revalidates
every affected path:

```ts title="actions.ts"
'use server'

import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
import { z } from 'zod'
import { validationSchema } from './config'
import { updateUsuario } from '@/services/usuarios'

const BASE_PATH = '/admin/usuarios'

// Empty strings break Zod — normalize them to null first
function processFormData(formData: FormData) {
  const processed: Record<string, unknown> = {}
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(Object.fromEntries(formData.entries()))) {
    processed[key] = value === '' ? null : value
  }
  return processed
}

export async function updateUsuarioAction(formData: FormData) {
  const id = formData.get('id') as string // EditPage injects a hidden id field
  if (!id) throw new Error('ID is required for update')

  try {
    const data = validationSchema.parse(processFormData(formData))
    await updateUsuario({ ...data, id })

    revalidatePath(BASE_PATH, 'layout')          // list + all subroutes
    revalidatePath(`${BASE_PATH}/${id}`, 'layout') // detail + subroutes

    return { success: true, message: 'User updated successfully' }
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof z.ZodError) {
      const fields = error.errors.map((e) => `${e.path.join('.')}: ${e.message}`)
      throw new Error('Invalid data: ' + fields.join(', '))
    }
    throw error
  }
}
```

Which variant to use is decided module-wide, not per page: React Query modules
invalidate query keys; Server Action modules call `revalidatePath`.

---

## Rules That Apply to Both Variants

### Validate twice

```tsx
// Client — instant field errors in the form
<EditPage validation={validationSchema} ... />

// Server — the route handler / server action parses again
const parsed = schema.safeParse(body) // never trust the client
```

Client-side validation is UX; server-side validation is security.

### Never spread untrusted input into Prisma

```ts
// ❌ data: { ...body }   — accepts any field the client sends
// ✅ list the fields explicitly, or use a parsed Zod result whose schema
//    only contains the editable fields
```

### Keep the schema shared

One `validationSchema` in `config.tsx`, imported by the form (client) and the
mutation path (action or route schema derived from it). Divergent schemas are
how "the form accepts it but the server rejects it" bugs are born.

---

## Troubleshooting

### "Cannot use 'use client' with async component"

Pick one: full client page (`use(params)` + `useQuery`) or async Server
Component without `'use client'`.

### "id is required for update"

`EditPage` injects the hidden `id` field only when it receives the `id` prop:

```tsx
<EditPage id={entity.id} data={entity} ... />
```

### Form submits but data doesn't refresh

- React Query variant: the mutation didn't invalidate — call
  `queryClient.invalidateQueries` for both `['usuarios']` and
  `['usuarios', id]`, or navigate after `await`ing the update.
- Server Action variant: missing `revalidatePath` for the affected routes.

### "Expected string, received null" (Zod)

Empty inputs arrive as `''` in `FormData`. Either normalize with a
`processFormData` helper (Server Action variant) or make the schema accept the
empty case, as the password field does:

```ts
password: z.string().min(5).optional().or(z.literal(''))
```

### Toast doesn't appear after submit

`EditPage`/`CreatePage` toast the `FormActionResult` themselves. Return
`{ success, message? }` from the action — calling `toast()` inside a Server
Action does nothing.

# Performance

> React and Next.js performance rules for TelamonJS apps — bundle, request waterfalls, re-renders and rendering

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/performance.mdx

A checklist for writing or reviewing a component, form, list page or dashboard. It adapts
[Vercel's React best practices](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/react-best-practices)
to the TelamonJS architecture (React Query + a REST API, `CrudConfig`, Zustand), keeping only the
rules that apply here.

<Callout type='info' title='Correctness first'>
  No rule on this page justifies breaking one of the other patterns. When they disagree, the
  pattern wins.
</Callout>

---

## 1. Bundle (critical)

### Optimize barrels instead of deep imports

`@telamonjs/ui`, `lucide-react` and `@radix-ui/*` are barrels. Import from them normally
and let Next.js rewrite the imports:

```js title="next.config.js"
experimental: {
  optimizePackageImports: ['@telamonjs/ui', 'lucide-react'],
}
```

Don't switch to deep imports (`lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/...`): they lose their types under
`strict`. Apps generated by the CLI already ship this config. It also keeps a single react-query
instance: see [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting#no-queryclient-set).

### Load heavy components lazily

The library ships lazy versions; use them below the fold:

| Heavy | Lazy |
| --- | --- |
| Recharts (`LineChart`, `BarChart`, `PieChart`, `AreaChart`) | `LineChartLazy`, `BarChartLazy`, `PieChartLazy`, `AreaChartLazy` |
| Code editor | `DynamicCodeEditor` |

### Load on use

Content of a rarely opened dialog, tab or panel goes behind an `import()` triggered when it opens,
not at the top of the file. To make it feel instant, start the `import()` on the opening button's
`onMouseEnter`/`onFocus`.

---

## 2. Request waterfalls (critical)

### `Promise.all` for independent awaits

This applies to any `queryFn`/`mutationFn` that makes more than one call:

```ts
// ❌ two round-trips in series
const user = await usersApi.get(id)
const roles = await rolesApi.list()

// ✅ in parallel
const [user, roles] = await Promise.all([usersApi.get(id), rolesApi.list()])
```

### `await` only in the branch that needs it

Don't await a value before an `if` that can return early without it.

### Independent queries don't chain

Two `useQuery` calls without a real dependency run in parallel. Use `enabled: !!x` only when the
second query truly needs the first one's result — an artificial dependency is an invisible
waterfall.

### One boundary per data region

Wrap each data region in its own `DataBoundary` (error boundary + Suspense + empty state) instead
of one boundary for the whole page, so whatever arrives first shows first.

---

## 3. Server/Client boundary (high)

Everything that crosses from a Server Component to a Client Component is serialized into the HTML.
Pass `{ id, name }`, not the whole entity, and never pass the same object twice under different
props.

---

## 4. Re-renders (medium)

- **Derive state during render, not in `useEffect`.**

  ```tsx
  // ❌ an extra render and duplicated state
  const [fullName, setFullName] = useState('')
  useEffect(() => setFullName(`${first} ${last}`), [first, last])

  // ✅
  const fullName = `${first} ${last}`
  ```

- **Never declare a component inside a component.** It remounts on every render, losing focus and
  state. This includes column `cell` renderers and field renderers: define them at module level —
  `config.tsx` is a module, so `columns` declared there are fine.
- **Keep non-primitive values stable.** Prop defaults (`items = []`), `columns`, `sections` and
  option objects live at module level or in `useMemo`; an inline literal passed to a memoized
  component breaks the memo on every render.
- **`useMemo` only for expensive work.** A simple expression with a primitive result
  (`a + b`, `list.length > 0`) doesn't need it.
- **Functional `setState`** — `setCount(c => c + 1)` keeps callbacks stable and avoids stale
  closures.
- **Lazy initial state** — `useState(() => parse(localStorage.getItem(key)))`, not
  `useState(parse(...))`, which runs on every render.
- **Interaction logic belongs in the handler.** What happens "because the user clicked" goes in
  `onClick`, not in a `useEffect` watching state.
- **Non-urgent work:** `useDeferredValue(query)` keeps an input responsive while filtering a large
  local list; `useTransition` replaces a hand-rolled `isLoading` state for actions.
- **Transient values in `useRef`** — scroll or mouse position, timers, the last seen value.
- **Zustand:** never use a dynamic selector inside a custom hook — see
  [Zustand Selector Pattern](/docs/patterns/zustand-selector), which takes precedence over the
  generic "subscribe to derived state" advice.

---

## 5. Rendering (medium)

- **Long lists outside a paginated table** (hundreds of rows or tree nodes):

  ```css
  .row {
    content-visibility: auto;
    contain-intrinsic-size: 0 48px;
  }
  ```

- **Ternary, not `&&`, with numbers.** `{count && <Badge />}` renders `0`; write
  `{count > 0 ? <Badge /> : null}`.
- **Client-only data without a flash.** Theme, density and `localStorage` preferences that change
  the first paint are applied by an inline script in `<head>` before hydration, not in a
  `useEffect` (which flashes). Use `suppressHydrationWarning` only on the node that diverges on
  purpose.

---

## 6. JavaScript (low to medium)

- Repeated lookups in a list (e.g. the option label in every `relationship` cell): build a `Map`
  once instead of a `find` per row.
- Membership tests: `Set.has`, not `array.includes` inside a loop.
- `filter().map()` over a large list: a single `flatMap` or loop.
- Sort without mutating props or state: `toSorted()`.
- Create `RegExp`s outside loops and render.

---

## Generic advice that does not apply

| Generic rule | Why not here | Use instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dedupe requests with SWR | Data goes through React Query | `CrudConfig.query` / `useQuery` |
| Server Actions as the primary data layer | The app talks to a REST API | API client + backend guards |
| `React.cache` / LRU caches on the server | Caching lives in React Query and the backend | `staleTime` / `invalidates` |
| `after()` for non-blocking side effects | Side effects belong to the backend | A background job ([Queue](/docs/queue)) |
| Parallel fetching in Server Components | Data is not fetched in Server Components | Section 2 above |
| Deep imports instead of barrels | They lose types; the barrels are optimizable | Section 1 above |

---

## Related

- [Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup) — one `QueryClient` for the app and the library
- [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting) — two copies of a peer dependency
- [Dashboard Pattern](/docs/patterns/dashboard) — memoized stats, virtualized side lists
- [Zustand Selector Pattern](/docs/patterns/zustand-selector)

# Accessibility & Testing

> Semantic test IDs, aria labels, and loading states across the framework

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/patterns/accessibility.mdx

Accessibility and testing patterns baked into `@telamonjs/ui`:

- **Much faster E2E navigation** — semantic selectors instead of brittle CSS classes
- **Reliable selectors** — predictable `data-testid` across the entire framework
- **WCAG 2.1 AA compliance** for screen readers

---

## Core Principles

### 1. Every interactive element has a test ID

```tsx
// ✅ Good - unique, semantic test ID
<Button data-testid='user-edit-button' onClick={handleEdit}>Edit</Button>

// ❌ Bad - no test ID
<Button onClick={handleEdit}>Edit</Button>
```

### 2. Every button has an aria label

```tsx
// ✅ Good - descriptive aria-label with context
<Button
  data-testid='row-action-edit-123'
  aria-label='Edit user John Doe'
  onClick={handleEdit}
>
  <Pencil />
</Button>

// ❌ Bad - icon-only button without aria-label
<Button onClick={handleEdit}>
  <Pencil />
</Button>
```

### 3. Every form field has accessibility attributes

```tsx
// ✅ Good - complete accessibility attributes
<Input
  data-testid='field-email'
  aria-label='Email Address'
  aria-required={true}
  aria-invalid={hasError}
  aria-describedby='field-email-error'
/>
```

### 4. Loading states use semantic attributes

```tsx
// ✅ Good - Button loading prop (automatic aria-busy)
<Button loading={isSubmitting} data-testid='form-submit-button'>
  Save
</Button>

// ❌ Bad - manual spinner without aria-busy
<Button disabled={isSubmitting}>
  {isSubmitting && <Spinner />}
  Save
</Button>
```

The `loading` prop automatically renders a spinner, adds `data-loading="true"` and `aria-busy="true"`,
and disables the button. When the button is idle both attributes are **absent** (not `"false"`).

---

## Test IDs and aria attributes the components emit

The built-in components generate their `data-testid` and aria attributes internally — there is no
helper to import. These are the values they render, so you can target them in tests and reuse the
same shapes in your custom components. Generated IDs are lowercase, with spaces turned into `-`.

| Area | `data-testid` |
| --- | --- |
| Form buttons | `form-submit-button`, `form-cancel-button`, `form-reset-button` |
| Form fields | `field-{name}` (also the input `id`), `field-{name}-error`, `field-{name}-description` |
| Table | `data-table`, `row-{id}`, `cell-{rowId}-{columnId}` |
| Row actions | `row-action-{action}-{id}` — e.g. `row-action-view-123`, `row-action-edit-123`, `row-action-delete-123`, `row-action-approve-123` |
| Toolbar | `toolbar-add`, `toolbar-refresh`, `toolbar-export`, `toolbar-filters`, `toolbar-columns`, `toolbar-search` |
| Pagination | `pagination-first`, `pagination-previous`, `pagination-next`, `pagination-last`, `pagination-page-{n}`, `pagination-page-size` |
| Detail pages | `detail-field-{name}`, `detail-action-{label}`, `detail-tab-{label}` |
| Modals | `modal`, `modal-close`, `modal-confirm`, `modal-cancel` |

**Pattern:** `{entity}-{action}-{target}-{suffix?}`

### Form fields

Every built-in field renderer emits:

- `data-testid` and `id`: `field-{name}`
- `aria-label`: the field `label`
- `aria-required="true"` when required, `aria-invalid="true"` when the field has an error
  (both absent otherwise)
- `aria-describedby`: `field-{name}-error` and/or `field-{name}-description`, when present

### Action buttons

Row and detail actions emit:

- `data-testid`: `row-action-{id}-{entityId}` when the action belongs to a record, otherwise
  `{id}-button` (e.g. `edit-button`)
- `aria-label`: `{Label} {entity} {identifier?}` — e.g. "Edit user John Doe" — or just the label
  when there is no entity
- `data-loading="true"` and `aria-busy="true"` while loading (absent when idle)

---

## Testing with These Patterns

### Playwright E2E

```typescript
test('Edit user flow', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/admin/users')

  await page.click('[data-testid="row-action-edit-123"]')
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="field-name"]')

  await page.fill('[data-testid="field-name"]', 'John Doe')
  await page.click('[data-testid="form-submit-button"]')

  // Wait for loading to finish — data-loading is removed when idle, never "false"
  await expect(page.getByTestId('form-submit-button')).not.toHaveAttribute('data-loading')
})
```

### Vitest + Testing Library

```typescript
const submitButton = screen.getByTestId('form-submit-button')
await user.click(submitButton)

await waitFor(() => {
  expect(submitButton).toHaveAttribute('data-loading', 'true')
  expect(submitButton).toHaveAttribute('aria-busy', 'true')
  expect(submitButton).toBeDisabled()
})
```

### Query priority

```typescript
// ✅ Preferred - test IDs (most reliable)
screen.getByTestId('user-edit-button')

// ✅ Good - aria-label for accessibility validation
screen.getByLabelText('Edit user John Doe')

// ⚠️ Avoid - CSS selectors (brittle) and text content (breaks with translations)
```

---

## Naming Conventions

### Test IDs — `{entity}-{action}-{target}-{suffix?}`

- kebab-case, specific, descriptive, with context (entity name, ID)
- ✅ `user-edit-button`, `field-email`, `row-action-delete-123`, `pagination-next`
- ❌ `btn1`, `EditButton`, `user_edit`

### Aria labels — `{Action} {entity} {identifier?}`

- Natural language, with context, meaningful for screen readers
- ✅ "Edit user John Doe", "Delete asset ABC-1234", "Next page"
- ❌ "Edit", "Button", "Click here"

---

## Lint Rules

The framework's own lint enforces two of these rules on its source. They are not part of the
published package, so treat them as review rules for your custom components:

- **Buttons** need a `data-testid` or an `aria-label` (an icon-only button always needs the label).
- **Inputs** without an associated `<label htmlFor>` need an `aria-label`.

---

## Coverage Checklist

**Forms:** submit/cancel buttons with test IDs and `loading`; all fields with `field-{name}` test IDs, `aria-label`, `aria-required`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby` for errors.

**DataTable:** row actions with `row-action-{action}-{id}` test IDs and contextual aria labels; toolbar buttons with `toolbar-*` test IDs.

**Pagination:** semantic test IDs on all controls; active page with `aria-current="page"`.

**Detail pages:** actions/fields/tabs with `detail-action-*`, `detail-field-*` and `detail-tab-*` test IDs.

**Loading states:** `loading` prop everywhere (never manual spinners) → `data-loading` + `aria-busy` + disabled.

Everything above is applied automatically by the built-in components — follow the same patterns in your **custom** actions, fields, and renderers.

Finally, check the result with a real screen reader (VoiceOver on macOS, NVDA on Windows):
navigate forms with the keyboard only, and confirm every button is announced with its context and
every validation error is read out.

---

- [ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)

# Components

> Every component of @telamonjs/ui, grouped as in the sidebar

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/index.mdx

Every component is exported by `@telamonjs/ui`; each page lists its props and
examples. A CRUD module rarely touches most of them directly: `ListPage` renders the
list, the dialogs and the forms from a [`CrudConfig`](/docs/getting-started/crud-config),
and [Module structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) shows a complete module.
Not sure which one fits? See the [decision trees](/docs/reference).

## Shell & Layout

| Component | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [AdminShell](/docs/components/admin-shell) | The app shell: sidebar, Cmd+K command palette and breadcrumb |
| [AppShell](/docs/components/app-shell) | Lower-level layout primitive; use `AdminShell` unless it cannot express your shell |
| [ModernSidebar](/docs/components/modern-sidebar) | Hierarchical sidebar with string icons, composed by `AdminShell` |
| [CommandPalette](/docs/components/command-palette) | Keyboard-driven palette (Cmd+K) for navigation and actions |
| [Breadcrumb](/docs/components/breadcrumbs) | Breadcrumb primitives and the route-aware breadcrumb of the shell |
| [Tabs](/docs/components/tabs) | Tab navigation between related views |
| [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page) | Full-height page container with fullscreen support |
| [AdminHeader](/docs/components/admin-header) | Page header bar: title, icon, description, status, fullscreen toggle |
| [AdminTabs](/docs/components/admin-tabs) | `ContentTabs` that fill the height of a shell page |
| [TabToolbar](/docs/components/tab-toolbar) | Filters, search and actions inside a tab panel |

## CRUD & Data

| Component | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [ListPage](/docs/components/list-page) | The list of a module, rendered from its `CrudConfig`, with its dialogs |
| [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) | Table with sorting, filtering, pagination and row selection |
| [ReportTable](/docs/components/report-table) | Read-only report table with "load more" pagination |
| [MobileCard](/docs/components/mobile-card) | Card rendering of table rows on small screens |
| [QueryErrorState](/docs/components/query-error-state) | Error state of your own `useQuery`, with a pending "Try again" |

## Standalone Pages

Create, edit and view happen in dialogs by default. These pages are for forms that
outgrow a dialog; see [Standalone form pages](/docs/patterns/edit-page).

# AdminShell

> Canonical app shell — ModernSidebar + Cmd+K CommandPalette + ResponsiveBreadcrumb

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/admin-shell.mdx

`AdminShell` is the canonical shell for TelamonJS applications. It composes
`ModernSidebar` + `CommandPalette` (Cmd+K) + `ResponsiveBreadcrumb` + header actions into a
single client component.

---

## Basic Usage

Fetch the session on the server, pass it down to a small `'use client'` wrapper that renders
`AdminShell`. Menu icons are passed as **strings**, resolved internally via `getIcon` — never
```tsx title="src/components/providers/LayoutProviders.tsx"
'use client'
import { AdminShell, Toaster } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { menuConfig } from '@/config/menu'

export function LayoutProviders({ children, session }) {
  const router = useRouter()
  return (
    <>
      <AdminShell
        menuConfig={menuConfig}
        session={session ?? undefined}
        systemName='My App'
        logoUrl='/logo.png'
        onSignOut={() => router.push('/sign-out')}
      >
        {children}
      </AdminShell>
      <Toaster />
    </>
  )
}
```
```tsx title="app/admin/layout.tsx"
import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
import { LayoutProviders } from '@/components/providers/LayoutProviders'

export default async function AdminLayout({ children }) {
  const session = await auth()
  return <LayoutProviders session={session}>{children}</LayoutProviders>
}
```
```tsx title="src/config/menu.ts"
import type { MenuItem } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export const menuConfig: MenuItem[] = [
  { id: 'dashboard', type: 'single', title: 'Dashboard', href: '/admin', icon: 'LayoutDashboard' },
  {
    id: 'admin-group',
    type: 'group',
    title: 'Administration',
    icon: 'Settings',
    children: [
      { id: 'users', type: 'single', title: 'Users', href: '/admin/users', icon: 'Users' },
    ],
  },
]
```
```tsx
// src/config/menu.ts
{ id: 'users', type: 'single', title: 'Users', href: '/admin/users', permission: 'users.read' }

// LayoutProviders.tsx, with @telamonjs/permissions
<AdminShell menuConfig={menuConfig} can={perm => checker.can(session.user, perm)}>
```
```typescript
interface AdminShellProps {
  children: React.ReactNode
  menuConfig: MenuItem[]
  can?: (permission: string) => boolean
  session?: ModernSidebarProps['session']
  systemName?: string
  logoUrl?: string
  compactLogoUrl?: string
  logoHeight?: number | string
  logoMaxWidth?: number | string
  compactLogoHeight?: number | string
  compactLogoMaxWidth?: number | string
  onSignOut?: () => void
  onStopImpersonation?: () => Promise<void>
  showImpersonationBanner?: boolean // default false
  localeSwitcher?: boolean // default true
  profileHref?: string
  headerActions?: React.ReactNode
  themeToggle?: boolean // default false
  commandActions?: CommandPaletteItem[]
  breadcrumbProps?: AdminShellBreadcrumbProps
  className?: string
  contentClassName?: string
}
```
```tsx
'use client'
import { ShellPage, AdminHeader, AdminTabs, useTabUrlSync, type TabItem } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const TAB_VALUES = ['overview', 'details'] as const

const tabs: TabItem[] = [
  { value: 'overview', label: 'Overview', content: <OverviewTab /> },
  { value: 'details', label: 'Details', content: <DetailsTab /> },
]

export default function DashboardPage() {
  const { activeTab, setTab } = useTabUrlSync({ tabs: TAB_VALUES })
  return (
    <ShellPage>
      <AdminHeader title='Dashboard' />
      <AdminTabs tabs={tabs} value={activeTab} onValueChange={setTab} />
    </ShellPage>
  )
}
```

---

# AppShell

> Flexible application layout with multiple variants

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/app-shell.mdx

Flexible application layout component supporting multiple layout variants for different use cases.

<Callout type='info' title='Lower level; use AdminShell'>
  `AppShell` is a lower-level layout primitive. For an app shell, use
  [`AdminShell`](/docs/components/admin-shell), which ships the sidebar, Cmd+K and breadcrumb.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { AppShell, ModernSidebar } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function Layout({ children }) {
  return (
    <AppShell topbar={<Topbar />} sidebar={<ModernSidebar menuConfig={menuConfig} />}>
      {children}
    </AppShell>
  )
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface AppShellProps {
  children: React.ReactNode // Main content, rendered inside <main> (required)
  sidebar?: React.ReactNode // Desktop sidebar (hidden below lg, and with variant 'topnav')
  topbar?: React.ReactNode // Top bar, rendered inside a sticky <header>
  bottomNav?: React.ReactNode // Mobile bottom navigation (hidden from lg up)
  variant?: 'sidebar' | 'topnav' | 'hybrid' // default: 'sidebar'
  className?: string // Additional classes on the root element
}
```

The sidebar column width follows the shared sidebar state that `ModernSidebar` drives:
`w-64` expanded, `w-16` compact, collapsed to zero when hidden.

---

## Examples

### Sidebar Layout (default)

```tsx
<AppShell
  variant='sidebar'
  topbar={
    <div className='p-4'>
      <h1>My App</h1>
    </div>
  }
  sidebar={
    <nav className='p-4'>
      <ul>
        <li>
          <a href='/dashboard'>Dashboard</a>
        </li>
        <li>
          <a href='/users'>Users</a>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  }
>
  <div className='p-6'>{children}</div>
</AppShell>
```

Layout: `[Topbar] + [Sidebar | Content]`

### Top Navigation Layout

```tsx
<AppShell variant='topnav' topbar={<Topbar />}>
  <div className='container mx-auto p-6'>{children}</div>
</AppShell>
```

Layout: `[Topbar] + [Content]` — `sidebar` is ignored with `variant='topnav'`.

### Hybrid Layout with Bottom Navigation

```tsx
<AppShell
  variant='hybrid'
  topbar={<Topbar />}
  sidebar={<ModernSidebar menuConfig={menuConfig} />}
  bottomNav={<MobileBottomNav />}
>
  <div className='p-6'>{children}</div>
</AppShell>
```

Layout: `[Topbar] + [Sidebar | Content]` on desktop, `[Topbar] + [Content] + [Bottom nav]` on mobile.

### Without Topbar

```tsx
<AppShell sidebar={<ModernSidebar menuConfig={menuConfig} />}>{children}</AppShell>
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
'use client'

import { AppShell } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Home, Users, Settings } from 'lucide-react'
import Link from 'next/link'

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <AppShell
      variant='sidebar'
      topbar={
        <div className='flex items-center justify-between px-6 py-4'>
          <h1 className='text-xl font-bold'>Dashboard</h1>
          <button className='px-4 py-2 bg-blue-600 text-white rounded hover:bg-blue-700'>
            New Item
          </button>
        </div>
      }
      sidebar={
        <nav className='flex flex-col gap-2 p-4 bg-gray-50'>
          <Link
            href='/dashboard'
            className='flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-2 rounded hover:bg-gray-200'
          >
            <Home size={20} />
            <span>Dashboard</span>
          </Link>
          <Link
            href='/users'
            className='flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-2 rounded hover:bg-gray-200'
          >
            <Users size={20} />
            <span>Users</span>
          </Link>
          <Link
            href='/settings'
            className='flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-2 rounded hover:bg-gray-200'
          >
            <Settings size={20} />
            <span>Settings</span>
          </Link>
        </nav>
      }
    >
      <div className='p-6'>{children}</div>
    </AppShell>
  )
}
```

---

## Layout Variants Comparison

| Variant   | Topbar               | Sidebar (desktop) | Use Case                       |
| --------- | -------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `sidebar` | When `topbar` is set | ✅                | Standard app layout            |
| `topnav`  | When `topbar` is set | ❌                | Marketing pages, simple apps   |
| `hybrid`  | When `topbar` is set | ✅                | Sidebar plus top navigation    |

`bottomNav` renders below `lg` with any variant.

---

## Use Cases

- **Custom applications** - Need layout without AdminShell complexity
- **Marketing sites** - Landing pages with a top bar (`variant='topnav'`)
- **Documentation sites** - Sidebar navigation
- **Mobile-first apps** - Bottom navigation on small screens
- **Dashboards** - Custom dashboard layouts

---

## Responsive Behavior

**Desktop (≥1024px, `lg`):**

- Sidebar column visible (unless `variant='topnav'`), width from the sidebar state
- `bottomNav` hidden

**Below 1024px:**

- Sidebar column hidden
- `bottomNav` fixed to the bottom of the viewport; `<main>` gets bottom padding to clear it

---

## Best Practices

1. **Choose right variant** - Match layout to content type
2. **Consistent topbar** - Keep the topbar across all pages
3. **Mobile navigation** - Pass `bottomNav` (or a sidebar with its own mobile drawer, like `ModernSidebar`), since the sidebar column is hidden below `lg`
4. **Accessibility** - Use semantic HTML inside the slots

---

## Comparison: AppShell vs AdminShell

| Feature          | AppShell                | AdminShell                             |
| ---------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| **Complexity**   | Low (bring your own UI) | High (opinionated, batteries included) |
| **Menu system**  | Custom                  | Built-in hierarchical menu             |
| **Breadcrumbs**  | Custom                  | Auto-generated                         |
| **User menu**    | Custom                  | Built-in with avatar                   |
| **Cmd+K**        | Custom                  | Built-in `CommandPalette`              |
| **Use when**     | Need flexibility        | Need complete admin solution           |

**Decision tree:**

- ✅ **Use AppShell** - Custom layouts, non-admin apps, marketing sites
- ✅ **Use AdminShell** - Admin panels, dashboards, internal tools

---

## Accessibility

- Slots render inside semantic landmarks: `topbar` in `<header>`, `sidebar` in `<aside>`,
  `children` in `<main>`, `bottomNav` in `<nav>` — don't wrap `children` in another `<main>`
- Skip to main content link (recommended)

---

## Sticky Header Pattern

The topbar is already rendered inside a sticky, blurred `<header>` — pass only its content:

```tsx
<AppShell
  topbar={
    <div className='flex items-center justify-between px-6 py-4'>
      <h1>My App</h1>
      <nav>{/* Navigation */}</nav>
    </div>
  }
>
  {children}
</AppShell>
```

---

## Related Components

- [AdminShell](/docs/components/admin-shell) - Canonical app shell (sidebar + Cmd+K + breadcrumb)
- [ModernSidebar](/docs/components/modern-sidebar) - Standalone sidebar

---

## See Also

- Layout Patterns - Layout design patterns
- Responsive Design - Mobile-first approach

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

---

# ModernSidebar

> Modern hierarchical sidebar — compact/expanded, mobile drawer, string-based icons

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/modern-sidebar.mdx

`ModernSidebar` is the sidebar composed internally by [`AdminShell`](/docs/components/admin-shell).
Use it standalone only when you need a custom shell composition — for the canonical app shell,
use `AdminShell` instead.

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { ModernSidebar } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { menuConfig } from '@/config/menu'

;<ModernSidebar
  menuConfig={menuConfig}
  session={session}
  systemName='My App'
  onSignOut={() => router.push('/sign-out')}
/>
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface ModernSidebarProps {
  menuConfig?: MenuItem[] // default: []
  session?: {
    user?: { name?: string; email?: string; role?: { name?: string } }
    isImpersonating?: boolean
    originalUser?: { name?: string }
  }
  systemName?: string
  logoUrl?: string // default: '/logo.png'
  compactLogoUrl?: string
  logoClassName?: string
  logoStyle?: React.CSSProperties
  logoHeight?: number | string
  logoMaxWidth?: number | string
  compactLogoHeight?: number | string // falls back to logoHeight
  compactLogoMaxWidth?: number | string // falls back to logoMaxWidth
  onSignOut?: () => void
  onStopImpersonation?: () => Promise<void>
  mobileTriggerPosition?: 'top-left' | 'bottom-right' // default: 'top-left'
  showUserAvatar?: boolean // default: true
  showUserRole?: boolean // default: true
  footerContent?: React.ReactNode // rendered below the user info
  localeSwitcher?: boolean // default: true
  profileHref?: string // enables the user menu "Profile" item
  className?: string
}
```

---

## Features

- Compact (icon-only) / expanded modes with a mobile drawer fallback
- Hierarchical menu (`type: 'single' | 'group' | 'separator'`)
- Icons resolved by **string** via `getIcon`/`setIconResolver` — no `LucideIcon` cast needed
- Avatar, role display, and a "back to original user" item while impersonating

---

## See Also

- [AdminShell](/docs/components/admin-shell) - Canonical shell composing this sidebar
- [Provider Setup Pattern](/docs/patterns/provider-setup) - Icon resolver setup
- [CommandPalette](/docs/components/command-palette) - Cmd+K, composed inside `AdminShell`

---

# CommandPalette

> Keyboard-driven command palette (Cmd+K) for quick navigation and actions

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/command-palette.mdx

Keyboard-driven command palette (Cmd+K) for quick navigation, search, and actions inspired by VS Code and Linear. Built on [cmdk](https://cmdk.paco.me/).

<Callout type='success' title='Power User Tool'>
  `CommandPalette` dramatically improves navigation speed - users can access any
  page or action with just a few keystrokes. It is part of the canonical app
  shell (see [AdminShell](/docs/components/admin-shell)).
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
'use client'

import { CommandPalette, type CommandPaletteItem } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Home, Users } from 'lucide-react'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function AppCommandPalette() {
  const router = useRouter()

  const items: CommandPaletteItem[] = [
    {
      id: 'dashboard',
      label: 'Go to Dashboard',
      type: 'navigation',
      icon: Home,
      href: '/admin',
      keywords: ['home', 'overview'],
    },
    {
      id: 'users',
      label: 'Go to Users',
      type: 'navigation',
      icon: Users,
      href: '/admin/users',
      keywords: ['people', 'accounts'],
    },
  ]

  return (
    <CommandPalette
      items={items}
      onSelect={item => item.href && router.push(item.href)}
    />
  )
}
```

Press `Cmd+K` (Mac) or `Ctrl+K` (Windows/Linux) to open (enabled by default).

<Callout type='warn' title='The prop is `items`, and navigation is yours'>
  `CommandPalette` uses `items: CommandPaletteItem[]`: grouping comes from the item's `type`, the
  per-item callback is `onSelect`, and `href` is data — wire navigation in the component-level
  `onSelect` (e.g. `router.push`). There is no built-in recent-commands storage; feed
  `type: 'recent'` items yourself if you want that group.
</Callout>

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    items: { description: 'Command items — grouped in the UI by their type', type: 'CommandPaletteItem[]', required: true },
    onSelect: { description: 'Called with the selected item (after the item’s own onSelect). The palette closes automatically', type: '(item: CommandPaletteItem) => void' },
    placeholder: { description: 'Search input placeholder (localized default from the shell.searchPlaceholder message)', type: 'I18nText', default: "t('shell.searchPlaceholder')" },
    open: { description: 'Controlled open state (pair with onOpenChange)', type: 'boolean' },
    onOpenChange: { description: 'Called when the open state changes', type: '(open: boolean) => void' },
    enableShortcut: { description: 'Register the global Cmd/Ctrl + shortcutKey listener', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    shortcutKey: { description: 'Key combined with Cmd/Ctrl to toggle', type: 'string', default: "'k'" },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

### CommandPaletteItem

<TypeTable
  type={{
    id: { description: 'Unique item ID', type: 'string', required: true },
    label: { description: 'Display label — a literal or msg()', type: 'I18nText', required: true },
    type: {
      description: 'Group the item renders under — localized headings (Navigation, Actions, Search, Recent in en)',
      type: "'navigation' | 'action' | 'search' | 'recent'",
      required: true,
    },
    icon: { description: 'Icon component reference (e.g. lucide icon)', type: 'IconComponent' },
    shortcut: { description: 'Keyboard shortcut display text (e.g. "⌘N") — display only, not registered', type: 'string' },
    keywords: { description: 'Extra terms for search matching', type: 'string[]' },
    onSelect: { description: 'Action executed when this item is selected', type: '() => void' },
    href: { description: 'Navigation URL — data only, consumed by your component-level onSelect', type: 'string' },
    disabled: { description: 'Leaves the item out of the palette', type: 'boolean' },
  }}
/>

---

## Examples

### With Actions

```tsx
import { Plus, Download } from 'lucide-react'

const items: CommandPaletteItem[] = [
  {
    id: 'new-user',
    label: 'Create New User',
    type: 'action',
    icon: Plus,
    shortcut: '⌘N',
    onSelect: () => openCreateUserDialog(),
  },
  {
    id: 'export',
    label: 'Export Data',
    type: 'action',
    icon: Download,
    onSelect: () => openExportDialog(),
  },
]

<CommandPalette items={items} />
```

### Controlled

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import {
  CommandPalette,
  Button,
  type CommandPaletteItem,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function Toolbar({ items }: { items: CommandPaletteItem[] }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)

  return (
    <>
      <Button variant='outline' onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Search... <kbd className='ml-2 text-xs'>⌘K</kbd>
      </Button>

      <CommandPalette
        items={items}
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
      />
    </>
  )
}
```

### Custom Shortcut

```tsx
<CommandPalette items={items} shortcutKey='p' />  {/* Cmd/Ctrl+P */}
<CommandPalette items={items} enableShortcut={false} />  {/* controlled only */}
```

The shortcut always combines `shortcutKey` with Cmd/Ctrl — a bare `/` trigger
is not supported.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/app-command-palette.tsx"
'use client'

import { CommandPalette, type CommandPaletteItem } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Home, Users, Package, Plus, Moon, Sun } from 'lucide-react'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { useTheme } from 'next-themes'

export default function AppCommandPalette() {
  const router = useRouter()
  const { setTheme } = useTheme()

  const items: CommandPaletteItem[] = [
    // Navigation group
    { id: 'nav-dashboard', label: 'Go to Dashboard', type: 'navigation', icon: Home, href: '/admin', keywords: ['home'] },
    { id: 'nav-users', label: 'Go to Users', type: 'navigation', icon: Users, href: '/admin/users', keywords: ['people', 'accounts'] },
    { id: 'nav-products', label: 'Go to Products', type: 'navigation', icon: Package, href: '/admin/products' },

    // Actions group
    { id: 'action-new-user', label: 'Create New User', type: 'action', icon: Plus, shortcut: '⌘N', href: '/admin/users/new' },
    { id: 'theme-light', label: 'Switch to Light Theme', type: 'action', icon: Sun, onSelect: () => setTheme('light') },
    { id: 'theme-dark', label: 'Switch to Dark Theme', type: 'action', icon: Moon, onSelect: () => setTheme('dark') },
  ]

  return (
    <CommandPalette
      items={items}
      placeholder='Type a command or search...'
      onSelect={item => item.href && router.push(item.href)}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Search & Filtering

Filtering comes from cmdk (accent-insensitive) — type to filter across labels, with `keywords`
adding extra matchable terms per item:

```tsx
{
  label: 'Go to Users',
  keywords: ['people', 'accounts', 'customers'],
  // Also matches: "people", "accounts", "customers"
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Quick navigation** - Jump to any page instantly
- **Actions** - Execute common operations
- **Settings** - Toggle themes, preferences
- **Admin tools** - Debug, clear cache, etc.

---

## Best Practices

1. **Add all pages** - Every major page should have a `navigation` item
2. **Use keywords** - Add search aliases for better discovery
3. **Group by type** - `navigation` / `action` / `search` / `recent` drive the section headings
4. **Clear labels** - Use action-oriented labels ("Go to...", "Create...")
5. **Add icons** - Improve visual scanning
6. **Limit items** - 50-100 max; filtering is client-side and instant

---

## Keyboard Shortcuts

- `Cmd+K` / `Ctrl+K` - Toggle palette (configurable via `shortcutKey`)
- `↓` / `↑` - Move selection
- `Enter` - Execute selected item
- `Esc` - Close palette

---

## Accessibility

- Keyboard-only operation (cmdk + Radix Dialog)
- Focus trapped in the dialog while open
- `shortcut` text renders as a `<kbd>` hint next to the item

---

## Related Components

- [AdminShell](/docs/components/admin-shell) - Canonical shell (palette included)
- [ModernSidebar](/docs/components/modern-sidebar) - Primary navigation

# Breadcrumb

> Breadcrumb primitives, plus the route-aware breadcrumbs used by the admin shell

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/breadcrumbs.mdx

The library ships two layers of breadcrumbs:

- **Primitives** — `Breadcrumb`, `BreadcrumbList`, `BreadcrumbItem`, `BreadcrumbLink`,
  `BreadcrumbPage`, `BreadcrumbSeparator`, `BreadcrumbEllipsis` (root entry). Plain styled
  elements: you decide every item.
- **Route-aware** — `ResponsiveBreadcrumb` (root entry) builds the trail from the current
  pathname. [AdminShell](/docs/components/admin-shell) already renders
  `ResponsiveBreadcrumb` in its header, so most apps never mount one themselves.

---

## Primitives

```tsx
import Link from 'next/link'
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function UserBreadcrumb({ name }: { name: string }) {
  return (
    <Breadcrumb>
      <BreadcrumbList>
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink asChild>
            <Link href='/admin'>Home</Link>
          </BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbLink asChild>
            <Link href='/admin/users'>Users</Link>
          </BreadcrumbLink>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
        <BreadcrumbSeparator />
        <BreadcrumbItem>
          <BreadcrumbPage>{name}</BreadcrumbPage>
        </BreadcrumbItem>
      </BreadcrumbList>
    </Breadcrumb>
  )
}
```

| Part | Renders | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Breadcrumb` | `<nav aria-label="breadcrumb">` | Accepts every `nav` prop |
| `BreadcrumbList` | `<ol>` | Flex row, wraps on small screens |
| `BreadcrumbItem` | `<li>` | |
| `BreadcrumbLink` | `<a>` | `asChild` renders your own element (e.g. Next.js `Link`) |
| `BreadcrumbPage` | `<span aria-current="page">` | The current page, not a link |
| `BreadcrumbSeparator` | `<li aria-hidden>` | Chevron by default; pass `children` for a custom separator |
| `BreadcrumbEllipsis` | `<span aria-hidden>` | "More" icon for collapsed items, with an sr-only label |

There is no `items` array prop: compose the parts. To collapse a long trail, render
`BreadcrumbEllipsis` (optionally as a [DropdownMenu](/docs/components/dropdown-menu) trigger)
in place of the middle items.

---

## Route-aware breadcrumbs: ResponsiveBreadcrumb

Builds segments from the pathname and the menu tree: menu routes get their menu label and icon,
record ids become entity segments, and `create`/`edit`/`view` segments become action segments.
Desktop shows up to five items (middle items collapse into a dropdown); mobile shows a home icon
and the last segment.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `menuConfig` | `MenuItem[]` | `[]` | Menu tree used to label segments |
| `customSegments` | `BreadcrumbCustomSegments` | `{}` | Overrides keyed by full path (`/admin/settings`) or by segment (`settings`): a label, or `{ label, href }` to link a segment that is not a menu route |
| `showActions` | `boolean` | `true` | Shows a "creating/editing/viewing" badge on create/edit/view pages |
| `className` | `string` | — | Classes on the `nav` |

Inside `AdminShell`, pass overrides through `breadcrumbProps`:

```tsx
<AdminShell
  menuConfig={menu}
  breadcrumbProps={{ customSegments: { '/admin/settings': { label: 'Settings', href: '/admin/settings' } } }}
>
  {children}
</AdminShell>
```

---

## Accessibility

- The primitives render a labelled `nav` with an ordered list; the current page carries
  `aria-current="page"`.
- Separators and the ellipsis are `aria-hidden`, so screen readers announce only the items.

---

## Related

- [AdminShell](/docs/components/admin-shell) — renders the route-aware breadcrumb in its header
- [ModernSidebar](/docs/components/modern-sidebar) - Primary navigation
- [Tabs](/docs/components/tabs) — in-page navigation

# Tabs

> Tab navigation component for switching between related views

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/tabs.mdx

Tab navigation component for organizing and switching between related content views or sections.

<Callout type='info' title='Content Organization'>
  `Tabs` help organize related information without cluttering the interface or
  requiring page navigation.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import {
  Tabs,
  TabsList,
  TabsTrigger,
  TabsContent,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function SettingsPage() {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue='profile'>
      <TabsList>
        <TabsTrigger value='profile'>Profile</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value='account'>Account</TabsTrigger>
        <TabsTrigger value='security'>Security</TabsTrigger>
      </TabsList>

      <TabsContent value='profile'>{/* Profile settings */}</TabsContent>

      <TabsContent value='account'>{/* Account settings */}</TabsContent>

      <TabsContent value='security'>{/* Security settings */}</TabsContent>
    </Tabs>
  )
}
```

---

## Props

`Tabs`, `TabsList`, `TabsTrigger` and `TabsContent` are styled [Radix Tabs](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/tabs)
parts and accept the Radix props. The ones you use most:

```typescript
// Tabs (Radix Tabs.Root)
{
  defaultValue?: string // Initial active tab
  value?: string // Controlled active tab
  onValueChange?: (value: string) => void // Tab change callback
  orientation?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' // Arrow-key direction (default 'horizontal')
  activationMode?: 'automatic' | 'manual' // default 'automatic'
  className?: string
  children: React.ReactNode
}

// TabsTrigger (Radix Tabs.Trigger)
{
  value: string // Tab identifier (required)
  disabled?: boolean // Disable tab
  className?: string
  children: React.ReactNode // Tab label — put icons and badges here
}

// TabsContent (Radix Tabs.Content)
{
  value: string // Tab identifier (required)
  forceMount?: true // Keep mounted while inactive
  className?: string
  children: React.ReactNode
}
```

`TabsTrigger` has no `icon` or `badge` prop. For a data-driven tab bar with icons and badges,
use [`ContentTabs`](/docs/components/admin-tabs) (`TabItem.icon` / `TabItem.badge`).

---

## Examples

### Basic Tabs

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue='overview'>
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value='overview'>Overview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='analytics'>Analytics</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='reports'>Reports</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>

  <TabsContent value='overview'>Overview content</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value='analytics'>Analytics content</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value='reports'>Reports content</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

### With Icons

```tsx
import { User, Settings, Bell, Shield } from 'lucide-react'
;<Tabs defaultValue='profile'>
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value='profile' className='gap-2'>
      <User className='h-4 w-4' /> Profile
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='settings' className='gap-2'>
      <Settings className='h-4 w-4' /> Settings
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='notifications' className='gap-2'>
      <Bell className='h-4 w-4' /> Notifications
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='security' className='gap-2'>
      <Shield className='h-4 w-4' /> Security
    </TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>

  {/* Content */}
</Tabs>
```

### With Badges

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@telamonjs/ui'
;<Tabs defaultValue='all'>
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value='all'>All Orders</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='pending' className='gap-2'>
      Pending <Badge variant='secondary'>12</Badge>
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='processing' className='gap-2'>
      Processing <Badge variant='secondary'>5</Badge>
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='completed' className='gap-2'>
      Completed <Badge variant='secondary'>150</Badge>
    </TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>

  {/* Content */}
</Tabs>
```

### Controlled Tabs

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'

export default function ControlledTabs() {
  const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState('tab1')

  return (
    <>
      <Button onClick={() => setActiveTab('tab2')}>Jump to Tab 2</Button>

      <Tabs value={activeTab} onValueChange={setActiveTab}>
        <TabsList>
          <TabsTrigger value='tab1'>Tab 1</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value='tab2'>Tab 2</TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value='tab3'>Tab 3</TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>

        <TabsContent value='tab1'>Content 1</TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value='tab2'>Content 2</TabsContent>
        <TabsContent value='tab3'>Content 3</TabsContent>
      </Tabs>
    </>
  )
}
```

### Vertical Tabs

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue='general' orientation='vertical' className='flex gap-4'>
  <TabsList className='h-auto flex-col items-stretch'>
    <TabsTrigger value='general'>General</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='appearance'>Appearance</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='notifications'>Notifications</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='privacy'>Privacy</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>

  <TabsContent value='general'>{/* Content */}</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value='appearance'>{/* Content */}</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value='notifications'>{/* Content */}</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value='privacy'>{/* Content */}</TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

Layout: Tabs on left, content on right. `orientation` only switches arrow-key navigation to
up/down — the column layout comes from the classes.

### Disabled Tabs

```tsx
<Tabs defaultValue='tab1'>
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value='tab1'>Available</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='tab2' disabled>
      Coming Soon
    </TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value='tab3' disabled>
      Premium Only
    </TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>

  {/* Content */}
</Tabs>
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { use } from 'react'
import {
  Tabs,
  TabsList,
  TabsTrigger,
  TabsContent,
  Badge,
  DetailCard,
  DetailField,
  DataTable,
  Timeline,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { User, ShoppingCart, Activity, Settings } from 'lucide-react'
import { getUser, getUserOrders, getUserActivity } from './service'

export default function UserDetailPage({
  params,
}: {
  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
}) {
  const { id } = use(params)
  const user = use(getUser(id))
  const orders = use(getUserOrders(id))
  const activity = use(getUserActivity(id))

  return (
    <div className='container py-6'>
      <h1 className='text-3xl font-bold mb-6'>{user.name}</h1>

      <Tabs defaultValue='profile'>
        <TabsList>
          <TabsTrigger value='profile' className='gap-2'>
            <User className='h-4 w-4' /> Profile
          </TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value='orders' className='gap-2'>
            <ShoppingCart className='h-4 w-4' /> Orders
            <Badge variant='secondary'>{orders.length}</Badge>
          </TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value='activity' className='gap-2'>
            <Activity className='h-4 w-4' /> Activity
          </TabsTrigger>
          <TabsTrigger value='settings' className='gap-2'>
            <Settings className='h-4 w-4' /> Settings
          </TabsTrigger>
        </TabsList>

        <TabsContent value='profile'>
          <div className='mt-6 space-y-6'>
            <DetailCard title='Personal Information'>
              <DetailField label='Name' value={user.name} />
              <DetailField label='Email' value={user.email} />
              <DetailField label='Phone' value={user.phone} />
            </DetailCard>

            <DetailCard title='Address'>
              <DetailField label='Street' value={user.address.street} />
              <DetailField label='City' value={user.address.city} />
            </DetailCard>
          </div>
        </TabsContent>

        <TabsContent value='orders'>
          <div className='mt-6'>
            <DataTable columns={orderColumns} data={orders} />
          </div>
        </TabsContent>

        <TabsContent value='activity'>
          <div className='mt-6'>
            <Timeline items={activity} />
          </div>
        </TabsContent>

        <TabsContent value='settings'>
          <div className='mt-6 space-y-6'>{/* Settings forms */}</div>
        </TabsContent>
      </Tabs>
    </div>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Settings pages** - Organize settings by category
- **User profiles** - Separate profile, orders, activity
- **Product details** - Overview, specifications, reviews
- **Dashboard views** - Different data perspectives
- **Form sections** - Multi-section forms (alternative to wizard)
- **Data tables** - Filter/categorize data

---

## URL Sync (Optional)

**Sync active tab with URL:**

```tsx
'use client'

import { useSearchParams, useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function URLSyncedTabs() {
  const router = useRouter()
  const searchParams = useSearchParams()
  const tab = searchParams.get('tab') || 'overview'

  function handleTabChange(value: string) {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams)
    params.set('tab', value)
    router.push(`?${params.toString()}`)
  }

  return (
    <Tabs value={tab} onValueChange={handleTabChange}>
      {/* Tabs */}
    </Tabs>
  )
}
```

Now tabs persist through page reloads and can be bookmarked/shared. `useTabUrlSync` from
`@telamonjs/ui` packages this pattern: `const { activeTab, setTab } = useTabUrlSync({ tabs: ['overview', 'reports'] })`.

---

## Best Practices

1. **Limit tabs** - 3-7 tabs optimal (use dropdown for more)
2. **Short labels** - 1-2 words per tab
3. **Related content** - Only group related content
4. **Default tab** - Choose most important/common tab
5. **Persist state** - Remember active tab (localStorage or URL)
6. **Lazy load** - Load content when tab activated
7. **Responsive** - Stack or scroll on mobile

---

## Accessibility

- ✅ Keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow keys, Home, End) — from Radix Tabs
- ✅ ARIA roles (`tablist`, `tab`, `tabpanel`)
- ✅ `aria-selected` and `aria-controls`
- ✅ Focus management
- ✅ Screen reader announcements
- ✅ Disabled state properly communicated

**Keyboard shortcuts:**

- `Tab` - Move focus into the tab list (active trigger), then into the panel
- `Arrow Left/Right` - Navigate between tabs (`Up/Down` with `orientation='vertical'`)
- `Home/End` - First/last tab
- `Enter/Space` - Activate focused tab (with `activationMode='manual'`; otherwise focus activates)

---

## Performance

**Lazy loading content:**

```tsx
import { lazy, Suspense } from 'react'

const AnalyticsTab = lazy(() => import('./tabs/analytics'))
const ReportsTab = lazy(() => import('./tabs/reports'))

<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <TabsList>{/* Triggers */}</TabsList>

  <TabsContent value="overview">{/* Always loaded */}</TabsContent>

  <TabsContent value="analytics">
    <Suspense fallback={<Loading />}>
      <AnalyticsTab />
    </Suspense>
  </TabsContent>

  <TabsContent value="reports">
    <Suspense fallback={<Loading />}>
      <ReportsTab />
    </Suspense>
  </TabsContent>
</Tabs>
```

---

## Responsive Design

**Mobile:**

- Horizontal scroll for many tabs
- Stack vertically for wide tabs
- Use dropdown menu for 5+ tabs

```tsx
// Automatic horizontal scroll on mobile
<TabsList className='w-full overflow-x-auto'>{/* Many tabs */}</TabsList>
```

# ShellPage

> Full-height composable page container with CSS fullscreen support

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/shell-page.mdx

Full-height container for admin pages, and the root of the composable shell trio: `ShellPage` + [AdminHeader](/docs/components/admin-header) + [AdminTabs](/docs/components/admin-tabs). Provides a fullscreen toggle (CSS-based, `fixed inset-0 z-50`, so Radix portals keep working) with an ESC listener, and exposes its state to its children.

```tsx
import { ShellPage, AdminHeader, AdminTabs } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<ShellPage>
  <AdminHeader title='Alerts' description='Manage alert rules' icon='Bell' />
  <AdminTabs tabs={tabs} value={activeTab} onValueChange={setTab} />
</ShellPage>
```

<Callout type='info' title='Composable pieces'>
  Compose `ShellPage` + `AdminHeader` + `AdminTabs` — independent, reusable pieces optimized for
  dashboards with tabs, maps, and real-time UIs.
</Callout>

---

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowFullscreen` | `boolean` | `true` | Enable the fullscreen toggle |
| `className` | `string` | - | Extra classes on the container |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | - | Page content (header, tabs, content) |

---

## Context

`ShellPage` provides a context, consumed via the [useShellPage](/docs/hooks/use-shell-page) hook:

```tsx
const shell = useShellPage()
// { isFullscreen: boolean, toggleFullscreen: () => void } | null
```

`AdminHeader` consumes this context automatically to render its fullscreen button — no wiring needed.

---

## Behavior

- **Fullscreen** is pure CSS (`fixed inset-0 z-50 h-screen bg-background`) — no Fullscreen API, so dialogs and dropdowns rendered in portals keep working.
- **ESC** exits fullscreen while active.
- The container is `flex flex-col h-full`, so children like `AdminTabs` (with `fillHeight`) or `ShellContent` can fill the remaining viewport.

## Pages Without Tabs

For pages without tabs, use `ShellContent` as the content area:

| `fullHeight` | Layout | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `true` (default) | `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-hidden` | Maps, viewport-filling content |
| `false` | `flex-1 overflow-auto` | Naturally scrolling content |

`ShellContent` also takes `padding` (default `false`; adds `p-4 lg:p-6`) and `className`.

```tsx
<ShellPage>
  <AdminHeader title='Live Map' icon='Map' />
  <ShellContent fullHeight>
    <MapComponent />
  </ShellContent>
</ShellPage>
```

---

## Related

- [AdminHeader](/docs/components/admin-header) — header bar with fullscreen toggle
- [AdminTabs](/docs/components/admin-tabs) — height-filling tabs
- [useTabUrlSync](/docs/hooks/use-tab-url-sync) — URL-driven tab state
- [useShellPage](/docs/hooks/use-shell-page) — fullscreen context hook
