# AdminHeader

> Pure header bar with title, icon, description, status, and fullscreen toggle

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/admin-header.mdx

Pure header bar for admin pages: icon + title + description on the left, status indicator, custom actions, and a fullscreen toggle on the right. Designed to sit at the top of a [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page).

```tsx
import { AdminHeader } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<AdminHeader
  title='Alert Center'
  description='Manage alert rules and notifications'
  icon='Bell'
/>
```

---

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `I18nText` | - | Page title (required) |
| `description` | `I18nText` | - | Secondary line under the title |
| `icon` | `string \| IconComponent` | - | Header icon — string key resolved via `getIcon()` (preferred) or a direct component |
| `status` | `DashboardStatus` | - | Status indicator (`'online' \| 'offline' \| 'loading' \| 'error'`) |
| `statusLabel` | `I18nText` | - | Label next to the status dot |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` | - | Custom actions rendered before the fullscreen button |
| `allowFullscreen` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the fullscreen button (only when a toggle is available) |
| `isFullscreen` | `boolean` | - | Manual override when used outside `ShellPage` |
| `onFullscreenToggle` | `() => void` | - | Manual override when used outside `ShellPage` |
| `className` | `string` | - | Extra classes |

---

## Fullscreen Integration

`AdminHeader` auto-consumes the `ShellPage` context via [useShellPage](/docs/hooks/use-shell-page):

- **Inside `ShellPage`:** the fullscreen button appears automatically and toggles the shell.
- **Standalone:** pass `isFullscreen` + `onFullscreenToggle` manually, or the button is hidden.

```tsx
// Standalone usage (outside ShellPage)
<AdminHeader
  title='Reports'
  isFullscreen={isFs}
  onFullscreenToggle={() => setIsFs((v) => !v)}
/>
```

---

## Icons by String

Prefer string icon keys resolved through the app's icon registry, registered once at boot with `setIconResolver`:

```tsx
<AdminHeader title='Registrations' icon='Database' />
```

See [Provider Setup](/docs/patterns/provider-setup) for the icon resolver configuration.

- [AdminTabs](/docs/components/admin-tabs) — tabs below the header
- [TabToolbar](/docs/components/tab-toolbar) — toolbar inside tab panels

# AdminTabs

> ContentTabs wrapper with height-filling CSS for shell page layouts

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/admin-tabs.mdx

`ContentTabs` wrapper for page layouts. Injects `flex-1 min-h-0` (plus child selectors) so tab panels fill the remaining height of a [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page) — essential for maps and other viewport-filling content. `ContentTabs` itself is not modified; dialogs keep using it directly.

```tsx
import { ShellPage, AdminHeader, AdminTabs } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useTabUrlSync } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const tabDefs = [
  { value: 'overview', label: 'Overview', icon: 'LayoutDashboard', content: <OverviewTab /> },
  { value: 'rules', label: 'Rules', icon: 'ListChecks', content: <RulesTab /> },
]

export default function AlertsPage() {
  const { activeTab, setTab } = useTabUrlSync({ tabs: tabDefs.map((t) => t.value) })

  return (
    <ShellPage>
      <AdminHeader title='Alerts' icon='Bell' />
      <AdminTabs tabs={tabDefs} value={activeTab} onValueChange={setTab} />
    </ShellPage>
  )
}
```

---

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` | `TabItem[]` | - | Tab definitions (value, label, shortLabel, icon, badge, content) |
| `value` | `string` | - | Controlled active tab |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Tab change callback |
| `fillHeight` | `boolean` | `true` | Fill remaining height — use for full-height content like maps |
| `compact` | `boolean` | `false` | Compact tab sizing |
| `variant` | `ContentTabsVariant` | `'default'` | ContentTabs visual variant (`'default' \| 'underline' \| 'pill' \| 'glass' \| 'gradient'`) |
| `className` | `string` | - | Extra classes |

---

## URL-Driven Tabs

Pair with [useTabUrlSync](/docs/hooks/use-tab-url-sync) so the URL is the source of truth (`?tab=rules` deep-links to a tab, and the browser Back button returns to the previous tab):

```tsx
const { activeTab, setTab } = useTabUrlSync({ tabs: visibleDefs.map((d) => d.value) })

<AdminTabs tabs={tabs} value={activeTab} onValueChange={setTab} />
```

---

## Related

- [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page) — full-height container
- [AdminHeader](/docs/components/admin-header) — header above the tabs
- [TabToolbar](/docs/components/tab-toolbar) — filters/search/actions inside tab panels
- [useTabUrlSync](/docs/hooks/use-tab-url-sync) — deep-linkable tab state

# TabToolbar

> Composable compound toolbar for filters, search, and actions inside tab panels

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/tab-toolbar.mdx

Compound component for building toolbars inside tab panels — filters, search, counters, refresh, and live status. The root lays its children out as a two-column grid on small screens and a single row from the `lg` breakpoint. Compose exactly the pieces you need from its sub-components.

```tsx
import { TabToolbar } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<TabToolbar>
  <TabToolbar.Search placeholder='Search...' value={search} onChange={setSearch} />
  <TabToolbar.Spacer />
  <TabToolbar.LiveIndicator connected={isConnected} />
  <TabToolbar.Refresh onClick={refetch} loading={isFetching} />
</TabToolbar>
```

---

## Sub-Components

| Sub-component | Purpose | Main props |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TabToolbar.Select` | Generic dropdown | `options`, `value`, `onChange` |
| `TabToolbar.PeriodSelector` | Period buttons | `options`, `value`, `onChange`, `loading?`, `icon?` |
| `TabToolbar.StatsPills` | Inline stat badges | `items: TabToolbarStatPill[]` |
| `TabToolbar.Search` | Search input with icon | `placeholder`, `value`, `onChange` |
| `TabToolbar.Refresh` | Refresh button with spin | `onClick`, `loading?` |
| `TabToolbar.Counter` | Result counter | `count`, `label` (string or `(count) => string`), `loading?`, `countIncluded?` |
| `TabToolbar.AutoRefresh` | Auto-refresh status toggle showing live/paused and the last update time (doesn't spin — pair with `Refresh`) | `enabled`, `onToggle: () => void`, `updatedAt?`, `loading?` |
| `TabToolbar.Fullscreen` | Fullscreen toggle | `isFullscreen`, `onToggle` |
| `TabToolbar.Spacer` | Flex spacer (pushes items right) | - |
| `TabToolbar.LiveIndicator` | SSE/WebSocket status pill | `connected`, `onlineLabel?`, `offlineLabel?` |
| `TabToolbar.FilterButtons` | Button-group filter; the "all" value (the first option, or `allValue`) is not rendered, and an active button toggles back to it | `options: TabToolbarFilterButtonOption[]`, `value`, `onChange`, `allValue?` |
| `TabToolbar.FilterSelect` | Dropdown filter with optional dot and count per option | `options`, `value`, `onChange`, `label?` |
| `TabToolbar.AddButton` | Primary "create" button | `onClick`, `label?`, `onPrefetch?` |
| `TabToolbar.DateRange` | Date range picker (lazy-loaded) | `value: DateRange`, `onChange`, `maxDays?` (default `7`), `labels?` |

Root props: `children`, `className?`.

**Exported types:** `TabToolbarSelectOption`, `TabToolbarPeriodOption`, `TabToolbarStatPill`, `TabToolbarFilterButtonOption`. `DateRange` comes from `@telamonjs/ui/pickers`.

---

## LiveIndicator

Real-time connection status pill for SSE/WebSocket-backed tabs:

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `connected` | `boolean` | - | Connection state |
| `onlineLabel` | `string` | `'Ao vivo'` | Label when connected (green pulsing dot) |
| `offlineLabel` | `string` | `'Offline'` | Label when disconnected (red dot) |
| `className` | `string` | - | Extra classes |

---

## Full Example

`TabToolbarStatPill` needs a `key`, an `icon` component and a `color` class, which is applied to the icon and the value.

```tsx
import { Wifi, WifiOff } from 'lucide-react'

<TabToolbar>
  <TabToolbar.PeriodSelector
    options={[
      { value: '24h', label: '24h' },
      { value: '7d', label: '7 days' },
      { value: '30d', label: '30 days' },
    ]}
    value={period}
    onChange={setPeriod}
  />
  <TabToolbar.StatsPills
    items={[
      { key: 'online', label: 'Online', value: stats.online, icon: Wifi, color: 'text-green-600' },
      { key: 'offline', label: 'Offline', value: stats.offline, icon: WifiOff, color: 'text-red-600' },
    ]}
  />
  <TabToolbar.Spacer />
  <TabToolbar.Counter count={rows.length} label='results' loading={isLoading} />
  <TabToolbar.AutoRefresh enabled={auto} onToggle={() => setAuto((v) => !v)} />
  <TabToolbar.Refresh onClick={refetch} loading={isFetching} />
</TabToolbar>
```

---

## Related

- [AdminTabs](/docs/components/admin-tabs) — the tab panels this toolbar lives in
- [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page) — page container
- [AdminHeader](/docs/components/admin-header) — page-level header (title/status/fullscreen)

# ListPage

> Complete list page rendered from a single CrudConfig — search, sort, pagination, dialogs

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/list-page.mdx

Complete list page component driven by a single `CrudConfig` — built-in search, sorting,
pagination, row/header actions, and CRUD dialogs.

`ListPage` takes a single `config: CrudConfig<T, TFormData>` prop: title, columns, data and
loading all live in `config`.

---

## Basic Usage

Data loading, search, and mutations all come from `config` — built with React Query
(`config.query.queryFn` fetches from your REST API; `config.mutations.*` handle create/update/delete).

```tsx title="config.tsx"
'use client'
import { type CrudConfig } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { usersApi } from '@/lib/api/users-client'

export const config: CrudConfig<User, UserFormData> = {
  module: { name: 'users', title: 'Users', description: 'Manage system users', route: '/admin/users' },
  list: { title: 'Users', description: 'Registered users', columns, searchPlaceholder: 'Search by name or email...' },
  form: { sections, validation: validationSchema },
  // queryFn resolves PaginatedResponse<User> ({ data, total, page, totalPages })
  query: { queryKey: ['users'], queryFn: usersApi.list },
  mutations: {
    // mutationFn resolves { success, data? } — shape it here, not in the API client
    create: {
      mutationFn: async (data) => ({ success: true, data: await usersApi.create(data) }),
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
    update: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id, data }) => ({ success: true, data: await usersApi.update(id, data) }),
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
    delete: {
      mutationFn: async ({ id }) => {
        await usersApi.delete(id)
        return { success: true }
      },
      invalidates: [['users']],
    },
  },
}
```

```tsx title="page.tsx"
import { ListPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { config } from './config'

export default function UsersPage() {
  return <ListPage config={config} />
}
```

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    config: {
      description: 'Complete CRUD configuration — module/list/form/query/mutations',
      type: 'CrudConfigWithAnyForm<TData>',
      required: true,
    },
    tableId: {
      description: 'Unique table ID for the Zustand store',
      type: 'string',
      default: 'config.module.route',
    },
    urlSync: {
      description: 'Sync pagination/search/sort state with URL query params',
      type: 'boolean',
      default: 'false',
    },
    embedded: {
      description: 'Render without the page chrome — for use inside a tab (AdminTabs)',
      type: 'boolean',
      default: 'false',
    },
  }}
/>

Use `CrudConfigWithAnyForm<TData>` (not `as any`) when a helper needs to accept a config with
any form-data shape — `TFormData` on `CrudConfig` is invariant.

<details>
<summary>Full interface (includes filters, bulk actions, toolbar slots)</summary>

```typescript
interface ListPageProps<TData> {
  config: CrudConfigWithAnyForm<TData>
  tableId?: string
  urlSync?: boolean
  urlFilters?: Record<string, 'string' | 'number'>
  cardComponent?: ComponentType<{ data: TData; onClick?: (data: TData) => void }>
  className?: string
  onRefreshAction?: () => Promise<void | { success: boolean }>
  filterOptions?: ColumnFilterConfig
  loadFilterOptions?: () => Promise<ColumnFilterConfig>
  enableBulkActions?: boolean
  bulkActions?: BulkAction<TData>[]
  headerActions?: Array<{
    label: string
    icon?: ReactNode
    onClick: () => void
    variant?: 'default' | 'destructive' | 'outline' | 'secondary' | 'ghost'
    loading?: boolean
  }>
  disableAutoRefresh?: boolean
  errorBoundary?: boolean
  errorFallback?: ReactNode
  toolbarPrepend?: ReactNode
  toolbarContent?: ReactNode | ((state: ListQueryState) => ReactNode)
  filtersPanel?: ReactNode
  activeFilters?: Array<{ key: string; label: string; onRemove: () => void }>
  onClearFilters?: () => void
  footerContent?: ReactNode
  embedded?: boolean
  dialogUrlSync?: boolean // default true
}
```

</details>

---

## Column Definitions

`config.list.columns` takes `CrudColumnDef<T>` — a TanStack Table column definition whose
`header` also accepts an `I18nText`:

```tsx title="config.tsx"
import type { CrudColumnDef } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export const columns: CrudColumnDef<User>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
  { accessorKey: 'email', header: 'Email' },
  {
    accessorKey: 'role',
    header: 'Role',
    cell: ({ row }) => {
      const role = row.original.role
      return <Badge variant={role === 'ADMIN' ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>{role}</Badge>
    },
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'createdAt',
    header: 'Created At',
    cell: ({ row }) => new Date(row.original.createdAt).toLocaleDateString(),
  },
]
```

---

## Row and Header Actions

Row actions live in `config.actionsConfig` (`DataTableActionsConfig`); toolbar buttons are the
`headerActions` prop of `ListPage`:

```tsx title="config.tsx"
export const config: CrudConfig<User, UserFormData> = {
  // ...
  actionsConfig: {
    custom: [
      { id: 'open-page', label: 'Open page', href: row => `/admin/users/${row.id}` },
      { id: 'reset', label: 'Reset password', onClick: row => resetPassword(row.id), variant: 'destructive' },
    ],
  },
}
```

```tsx title="page.tsx"
<ListPage
  config={config}
  headerActions={[{ label: 'Import', onClick: handleImport, variant: 'outline' }]}
/>
```

`create`/`update`/`delete` row and header actions (edit/view/create dialogs) are wired
automatically from `config.dialogs` and `config.mutations` — see the
[Dialog Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern#dialogs) and
[ListPage Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) for the full dialog configuration.

---

## Embedded (Dashboard Tabs)

Inside a tabbed dashboard (`ShellPage` + `AdminHeader` + `AdminTabs`), render the list with
`embedded` to drop the outer page chrome:

```tsx
<ListPage config={config} embedded />
```

---

## Features

**Built-in:**

- ✅ Pagination (client or server-side, driven by `config.query`)
- ✅ Search (debounced)
- ✅ Sorting (click column headers; `list.sortParam` picks [what `sortBy` carries](/docs/patterns/react-query#what-sortby-carries))
- ✅ Filtering (column filters and `list.toolbar.filters`)
- ✅ Row actions (contextual menu) and header actions (toolbar buttons)
- ✅ Create/edit/view/delete dialogs from `config.dialogs` + `config.mutations`
- ✅ Mobile-responsive (switches to cards)
- ✅ Loading, empty, and error states
- ✅ Excel/CSV/PDF export (`list.enableExport`): the loaded rows, every matching row (`list.exportAll`) or your backend (`list.onExport`) — see [exporting every row](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern#exporting-every-row-or-exporting-on-the-server)

---

## Best Practices

1. Keep `columns`, `sections`, `validation`, `query`, and `mutations` together in one
   `config.tsx` (Page Config Pattern)
2. Use `queryKey`/`invalidates` consistently so mutations refresh the right list
3. Provide `searchPlaceholder` for better UX
4. Use `embedded` inside `AdminTabs`, not a standalone page per module

---

## Related Components

- [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) - Lower-level table (more customization)
- [MobileCard](/docs/components/mobile-card) - Card component for mobile view

---

## See Also

- [ListPage Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) - Best practices, dialogs
- [Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) - Fetch/mutate via CrudConfig

---

---

# DataTable

> Advanced data table with sorting, filtering, pagination, and row selection

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/data-table.mdx

Advanced data table component built on TanStack Table with sorting, filtering, pagination, row selection, and mobile responsiveness.

<Callout type='info' title='Lower-Level Component'>
  `DataTable` is a lower-level component. For most use cases, use
  [ListPage](/docs/components/list-page) which wraps DataTable with additional
  features.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import type { ColumnDef } from '@tanstack/react-table'

interface User {
  id: string
  name: string
  email: string
  role: string
}

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
  { accessorKey: 'email', header: 'Email' },
  { accessorKey: 'role', header: 'Role' },
]

export default function UsersTable({ users }: { users: User[] }) {
  return <DataTable columns={columns} data={users} />
}
```

---

## Props

<Callout type='info' title='Most-used props'>
  This table covers the props most consumers reach for; `DataTableProps` has the full list.
</Callout>

<TypeTable
  type={{
    columns: { description: 'TanStack Table column definitions', type: 'ColumnDef<TData, TValue>[]', required: true },
    data: { description: 'Data array to display (current page only for server-side pagination)', type: 'TData[]', required: true },
    tableId: { description: 'Unique table ID for the Zustand store', type: 'string', default: 'pathname' },
    title: { description: 'Table title displayed above the toolbar', type: 'string' },
    searchPlaceholder: { description: 'Placeholder for the global search input (localized default)', type: 'string', default: "t('list.search')" },
    enableSearch: { description: 'Enable global search', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    enableExport: { description: 'Enable export (Excel/CSV/PDF) button', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    exportMenuProps: { description: 'Extra props for the built-in export menu: `loadAll` + `allCount` (export every server page instead of the table rows), `onServerExport` (app-side export), `formats`, `filename`', type: 'DataTableExportMenuProps<TData>' },
    enablePagination: { description: 'Enable pagination controls', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    pageSize: { description: 'Initial page size', type: 'number', default: '10' },
    manualPagination: { description: 'Enable server-side pagination (manual control)', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    pageCount: { description: 'Total page count (server-side pagination)', type: 'number' },
    currentPage: { description: 'Current page, 1-indexed (server-side pagination)', type: 'number' },
    totalItems: { description: 'Total items count (server-side pagination)', type: 'number' },
    onPaginationChange: { description: 'Fired when pagination changes', type: '(page: number, pageSize: number) => void' },
    onSearchChange: { description: 'Fired when the global search changes (debounced 300ms). Server-side only', type: '(search: string) => void' },
    enableRowSelection: { description: 'Enable row selection checkboxes', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    actionsConfig: { description: 'Row actions column configuration', type: 'DataTableActionsConfig<TData>' },
    onRowClick: { description: 'Fired when a row is clicked', type: '(row: TData) => void', default: "router.push('${pathname}/${id}')" },
    rowClickNavigation: { description: 'Default row-click navigation when there is no onRowClick; false for lists without a detail route', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    cardComponent: { description: 'Custom card component for the mobile view', type: 'React.ComponentType<{ data: TData; onClick?: (data: TData) => void }>' },
    loading: { description: 'Show loading skeleton', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    error: { description: 'Error message to display', type: 'string' },
    emptyTitle: { description: 'Empty state title (localized default)', type: 'string', default: "t('list.empty')" },
    emptyDescription: { description: 'Empty state description (localized default)', type: 'string', default: "t('list.emptyDescription')" },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes on the container', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

---

## Examples

### With Sorting

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={columns}
  data={users}
  // Sorting enabled by default - click headers to sort
/>
```

**Column configuration:**

```tsx
const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
  {
    accessorKey: 'name',
    header: 'Name',
    enableSorting: true, // ✅ Sortable (default)
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'email',
    header: 'Email',
    enableSorting: false, // ❌ Not sortable
  },
]
```

### With Pagination

```tsx
<DataTable columns={columns} data={users} pageSize={25} />
```

Pagination controls render while `enablePagination` is `true` (the default).

### With Row Selection

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function UsersTable({ users }: { users: User[] }) {
  return <DataTable columns={columns} data={users} enableRowSelection />
}
```

`enableRowSelection` renders checkboxes and manages selection state internally
(Zustand store keyed by `tableId`) — there is no `rowSelection`/`onRowSelectionChange`
prop to control it externally.

### With Row Actions

```tsx
import { DataTable } from '@telamonjs/ui'

;<DataTable
  columns={columns}
  data={users}
  actionsConfig={{
    standard: {
      view: { href: row => `/users/${row.id}` },
      edit: { href: row => `/users/${row.id}/edit` },
      delete: {
        onClick: row => handleDelete(row.id),
        confirmDialog: true,
      },
    },
  }}
/>
```

`actionsConfig` (type `DataTableActionsConfig<TData>`) injects the actions
column — there is no `rowActions` render-prop.

### Custom Cell Rendering

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
  {
    accessorKey: 'name',
    header: 'Name',
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'role',
    header: 'Role',
    cell: ({ row }) => {
      const role = row.original.role
      return (
        <Badge variant={role === 'ADMIN' ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>
          {role}
        </Badge>
      )
    },
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'createdAt',
    header: 'Created',
    cell: ({ row }) => {
      return new Date(row.original.createdAt).toLocaleDateString()
    },
  },
]
```

Use `cell` function to customize rendering.

### Global Search

`enableSearch` (default `true`) renders the search input and filters
client-side automatically — no external filter state is needed:

```tsx
<DataTable columns={columns} data={users} searchPlaceholder='Search users...' />
```

For server-side pagination, wire `onSearchChange` instead (debounced 300ms):

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={columns}
  data={users}
  manualPagination
  onSearchChange={search => refetch({ search })}
/>
```

### Custom Mobile Card

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={columns}
  data={users}
  cardComponent={({ data }) => (
    <div className='p-4 space-y-2'>
      <div className='font-semibold'>{data.name}</div>
      <div className='text-sm text-muted-foreground'>{data.email}</div>
      <Badge>{data.role}</Badge>
    </div>
  )}
/>
```

`cardComponent` (type `React.ComponentType<{ data: TData; onClick?: (data: TData) => void }>`)
replaces the default mobile card renderer.

### Loading State

```tsx
<DataTable columns={columns} data={users} loading={isLoading} />
```

Shows skeleton loading state.

### Empty State

```tsx
<DataTable
  columns={columns}
  data={[]}
  emptyTitle='No users found'
  emptyDescription='Create your first user to get started.'
/>
```

`emptyTitle`/`emptyDescription` customize the empty state — there is no single `emptyMessage` prop.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="app/admin/users/components/users-table.tsx"
'use client'

import { DataTable, Badge } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import type { ColumnDef } from '@tanstack/react-table'

interface User {
  id: string
  name: string
  email: string
  role: 'USER' | 'ADMIN'
  active: boolean
  createdAt: string
}

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
  {
    accessorKey: 'name',
    header: 'Name',
    enableSorting: true,
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'email',
    header: 'Email',
    enableSorting: true,
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'role',
    header: 'Role',
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <Badge variant={row.original.role === 'ADMIN' ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>
        {row.original.role}
      </Badge>
    ),
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'active',
    header: 'Status',
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <Badge variant={row.original.active ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>
        {row.original.active ? 'Active' : 'Inactive'}
      </Badge>
    ),
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'createdAt',
    header: 'Created',
    cell: ({ row }) => new Date(row.original.createdAt).toLocaleDateString(),
    enableSorting: true,
  },
]

export default function UsersTable({ users }: { users: User[] }) {
  async function handleDelete(id: string) {
    if (confirm('Are you sure you want to delete this user?')) {
      // Delete logic
    }
  }

  return (
    <DataTable
      columns={columns}
      data={users}
      pageSize={10}
      enableRowSelection
      actionsConfig={{
        standard: {
          view: { href: row => `/admin/users/${row.id}` },
          edit: { href: row => `/admin/users/${row.id}/edit` },
          delete: {
            onClick: row => handleDelete(row.id),
            confirmDialog: true,
          },
        },
      }}
      emptyTitle='No users found'
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Column Definition API

**Common properties:**

```tsx
{
  accessorKey: 'fieldName',        // Data field key
  header: 'Display Name',          // Column header
  cell: ({ row }) => <Custom />,   // Custom cell renderer
  enableSorting: true,             // Allow sorting
  enableHiding: true,              // Allow hiding column
  size: 200,                       // Column width in px
}
```

**Advanced features:**

- `accessorFn` - Custom accessor function
- `sortingFn` - Custom sorting logic
- `filterFn` - Custom filtering logic
- `meta` - Store custom metadata

See [TanStack Table Docs](https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/api/core/column-def) for full API.

---

## Responsive Behavior

| Screen Size           | Behavior                            |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| **Desktop (≥ 768px)** | Full table with all columns         |
| **Mobile (< 768px)**  | Switches to card view automatically |

Mobile cards show:

- Custom renderer if provided via `cardComponent`
- Default card with all fields if no custom renderer

---

## Best Practices

1. **Define columns in config.tsx** - Follow Page Config Pattern
2. **Use cell renderers** - For badges, dates, custom formatting
3. **Enable sorting** - For better UX on large datasets
4. **Add row actions** - Common operations easily accessible
5. **Provide empty state** - Custom message for empty data
6. **Custom mobile cards** - Optimize mobile UX

---

## Performance

**Optimization tips:**

- ✅ Use `useMemo` for columns definition
- ✅ Virtualize rows for 1000+ records (react-virtual)
- ✅ Server-side pagination for 10,000+ records
- ✅ Debounce search input
- ✅ Lazy load row actions menu

**Example:**

```tsx
const columns = useMemo<ColumnDef<User>[]>(
  () => [
    { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
    // ...
  ],
  []
)
```

---

## Accessibility

- Semantic `<table>` element
- Sortable headers keyboard accessible (Enter to sort)
- Row selection with keyboard (Space to toggle)
- ARIA labels for sorting state
- Focus visible states
- Screen reader announcements for updates

---

## Related Components

- [ListPage](/docs/components/list-page) - Higher-level list with filters (recommended)
- [MobileCard](/docs/components/mobile-card) - Mobile card component

---

## See Also

- [TanStack Table Documentation](https://tanstack.com/table/v8) - Full API reference
- [ListPage Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) - Best practices
- [Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) - Organize columns

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# ReportTable

> Read-only table with progressive "load more" pagination for reports and dashboards

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/report-table.mdx

A plain, read-only table for report sections and dashboard cards: it renders the first
`pageSize` rows, a "load more" button for the rest and a "Showing X of Y records" line. It
has no sorting, filtering or row actions — for CRUD lists use [ListPage](/docs/components/list-page)
or [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table). Also exported as `SimpleTable`.

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
'use client'

import { ReportTable } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const columns = [
  { key: 'month', header: 'Month' },
  { key: 'customer.name', header: 'Customer' }, // dot paths read nested values
  {
    key: 'total',
    header: 'Total',
    className: 'text-right',
    render: (row: Revenue) => row.total.toFixed(2),
  },
]

export function RevenueTable({ rows }: { rows: Revenue[] }) {
  return <ReportTable data={rows} columns={columns} pageSize={20} />
}
```

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    data: { description: 'Rows to show (all of them — pagination is client-side)', type: 'T[]', required: true },
    columns: { description: 'Columns: `key` (dot paths allowed), `header`, optional `render(item, index)` and `className`', type: 'ReportTableColumn<T>[]', required: true },
    pageSize: { description: 'Rows shown first and added by each "load more"', type: 'number', default: '50' },
    maxHeight: { description: 'Max height of the scroll box', type: 'string', default: "'400px'" },
    stickyHeader: { description: 'Keep the header row visible while scrolling', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    showFooter: { description: 'Show the "Showing X of Y records" line under the table', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    emptyMessage: { description: 'Text shown when `data` is empty', type: 'string' },
    labels: { description: 'Override the built-in texts (`empty`, `loadMore`, `showing`, `of`, `records`, `remaining`)', type: 'Partial<ReportTableLabels>' },
    scrollProps: { description: "Attributes for the scroll box — pass `{ tabIndex: 0, role: 'region', 'aria-label': '…' }` so keyboard users can scroll it", type: 'object' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes on the wrapper', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

---

## Examples

### Without the Footer

```tsx
<ReportTable data={topProducts} columns={columns} pageSize={10} showFooter={false} />
```

Hide the count line when the surrounding card already states the total, or when the table
is short enough that the count adds nothing.

### Keyboard-Scrollable Region

```tsx
<ReportTable
  data={rows}
  columns={columns}
  maxHeight='300px'
  scrollProps={{ tabIndex: 0, role: 'region', 'aria-label': 'Revenue by month' }}
/>
```

---

## Related Components

- [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) - Sorting, filtering, selection and row actions
- [ExportButtons](/docs/components/export-button) - Export the same rows to CSV, Excel or PDF

---

# MobileCard

> Card component for mobile-responsive data display in tables

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/mobile-card.mdx

Card component that displays one table row on mobile, built from the same TanStack column
definitions as the table, with an actions menu and selection state.

<Callout type='info' title='Auto-used by DataTable'>
  `MobileCard` is automatically used by [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table)
  on mobile screens. You typically don't need to use it directly unless building
  custom mobile layouts.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { MobileCard } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import type { ColumnDef } from '@tanstack/react-table'

interface User {
  id: string
  name: string
  email: string
  role: string
}

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
  { accessorKey: 'email', header: 'Email' },
  { accessorKey: 'role', header: 'Role' },
]

export function UserCard({ user }: { user: User }) {
  return <MobileCard data={user} columns={columns} />
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
{
  data: TData // Row data (required)
  columns: ColumnDef<TData, TValue>[] // TanStack column definitions (required)
  onSelect?: (data: TData) => void // Card click
  isSelected?: boolean // Shows a ring border when true
  actions?: Array<{
    label: string
    onClick: (data: TData) => void
    variant?: 'default' | 'destructive'
  }> // Rendered in a 3-dot dropdown menu in the top-right corner
}
```

There is no `fields`, `variant`, `onClick` or `className` prop — the card layout comes from
`columns`.

---

## Column Mapping

The card uses the first 4 columns, skipping `select`, `actions` and an `id` accessor:

- **Column 1:** title (bold)
- **Column 2:** subtitle (small, muted)
- **Columns 3-4:** detail rows, labelled with the column `header`; empty values are skipped

Boolean values render as a localized Yes/No badge. Put the most important data in the first
columns and keep headers short — they become the labels.

---

## Examples

### Custom Rendering

A column with an `accessorKey` (or `accessorFn`) shows the raw value. To render custom content,
define the column with an `id` and a `cell` instead:

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
  { accessorKey: 'email', header: 'Email' },
  {
    id: 'role',
    header: 'Role',
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <Badge variant={row.original.role === 'ADMIN' ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>
        {row.original.role}
      </Badge>
    ),
  },
  {
    id: 'createdAt',
    header: 'Created',
    cell: ({ row }) => new Date(row.original.createdAt).toLocaleDateString(),
  },
]

<MobileCard data={user} columns={columns} />
```

### With Actions

```tsx
<MobileCard
  data={user}
  columns={columns}
  actions={[
    { label: 'View', onClick: u => router.push(`/users/${u.id}`) },
    { label: 'Edit', onClick: u => router.push(`/users/${u.id}/edit`) },
    { label: 'Delete', onClick: u => handleDelete(u.id), variant: 'destructive' },
  ]}
/>
```

Actions appear in a dropdown menu in the top-right corner; selecting one does not trigger
`onSelect`. Inside `DataTable`, pass them as `cardActions`.

### Selectable Card

```tsx
const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null)

<MobileCard
  data={user}
  columns={columns}
  isSelected={selectedId === user.id}
  onSelect={u => setSelectedId(u.id)}
/>
```

The whole card is clickable and calls `onSelect` with the row data.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/user-mobile-list.tsx"
'use client'

import { MobileCard, Badge } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import type { ColumnDef } from '@tanstack/react-table'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

interface User {
  id: string
  name: string
  email: string
  role: 'USER' | 'ADMIN'
  active: boolean
}

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
  { accessorKey: 'name', header: 'Name' },
  { accessorKey: 'email', header: 'Email' },
  {
    id: 'role',
    header: 'Role',
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <Badge variant={row.original.role === 'ADMIN' ? 'default' : 'secondary'}>
        {row.original.role}
      </Badge>
    ),
  },
  { accessorKey: 'active', header: 'Active' }, // boolean → Yes/No badge
]

export function UserMobileList({ users }: { users: User[] }) {
  const router = useRouter()

  async function handleDelete(id: string) {
    if (confirm('Delete this user?')) {
      // Delete logic
    }
  }

  return (
    <div className='grid gap-4'>
      {users.map(user => (
        <MobileCard
          key={user.id}
          data={user}
          columns={columns}
          onSelect={u => router.push(`/admin/users/${u.id}`)}
          actions={[
            { label: 'Edit', onClick: u => router.push(`/admin/users/${u.id}/edit`) },
            { label: 'Delete', onClick: u => handleDelete(u.id), variant: 'destructive' },
          ]}
        />
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}
```

---

## When to Use

Use `MobileCard` when:

- ✅ Building custom mobile layouts for tables
- ✅ Creating mobile-optimized list views
- ✅ Need different mobile layout than desktop table
- ✅ Building responsive dashboards

**Don't use directly when:**

- ❌ Using DataTable (already includes MobileCard)
- ❌ Using ListPage (already includes MobileCard)
- ❌ Desktop-only interfaces

For a fully custom card inside `DataTable`/`ListPage`, pass `cardComponent` instead.

---

## Best Practices

1. **Prioritize important fields** - Only the first 4 columns are shown
2. **Use custom rendering** - Format dates, badges, status with `cell` columns
3. **Limit actions** - Show only the most common operations
4. **Show visual hierarchy** - Order columns so title and subtitle carry the key data
5. **Test on real devices** - Emulators don't show actual mobile UX

---

## Responsive Design

**DataTable automatically switches:**

- **Desktop (≥ 768px):** Full table view
- **Mobile (< 768px):** MobileCard view

**Manual breakpoint:**

```tsx
import { useIsMobile, DataTable, MobileCard } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function UserList({ users }) {
  const isMobile = useIsMobile() // < 768px

  if (isMobile) {
    return users.map(user => <MobileCard key={user.id} data={user} columns={columns} />)
  }

  return <DataTable columns={columns} data={users} />
}
```

---

## Accessibility

- Title renders as an `<h3>`
- The actions trigger is a button with an accessible label (localized "open row actions")
- Destructive actions are styled distinctly in the menu
- The card itself is a clickable container, not a button — for keyboard-reachable navigation,
  provide an action or a link in a `cell`

---

## Related Components

- [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) - Uses MobileCard automatically
- [ListPage](/docs/components/list-page) - Higher-level list component
- Card - Base card component

---

## See Also

- [ListPage Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) - Responsive lists
- Mobile-First Design - Best practices

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# ConfirmActionDialog

> Confirmation dialog for an async action, with validated inputs, free content, a dialog- or caller-controlled pending state and inline errors

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/confirm-action-dialog.mdx

The dialog behind `confirmDialog` on the row and menu actions of a `ListPage`, available for any
other button. It stays open while the action runs, closes when it succeeds and shows the error
when it fails, so the user can retry without retyping what they filled in.

```tsx
import { Button, ConfirmActionDialog } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<ConfirmActionDialog
  title='Reject request?'
  description='The requester is notified with your reason.'
  confirmText='Reject'
  variant='destructive'
  inputs={[{ name: 'reason', label: 'Reason', type: 'textarea', required: true }]}
  onConfirm={({ reason }) => requestsApi.reject(request.id, reason)}
>
  <Button variant='destructive'>Reject</Button>
</ConfirmActionDialog>
```

---

## Behavior

- **Pending**: while the promise returned by `onConfirm` is pending, both buttons are disabled,
  the confirm button shows a spinner (and `pendingText`, if set) and the dialog cannot be
  dismissed.
- **Success**: when `onConfirm` resolves, the dialog closes.
- **Failure**: when it rejects, the dialog stays open and shows the error's `message` (or a
  localized fallback). Resolve `false` instead to stay open without a message — for an error
  you already reported, such as in a toast.
- **Inputs**: `text`, `textarea`, `select` and `date` (the native date input, value
  `YYYY-MM-DD`). A `required` input left empty (or blank), a trimmed value outside
  `minLength`/`maxLength`, a `date` outside `min`/`max` and an input whose `validate` returns a
  message block the confirm and are marked invalid. Values reach `onConfirm` keyed by `name`;
  every opening starts again from `defaultValue`.
- **Live counts**: a `minLength`/`maxLength` input shows how many characters are missing (or
  over) as the user types, before any attempt, so the reason is visible without clicking.
- **`disableUntilValid`** keeps the confirm disabled while any input fails. Every failing field
  then shows its message live: muted while untouched, as an error once edited or after an
  attempt. Without it the confirm stays enabled and messages show from the first attempt.
- **`confirmDisabled`** disables only the confirm button, from your own state.
- **Focus**: with `inputs`, the first field is focused on open, so a reason can be typed right
  away; without inputs, focus starts on Cancel, the safe default for a destructive confirmation.

Pass `open` / `onOpenChange` to control it (for example from a menu item), or a `children`
trigger and nothing else to let it own its state. `children` is always the trigger; content
inside the dialog goes in `body`.

## Caller-controlled pending

When you already run the action yourself — typically a React Query mutation — pass `pending`.
Its presence (even `false`) hands the lifecycle to you: confirming calls `onConfirm` and never
closes the dialog, so it stays locked on `pendingText` until you close it when the mutation
settles. While `pending` is `true` both buttons are disabled and the dialog cannot be dismissed.
A rejected promise from `onConfirm` still shows its message.

```tsx
const publish = useMutation({
  mutationFn: () => api.publish(id),
  onSuccess: () => setOpen(false),
})

<ConfirmActionDialog
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  title={<>Publish <strong>{name}</strong>?</>}
  description='Candidates see it right away.'
  pending={publish.isPending}
  pendingText='Publishing...'
  onConfirm={() => publish.mutate()}
/>
```

## Free content and custom validation

`title` and `description` take JSX as well as text or `msg()` (the description renders inside
a `<p>`, so keep it phrasing content). `body` renders anything between the description and the
buttons. For fields, prefer `inputs` with `validate`: it receives the field value and every
value, and returns the message to show (text or `msg()`) or `undefined`. Messages appear from
the first confirm attempt on and update as the user types.

```tsx
<ConfirmActionDialog
  title='Write off invoice?'
  variant='destructive'
  body={<p className='text-sm'>Balance: {formatMoney(invoice.balance)}</p>}
  inputs={[
    { name: 'date', label: 'Effective date', type: 'date', required: true },
    {
      name: 'word',
      label: 'Type WRITE OFF to confirm',
      type: 'text',
      validate: value => (value === 'WRITE OFF' ? undefined : 'Type WRITE OFF'),
    },
  ]}
  onConfirm={({ date }) => invoicesApi.writeOff(invoice.id, date)}
>
  <Button variant='destructive'>Write off</Button>
</ConfirmActionDialog>
```

For anything `inputs` cannot express, render your own fields in `body` and gate the button with
`confirmDisabled`.

## Input options

| Option | Applies to | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | all | blocks while empty or blank |
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `text`, `textarea` | length of the trimmed value; live count while it fails. `minLength` checks an optional field only once it is filled |
| `min` / `max` | `date` | `YYYY-MM-DD`, set on the native input (the picker greys out other days) and validated |
| `validate(value, values)` | all | your rule: return the message, or `undefined` |
| `options` | `select` | strings, or `{ value, label }` when the value is a code (the label is `I18nText`) |
| `placeholder` | all | the `select` prompt, or the native placeholder |
| `description` | all | help text under the field, announced with it |
| `rows` | `textarea` | visible rows |
| `suggestions` | `text` | a native `<datalist>`: suggestions, any value still accepted |
| `inputMode` / `autoComplete` | `text`, `textarea` | native attributes (`'decimal'`, `'off'`…) |

```tsx
<ConfirmActionDialog
  title='Remove the record?'
  variant='destructive'
  disableUntilValid
  inputs={[
    { name: 'reason', label: 'Reason', type: 'textarea', required: true, minLength: 5, rows: 3,
      description: 'Kept in the audit trail.' },
  ]}
  onConfirm={({ reason }) => recordsApi.remove(id, reason.trim())}
>
  <Button variant='destructive'>Remove</Button>
</ConfirmActionDialog>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onConfirm` | `(values: Record<string, string>) => unknown` | required |
| `open` / `onOpenChange` | `boolean` / `(open: boolean) => void` | uncontrolled |
| `children` | `ReactNode` — the element that opens it | — |
| `title` | `I18nText \| ReactNode` | localized "Confirm action" |
| `description` | `I18nText \| ReactNode` | — |
| `body` | `ReactNode` — between the description and the buttons | — |
| `confirmText` / `cancelText` | `I18nText` | localized "Confirm" / "Cancel" |
| `pendingText` | `I18nText` — confirm label while pending | `confirmText` |
| `pending` | `boolean` — caller-controlled pending, no auto-close | dialog-owned |
| `confirmDisabled` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `variant` | `'default' \| 'destructive'` | `'default'` |
| `inputs` | `ConfirmDialogInput[]` — see [Input options](#input-options) | — |
| `disableUntilValid` | `boolean` — confirm off while an input fails, messages live | `false` |

## Migrating a local copy

Apps that kept their own confirmation dialog (controlled, `pending`, JSX title, free content)
can switch to this one by renaming two props: the local `children` (content) becomes `body`,
and hard-coded "Confirm"/"Cancel" labels become the localized defaults. `open`,
`onOpenChange`, `title`, `description`, `confirmText`, `pendingText`, `pending`, `variant`,
`confirmDisabled` and `onConfirm` keep their meaning.

A local "reason" dialog (a textarea whose confirm unlocks at N characters) becomes an input with
`required`, `minLength: N` and `disableUntilValid`: the live count replaces the hand-written
check, and the trimmed value is what the rule measures.

## In row actions

`ActionConfig.confirmDialog` renders this dialog with the same `title`, `description`, button
texts, `variant`, `inputs` (every input option) and `disableUntilValid`. Its `inputs` reach the
action as a second argument, only when inputs are declared (handlers written for the row alone
keep working):

```tsx
actionsConfig: {
  custom: [
    {
      id: 'reject',
      label: 'Reject',
      handler: (row, ctx) => requestsApi.reject(row.id, ctx?.inputs.reason ?? ''),
      confirmDialog: {
        title: row => `Reject ${row.number}?`,
        variant: 'destructive',
        inputs: [{ name: 'reason', label: 'Reason', type: 'textarea', required: true }],
      },
    },
  ],
},
```

A failing row action shows its error toast as before and keeps the dialog open for a retry.

## Related

- [ListPage Pattern — Row Actions](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern#row-actions)
- [Dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs)

---

# QueryErrorState

> Error state of a query with a localized title, the error's message and a "Try again" button that stays pending while it retries

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/query-error-state.mdx

The error UI for screens that run their own `useQuery`. Without it, a failed request leaves the
screen blank or loading forever. The CRUD view and edit dialogs use the same component when their
record fails to load.

```tsx
'use client'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { QueryErrorState } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function GradingSheet({ id }: { id: string }) {
  const { data, error, isError, refetch } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['grading-sheet', id],
    queryFn: () => sheetsApi.get(id),
  })

  if (isError) return <QueryErrorState error={error} onRetry={refetch} />
  // ...
}
```

---

## Behavior

- **Title**: `title`, or the localized "Failed to load data".
- **Message**: `description` when given, otherwise the message of `error`: an `Error`, a string,
  or any object with a string `message` (most API client errors). Without a usable message only
  the title shows.
- **Retry**: the button appears only with `onRetry`. It is called with no arguments, so
  `onRetry={refetch}` is safe. While the promise it returns is pending, the button is disabled and
  shows a spinner (`aria-busy`). Extra clicks are ignored. A rejected promise ends the pending
  state and is logged; the error state stays on screen.
- **`retrying`** drives the pending state from your side, for example `retrying={query.isFetching}`
  when something else triggers the refetch.
- The button is `type="button"`, so the state can sit inside a form. The root is an
  `role="alert"` region, announced when it appears.

## Several queries

Retry them together by returning one promise:

```tsx
<QueryErrorState
  title='Could not load this correction'
  error={sheet.error ?? files.error}
  onRetry={() => Promise.all([sheet.refetch(), files.refetch()])}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `error` | `unknown`: `Error`, string or `{ message: string }` | — |
| `title` | `I18nText` | localized "Failed to load data" |
| `description` | `I18nText`, replaces the message of `error` | message of `error` |
| `onRetry` | `() => unknown`, pending while its promise runs | no button |
| `retrying` | `boolean`, caller-driven pending | `false` |
| `retryLabel` | `I18nText` | localized "Try again" |
| `className` | `string` | — |

## Migrating a local `QueryErrorAlert`

Apps that kept a local `QueryErrorAlert({ message, onRetry })` can switch by renaming one prop:

| Local | `QueryErrorState` |
| --- | --- |
| `message="Could not load the board."` | `title="Could not load the board."` (or `description`, under the default title) |
| `onRetry={() => refetch()}` | `onRetry={refetch}`: the button now waits for the refetch |
| `message={errorMessage(error, fallback)}` | `error={error}` + `title={fallback}` |
| hard-coded "Try again" | localized default (or `retryLabel`) |

The local copies added a bottom margin (`mb-4`); pass `className='mb-4'` where the layout relied
on it.

## Related

- [DetailAlert](/docs/components/detail-alert): informational alerts without an action
- [ListPage](/docs/components/list-page): its lists already render their own error state with retry

---

# CreatePage

> Page wrapper for create forms with consistent layout

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/create-page.mdx

Page wrapper for create forms: renders a [`CreateForm`](/docs/components/create-form) from `sections` + `action`, inside a card with a title and description.

<Callout type='info' title='Dialogs are the default'>
  Generated CRUD modules create, edit and view records in [dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs).
  `CreatePage` is for the cases that need a [standalone form page](/docs/patterns/edit-page).
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { CreatePage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { createUser } from './actions'
import { formSections, validationSchema } from './config'

export default function CreateUserPage() {
  return (
    <CreatePage
      title='Create New User'
      description='Add a new user to the system'
      sections={formSections}
      action={createUser}
      validation={validationSchema}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface CreatePageProps<T = Record<string, unknown>> {
  sections: FormSection[] | readonly FormSection[] // Form sections (required)
  action: (formData: FormData) => Promise<FormActionResult<T> | void> // Server Action (required)
  defaultValues?: Partial<T> // Initial values
  validation?: z.ZodType // Zod schema

  // Layout
  title?: I18nText // Page title — without it, the form renders with no card wrapper
  description?: I18nText // Shown under the title

  // Passed to CreateForm
  submitText?: I18nText // Default: localized "Create" (dialog.createSubmit)
  cancelAction?: () => void // Cancel button handler
  onSuccess?: (result: FormActionResult<T>) => void
  grid?: string // Grid columns: '1', '2', '3', '4'
  useTabs?: boolean // Default: false
  hideButtons?: boolean // Hide submit/cancel buttons
}
```

Like `CreateForm`, it drops sections and fields marked `editOnly`, and fields of `type: 'crud'`.

---

## Examples

### Basic Create Page

```tsx
<CreatePage sections={formSections} action={createUser} />
```

### With Title and Description

```tsx
<CreatePage
  title='Create New Product'
  description='Add a new product to your catalog'
  sections={formSections}
  action={createProduct}
/>
```

### With Default Values

```tsx
<CreatePage
  title='Create Order'
  sections={formSections}
  action={createOrder}
  defaultValues={{ status: 'draft' }}
/>
```

### With Validation and Submit Text

```tsx
import { CreatePage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { createProduct } from './actions'
import { validationSchema, formSections } from './config'

export default function CreateProductPage() {
  return (
    <CreatePage
      title='Create Product'
      description='Add a new product to your inventory'
      sections={formSections}
      action={createProduct}
      validation={validationSchema}
      submitText='Create Product'
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="app/admin/users/new/page.tsx"
import { CreatePage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
import { createUser } from '../actions'
import { validationSchema, formSections } from '../config'

export default function CreateUserPage() {
  async function handleSubmit(data: FormData) {
    'use server'

    const result = await createUser(data)

    if (result.success) {
      redirect(`/admin/users/${result.data.id}`)
    }

    return result // { success: false, message, errors } reaches the form
  }

  return (
    <CreatePage
      title='Create New User'
      description='Add a new user with role and permissions'
      sections={formSections}
      action={handleSubmit}
      validation={validationSchema}
      submitText='Create User'
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **CRUD create routes** - `/admin/users/new`
- **New record forms** - Adding entities to database
- **Data entry** - User-facing creation forms
- **Onboarding** - New item setup wizards

---

## Layout Behavior

**CreatePage provides:**

1. **Card container** - Form wrapped in a card with padding (only when `title` is set)
2. **Card header** - Title and description
3. **Consistent spacing** - Standard margins and padding
4. **Responsive layout** - Mobile-friendly

Without `title`, `CreatePage` renders the bare `CreateForm`.

**Visual hierarchy:**

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│  [Title]            │
│  [Description]      │
├─────────────────────┤
│  [Form Fields]      │
│                     │
│  [Form Fields]      │
│                     │
│  [Submit] [Cancel]  │
└─────────────────────┘
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Always provide title** - Clear page context
2. **Add description** - Explain purpose when not obvious
3. **Redirect on success** - Navigate to detail or list page
4. **Handle errors** - Return `{ success: false, message, errors }` from the Server Action
5. **Cancel button** - Pass `cancelAction` (from a Client Component)

---

## Pattern: Page Config + CreatePage

**Recommended structure:**

```tsx
// config.tsx
export const validationSchema = z.object({ ... })
export const formSections: FormSection[] = [ ... ]

// adicionar/page.tsx
import { CreatePage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { createEntity } from '../actions'
import { validationSchema, formSections } from '../config'

export default function CreateEntityPage() {
  return (
    <CreatePage
      title="Create Entity"
      sections={formSections}
      action={createEntity}
      validation={validationSchema}
    />
  )
}
```

**Benefits:**

- Config centralized in one file
- Page logic minimal and clean
- Easy to maintain
- Consistent with Page Config Pattern

---

## Comparison: CreatePage vs Manual Layout

### With CreatePage (Recommended)

```tsx
// Concise
export default function CreateUserPage() {
  return (
    <CreatePage title='Create User' sections={formSections} action={createUser} />
  )
}
```

### Without CreatePage (Manual)

```tsx
// Verbose
export default function CreateUserPage() {
  return (
    <div className='container mx-auto py-6'>
      <div className='mb-6'>
        <h1 className='text-3xl font-bold'>Create User</h1>
      </div>
      <div className='bg-card rounded-lg border p-6'>
        <UserCreateForm />
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

**CreatePage provides:** Consistent styling, less boilerplate, easier maintenance.

---

## Accessibility

- Semantic HTML structure
- The title renders in a `section`, not a heading element, so it does not compete with the page `h1`
- Screen reader friendly layout

---

## Related Components

- [CreateForm](/docs/components/create-form) - Form component for creation
- [EditPage](/docs/components/edit-page) - Page wrapper for editing
- [BaseFormPage](/docs/components/base-form-page) - Base wrapper
- [ListPage](/docs/components/list-page) - List page component

- [Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) - CRUD module structure
- [CRUD Pattern](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) - Full CRUD implementation

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# EditPage

> Complete page wrapper for edit forms with tabs support

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/edit-page.mdx

Complete page wrapper for edit forms with tabs support.

<Callout type='info' title='Dialogs are the default'>
  Generated CRUD modules create, edit and view records in [dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs).
  `EditPage` is for the cases that need a [standalone form page](/docs/patterns/edit-page).
</Callout>

---

## Usage

### Basic Example

```tsx title="app/admin/users/[id]/edit/page.tsx"
import { EditPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { updateUserAction } from '../../actions'
import { formSections, validationSchema } from '../../config'
import { getUser } from '@/services/users'

export default async function EditUserPage({ params }) {
  const { id } = await params
  const user = await getUser(id)

  return (
    <EditPage
      id={id}
      data={user}
      sections={formSections}
      action={updateUserAction}
      validation={validationSchema}
      useTabs={true}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Features

### 1. Required Props Enforcement

TypeScript enforces `id` and `data` as required:

```tsx
// ✅ Correct - id and data required
<EditPage
  id={user.id}
  data={user}
  sections={formSections}
  action={updateAction}
/>

// ❌ Error - TypeScript error without id or data
<EditPage
  sections={formSections}
  action={updateAction}
/>
```

### 2. Nested Data

EditPage takes nested data (e.g. a Prisma `include`) as is; fields named with dot notation read and submit the nested values:

```tsx
// Prisma returns nested data
const user = await prisma.user.findUnique({
  where: { id },
  include: {
    person: true, // Nested object
  },
})

// user = {
//   id: "1",
//   person: { name: "John", cpf: "12345" }
// }

// A field named 'person.name' shows "John";
// on submit, the FormData carries 'person.name' and 'person.cpf'
```

So the fields only need the dotted names:

```tsx
const formSections: FormSection[] = [
  {
    label: 'Person',
    fields: [
      { name: 'person.name', label: 'Name', type: 'text' },
      { name: 'person.cpf', label: 'CPF', type: 'text' },
    ],
  },
]
```

### 3. Tab Support

Enable tabs for complex forms with multiple sections:

```tsx
<EditPage
  id={id}
  data={data}
  sections={formSections}
  action={updateAction}
  useTabs={true} // ← Renders sections as tabs
/>
```

### 4. Submit Text

Default submit text is the localized "Save" (`common.save`):

```tsx
<EditPage
  id={id}
  data={data}
  sections={formSections}
  action={updateAction}
  submitText='Update User' // Custom text
/>
```

---

## Props

```tsx
interface EditPageProps<T = Record<string, unknown>> {
  // Required
  id: string // Entity ID
  data: Partial<T> // Entity data (nested data is fine)
  sections: FormSection[] | readonly FormSection[] // Form sections
  action: (formData: FormData) => Promise<FormActionResult<T> | void>

  // Validation
  validation?: z.ZodType // Zod validation schema

  // Layout
  title?: I18nText // Page title — without it, the form renders with no wrapper
  description?: I18nText // Shown under the title

  // UI
  submitText?: I18nText // Default: localized "Save"
  cancelAction?: () => void // Cancel button handler
  grid?: string // Grid columns: '1', '2', '3', '4'
  hideButtons?: boolean // Hide submit/cancel buttons
  useTabs?: boolean // Render sections as tabs (default: true)

  // Callbacks
  onSuccess?: (result: FormActionResult<T>) => void
}
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="app/admin/processes/[id]/edit/edit-process.tsx"
'use client'

import { EditPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
import { updateProcessAction } from '../../actions'
import { formSections, validationSchema } from '../../config'

// Rendered by the Server Component page, which fetches `process`
export function EditProcess({ id, process }) {
  const router = useRouter()

  return (
    <EditPage
      id={id}
      data={process}
      title='Edit Process'
      sections={formSections}
      action={updateProcessAction}
      validation={validationSchema}
      useTabs={true}
      submitText='Update Process'
      onSuccess={result => {
        if (result.success) {
          router.push(`/admin/processes/${id}`)
        }
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## EditPage vs AdminForm

| Feature               | EditPage      | AdminForm |
| --------------------- | ------------- | --------- |
| **Purpose**           | Edit-specific | Generic   |
| **id prop**           | ✅ Required   | Optional  |
| **data prop**         | ✅ Required   | Optional  |
| **Nested data**       | ✅ As is      | ✅ As is  |
| **Title card**        | ✅ `title`    | ❌        |
| **Submit text**       | "Save"        | "Save"    |
| **TypeScript safety** | ✅ High       | ⚠️ Medium |
| **Use case**          | Edit pages    | Any form  |

**Recommendation:** Use `EditPage` for edit pages: `id` and `data` are required, so a missing record fails at compile time.

---

## Nested Data Pattern

Pass the record as it comes from the database; there is no need to flatten it first:

```tsx
'use client'

import { EditPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function EditUserForm({ user }) {
  return (
    <EditPage
      id={user.id}
      data={user} // { person: { name, cpf }, address: { street, city } }
      sections={formSections} // fields named 'person.name', 'address.city', ...
      action={updateAction}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## With Server Actions

```tsx title="app/admin/users/[id]/edit/page.tsx"
import { EditPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { updateUserAction } from '../../actions'
import { formSections } from '../../config'
import { getUser } from '@/services/users'

export default async function EditUserPage({ params }) {
  const { id } = await params
  const user = await getUser(id)

  return (
    <EditPage
      id={id}
      data={user}
      sections={formSections}
      action={updateUserAction}
    />
  )
}
```

```tsx title="actions.ts"
'use server'

import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
import { updateUser } from '@/services/users'

export async function updateUserAction(formData: FormData) {
  const id = formData.get('id') as string
  const data = Object.fromEntries(formData)

  const result = await updateUser(id, data)

  if (result.success) {
    revalidatePath(`/admin/users/${id}`)
    revalidatePath('/admin/users')
  }

  return result
}
```

---

## Best Practices

### 1. Always Use for Edit Pages

```tsx
// ✅ Good - Semantic and type-safe
<EditPage id={id} data={data} sections={sections} action={updateAction} />

// ❌ Bad - Less semantic
<AdminForm id={id} data={data} sections={sections} action={updateAction} />
```

### 2. Enable Tabs for Complex Forms

```tsx
// ✅ Good - Better UX for 4+ sections
<EditPage
  id={id}
  data={data}
  sections={formSections}
  action={updateAction}
  useTabs={true}
/>
```

### 3. Handle Success Callbacks

```tsx
<EditPage
  id={id}
  data={data}
  sections={sections}
  action={updateAction}
  onSuccess={result => {
    if (result.success) {
      toast.success('Updated successfully!')
      router.push(`/admin/entity/${id}`)
    }
  }}
/>
```

### 4. Fetch Data Server-Side

```tsx
// ✅ Good - Server Component
export default async function EditEntityPage({ params }) {
  const { id } = await params
  const data = await getData(id)  // Server-side fetch

  return <EditPage id={id} data={data} ... />
}

// ❌ Bad - Client Component with loading state
'use client'
export default function EditEntityPage({ params }) {
  const [data, setData] = useState(null)
  useEffect(() => { fetchData() }, [])  // Unnecessary complexity

  if (!data) return <Loading />
  return <EditPage id={params.id} data={data} ... />
}
```

- [EditForm](/docs/components/edit-form) - Edit form wrapper (lower level)

  Use EditPage for standalone edit pages: required `id`/`data`, nested data
  as is, and an optional title card.
</Callout>

# BaseFormPage

> DRY wrapper for form pages with conditional PageContent wrapping

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/base-form-page.mdx

Base wrapper component for form pages that provides consistent layout with conditional PageContent wrapping.

<Callout type='info' title='Dialogs are the default'>
  Generated CRUD modules create, edit and view records in [dialogs](/docs/patterns/dialogs).
  `BaseFormPage` is for the cases that need a [standalone form page](/docs/patterns/edit-page).
</Callout>

`BaseFormPage` is the layer under `CreatePage` and `EditPage`; most standalone pages should use those instead.

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { BaseFormPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { UserForm } from './form'

export default function CreateUserPage() {
  return (
    <BaseFormPage
      formComponent={<UserForm />}
      title='Create User'
      variant='card'
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface BaseFormPageProps {
  formComponent: React.ReactNode // Form component (required)
  title?: I18nText // Page title — without it, formComponent renders bare
  description?: I18nText // Shown under the title
  variant?: 'card' | 'plain' // PageContent variant (default: 'card')
}

// With a title:
// 'card': PageContent with a card (title in the card header)
// 'plain': PageContent without a card (title above the form)
// Without a title, `variant` is ignored and formComponent renders as is.
```

---

## Variants

### Card Variant (Default)

```tsx
<BaseFormPage formComponent={<MyForm />} title='Create Item' variant='card' />
```

**Result:**

- Form wrapped in PageContent
- Card-style container with padding
- Consistent spacing and borders
- Best for standard forms

### Plain Variant

```tsx
<BaseFormPage formComponent={<MyForm />} title='Edit Item' variant='plain' />
```

**Result:**

- Form wrapped in PageContent, without a card
- Title and description above the form
- Used by `EditPage`

### No Title

```tsx
<BaseFormPage formComponent={<MyForm />} />
```

**Result:**

- Form rendered directly, no PageContent wrapper
- Full layout control to the form component
- Best for custom layouts or multi-step wizards

---

## Examples

### With Title and Description

```tsx
<BaseFormPage
  formComponent={<UserForm />}
  title='Create New User'
  description='Add a new user to the system with role and permissions'
  variant='card'
/>
```

### Custom Layout (No Title)

```tsx
<BaseFormPage
  formComponent={
    <div className='max-w-4xl mx-auto p-6'>
      <h1>Custom Form Layout</h1>
      <MultiStepForm />
    </div>
  }
/>
```

---

## Use Cases

**✅ When to use BaseFormPage:**

- Building custom page wrappers (like CreatePage, EditPage)
- Need conditional PageContent wrapping
- Creating domain-specific form page components

**❌ When NOT to use BaseFormPage:**

- Regular form pages → Use `CreatePage` or `EditPage`
- Custom layouts → Use form components directly
- Multi-step wizards → Use `ZustandForm` with custom layout

---

## Used By

BaseFormPage is the foundation for these components:

### CreatePage

```tsx
// CreatePage, simplified
export function CreatePage({ title, description, ...formProps }: CreatePageProps) {
  return (
    <BaseFormPage
      formComponent={<CreateForm {...formProps} />}
      title={title}
      description={description}
      variant='card'
    />
  )
}
```

### EditPage

```tsx
// EditPage, simplified
export function EditPage({ title, description, ...formProps }: EditPageProps) {
  return (
    <BaseFormPage
      formComponent={<EditForm {...formProps} />}
      title={title}
      description={description}
      variant='plain'
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/custom-wizard-page.tsx"
import { BaseFormPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { MultiStepWizard, type WizardStep } from './wizard'

interface CustomWizardPageProps {
  title: string
  steps: WizardStep[]
}

export function CustomWizardPage({ title, steps }: CustomWizardPageProps) {
  return (
    <BaseFormPage
      formComponent={
        <div className='container max-w-4xl mx-auto py-8'>
          <div className='mb-8'>
            <h1 className='text-3xl font-bold'>{title}</h1>
            <p className='text-muted-foreground'>
              Complete all steps to finish the process
            </p>
          </div>
          <MultiStepWizard steps={steps} />
        </div>
      }
    />
  )
}

// Usage
export default function OnboardingPage() {
  return <CustomWizardPage title='User Onboarding' steps={onboardingSteps} />
}
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Prefer high-level wrappers** - Use CreatePage/EditPage when possible
2. **Card for standard forms** - Use `variant="card"` for typical CRUD forms
3. **No title for custom layouts** - Omit `title` when the form handles its own layout
4. **Title and description** - Add context for users
5. **Reusable wrappers** - Create domain-specific wrappers on top of BaseFormPage

---

## Comparison: BaseFormPage vs Higher-Level Wrappers

| Feature         | BaseFormPage          | CreatePage           | EditPage          |
| --------------- | --------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------- |
| **Purpose**     | Base wrapper          | Create forms         | Edit forms        |
| **Variant**     | Flexible              | Always `card`        | Always `plain`    |
| **Form filter** | None                  | Filters `editOnly` and `crud` | None     |
| **Props**       | Minimal               | CreateForm-specific  | EditForm-specific |
| **Use when**    | Building custom pages | Creating new records | Editing existing  |

---

## Architecture Benefits

**DRY principle:**

- Eliminates duplicated PageContent logic
- Centralized layout handling
- Consistent page structure

**Flexibility:**

- `variant` prop allows card or plain layouts
- Works with any form component
- Extensible for custom wrappers
- Single source of truth for form page layout

---

- [CreatePage](/docs/components/create-page) - High-level create page wrapper
- [EditPage](/docs/components/edit-page) - High-level edit page wrapper
- [CreateForm](/docs/components/create-form) - Form for creation
- [EditForm](/docs/components/edit-form) - Form for editing

---

- [Form Pattern](/docs/patterns/form-pattern) - Complete form pattern guide
- [Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) - CRUD module structure
