# DetailStatsGrid

> Grid of metric cards for displaying statistics

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/detail-stats-grid.mdx

Grid component for displaying metrics, KPIs, and statistics in detail pages.

<Callout type='info' title='Detail Components Pattern'>
  `DetailStatsGrid` is part of the [Detail Components
  Pattern](/docs/patterns/detail-page).
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { DetailStatsGrid } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function UserDetail({ stats }) {
  return (
    <DetailStatsGrid
      stats={[
        { label: 'Total Posts', value: stats.postsCount },
        { label: 'Comments', value: stats.commentsCount },
        { label: 'Likes', value: stats.likesCount },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface DetailStatsGridProps {
  stats: StatConfig[] // Array of stats to display
  columns?: 2 | 3 | 4 // Number of columns (default: 2)
  className?: string // Additional classes
}

interface StatConfig {
  label: I18nText // Stat label
  value: string | number | React.ReactNode // Stat value
  icon?: LucideIcon // Optional icon before the label
  color?: 'default' | 'success' | 'danger' | 'warning' | 'info' // Value text color (default: 'default')
  description?: I18nText // Optional text below the value
}
```

`StatConfig` is exported from `@telamonjs/ui` and `@telamonjs/ui/detail`. There is no `trend`, `href` or `variant` prop.

---

## Examples

### Basic Stats

```tsx
<DetailStatsGrid
  stats={[
    { label: 'Revenue', value: '$12,345' },
    { label: 'Users', value: 1234 },
    { label: 'Orders', value: 567 },
  ]}
/>
```

Displays the stats in a 2-column grid (the default).

### With Icons

```tsx
import { DollarSign, Users, ShoppingCart, TrendingUp } from 'lucide-react'
;<DetailStatsGrid
  stats={[
    { label: 'Revenue', value: '$12,345', icon: DollarSign },
    { label: 'Users', value: 1234, icon: Users },
    { label: 'Orders', value: 567, icon: ShoppingCart },
    { label: 'Growth', value: '+23%', icon: TrendingUp },
  ]}
/>
```

Icons improve visual recognition and hierarchy.

### With Colors and Descriptions

```tsx
<DetailStatsGrid
  columns={3}
  stats={[
    {
      label: 'Revenue',
      value: '$12,345',
      color: 'success',
      description: '+12% vs last month',
    },
    {
      label: 'Users',
      value: 1234,
      color: 'info',
      description: '+5% vs last month',
    },
    {
      label: 'Churn',
      value: '2.3%',
      color: 'danger',
      description: '-0.5% vs last month',
    },
  ]}
/>
```

`color` tints the value text; `description` adds context below it.

### Linked Values

```tsx
<DetailStatsGrid
  stats={[
    {
      label: 'Posts',
      value: <Link href={`/users/${userId}/posts`}>42</Link>,
    },
    {
      label: 'Comments',
      value: <Link href={`/users/${userId}/comments`}>128</Link>,
    },
  ]}
/>
```

`value` accepts a `ReactNode`, so a link can drill down to the related list.

### Custom Columns

```tsx
// 2 columns
<DetailStatsGrid
  columns={2}
  stats={stats}
/>

// 4 columns
<DetailStatsGrid
  columns={4}
  stats={stats}
/>
```

---

## Responsive Behavior

The grid uses `grid-cols-{columns}` at every screen size: it does not collapse on mobile. For narrow containers, use `columns={2}` or pass breakpoint classes through `className` (e.g. `className='grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4'`).

---

## Complete Example

```tsx
import { DetailStatsGrid } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { DollarSign, Users, ShoppingCart, TrendingUp } from 'lucide-react'

export default function DashboardStats({ stats }) {
  return (
    <DetailStatsGrid
      columns={4}
      stats={[
        {
          label: 'Total Revenue',
          value: `$${stats.revenue.toLocaleString()}`,
          icon: DollarSign,
          color: stats.revenue > stats.lastMonthRevenue ? 'success' : 'danger',
          description: `${stats.revenueGrowth}% vs last month`,
        },
        {
          label: 'Active Users',
          value: stats.activeUsers.toLocaleString(),
          icon: Users,
          description: '+12% vs last month',
        },
        {
          label: 'Total Orders',
          value: stats.orders.toLocaleString(),
          icon: ShoppingCart,
          description: '+8% vs last month',
        },
        {
          label: 'Conversion Rate',
          value: `${stats.conversionRate}%`,
          icon: TrendingUp,
          color: stats.conversionRate > 3 ? 'success' : 'default',
          description: '+0.5% vs last month',
        },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Keep metrics simple** - Show only the most important KPIs
2. **Use consistent time ranges** - All comparisons should cover the same periods
3. **Add context** - Use descriptions to explain what the numbers mean
4. **Use color for meaning** - `success`/`danger`/`warning` only when the value signals something
5. **Limit number of stats** - 3-6 stats per grid for optimal readability
6. **Format numbers** - Use locale formatting for large numbers

---

## When to Use

Use `DetailStatsGrid` when:

- ✅ Displaying metrics/KPIs in dashboard or detail pages
- ✅ Showing summary statistics at the top of a page
- ✅ Comparing multiple data points side-by-side
- ✅ Building analytics or reporting interfaces

**Don't use when:**

- ❌ Displaying single metrics → Use DetailCard with single value
- ❌ Complex charts needed → Use Chart components
- ❌ Tabular data → Use DataTable

---

## Accessibility

- Each stat is a card with its label as visible text
- Icons are decorative and sit next to the visible label
- Color is never the only signal: pair it with a `description`

---

## Related Components

- [DetailCard](/docs/components/detail-card) - Card for grouping fields
- [DetailLayout](/docs/components/detail-layout) - Page layout
- [BarChart](/docs/components/bar-chart) - For detailed charts
- [LineChart](/docs/components/line-chart) - For trend visualization

---

## See Also

- [Detail Views](/docs/patterns/detail-page) - Complete pattern guide
- [Dashboard Components](/docs/components#dashboard) - Dashboard-specific components

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

---

# DetailStatus

> Status badge component for displaying entity states

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/detail-status.mdx

Status badge component that maps a raw status value (e.g. `'PENDING'`) to a label, badge variant and optional icon through a config object.

<Callout type='info' title='Detail Components Pattern'>
  `DetailStatus` is part of the [Detail Components
  Pattern](/docs/patterns/detail-page).
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { DetailCard, DetailField, DetailStatus } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function OrderDetail({ order }) {
  return (
    <DetailCard title='Order Info'>
      <DetailField
        label='Status'
        value={
          <DetailStatus
            status={order.status}
            statusConfig={{
              PENDING: { label: 'Pending', variant: 'secondary' },
              COMPLETED: { label: 'Completed', variant: 'default' },
              CANCELLED: { label: 'Cancelled', variant: 'destructive' },
            }}
          />
        }
      />
    </DetailCard>
  )
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface DetailStatusProps {
  status: string // Current status value (e.g. 'ACTIVE', 'PENDING')
  statusConfig: Record<string, StatusConfig> // Status value → display config
  fallback?: StatusConfig // Config for values missing from statusConfig
}

interface StatusConfig {
  label: I18nText // Text shown in the badge
  variant: 'default' | 'secondary' | 'destructive' | 'outline' // Badge variant
  icon?: LucideIcon // Optional icon before the label
  className?: string // Extra classes (e.g. custom colors)
}
```

`DetailStatusProps` and `StatusConfig` are exported from `@telamonjs/ui` and `@telamonjs/ui/detail`. There is no `variant`, `icon` or `pulse` prop on `DetailStatus` itself: everything comes from the config entry.

When `status` is not in `statusConfig` and no `fallback` is given, the raw status is shown as the label with the `outline` variant.

---

## Examples

### Badge Variants

```tsx
const statusConfig: Record<string, StatusConfig> = {
  ACTIVE: { label: 'Active', variant: 'default' },
  INACTIVE: { label: 'Inactive', variant: 'secondary' },
  BLOCKED: { label: 'Blocked', variant: 'destructive' },
  DRAFT: { label: 'Draft', variant: 'outline' },
}

<DetailStatus status={user.status} statusConfig={statusConfig} />
```

**Visual mapping:**

- **default** - Primary color (active, completed)
- **secondary** - Muted (inactive, archived)
- **destructive** - Red (failed, cancelled, blocked)
- **outline** - Bordered, neutral (draft, unknown)

### With Icons and Custom Colors

```tsx
import { CheckCircle, Clock, XCircle } from 'lucide-react'

const orderStatusConfig: Record<string, StatusConfig> = {
  APPROVED: {
    label: 'Approved',
    variant: 'outline',
    icon: CheckCircle,
    className: 'border-green-600 text-green-700',
  },
  PENDING: {
    label: 'Pending Review',
    variant: 'outline',
    icon: Clock,
    className: 'border-yellow-500 text-yellow-700',
  },
  REJECTED: { label: 'Rejected', variant: 'destructive', icon: XCircle },
}

<DetailStatus status={order.status} statusConfig={orderStatusConfig} />
```

Use `className` for colors the four badge variants don't cover.

### Fallback for Unknown Values

```tsx
<DetailStatus
  status={order.status}
  statusConfig={orderStatusConfig}
  fallback={{ label: 'Unknown', variant: 'outline' }}
/>
```

### Shared Config

```tsx title="lib/status-configs.ts"
import type { StatusConfig } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export const orderStatusConfig: Record<string, StatusConfig> = {
  DRAFT: { label: 'Draft', variant: 'outline' },
  PENDING: { label: 'Pending', variant: 'secondary' },
  COMPLETED: { label: 'Completed', variant: 'default' },
  CANCELLED: { label: 'Cancelled', variant: 'destructive' },
}
```

Centralized mapping ensures consistent status colors across the app.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx
import { DetailCard, DetailStatus, DetailField } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import type { StatusConfig } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { CheckCircle, Clock, XCircle } from 'lucide-react'

const orderStatusConfig: Record<string, StatusConfig> = {
  DRAFT: { label: 'Draft', variant: 'outline' },
  PENDING: { label: 'Pending', variant: 'secondary', icon: Clock },
  PROCESSING: { label: 'Processing', variant: 'secondary', icon: Clock },
  COMPLETED: { label: 'Completed', variant: 'default', icon: CheckCircle },
  CANCELLED: { label: 'Cancelled', variant: 'destructive', icon: XCircle },
}

export default function OrderDetail({ order }: { order: Order }) {
  return (
    <DetailCard title='Order Information'>
      <DetailField label='Order ID' value={order.id} />
      <DetailField
        label='Status'
        value={
          <DetailStatus
            status={order.status}
            statusConfig={orderStatusConfig}
          />
        }
      />
      <DetailField label='Total' value={`$${order.total}`} />
      <DetailField
        label='Created'
        value={new Date(order.createdAt).toLocaleDateString()}
      />
    </DetailCard>
  )
}
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Consistent color mapping** - Use the same config for the same entity across the app
2. **Add icons when needed** - Improve recognition for common statuses
3. **Centralize configs** - Keep one `Record<string, StatusConfig>` per entity
4. **Provide a fallback** - Handle values the backend may add later
5. **Semantic variants** - Choose variant based on meaning, not aesthetics

---

## Variant Guidelines

| Variant         | Use For                    | Examples                              |
| --------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| **default**     | Positive, completed states | Active, Approved, Published, Verified |
| **secondary**   | Intermediate, muted states | Pending, Inactive, Archived           |
| **destructive** | Negative, failed states    | Rejected, Cancelled, Failed, Blocked  |
| **outline**     | Neutral, unknown           | Draft, Unknown, N/A                   |

---

## Accessibility

- Status is always shown as text (not color alone)
- Sufficient color contrast ratios (WCAG AA) on the built-in variants
- Icons are decorative; the label carries the meaning

---

## Related Components

- [DetailField](/docs/components/detail-field) - Display label-value pairs
- [DetailCard](/docs/components/detail-card) - Card wrapper
- [StatusBadge](/docs/components/status-badge) - Standalone status badge
- Badge - General purpose badge (lower-level)

---

## See Also

- [Detail Views](/docs/patterns/detail-page) - Complete pattern guide
- [Quick Start](/docs/getting-started/quick-start) - CRUD example

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# DetailAlert

> Alert component for displaying contextual messages in detail pages

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/detail-alert.mdx

Alert component for displaying contextual messages, warnings, and important information in detail pages.

<Callout type='info' title='Detail Components Pattern'>
  `DetailAlert` is part of the [Detail Components
  Pattern](/docs/patterns/detail-page).
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { DetailLayout, DetailAlert } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function UserDetail({ user }) {
  return (
    <DetailLayout
      title={user.name}
      alerts={[
        {
          variant: 'warning',
          title: 'Email Not Verified',
          message: 'This user has not verified their email address.',
        },
      ]}
      leftColumn={<UserInfo user={user} />}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface DetailAlertProps {
  variant?: AlertVariant // Visual variant (default: 'info')
  title: I18nText // Alert title (required)
  message?: I18nText | React.ReactNode // Alert message, plain or rich content
  icon?: LucideIcon // Custom icon (overrides default)
  dismissible?: boolean // Show a close button (default: false)
  onDismiss?: () => void // Dismiss callback (the button renders only when set)
  className?: string // Additional classes
}

type AlertVariant =
  | 'info' // Blue - Informational
  | 'success' // Green - Success messages
  | 'warning' // Yellow - Warnings
  | 'danger' // Red - Errors
```

---

## Examples

### Alert Variants

```tsx
<div className='space-y-4'>
  <DetailAlert
    variant='info'
    title='Information'
    message='This is an informational message.'
  />

  <DetailAlert
    variant='success'
    title='Success'
    message='Your changes have been saved successfully.'
  />

  <DetailAlert
    variant='warning'
    title='Warning'
    message='This action cannot be undone. Please proceed with caution.'
  />

  <DetailAlert
    variant='danger'
    title='Error'
    message='An error occurred while processing your request.'
  />
</div>
```

**Default icons:**

- **info** - Info icon (blue)
- **success** - CheckCircle2 icon (green)
- **warning** - AlertTriangle icon (yellow)
- **danger** - AlertCircle icon (red)

### Without Message

```tsx
<DetailAlert variant='info' title='User has been inactive for 30 days.' />
```

`title` is required; `message` is optional for simple notices.

### Dismissible Alerts

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'

export default function UserDetail({ user }) {
  const [showAlert, setShowAlert] = useState(true)

  if (!showAlert) return null

  return (
    <DetailAlert
      variant='warning'
      title='Action Required'
      message='Please update your profile information.'
      dismissible
      onDismiss={() => setShowAlert(false)}
    />
  )
}
```

Adds a close button that calls `onDismiss` when clicked.

### With Action Buttons

```tsx
<DetailAlert
  variant='warning'
  title='Subscription Expiring'
  message={
    <div className='space-y-2'>
      <p>Your subscription expires in 3 days.</p>
      <div className='flex gap-2'>
        <Button variant='outline' size='sm'>
          Remind Me Later
        </Button>
        <Button size='sm'>Renew Now</Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  }
/>
```

There is no `actions` prop: `message` accepts a `ReactNode`, so put buttons inside it.

### Custom Icons

```tsx
import { Mail } from 'lucide-react'
;<DetailAlert
  variant='info'
  title='Email Verification'
  message='Check your inbox for a verification email.'
  icon={Mail}
/>
```

Override default icon with custom Lucide icon.

### In DetailLayout (Recommended)

```tsx
<DetailLayout
  title='User Profile'
  alerts={[
    {
      variant: 'warning',
      title: 'Email Not Verified',
      message: 'This user has not verified their email address.',
    },
    {
      variant: 'info',
      title: 'Last Login',
      message: 'User last logged in 2 hours ago.',
    },
  ]}
  leftColumn={<UserInfo user={user} />}
/>
```

DetailLayout renders alerts at the top of the page automatically.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx
'use client'

import { DetailLayout, DetailAlert, DetailCard } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'
import { useState } from 'react'

export default function OrderDetail({ order }) {
  const [alertDismissed, setAlertDismissed] = useState(false)

  const alerts = []

  // Conditional alerts based on order status
  if (order.status === 'PENDING' && !alertDismissed) {
    alerts.push({
      variant: 'warning' as const,
      title: 'Payment Pending',
      message: (
        <div className='space-y-2'>
          <p>This order is awaiting payment confirmation.</p>
          <Button size='sm' onClick={() => handleSendReminder(order.id)}>
            Send Payment Reminder
          </Button>
        </div>
      ),
      dismissible: true,
      onDismiss: () => setAlertDismissed(true),
    })
  }

  if (order.shippingDelay) {
    alerts.push({
      variant: 'danger' as const,
      title: 'Shipping Delayed',
      message: `Expected delivery delayed by ${order.shippingDelay} days due to carrier issues.`,
    })
  }

  if (order.refundProcessing) {
    alerts.push({
      variant: 'info' as const,
      title: 'Refund Processing',
      message:
        'A refund is being processed for this order. It will be completed within 5-7 business days.',
    })
  }

  return (
    <DetailLayout
      title={`Order #${order.id}`}
      alerts={alerts}
      leftColumn={
        <DetailCard title='Order Details'>{/* Order details */}</DetailCard>
      }
    />
  )
}

async function handleSendReminder(orderId: string) {
  // Send payment reminder logic
}
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Use appropriate variants** - Choose variant based on severity
2. **Keep messages concise** - 1-2 sentences max for better scannability
3. **Provide actions when needed** - Help users resolve the issue
4. **Don't overuse** - Too many alerts reduce effectiveness
5. **Make dismissible when appropriate** - Non-critical info should be dismissible
6. **Position at top** - Use DetailLayout's alerts prop for page-level alerts

---

## Variant Guidelines

| Variant     | Use For                | Examples                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| **info**    | Informational messages | Updates, tips, notifications                      |
| **success** | Positive confirmations | Saved, updated, completed actions                 |
| **warning** | Important notices      | Missing data, expiring items, confirmation needed |
| **danger**  | Critical issues        | Errors, failures, blocked actions                 |

---

## When to Use

Use `DetailAlert` when:

- ✅ Displaying contextual warnings/errors on detail pages
- ✅ Showing status updates or notifications
- ✅ Providing actionable feedback
- ✅ Highlighting important information requiring attention

**Don't use when:**

- ❌ Global app-level notifications → Use Toast/Notification system
- ❌ Form validation errors → Use field-level errors
- ❌ Loading states → Use Skeleton/Spinner
- ❌ Static help text → Use regular text/Callout

---

## Accessibility

- Proper color contrast ratios (WCAG AA)
- Icons complement text (not sole indicator)
- Keyboard navigable dismiss button with a localized `aria-label`
- No `role="alert"`: the alert is static content, not a live announcement

---

## Related Components

- [DetailLayout](/docs/components/detail-layout) - Page layout with built-in alerts
- Callout - Documentation callouts (docs sites)
- Toast - Temporary notifications

---

## See Also

- [Detail Views](/docs/patterns/detail-page) - Complete pattern guide
- [Quick Start](/docs/getting-started/quick-start) - CRUD example

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# DetailAvatar

> Avatar component with fallback initials and zoomable preview

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/detail-avatar.mdx

Avatar component for displaying user profile pictures with automatic fallback to initials and optional zoom preview.

<Callout type='info' title='Detail Components Pattern'>
  `DetailAvatar` is part of the [Detail Components
  Pattern](/docs/patterns/detail-page).
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { DetailCard, DetailAvatar } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function UserDetail({ user }) {
  return (
    <DetailCard title='Profile'>
      <DetailAvatar name={user.name} imageUrl={user.avatar} />
    </DetailCard>
  )
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface DetailAvatarProps {
  name: string // Person's name (shown beside the avatar; first letter is the fallback)
  subtitle?: string // Secondary text below the name (e.g. email, enrollment)
  imageUrl?: string // Avatar image URL
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' // Avatar size (default: 'lg')
  fallbackColor?: string // Tailwind gradient classes for the fallback (default: 'from-blue-500 to-indigo-600')
  zoomable?: boolean // Click-to-zoom preview (default: true)
  className?: string // Additional classes
}
```

**Sizes:**

- `sm` - 64×64px
- `md` - 80×80px
- `lg` - 96×96px (default)
- `xl` - 128×128px

---

## Examples

### Basic Avatar

```tsx
<DetailAvatar name='John Doe' imageUrl='https://example.com/avatar.jpg' />
```

Displays avatar image with rounded circle.

### Without Image (Initials Fallback)

```tsx
<DetailAvatar name='John Doe' />
```

When no `imageUrl` is provided (or the image fails to load), displays the first letter "J" on a gradient background.

### Different Sizes

```tsx
<div className='flex items-center gap-4'>
  <DetailAvatar name='John Doe' imageUrl={url} size='sm' />
  <DetailAvatar name='John Doe' imageUrl={url} size='md' />
  <DetailAvatar name='John Doe' imageUrl={url} size='lg' />
  <DetailAvatar name='John Doe' imageUrl={url} size='xl' />
</div>
```

### Zoomable Preview

```tsx
<DetailAvatar name='John Doe' imageUrl={user.avatar} size='lg' zoomable />
```

Clicking avatar opens full-size preview modal. Zoom is on by default; pass `zoomable={false}` to disable it.

### With Subtitle

```tsx
<DetailAvatar
  name='John Doe'
  subtitle='john@example.com'
  imageUrl={user.avatar}
/>
```

The name and subtitle render beside the avatar.

### Custom Fallback Color

```tsx
<DetailAvatar name='Acme Corp' fallbackColor='from-emerald-500 to-teal-600' />
```

`fallbackColor` takes the Tailwind gradient classes used when there is no image.

### In Two-Column Layout

```tsx
<DetailLayout
  title={user.name}
  leftColumn={<UserInfoCard user={user} />}
  rightColumn={
    <DetailCard title='Profile Picture'>
      <DetailAvatar
        name={user.name}
        imageUrl={user.avatar}
        size='xl'
        zoomable
      />
    </DetailCard>
  }
/>
```

Common pattern: Avatar in right sidebar.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx
import {
  DetailLayout,
  DetailCard,
  DetailAvatar,
  DetailField,
  DetailStatus,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { User, Mail, Calendar } from 'lucide-react'

export default function UserDetailPage({ user }) {
  return (
    <DetailLayout
      title={user.name}
      description={user.email}
      leftColumn={
        <DetailCard title='User Information' icon={User}>
          <DetailField label='Name' value={user.name} />
          <DetailField label='Email' value={user.email} icon={Mail} />
          <DetailField label='Role' value={user.role} />
          <DetailField
            label='Status'
            value={
              <DetailStatus
                status={user.active ? 'ACTIVE' : 'INACTIVE'}
                statusConfig={{
                  ACTIVE: { label: 'Active', variant: 'default' },
                  INACTIVE: { label: 'Inactive', variant: 'secondary' },
                }}
              />
            }
          />
          <DetailField
            label='Member Since'
            value={new Date(user.createdAt).toLocaleDateString()}
            icon={Calendar}
          />
        </DetailCard>
      }
      rightColumn={
        <DetailCard title='Profile Picture'>
          <div className='flex flex-col items-center gap-4'>
            <DetailAvatar
              name={user.name}
              imageUrl={user.avatar}
              size='xl'
              zoomable
            />
            <Button variant='outline' size='sm'>
              Upload New Photo
            </Button>
          </div>
        </DetailCard>
      }
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Fallback Behavior

### Image States:

1. **Success:** Displays image
2. **Error:** Falls back to the initial
3. **No URL:** Shows the initial immediately

### Initial:

```typescript
// "John Doe" → "J"  (first character, uppercased)
// "mary" → "M"
```

### Background Color:

The fallback uses the `fallbackColor` gradient (default `from-blue-500 to-indigo-600`) for every name.

---

## Best Practices

1. **Always provide name** - Required for accessibility and fallback
2. **Use zoomable for profile pages** - Let users view full-size image
3. **Optimize images** - Resize to 256×256px or smaller for performance
4. **Handle missing images** - The initial fallback ensures graceful degradation
5. **Choose appropriate size** - sm for lists, lg/xl for detail pages

---

## Performance

**Image Optimization:**

- Uses Next.js `<Image>` component internally
- Automatic WebP/AVIF conversion and lazy loading (Next.js defaults)
- Remote image hosts must be allowed in `next.config` `images.remotePatterns`

**Recommendations:**

- Serve images from CDN
- Size images at 2x desired display size (for retina)

---

## Accessibility

- Semantic `<img>` with proper alt text (user name)
- The name is rendered as visible text next to the avatar
- Zoom trigger is a `<button>` with a localized `aria-label`
- Focus trap in zoom preview
- Escape key closes modal

- [DetailLayout](/docs/components/detail-layout) - Page layout

- [Detail Views](/docs/patterns/detail-page) - Complete pattern guide
- Image Optimization Guide - Best practices for images

# DetailActions

> Action buttons card for detail pages with common operations

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/detail-actions.mdx

Card component for displaying action buttons in detail pages with consistent styling and layout.

<Callout type='info' title='Detail Components Pattern'>
  `DetailActions` is part of the [Detail Components
  Pattern](/docs/patterns/detail-page).
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { DetailActions } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function UserDetail({ user }) {
  return (
    <DetailActions
      actions={[
        {
          label: 'Edit',
          href: `/admin/users/${user.id}/edit`,
          variant: 'default',
        },
        {
          label: 'Delete',
          onClick: () => handleDelete(user.id),
          variant: 'destructive',
        },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface DetailActionsProps {
  actions: ActionButton[] // Array of actions
  title?: I18nText // Card title (default: "Quick Actions")
  layout?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' // Layout direction (default: 'vertical')
  className?: string // Additional classes
}

interface ActionButton {
  label: I18nText // Button text
  href?: string // Link destination (renders a Next.js Link)
  onClick?: () => void // Click handler (for operations)
  variant?: ButtonVariant // Button visual style (default: 'outline')
  size?: 'default' | 'sm' | 'lg' | 'icon' // Button size (default: 'sm')
  icon?: LucideIcon // Optional icon (Lucide)
  disabled?: boolean // Disable action
  loading?: boolean // Show loading state
  showExternalIcon?: boolean // Arrow icon after the label (href actions only)
  id?: string // Identifier used for the test ID
}

type ButtonVariant =
  | 'default'
  | 'destructive'
  | 'outline'
  | 'secondary'
  | 'ghost'
  | 'link'
```

`DetailActionsProps` and `ActionButton` are exported from `@telamonjs/ui` and `@telamonjs/ui/detail`.

---

## Examples

### Basic Actions

```tsx
<DetailActions
  actions={[
    { label: 'Edit', href: '/edit' },
    { label: 'Delete', onClick: handleDelete, variant: 'destructive' },
  ]}
/>
```

Simple edit + delete actions.

### With Icons

```tsx
import { Edit, Trash2, Mail, Download } from 'lucide-react'
;<DetailActions
  actions={[
    { label: 'Edit', href: `/users/${id}/edit`, icon: Edit },
    {
      label: 'Delete',
      onClick: handleDelete,
      icon: Trash2,
      variant: 'destructive',
    },
    {
      label: 'Send Email',
      onClick: handleEmail,
      icon: Mail,
      variant: 'outline',
    },
    {
      label: 'Download',
      onClick: handleDownload,
      icon: Download,
      variant: 'secondary',
    },
  ]}
/>
```

Icons improve recognition and visual hierarchy.

### With Confirmation

```tsx
<DetailActions
  actions={[
    {
      label: 'Delete User',
      variant: 'destructive',
      onClick: () => {
        if (window.confirm('Delete this user? This action cannot be undone.')) {
          handleDelete()
        }
      },
    },
  ]}
/>
```

`DetailActions` has no built-in confirmation: confirm inside `onClick` (with `window.confirm` or your own `AlertDialog`) before running the action.

### With Loading State

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'

export default function UserActions({ userId }) {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)

  async function handleExport() {
    setLoading(true)
    await exportUserData(userId)
    setLoading(false)
  }

  return (
    <DetailActions
      actions={[
        {
          label: 'Export Data',
          onClick: handleExport,
          loading,
          disabled: loading,
        },
      ]}
    />
  )
}
```

Disables button and shows spinner during async operations.

### Horizontal Layout

```tsx
<DetailActions
  layout='horizontal'
  actions={[
    { label: 'Edit', href: '/edit' },
    { label: 'Delete', onClick: handleDelete, variant: 'destructive' },
  ]}
/>
```

Actions displayed side-by-side (useful for header).

### In Two-Column Layout

```tsx
<DetailLayout
  title={user.name}
  leftColumn={<UserInfoCard user={user} />}
  rightColumn={
    <>
      <DetailCard title='Avatar'>
        <DetailAvatar name={user.name} imageUrl={user.avatar} />
      </DetailCard>

      <DetailActions
        actions={[
          { label: 'Edit', href: `/users/${user.id}/edit`, icon: Edit },
          { label: 'Send Email', onClick: handleEmail, icon: Mail },
          {
            label: 'Delete',
            onClick: handleDelete,
            icon: Trash2,
            variant: 'destructive',
          },
        ]}
      />
    </>
  }
/>
```

Common pattern: Actions in right sidebar below avatar.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx
'use client'

import {
  DetailLayout,
  DetailActions,
  DetailCard,
  DetailField,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Edit, Trash2, Mail, Lock, Download } from 'lucide-react'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'

export default function UserDetailPage({ user }) {
  const router = useRouter()
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)

  async function handleDelete() {
    setLoading(true)
    await deleteUser(user.id)
    router.push('/admin/users')
  }

  async function handleSendEmail() {
    setLoading(true)
    await sendWelcomeEmail(user.email)
    setLoading(false)
  }

  async function handleResetPassword() {
    setLoading(true)
    await sendPasswordReset(user.email)
    setLoading(false)
  }

  async function handleExport() {
    setLoading(true)
    await exportUserData(user.id)
    setLoading(false)
  }

  return (
    <DetailLayout
      title={user.name}
      description={user.email}
      leftColumn={
        <DetailCard title='User Information'>
          <DetailField label='Name' value={user.name} />
          <DetailField label='Email' value={user.email} />
          <DetailField label='Role' value={user.role} />
        </DetailCard>
      }
      rightColumn={
        <DetailActions
          actions={[
            {
              label: 'Edit User',
              href: `/admin/users/${user.id}/edit`,
              icon: Edit,
              variant: 'default',
            },
            {
              label: 'Send Email',
              onClick: handleSendEmail,
              icon: Mail,
              variant: 'outline',
              disabled: loading,
            },
            {
              label: 'Reset Password',
              onClick: handleResetPassword,
              icon: Lock,
              variant: 'outline',
              disabled: loading,
            },
            {
              label: 'Export Data',
              onClick: handleExport,
              icon: Download,
              variant: 'secondary',
              disabled: loading,
            },
            {
              label: 'Delete User',
              onClick: () => {
                if (window.confirm('Delete this user? This cannot be undone.')) {
                  handleDelete()
                }
              },
              icon: Trash2,
              variant: 'destructive',
              disabled: loading,
            },
          ]}
        />
      }
    />
  )
}

// Server Actions
async function deleteUser(id: string) {
  /* ... */
}
async function sendWelcomeEmail(email: string) {
  /* ... */
}
async function sendPasswordReset(email: string) {
  /* ... */
}
async function exportUserData(id: string) {
  /* ... */
}
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Order by importance** - Most common actions first (Edit, View, etc.)
2. **Use appropriate variants** - Destructive for delete, outline for secondary
3. **Add confirmations** - Always confirm destructive actions
4. **Show loading states** - Disable during async operations
5. **Limit actions** - 3-6 actions max for clarity
6. **Use icons** - Improve recognition for common operations
7. **Place in sidebar** - Use right column in two-column layouts

---

## Button Variant Guidelines

| Variant         | Use For           | Examples                  |
| --------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- |
| **default**     | Primary actions   | Edit, Update, Save        |
| **destructive** | Dangerous actions | Delete, Remove, Revoke    |
| **outline**     | Secondary actions | Send Email, Export, Print |
| **secondary**   | Tertiary actions  | Download, Copy, Share     |
| **ghost**       | Subtle actions    | View Details, More Info   |
| **link**        | Navigation        | View Related, Go to...    |

---

## Accessibility

- Semantic `<button>` and `<a>` elements
- Keyboard navigable (Tab, Enter, Space)
- Focus visible states
- ARIA labels for icon-only buttons
- Disabled state prevents interaction
- Loading state exposed via `aria-busy`

- [DetailLayout](/docs/components/detail-layout) - Page layout with sidebar support
- [DetailCard](/docs/components/detail-card) - Card wrapper
- Button - Underlying button component

- Server Actions Best Practices - Async operations

# PermissionMatrix

> Roles × permissions grid of checkboxes, grouped by permission group, with search, group "select all" and per-cell pending state

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/permission-matrix.mdx

The roles screen every admin ends up writing: roles as columns, permissions as rows under their
group, a checkbox per cell. It is pure UI: your app loads the roles and permissions and persists
each toggle. Together with [AuditChangesViewer](/docs/components/audit-changes-viewer) it is one of
the building blocks of the upcoming admin kit.

```tsx
'use client'
import { useQuery, useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { PermissionMatrix, QueryErrorState } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function RolesMatrix() {
  const qc = useQueryClient()
  const { data, error, refetch } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['roles-matrix'], queryFn: rolesApi.matrix })
  const toggle = useMutation({
    mutationFn: (v: { roleId: string; permissionId: string; next: boolean }) =>
      v.next ? rolesApi.grant(v.roleId, v.permissionId) : rolesApi.revoke(v.roleId, v.permissionId),
  })

  if (error) return <QueryErrorState error={error} onRetry={refetch} />
  if (!data) return null

  const byRole = new Map(data.roles.map(r => [r.id, new Set(r.permissionIds)]))
  return (
    <PermissionMatrix
      roles={data.roles.map(r => ({ id: r.id, label: r.name, system: r.isSystem }))}
      permissions={data.permissions.map(p => ({ id: p.id, code: p.code, group: p.category, description: p.description }))}
      granted={(roleId, permissionId) => byRole.get(roleId)?.has(permissionId) ?? false}
      onToggle={async (roleId, permissionId, next) => {
        await toggle.mutateAsync({ roleId, permissionId, next })
        await qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['roles-matrix'] })
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Behavior

- **Layout**: one column per role, one row per permission, rows grouped by `group` in order of
  first appearance. The header row and the permission column stay sticky while the grid scrolls in
  both directions, so wide role sets work on small screens.
- **`granted`** is a function, so any storage works: `role.permissionIds`, a `Map` of sets, or a
  role that holds everything (`(roleId) => roleId === superId || …`).
- **Toggling**: each click calls `onToggle(roleId, permissionId, next)`. When it returns a promise,
  the cell shows the new value right away, is disabled and `aria-busy` until the promise settles.
  A rejection rolls the cell back and shows a toast with the error's message, or a localized
  fallback. Resolve after `granted` reflects the change (await the refetch, as above), or the cell
  flickers back for a moment.
- **Group "select all"**: the group row has a checkbox per role, checked, unchecked or mixed. It
  calls `onToggle` once for each cell that differs, and only for the permissions the search left
  visible. A failing batch shows a single toast. Hide it with `selectAllInGroup={false}`.
- **Read-only**: roles flagged `system` are locked by default. `readOnly={true}` locks every cell.
  `readOnly={roleId => …}` decides per role and replaces the `system` default. Without `onToggle`
  the whole matrix is read-only.
- **Search** filters by code, label, description and group (case-insensitive). Hide it with
  `searchable={false}`.
- **Accessibility**: a real `<table>` with a caption, column headers per role and row headers per
  permission. Every checkbox is labelled with its permission and role, such as "Read posts for
  Editor" (the group ones "All posts permissions for Editor"), reachable with Tab and toggled with
  Space.
- Text comes from the library messages (`telamonjs.admin.permissionMatrix.*`); role, permission and
  group labels accept `I18nText`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `roles` | `PermissionMatrixRole[]`: `{ id, label: I18nText, system? }` | required |
| `permissions` | `PermissionMatrixPermission[]`: `{ id, code, label?: I18nText, group, description?: I18nText, badge?: I18nText }` (`badge`: a short tag next to the name, e.g. the action) | required |
| `granted` | `(roleId, permissionId) => boolean` | required |
| `onToggle` | `(roleId, permissionId, next) => void \| Promise<unknown>` | read-only |
| `readOnly` | `boolean \| ((roleId) => boolean)` | `system` roles locked |
| `groupLabels` | `Record<string, I18nText>`, display names of `group` values | the raw group |
| `selectAllInGroup` | `boolean` | `true` |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `true` |
| `className` | `string`, classes of the scroll container | height `min(70vh, 720px)` |

## What stays in your app

Loading and saving, role management (create, rename, delete, end sessions), a "save per role" batch
flow (keep local edits in state and pass them through `granted`/`onToggle`), and anything beyond
role ↔ permission grants, such as per-user overrides or attribute-based rules.

## Related

- [AuditChangesViewer](/docs/components/audit-changes-viewer): what an audit entry changed
- [Permissions](/docs/packages/permissions): checking the permissions this matrix grants

---

# AuditChangesViewer

> Renders an audit entry's payload, whether a field diff, before/after snapshots or a plain object, with secrets masked

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/audit-changes-viewer.mdx

The "what changed" panel of an audit log detail. Hand it whatever your audit trail stored and it
picks the layout. It is pure UI: no fetching. Together with
[PermissionMatrix](/docs/components/permission-matrix) it is one of the building blocks of the
upcoming admin kit.

```tsx
'use client'
import { AuditChangesViewer } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function AuditEntryChanges({ log }: { log: AuditLogRow }) {
  return log.before !== undefined || log.after !== undefined ? (
    <AuditChangesViewer before={log.before} after={log.after} />
  ) : (
    <AuditChangesViewer changes={log.changes} />
  )
}
```

---

## Payload shapes

| Payload | Rendered as |
| --- | --- |
| `changes={{ name: { old: 'Ann', new: 'Anna' } }}`: every entry is `{ old, new }`, `{ from, to }`, or `{ before, after }` as [`logger.audit()`](/docs/packages/logger) writes it | Field / Before / After table |
| `before={…} after={…}`, or `changes={{ before, after }}` | Field / Before / After, computed here: changed fields only, with a "Show all fields" toggle |
| `changes={{ title: 'Hello', tags: ['a'] }}`: any other object (a request body, metadata) | Field / Value list |
| an array, a number or free text | pretty-printed block |
| `null`, `undefined`, `{}` | localized "No changes recorded." |

- A JSON **string** (a text column holding JSON) is parsed first, for `changes`, `before` and
  `after`.
- **Nested values** (objects, arrays) are pretty-printed inside a native `<details>`, collapsed,
  with the entry count as the summary.
- **before/after**: fields are compared deeply (key order does not count). A creation
  (`before={null}`) lists every field of `after`. When nothing differs, the viewer says so and the
  toggle still shows every field. Unchanged fields render muted.
- `null` shows as `null` and a missing value as `—`, so "cleared" and "not recorded" stay distinct.

## Redaction

Keys containing `password`, `passwd`, `senha`, `secret`, `token`, `apikey`, `authorization`, `cookie` or
`privatekey` are masked at any depth, in every shape, before anything reaches the DOM. Matching is
case-insensitive and ignores `_` and `-`, so `passwordHash`, `api_token` and `clientSecret` are
covered. `redactKeys` adds keys to that list:

```tsx
<AuditChangesViewer changes={log.changes} redactKeys={['taxId', 'birthDate']} />
```

Redaction only hides values on screen. Keep secrets out of the audit trail on the server too.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `changes` | `unknown`: diff, `{ before, after }`, object, JSON string | — |
| `before` | `unknown`, snapshot before the change (takes precedence over `changes`) | — |
| `after` | `unknown`, snapshot after the change | — |
| `redactKeys` | `string[]`, added to the built-in list | — |
| `className` | `string` | — |

Labels come from the library messages (`telamonjs.admin.auditChanges.*`).

## What stays in your app

The rest of the audit detail: who, when, IP, user agent, action badges and entity names (compose
them with [DetailCard](/docs/components/detail-card) and [Tabs](/docs/components/tabs)), field
display names, and adapting other shapes. A list of changes, for example, becomes a diff in one line:
`Object.fromEntries(list.map(c => [c.field, { from: c.from, to: c.to }]))`.

## Related

- [PermissionMatrix](/docs/components/permission-matrix): roles × permissions grid
- [Logger](/docs/packages/logger): `audit()` writes the entries this viewer reads

---

# DashboardGrid

> Drag-and-drop dashboard layout for widgets, powered by react-grid-layout

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/dashboard-grid.mdx

Positions dashboard widgets on a responsive grid. Each widget is placed by a layout item
(`x`, `y`, `w`, `h` in grid units); with `editable`, users can drag and resize widgets and you
persist the new layout through `onLayoutChange`.

```tsx
'use client'

import { DashboardGrid, StatCard, generateDefaultLayout } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { DollarSign, Users, ShoppingCart, TrendingUp } from 'lucide-react'

const widgets = [
  { id: 'revenue', component: <StatCard label='Revenue' value={45231} icon={DollarSign} color='green' /> },
  { id: 'users', component: <StatCard label='Users' value={2543} icon={Users} color='blue' /> },
  { id: 'orders', component: <StatCard label='Orders' value={127} icon={ShoppingCart} color='purple' /> },
  { id: 'growth', component: <StatCard label='Growth' value='+12.5%' icon={TrendingUp} color='orange' /> },
]

export function Dashboard() {
  return <DashboardGrid widgets={widgets} layout={generateDefaultLayout(widgets.map(w => w.id))} />
}
```

<Callout type='info' title='Browser-only'>
  `react-grid-layout` is loaded dynamically on the client, so the grid renders nothing during
  SSR and appears after hydration. Use it inside a `'use client'` component. `react-grid-layout`
  is an optional peer dependency (`^1.5.0 || ^2.0.0`) — add it to your app to use the grid.
</Callout>

---

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `widgets` | `Widget[]` | — | Widgets to render (required) |
| `layout` | `Layout[]` | — | One layout item per widget, matched by `layout.i === widget.id` (required) |
| `onLayoutChange` | `(layout: Layout[]) => void` | — | Called after a drag/resize |
| `editable` | `boolean` | `false` | Enables drag and resize (drag handle appears on hover) |
| `rowHeight` | `number` | `60` | Row height in pixels |
| `breakpoints` | `{ lg?, md?, sm?, xs? }` | `{ lg: 1200, md: 996, sm: 768, xs: 480 }` | Container widths for each breakpoint |
| `responsiveCols` | `{ lg?, md?, sm?, xs? }` | `{ lg: 12, md: 10, sm: 6, xs: 4 }` | Column count per breakpoint |
| `compactType` | `'vertical' \| 'horizontal' \| null` | `'vertical'` | How items float to fill gaps |
| `className` | `string` | — | Classes on the wrapper |

The props type also declares `cols`, but the grid reads its column counts from
`responsiveCols` only — set that instead.

### Widget

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Unique id; must match a layout item's `i` |
| `component` | `ReactNode` | What the cell renders |
| `title` | `string` | Optional label |
| `type` | `string` | Optional category, for your own filtering |

### Layout item

`{ i, x, y, w, h }` plus the optional `minW`, `maxW`, `minH`, `maxH`, `static`,
`isDraggable`, `isResizable` and `isBounded` constraints. A layout item without a matching
widget is skipped (with a logged warning).

---

## generateDefaultLayout

Builds a left-to-right, top-to-bottom layout for a list of widget ids:

```ts
generateDefaultLayout(widgetIds: string[], options?: {
  cols?: number          // default 12
  defaultWidth?: number  // default 3
  defaultHeight?: number // default 2
}): Layout[]
```

---

## Editable layout

Persist the user's arrangement and restore it on the next visit:

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { DashboardGrid, StatCard, ChartWidget } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Users } from 'lucide-react'

const widgets = [
  { id: 'users', component: <StatCard label='Users' value={1234} icon={Users} color='blue' /> },
  { id: 'revenue', component: <ChartWidget title='Revenue' type='line' data={revenue} dataKeys={['value']} /> },
]

const initialLayout = [
  { i: 'users', x: 0, y: 0, w: 3, h: 2 },
  { i: 'revenue', x: 3, y: 0, w: 9, h: 4 },
]

export function EditableDashboard() {
  const [layout, setLayout] = useState(initialLayout)

  return (
    <DashboardGrid
      widgets={widgets}
      layout={layout}
      editable
      onLayoutChange={next => {
        setLayout(next)
        saveLayout(next) // your persistence (API, localStorage...)
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

For a static row of cards that never moves, a plain CSS grid
(`<div className='grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4'>`) is simpler than `DashboardGrid`.

---

- [StatCard](/docs/components/stats-card) — the metric widget
- [ChartWidget](/docs/components/chart-widget) — chart inside a card
- [Dashboard Pattern](/docs/patterns/dashboard)

# ChartWidget

> Dashboard widget that renders a line, bar, or pie chart in a card

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/chart-widget.mdx

Dashboard widget that renders a Recharts chart (line, bar, or pie) inside a
card with title, description, and an optional header action. You pass `data`
and a `type` — the widget renders the chart itself; it does **not** take a
chart as children.

<Callout type='warn' title='Data-driven API'>
  The API is data-driven: `data` + `type` + key configuration, listed below. Fetch, refresh and
  period state live in your page.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

Recharts is a dependency of `@telamonjs/ui`. The chart internals are
lazy-loaded, so recharts stays out of your bundle until a widget renders.

```tsx title="app/dashboard/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { ChartWidget } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const data = [
  { name: 'Jan', value: 4000 },
  { name: 'Feb', value: 3000 },
  { name: 'Mar', value: 5000 },
]

export default function DashboardPage() {
  return (
    <ChartWidget
      title='Monthly Sales'
      description='Revenue trend over time'
      data={data}
      type='line'
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    title: { description: 'Widget title', type: 'string', required: true },
    description: { description: 'Subtitle under the title', type: 'string' },
    data: { description: 'Chart data points (flat objects of strings/numbers)', type: 'ChartDataPoint[]', required: true },
    type: { description: 'Chart type', type: "'line' | 'bar' | 'pie'", default: "'line'" },
    xAxisKey: { description: 'Data key for the X axis (line/bar)', type: 'string', default: "'name'" },
    dataKeys: { description: 'Data keys plotted as series (line/bar)', type: 'string[]', default: "['value']" },
    valueKey: { description: 'Data key for slice values (pie)', type: 'string', default: "'value'" },
    nameKey: { description: 'Data key for slice labels (pie)', type: 'string', default: "'name'" },
    colors: { description: 'Series/slice colors (defaults to the built-in palette)', type: 'string[]' },
    height: { description: 'Chart height in pixels', type: 'number', default: '300' },
    headerAction: { description: 'Content on the right of the header (filters, refresh button, links)', type: 'ReactNode' },
    showLegend: { description: 'Show the legend', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    showGrid: { description: 'Show the cartesian grid (line/bar)', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

```typescript
type ChartType = 'line' | 'bar' | 'pie'

interface ChartDataPoint {
  [key: string]: string | number
}
```

---

## Examples

### Multiple Series

```tsx
const data = [
  { name: 'Jan', revenue: 4000, target: 3500 },
  { name: 'Feb', revenue: 3000, target: 3500 },
  { name: 'Mar', revenue: 5000, target: 4000 },
]

<ChartWidget
  title='Revenue vs Target'
  data={data}
  type='line'
  dataKeys={['revenue', 'target']}
  colors={['#3b82f6', '#94a3b8']}
/>
```

### Bar and Pie

```tsx
<ChartWidget
  title='Sales by Category'
  data={salesByCategory}
  type='bar'
  xAxisKey='category'
  dataKeys={['total']}
/>

<ChartWidget
  title='Market Share'
  data={marketShare}
  type='pie'
  nameKey='company'
  valueKey='share'
  showGrid={false}
/>
```

### Header Action (refresh / period selector)

The widget has no built-in period selector — put your control in
`headerAction` and drive `data` from your own state:

```tsx
'use client'

import { ChartWidget } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { useState } from 'react'
import { metricsApi } from '@/lib/api/metrics-client'

export function SalesWidget() {
  const [period, setPeriod] = useState('30d')

  const { data = [] } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['sales', period],
    queryFn: () => metricsApi.sales(period),
  })

  return (
    <ChartWidget
      title='Sales Revenue'
      description='Total sales over selected period'
      data={data}
      type='line'
      dataKeys={['revenue']}
      headerAction={
        <select
          value={period}
          onChange={e => setPeriod(e.target.value)}
          className='rounded border px-2 py-1 text-sm'
        >
          <option value='7d'>Last 7 days</option>
          <option value='30d'>Last 30 days</option>
          <option value='90d'>Last 90 days</option>
        </select>
      }
    />
  )
}
```

### Real-time Data

Polling or SSE both reduce to "update the array you pass as `data`":

```tsx
const { data = [] } = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['server-load'],
  queryFn: metricsApi.serverLoad,
  refetchInterval: 30_000,
})

<ChartWidget title='Server Load' data={data} type='line' dataKeys={['cpu', 'memory']} />
```

---

## ChartWidget vs standalone charts

| Situation | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Dashboard card with title/description chrome | `ChartWidget` |
| Chart embedded in your own layout/card | [LineChart](/docs/components/line-chart) / [BarChart](/docs/components/bar-chart) / [PieChart](/docs/components/pie-chart) / [AreaChart](/docs/components/area-chart) |
| Area chart in a widget | Standalone `AreaChart` inside your own card — `ChartWidget` only does line/bar/pie |

---

## Charts not wrapped by the package: use Recharts directly

`@telamonjs/ui` wraps line, bar, area and pie charts (donut is a
[PieChart option](/docs/components/pie-chart#donut)). For anything else,
such as radar, combined bar + line, scatter or funnel, compose Recharts yourself.
Add `recharts` to your app's own dependencies to import it, mark the file
`'use client'`, and reuse the palette (`#3b82f6`, `#10b981`, `#f59e0b`, ...) so
the result matches the built-in charts. Wrap the chart in a
[BaseCard](/docs/components/base-card) to get the widget chrome.

### Radar

Compare a few entities across 3-8 metrics on the same scale.

```tsx
'use client'

import {
  Legend,
  PolarAngleAxis,
  PolarGrid,
  PolarRadiusAxis,
  Radar,
  RadarChart,
  ResponsiveContainer,
} from 'recharts'

const data = [
  { metric: 'Speed', productA: 80, productB: 65 },
  { metric: 'Reliability', productA: 95, productB: 80 },
  { metric: 'Comfort', productA: 70, productB: 90 },
  { metric: 'Safety', productA: 90, productB: 85 },
]

export function ProductScorecard() {
  return (
    <ResponsiveContainer width='100%' height={300}>
      <RadarChart data={data}>
        <PolarGrid />
        <PolarAngleAxis dataKey='metric' />
        <PolarRadiusAxis domain={[0, 100]} />
        <Radar name='Product A' dataKey='productA' stroke='#3b82f6' fill='#3b82f6' fillOpacity={0.5} />
        <Radar name='Product B' dataKey='productB' stroke='#10b981' fill='#10b981' fillOpacity={0.5} />
        <Legend />
      </RadarChart>
    </ResponsiveContainer>
  )
}
```

### Bars + line (dual axis)

An absolute measure as bars and a rate or count as a line, each on its own Y axis.

```tsx
'use client'

import {
  Bar,
  CartesianGrid,
  ComposedChart,
  Legend,
  Line,
  ResponsiveContainer,
  Tooltip,
  XAxis,
  YAxis,
} from 'recharts'

const data = [
  { name: 'Jan', revenue: 4000, orders: 120 },
  { name: 'Feb', revenue: 3000, orders: 98 },
  { name: 'Mar', revenue: 5000, orders: 150 },
]

export function RevenueAndOrders() {
  return (
    <ResponsiveContainer width='100%' height={300}>
      <ComposedChart data={data}>
        <CartesianGrid strokeDasharray='3 3' />
        <XAxis dataKey='name' />
        <YAxis yAxisId='left' />
        <YAxis yAxisId='right' orientation='right' />
        <Tooltip />
        <Legend />
        <Bar yAxisId='left' dataKey='revenue' fill='#3b82f6' name='Revenue' />
        <Line yAxisId='right' type='monotone' dataKey='orders' stroke='#f59e0b' name='Orders' />
      </ComposedChart>
    </ResponsiveContainer>
  )
}
```

When both series share a scale, drop the second `YAxis` and the `yAxisId` props.
See the [Recharts API](https://recharts.org/en-US/api) for every chart type.

---

## Best Practices

1. **Right chart for the data** - Line for trends, bar for category comparison, pie for composition (few slices)
2. **Keep data flat** - `ChartDataPoint` is a flat record; pre-aggregate on the server
3. **Loading/empty are yours** - Wrap in your own skeleton/empty check before rendering the widget
4. **Limit series** - 2-3 `dataKeys` read best at widget size

---

- [DashboardGrid](/docs/components/dashboard-grid) - Dashboard layout
- [StatCard](/docs/components/stats-card) - Simple stat card

- [BarChart](/docs/components/bar-chart) - Standalone bar chart
