# StatCard

> Card for one dashboard metric — label, value, icon and color, with an optional animated count

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/stats-card.mdx

A dashboard card for one metric: a label, a value, an icon and a color, plus an optional
subtitle, badge and animated count. It comes in three looks (`outlined`, `tinted`, `accent`).
Import it from `@telamonjs/ui` (also available from `@telamonjs/ui/cards`,
together with `StatsGrid` and `StatCardSkeleton`).

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
'use client'

import { StatCard } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { DollarSign } from 'lucide-react'

export function RevenueCard() {
  return <StatCard label='Total Revenue' value={45231} icon={DollarSign} color='green' />
}
```

`icon` and `color` are required. Numbers are formatted with the active locale
(`formatNumber`, on by default); strings render as given.

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    label: { description: 'Metric name', type: 'I18nText', required: true },
    value: { description: 'Main value. Numbers are locale-formatted; strings render as is', type: 'string | number', required: true },
    icon: {
      description: 'Lucide component, or an icon name resolved through setIconResolver()',
      type: 'string | LucideIcon | ComponentType',
      required: true,
    },
    color: {
      description: 'Color of the icon and accents',
      type: "'blue' | 'green' | 'yellow' | 'red' | 'purple' | 'orange' | 'gray'",
      required: true,
    },
    variant: { description: 'Visual style', type: "'outlined' | 'tinted' | 'accent'", default: "'outlined'" },
    size: {
      description: '`tinted` honors all three; `accent` honors `compact` (and auto-compacts inside a dense StatsGrid)',
      type: "'mini' | 'compact' | 'default'",
    },
    subtitle: { description: 'Secondary line under the label (hidden at `mini`)', type: 'I18nText' },
    badge: {
      description: 'Small badge under the value (`outlined` and `accent`)',
      type: "{ text: I18nText; variant: 'success' | 'destructive' | 'warning' }",
    },
    animate: { description: 'Count up to the value — only when `value` is a number', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    animationDuration: { description: 'Count-up duration in ms', type: 'number', default: '500' },
    formatNumber: { description: 'Locale-format numeric values', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    onClick: { description: 'Renders the card inside a button', type: '() => void' },
    highlight: { description: 'Adds a colored ring', type: 'boolean' },
    pulse: { description: 'Pulsing dot next to the label while the value is above zero', type: 'boolean' },
    wrapLabel: { description: 'Wrap a long label instead of truncating (`outlined`/`accent`)', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

Text that truncates — the label (unless `wrapLabel`), the subtitle and the `tinted` value —
carries its full content in a native `title` tooltip, so a clipped value is still readable on
hover.

There is no `title`, `change`, `trend`, `description` or `footer` prop. Put a delta in
`badge` (formatting the sign yourself) and the comparison period in `subtitle`. For a card
with a trend arrow and a target, use [KPICard](/docs/components/kpi-card).

---

## Examples

### Variants

```tsx
<StatCard variant='outlined' label='Users' value={2543} icon={Users} color='blue' />
<StatCard variant='tinted' label='Users' value={2543} icon={Users} color='blue' />
<StatCard variant='accent' label='Users' value={2543} icon={Users} color='blue' />
```

### Delta in a badge

```tsx
<StatCard
  label='Revenue'
  value={45231}
  icon={DollarSign}
  color='green'
  subtitle='vs last month'
  badge={{ text: '+12.5%', variant: 'success' }}
/>
```

### Animated count

```tsx
<StatCard label='Online' value={stats.online} icon={Activity} color='green' animate />
```

Only numeric values animate; a string value renders immediately.

### Icon by name

```tsx
<StatCard label='Orders' value={127} icon='ShoppingCart' color='purple' />
```

String icons are resolved by the resolver your app registers with `setIconResolver()`.

### Clickable

```tsx
<StatCard label='Open tickets' value={12} icon={Inbox} color='red' pulse onClick={() => router.push('/tickets')} />
```

### Loading state

There is no `loading` prop. Render `StatCardSkeleton` (from `@telamonjs/ui/cards`)
while data is pending and swap in the cards once the values resolve.

```tsx
import { StatCardSkeleton } from '@telamonjs/ui/cards'

{isLoading ? <StatCardSkeleton count={4} /> : <DashboardStats stats={data} />}
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/dashboard-stats.tsx"
'use client'

import { StatCard } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { StatsGrid } from '@telamonjs/ui/cards'
import { DollarSign, Users, ShoppingCart, TrendingUp } from 'lucide-react'

interface DashboardStats {
  revenue: number
  revenueChange: number
  users: number
  orders: number
  conversion: number
}

function fmtChange(delta: number) {
  return `${delta >= 0 ? '+' : ''}${delta.toFixed(1)}%`
}

export function DashboardStats({ stats }: { stats: DashboardStats }) {
  return (
    <StatsGrid columns={4}>
      <StatCard
        label='Total Revenue'
        value={stats.revenue}
        icon={DollarSign}
        color='green'
        subtitle='vs last month'
        badge={{
          text: fmtChange(stats.revenueChange),
          variant: stats.revenueChange >= 0 ? 'success' : 'destructive',
        }}
      />
      <StatCard label='Active Users' value={stats.users} icon={Users} color='blue' animate />
      <StatCard label='Orders' value={stats.orders} icon={ShoppingCart} color='purple' animate />
      <StatCard label='Conversion Rate' value={`${stats.conversion.toFixed(2)}%`} icon={TrendingUp} color='orange' />
    </StatsGrid>
  )
}
```

`StatsGrid` from `@telamonjs/ui/cards` lays the cards out responsively
(`columns` 2–6, `gap` `sm`/`md`/`lg`); with 5 or more columns, `accent` cards switch to
their compact size. The root `StatsGrid` is a different component, used inside dialogs.

---

## Best Practices

1. **Pick one variant per dashboard** - mixing looks reads as noise
2. **Use color for meaning** - green/red for good/bad, the rest for categories
3. **Pass numbers, not formatted strings** - formatting follows the locale and `animate` works
4. **Put the comparison period in `subtitle`** - keep `label` short
5. **Consistent grid** - 2–4 columns on most dashboards

---

## Accessibility

- With `onClick`, the card renders inside a native `<button>`
- Color is never the only signal: label and value are always text

---

## Related Components

- [KPICard](/docs/components/kpi-card) - KPI card with trend arrow and target/progress
- [DetailStatsGrid](/docs/components/detail-stats-grid) - Multiple stats in a detail view
- [DashboardGrid](/docs/components/dashboard-grid) - Draggable widget grid
- [useAnimatedCounter](/docs/hooks/use-animated-counter) - The count-up behind `animate`

---

## See Also

- [Dashboard Pattern](/docs/patterns/dashboard) - Dashboard design

---

# KPICard

> Key Performance Indicator card with trend visualization

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/kpi-card.mdx

Card component for displaying Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) with a trend badge, a comparison label and an optional footer.

<Callout type='info' title='Dashboard Essential'>
  `KPICard` combines a metric, its trend and a comparison label to show a KPI at a glance.
  Import it from `@telamonjs/ui` or `@telamonjs/ui/charts`.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { KPICard } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { DollarSign } from 'lucide-react'

export default function Dashboard() {
  return (
    <KPICard
      title='Monthly Revenue'
      value='$45,231'
      icon={<DollarSign className='w-5 h-5' />}
      change={12.5}
      trend='up'
      changeLabel='vs last month'
    />
  )
}
```

<Callout type='warn' title='`icon` takes a rendered element'>
  `icon` is `React.ReactNode` — pass a rendered element (`<DollarSign className="w-5 h-5" />`),
  not a component reference (`icon={DollarSign}`).
</Callout>

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    title: { description: 'KPI title', type: 'string', required: true },
    value: { description: 'KPI value', type: 'string | number', required: true },
    change: { description: 'Trend percentage (drives the +/- sign and color)', type: 'number' },
    changeLabel: { description: 'Label next to the change value', type: 'string', default: "'vs. previous period' (localized)" },
    icon: { description: 'Icon element (already sized/rendered, not a component reference)', type: 'React.ReactNode' },
    trend: { description: 'Trend direction, controls the trend icon', type: "'up' | 'down' | 'neutral'" },
    loading: { description: 'Show loading skeleton', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
    description: { description: 'Secondary text below the value', type: 'string' },
    footer: { description: 'Custom content rendered below the description', type: 'React.ReactNode' },
  }}
/>

---

## Examples

### Basic KPI

```tsx
<KPICard title='Total Users' value='2,543' />
```

### With Icon

```tsx
import { Users } from 'lucide-react'
;<KPICard title='Active Users' value='1,892' icon={<Users className='w-5 h-5' />} />
```

There is no `iconColor`/`iconBackground` prop — style the icon element itself
(`<Users className="w-5 h-5 text-blue-600" />`) if you need a custom color.

### With Trend

```tsx
<KPICard
  title='Revenue'
  value='$45,231'
  icon={<DollarSign className='w-5 h-5' />}
  change={12.5}
  trend='up'
  changeLabel='vs last month'
/>
```

`trend` (`'up' | 'down' | 'neutral'`) controls the badge color and arrow;
`change` is the number shown inside it.

<Callout type='warn' title='No `isPositive` override'>
  `trend='down'` is always rendered red. For metrics where down is good (e.g. bounce rate), compute
  the visual trend yourself: `trend={bounceRateDelta < 0 ? 'up' : 'down'}`.
</Callout>

### With Description

```tsx
<KPICard
  title='Total Orders'
  value='1,234'
  description='Average: 41 per day'
  icon={<Package className='w-5 h-5' />}
  change={15.3}
  trend='up'
/>
```

There is no `subtitle` prop — use `description` (rendered below the value).

### With Footer

```tsx
import { KPICard, Progress } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<KPICard title='Premium Users' value='892' icon={<Star className='w-5 h-5' />} footer={<Progress value={62} />} />
```

`footer` accepts any `ReactNode`, rendered below a top border — there is no
built-in `badge` prop; render a `Badge`/`StatusBadge` inside `footer` (or next
to `title`) if you need one.

### Loading State

```tsx
<KPICard title='Revenue' value='$45,231' loading={true} />
```

Shows skeleton animation. There is no `onClick` prop — `KPICard` is not
interactive; wrap it in a `<Link>`/`<button>` if you need a clickable KPI.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/revenue-kpis.tsx"
'use client'

import { KPICard } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { DollarSign, TrendingUp, ShoppingCart, Users } from 'lucide-react'
import { use } from 'react'
import { getKPIs } from './service'

function trendOf(delta: number): 'up' | 'down' | 'neutral' {
  return delta > 0 ? 'up' : delta < 0 ? 'down' : 'neutral'
}

export default function RevenueKPIs() {
  const kpis = use(getKPIs())

  return (
    <div className='grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-6'>
      <KPICard
        title='Total Revenue'
        value={`$${kpis.revenue.toLocaleString()}`}
        description={`Goal: $${kpis.revenueGoal.toLocaleString()}`}
        icon={<DollarSign className='w-5 h-5 text-green-600' />}
        change={kpis.revenueTrend}
        trend={trendOf(kpis.revenueTrend)}
        changeLabel='vs last month'
      />

      <KPICard
        title='Conversion Rate'
        value={`${kpis.conversion.toFixed(2)}%`}
        icon={<TrendingUp className='w-5 h-5 text-blue-600' />}
        change={kpis.conversionTrend}
        trend={trendOf(kpis.conversionTrend)}
        changeLabel='vs last month'
      />

      <KPICard
        title='Total Orders'
        value={kpis.orders.toLocaleString()}
        icon={<ShoppingCart className='w-5 h-5 text-purple-600' />}
        change={kpis.ordersTrend}
        trend={trendOf(kpis.ordersTrend)}
        changeLabel='vs last month'
      />

      <KPICard
        title='Active Customers'
        value={kpis.customers.toLocaleString()}
        description={`Total: ${kpis.totalCustomers.toLocaleString()}`}
        icon={<Users className='w-5 h-5 text-orange-600' />}
        change={kpis.customersTrend}
        trend={trendOf(kpis.customersTrend)}
        changeLabel='vs last month'
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Dashboard KPIs** - Executive dashboards
- **Analytics** - Key metrics overview
- **Sales dashboards** - Revenue, orders, conversion
- **Marketing** - Campaign performance
- **Operations** - Efficiency metrics

---

## Trend Logic

**Automatic coloring (fixed, no override):**

- `trend='up'` → Green badge + up arrow
- `trend='down'` → Red badge + down arrow
- `trend='neutral'` → Muted badge + dash

`change` only supplies the number shown inside the trend badge (or, when
`trend` is omitted, as plain `+X%`/`-X%` text) — it does not drive the color
by itself. There is no sparkline support on `KPICard`; for a mini chart next
to a metric, compose your own chart component into `footer`, or use
[AreaChart](/docs/components/area-chart)/[LineChart](/docs/components/line-chart)
directly.

---

## Best Practices

1. **Clear titles** - Concise, descriptive metric names
2. **Format values** - Currency symbols, percentages, units
3. **Meaningful trends** - Show relevant comparison periods
4. **Consistent icons** - Use same icon set (Lucide)
5. **Color coding** - Match icon colors to brand
6. **Loading states** - Show skeleton while fetching
7. **Clickable when relevant** - Wrap in a link to the detail page

---

## Grid Layouts

**4-column dashboard:**

```tsx
<div className='grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4 gap-6'>
  <KPICard title='KPI 1' value='100' />
  <KPICard title='KPI 2' value='200' />
  <KPICard title='KPI 3' value='300' />
  <KPICard title='KPI 4' value='400' />
</div>
```

**Responsive:**

- Mobile: 1 column
- Tablet: 2 columns
- Desktop: 4 columns

---

## Accessibility

- Semantic HTML structure (built on `BaseCard`)
- Screen reader friendly values
- Color contrast compliant

---

## Performance

**Optimization:**

- Memoize `footer` content if it renders a chart
- Wrap in `React.memo` for grids with many cards

```tsx
import { memo } from 'react'

const MemoizedKPICard = memo(KPICard)
```

---

## Related Components

- [StatCard](/docs/components/stats-card) - Statistics card
- [DashboardGrid](/docs/components/dashboard-grid) - Layout for KPIs

---

## See Also

- [Dashboard Pattern](/docs/patterns/dashboard) - Dashboard design
- KPI Design - Effective KPI visualization

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

---

# LineChart

> Line chart component for visualizing trends over time

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/line-chart.mdx

Line chart component built on Recharts for visualizing trends, time series data, and continuous metrics.

<Callout type='info' title='Built on Recharts'>
  All chart components are built on [Recharts](https://recharts.org/) with
  pre-configured theming and responsive behavior. Recharts ships with
  `@telamonjs/ui` — no separate install.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { LineChart } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const data = [
  { name: 'Jan', revenue: 4000 },
  { name: 'Feb', revenue: 3000 },
  { name: 'Mar', revenue: 5000 },
  { name: 'Apr', revenue: 4500 },
  { name: 'May', revenue: 6000 },
  { name: 'Jun', revenue: 5500 },
]

export default function RevenueChart() {
  return <LineChart data={data} dataKeys={['revenue']} />
}
```

<Callout type='warn' title='The X axis reads the `name` field'>
  `LineChart` takes flat `dataKeys: string[]`, one line per key. The X axis is fixed to the `name`
  field of each data point (`ChartData` requires `name`). Colors come from the `colors` array,
  positionally matched to `dataKeys`.
</Callout>

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    data: { description: 'Chart data — each point needs a `name` field (X axis) plus numeric series fields', type: 'ChartData[]', required: true },
    dataKeys: { description: 'Field names plotted as lines (one line per key)', type: 'string[]', required: true },
    colors: { description: 'Line colors, matched by index to dataKeys (defaults to the built-in palette)', type: 'string[]' },
    height: { description: 'Chart height in pixels', type: 'number', default: '300' },
    showGrid: { description: 'Show the cartesian grid', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    showLegend: { description: 'Show the legend', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    xAxisLabel: { description: 'X axis label', type: 'string' },
    yAxisLabel: { description: 'Y axis label', type: 'string' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes on the wrapper', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

```typescript
// type exported from '@telamonjs/ui/charts'
interface ChartData {
  name: string
  [key: string]: string | number
}
```

There is no `loading`, `emptyMessage`, `showTooltip`, or per-line config —
the tooltip is always on, and styling per line is positional via `colors`.

---

## Examples

### Multiple Lines

```tsx
const data = [
  { name: 'Jan', revenue: 4000, expenses: 2400 },
  { name: 'Feb', revenue: 3000, expenses: 1398 },
  { name: 'Mar', revenue: 5000, expenses: 3200 },
]

<LineChart
  data={data}
  dataKeys={['revenue', 'expenses']}
  colors={['#3b82f6', '#ef4444']}
/>
```

### Axis Labels and Size

```tsx
<LineChart
  data={data}
  dataKeys={['revenue']}
  height={400}
  xAxisLabel='Month'
  yAxisLabel='Revenue (R$)'
/>
```

### Minimal (sparkline-ish)

```tsx
<LineChart
  data={data}
  dataKeys={['value']}
  height={120}
  showGrid={false}
  showLegend={false}
/>
```

### With React Query

```tsx
'use client'

import { LineChart } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { metricsApi } from '@/lib/api/metrics-client'

export function RevenueTrend() {
  const { data = [] } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['revenue-trend'],
    queryFn: metricsApi.revenueTrend, // [{ name: 'Jan', revenue: 4000 }, ...]
  })

  return <LineChart data={data} dataKeys={['revenue']} />
}
```

---

## Lazy Variant

`LineChartLazy` has the same props but code-splits the Recharts bundle,
loading it only when the chart mounts (a skeleton shows meanwhile):

```tsx
import { LineChartLazy } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<LineChartLazy data={data} dataKeys={['revenue']} />
```

Prefer the lazy variant on pages where the chart is below the fold or
conditional.

---

## Best Practices

1. **Name the X axis field `name`** - The component reads it; map your API data if needed
2. **Limit series** - 2-4 lines stay readable
3. **Stable colors** - Pass explicit `colors` so series keep their color across dashboards
4. **Time series order** - Sort `data` chronologically before passing

---

## Related Components

- [AreaChart](/docs/components/area-chart) - Filled trend chart
- [BarChart](/docs/components/bar-chart) - Category comparison
- [PieChart](/docs/components/pie-chart) - Composition
- [ChartWidget](/docs/components/chart-widget) - Chart inside a dashboard card

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

---

# BarChart

> Bar chart component for comparing values across categories

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/bar-chart.mdx

Bar chart component built on Recharts for comparing values across categories,
with vertical (default) or horizontal bars.

<Callout type='info' title='Built on Recharts'>
  All chart components are built on [Recharts](https://recharts.org/) with
  pre-configured theming and responsive behavior. Recharts ships with
  `@telamonjs/ui` — no separate install.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const data = [
  { name: 'Electronics', sales: 4000 },
  { name: 'Clothing', sales: 3000 },
  { name: 'Home', sales: 2000 },
  { name: 'Sports', sales: 2780 },
]

export default function SalesByCategory() {
  return <BarChart data={data} dataKeys={['sales']} />
}
```

<Callout type='warn' title='The category axis reads the `name` field'>
  `BarChart` takes flat `dataKeys: string[]`, one bar series per key. The category axis is
  fixed to the `name` field of each data point.
</Callout>

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    data: { description: 'Chart data — each point needs a `name` field (category) plus numeric series fields', type: 'ChartData[]', required: true },
    dataKeys: { description: 'Field names plotted as bar series (grouped side by side)', type: 'string[]', required: true },
    colors: { description: 'Bar colors, matched by index to dataKeys (defaults to the built-in palette)', type: 'string[]' },
    height: { description: 'Chart height in pixels', type: 'number', default: '300' },
    layout: {
      description: "'horizontal' = vertical bars over a category X axis (default); 'vertical' = horizontal bars with categories on the Y axis",
      type: "'horizontal' | 'vertical'",
      default: "'horizontal'",
    },
    showGrid: { description: 'Show the cartesian grid', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    showLegend: { description: 'Show the legend', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    xAxisLabel: { description: 'X axis label', type: 'string' },
    yAxisLabel: { description: 'Y axis label', type: 'string' },
    allowDecimals: { description: 'Whether the value axis may show fractional ticks — pass `false` for counts', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    categoryAxisWidth: { description: "Width in px of the category axis (the `name` labels) in `layout='vertical'`; ignored in `'horizontal'`", type: 'number', default: '60' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes on the wrapper', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

---

## Examples

### Grouped Series

```tsx
const data = [
  { name: 'Q1', online: 4000, stores: 2400 },
  { name: 'Q2', online: 3000, stores: 1398 },
  { name: 'Q3', online: 5000, stores: 3200 },
]

<BarChart
  data={data}
  dataKeys={['online', 'stores']}
  colors={['#3b82f6', '#10b981']}
/>
```

### Horizontal Bars

```tsx
<BarChart
  data={topProducts}
  dataKeys={['sales']}
  layout='vertical'
  height={400}
/>
```

Horizontal bars (`layout='vertical'`) work well for long category labels and
rankings. The rounded corners follow the layout: each bar is rounded at
its end (the top of a vertical bar, the right of a horizontal one).

### Counts and Long Labels

```tsx
<BarChart
  data={ticketsByTeam}
  dataKeys={['open']}
  layout='vertical'
  allowDecimals={false}
  categoryAxisWidth={160}
/>
```

`allowDecimals={false}` keeps the value axis on whole numbers (no `0.5` ticks for a
count); `categoryAxisWidth` widens the label column so long names are not clipped.

### With React Query

```tsx
'use client'

import { BarChart } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { metricsApi } from '@/lib/api/metrics-client'

export function SalesByCategory() {
  const { data = [] } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['sales-by-category'],
    queryFn: metricsApi.salesByCategory,
  })

  return <BarChart data={data} dataKeys={['total']} />
}
```

---

## Lazy Variant

`BarChartLazy` has the same props but code-splits the Recharts bundle:

```tsx
import { BarChartLazy } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<BarChartLazy data={data} dataKeys={['sales']} />
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Name the category field `name`** - Map your API data if it uses another key
2. **Sort deliberately** - Rankings descending, time buckets chronologically
3. **Few series** - 2-3 grouped series max; more becomes unreadable
4. **Horizontal for long labels** - Switch `layout` instead of rotating labels

---

## Related Components

- [LineChart](/docs/components/line-chart) - Trends over time
- [AreaChart](/docs/components/area-chart) - Filled trends
- [Charts not wrapped by the package](/docs/components/chart-widget#charts-not-wrapped-by-the-package-use-recharts-directly) - Bars + lines combined, with Recharts directly
- [ChartWidget](/docs/components/chart-widget) - Chart inside a dashboard card

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# AreaChart

> Area chart component for cumulative trends and stacked volumes

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/area-chart.mdx

Area chart component built on Recharts for visualizing volume over time —
optionally stacked to show how parts compose a total.

<Callout type='info' title='Built on Recharts'>
  All chart components are built on [Recharts](https://recharts.org/) with
  pre-configured theming and responsive behavior. Recharts ships with
  `@telamonjs/ui` — no separate install.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { AreaChart } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const data = [
  { name: 'Mon', visits: 1200 },
  { name: 'Tue', visits: 1900 },
  { name: 'Wed', visits: 1500 },
  { name: 'Thu', visits: 2200 },
  { name: 'Fri', visits: 2600 },
]

export default function TrafficChart() {
  return <AreaChart data={data} dataKeys={['visits']} />
}
```

<Callout type='warn' title='The X axis reads the `name` field'>
  Like the other charts, `AreaChart` takes flat `dataKeys: string[]`, one area per key, with the
  X axis fixed to the `name` field.
</Callout>

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    data: { description: 'Chart data — each point needs a `name` field (X axis) plus numeric series fields', type: 'ChartData[]', required: true },
    dataKeys: { description: 'Field names plotted as areas', type: 'string[]', required: true },
    colors: { description: 'Area colors, matched by index to dataKeys (defaults to the built-in palette)', type: 'string[]' },
    height: { description: 'Chart height in pixels', type: 'number', default: '300' },
    stacked: { description: 'Stack the areas (parts of a total) instead of overlapping them', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    showGrid: { description: 'Show the cartesian grid', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    showLegend: { description: 'Show the legend', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    xAxisLabel: { description: 'X axis label', type: 'string' },
    yAxisLabel: { description: 'Y axis label', type: 'string' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes on the wrapper', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

---

## Examples

### Stacked Areas

```tsx
const data = [
  { name: 'Jan', organic: 4000, paid: 2400, referral: 800 },
  { name: 'Feb', organic: 3000, paid: 1398, referral: 900 },
  { name: 'Mar', organic: 5000, paid: 3200, referral: 1100 },
]

<AreaChart
  data={data}
  dataKeys={['organic', 'paid', 'referral']}
  stacked
/>
```

Use `stacked` when the series sum to a meaningful total (traffic sources,
revenue streams); leave it off to compare independent trends.

### Overlapping Comparison

```tsx
<AreaChart
  data={data}
  dataKeys={['thisYear', 'lastYear']}
  colors={['#3b82f6', '#94a3b8']}
/>
```

### With React Query

```tsx
'use client'

import { AreaChart } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { metricsApi } from '@/lib/api/metrics-client'

export function TrafficBySource() {
  const { data = [] } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['traffic-by-source'],
    queryFn: metricsApi.trafficBySource,
  })

  return <AreaChart data={data} dataKeys={['organic', 'paid']} stacked />
}
```

---

## Lazy Variant

`AreaChartLazy` has the same props but code-splits the Recharts bundle:

```tsx
import { AreaChartLazy } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<AreaChartLazy data={data} dataKeys={['visits']} />
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Stack only real compositions** - Stacked areas imply the total matters
2. **Order stacked series** - Largest/most stable series at the bottom
3. **Name the X axis field `name`** - Map API data if needed
4. **Prefer LineChart for many series** - Overlapping areas get muddy past 2-3 series

---

## Related Components

- [LineChart](/docs/components/line-chart) - Trends without fill
- [BarChart](/docs/components/bar-chart) - Category comparison
- [Donut](/docs/components/pie-chart#donut) - Composition at one point in time
- [ChartWidget](/docs/components/chart-widget) - Chart inside a dashboard card

# PieChart

> Pie chart component for showing part-to-whole relationships

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/pie-chart.mdx

Pie chart component built on Recharts for visualizing part-to-whole relationships and proportions. With `innerRadius > 0` it renders as a donut.

<Callout type='warning' title='Use Sparingly'>
  Pie charts are best for showing 3-5 categories. For more categories or precise
  comparisons, consider using [BarChart](/docs/components/bar-chart) instead.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { PieChart } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const data = [
  { name: 'Desktop', value: 400 },
  { name: 'Mobile', value: 300 },
  { name: 'Tablet', value: 200 },
]

export default function DeviceChart() {
  return <PieChart data={data} dataKey='value' />
}
```

<Callout type='warn' title='The value prop is `dataKey`, colors come from `colors`'>
  The value field is **`dataKey`** (required), slice colors come from the `colors` array (cycled in
  data order — a `fill` field on the data is ignored), sizing is `height` + `outerRadius`, and
  there is no percentage/loading mode.
</Callout>

---

## Props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    data: { description: 'Chart data — objects with a label field and a numeric value field', type: 'ChartData[]', required: true },
    dataKey: { description: 'Field name holding each slice value', type: 'string', required: true },
    nameKey: { description: 'Field name holding each slice label', type: 'string', default: "'name'" },
    colors: { description: 'Slice colors, cycled in data order (defaults to the built-in 8-color palette)', type: 'string[]' },
    height: { description: 'Chart height in pixels', type: 'number', default: '300' },
    innerRadius: { description: 'Inner radius in px — 0 = pie, greater than 0 = donut', type: 'number', default: '0' },
    outerRadius: { description: 'Outer radius in px', type: 'number', default: '80' },
    showLabels: { description: 'Show slice labels next to the slices', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    showLegend: { description: 'Show the legend', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes on the wrapper', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

---

## Examples

### Custom Colors

```tsx
<PieChart
  data={[
    { name: 'Product A', value: 400 },
    { name: 'Product B', value: 300 },
    { name: 'Product C', value: 200 },
  ]}
  dataKey='value'
  colors={['#3b82f6', '#10b981', '#f59e0b']}
/>
```

Colors are applied by position — the first color goes to the first data item.

### Legend Only (no slice labels)

```tsx
<PieChart data={data} dataKey='value' showLabels={false} />
```

### Custom Field Names

```tsx
const traffic = [
  { source: 'Organic Search', visitors: 12500 },
  { source: 'Direct', visitors: 8200 },
]

<PieChart data={traffic} dataKey='visitors' nameKey='source' />
```

---

## Donut

A donut is `PieChart` with `innerRadius > 0`.
The ring thickness is `outerRadius - innerRadius`.

```tsx
import { PieChart } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const data = [
  { name: 'Completed', value: 620 },
  { name: 'In Progress', value: 210 },
  { name: 'Pending', value: 120 },
]

export function TasksChart() {
  return <PieChart data={data} dataKey='value' innerRadius={60} outerRadius={90} />
}
```

### Centered KPI

The component has no center-metric prop. Overlay one with CSS:

```tsx
<div className='relative'>
  <PieChart
    data={data}
    dataKey='value'
    innerRadius={60}
    outerRadius={90}
    showLabels={false}
  />
  <div className='pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 flex flex-col items-center justify-center'>
    <span className='text-3xl font-bold'>950</span>
    <span className='text-sm text-muted-foreground'>total tasks</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

### Thin ring

```tsx
<PieChart
  data={data}
  dataKey='value'
  innerRadius={80}
  outerRadius={90}
  showLabels={false}
  height={260}
/>
```

On rings, `showLabels={false}` plus the legend reads cleaner, and a 20-40px ring
balances legibility and weight.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/traffic-sources.tsx"
'use client'

import { PieChart, BaseCard } from '@telamonjs/ui'

interface TrafficSource {
  name: string
  value: number
}

export default function TrafficSources({ data }: { data: TrafficSource[] }) {
  const total = data.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.value, 0)

  return (
    <BaseCard
      title='Traffic Sources'
      description={`${total.toLocaleString()} total visitors`}
    >
      <PieChart data={data} dataKey='value' height={350} />
    </BaseCard>
  )
}
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Limit slices** - 3-5 categories max (combine small slices into "Other")
2. **Order by size** - Largest slice first (data order = drawing order)
3. **Use distinct colors** - Pass explicit `colors` when the default palette doesn't fit
4. **Provide totals** - Show the total value in the surrounding card
5. **Consider alternatives** - Bar charts are often better for 5+ categories

---

## When NOT to Use Pie Charts

❌ **Don't use when:**

- More than 5-6 categories
- Precise value comparison needed
- Values are very similar (hard to distinguish slices)
- Showing trends over time (use LineChart)

✅ **Use instead:**

- [BarChart](/docs/components/bar-chart) - For comparisons
- [Donut](#donut) - For emphasis on the total
- [LineChart](/docs/components/line-chart) - For trends

---

## Accessibility

- Tooltip shows exact values on hover/focus
- Don't rely on color alone — keep `showLabels` on or pair with a legend
- Prefer high-contrast custom `colors` when brand colors are too similar

---

## Related Components

- [BarChart](/docs/components/bar-chart) - Better for comparisons
- [KPICard](/docs/components/kpi-card) - Standalone KPI display
- [ChartWidget](/docs/components/chart-widget) - Chart inside a dashboard card, and charts the package does not wrap

---

## See Also

- [Recharts Documentation](https://recharts.org/en-US/api/PieChart) - Full API reference

---

# Timeline

> Timeline component for displaying chronological events and activities

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/timeline.mdx

Timeline component for displaying chronological events, activities, and status updates in a vertical or horizontal layout.

<Callout type='info' title='Business Component'>
  `Timeline` is perfect for activity feeds, order tracking, audit logs, and any
  chronological data visualization. Import it from `@telamonjs/ui` or `@telamonjs/ui/business`.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { Timeline, type TimelineItem } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const events = [
  {
    id: '1',
    title: 'Order Placed',
    description: 'Customer placed order #12345',
    timestamp: new Date('2024-01-20T10:30:00Z'),
    variant: 'success',
  },
  {
    id: '2',
    title: 'Payment Confirmed',
    description: 'Payment processed successfully',
    timestamp: new Date('2024-01-20T10:32:00Z'),
    variant: 'success',
  },
  {
    id: '3',
    title: 'Order Shipped',
    description: 'Package handed to carrier',
    timestamp: new Date('2024-01-21T14:15:00Z'),
  },
] satisfies TimelineItem[]

export default function OrderTimeline() {
  return <Timeline items={events} />
}
```

Each item's `timestamp` is rendered as relative time ("2 hours ago"), in the active locale.

---

## Props

```typescript
interface TimelineProps {
  items: TimelineItem[] // Timeline events (required)
  variant?: 'vertical' | 'horizontal' // Layout direction (default: 'vertical')
  showConnector?: boolean // Show line between events (default: true)
  className?: string // Additional classes
}

interface TimelineItem {
  id: string // Unique identifier
  title: string // Event title
  description?: string // Event description
  timestamp: Date // Event time (required), shown as relative time
  user?: { name: string; avatar?: string } // Actor, shown with an avatar
  icon?: React.ReactNode // Rendered element inside the dot (default: the item's 1-based index)
  variant?: 'default' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error' // Dot/connector color (default: 'default')
}
```

`TimelineItem` and `TimelineProps` are exported types. There is no `status`, `content`,
`iconColor` or `orientation` — use `variant` on the item for color and `variant` on the
`Timeline` for layout.

---

## Examples

### Vertical Timeline (Default)

```tsx
<Timeline
  items={[
    {
      id: '1',
      title: 'Account Created',
      description: 'User signed up successfully',
      timestamp: new Date('2024-01-15T09:00:00Z'),
      variant: 'success',
    },
    {
      id: '2',
      title: 'Email Verified',
      description: 'User verified their email address',
      timestamp: new Date('2024-01-15T09:15:00Z'),
      variant: 'success',
    },
    {
      id: '3',
      title: 'Profile Setup',
      description: 'Currently adding profile information',
      timestamp: new Date(),
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### With Custom Icons

`icon` is a rendered element, not a component reference:

```tsx
import { ShoppingCart, CreditCard, Truck } from 'lucide-react'
;<Timeline
  items={[
    {
      id: '1',
      title: 'Order Placed',
      timestamp: new Date('2024-01-20T10:30:00Z'),
      variant: 'success',
      icon: <ShoppingCart className='h-4 w-4' />,
    },
    {
      id: '2',
      title: 'Payment Confirmed',
      timestamp: new Date('2024-01-20T10:32:00Z'),
      variant: 'success',
      icon: <CreditCard className='h-4 w-4' />,
    },
    {
      id: '3',
      title: 'Out for Delivery',
      timestamp: new Date('2024-01-22T06:00:00Z'),
      icon: <Truck className='h-4 w-4' />,
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### With User

```tsx
<Timeline
  items={[
    {
      id: '1',
      title: 'Code Review Requested',
      timestamp: new Date('2024-01-20T14:00:00Z'),
      user: { name: 'John Doe', avatar: '/avatars/john.jpg' },
    },
    {
      id: '2',
      title: 'Review Completed',
      description: '2 approvals received',
      timestamp: new Date('2024-01-20T16:30:00Z'),
      user: { name: 'Jane Smith' },
      variant: 'success',
    },
  ]}
/>
```

Without `avatar`, the first letter of `name` is shown.

### Horizontal Timeline

```tsx
<Timeline
  variant='horizontal'
  items={[
    { id: '1', title: 'Step 1', timestamp: step1At, variant: 'success' },
    { id: '2', title: 'Step 2', timestamp: step2At, variant: 'success' },
    { id: '3', title: 'Step 3', timestamp: step3At },
  ]}
/>
```

Scrolls horizontally when the items don't fit. For a step-by-step progress view without
timestamps, use [ProgressTracker](/docs/components/progress-tracker).

### Error State

```tsx
<Timeline
  items={[
    {
      id: '1',
      title: 'Payment Initiated',
      timestamp: new Date('2024-01-20T10:00:00Z'),
      variant: 'success',
    },
    {
      id: '2',
      title: 'Payment Failed',
      description: 'Insufficient funds',
      timestamp: new Date('2024-01-20T10:01:00Z'),
      variant: 'error',
    },
  ]}
/>
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/order-tracking.tsx"
'use client'

import { Timeline, type TimelineItem } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import {
  Card,
  CardContent,
  CardDescription,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/card'
import { ShoppingCart, CreditCard, Package, Truck, Home } from 'lucide-react'

interface OrderEvent {
  id: string
  title: string
  description: string
  occurredAt: string
  failed?: boolean
}

const iconMap = {
  'Order Placed': ShoppingCart,
  'Payment Confirmed': CreditCard,
  'Package Prepared': Package,
  'Out for Delivery': Truck,
  Delivered: Home,
}

export default function OrderTracking({ events }: { events: OrderEvent[] }) {
  const timelineItems: TimelineItem[] = events.map(event => {
    const Icon = iconMap[event.title as keyof typeof iconMap]
    return {
      id: event.id,
      title: event.title,
      description: event.description,
      timestamp: new Date(event.occurredAt),
      variant: event.failed ? 'error' : 'success',
      icon: Icon ? <Icon className='h-4 w-4' /> : undefined,
    }
  })

  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Order Tracking</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>Track your order status in real-time</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <Timeline items={timelineItems} />
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Order tracking** - E-commerce shipment status
- **Activity feeds** - User actions, system events
- **Audit logs** - Security events, data changes
- **Process workflows** - Multi-step processes
- **Project milestones** - Development timeline
- **Status updates** - Ticket resolution, support cases
- **User onboarding** - Progress through setup steps

---

## Variant Colors

Each item's `variant` sets the color of its dot and connector:

| `variant` | Color |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | Blue |
| `success` | Green |
| `warning` | Yellow |
| `error` | Red |

There is no custom color per item; pick the closest `variant`.

---

## Best Practices

1. **Order chronologically** - Most recent first or last (be consistent)
2. **Use meaningful icons** - Match icons to event types
3. **Limit items** - Show 5-10 most recent, paginate rest
4. **Add descriptions** - Provide context for each event
5. **Use `variant` for meaning** - `success`/`error` for outcomes, `default` for neutral events

---

## Accessibility

- Timestamps render in a `<time>` element
- Event titles are `<h4>` headings
- Color is never the only signal: title and description are always text

---

## Performance

**Optimization tips:**

- Paginate or "load more" for long timelines
- Memoize the `items` array when it is derived from query data

**Example with pagination:**

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(1)
const itemsPerPage = 10
const visibleItems = items.slice(0, page * itemsPerPage)

<Timeline items={visibleItems} />
{visibleItems.length < items.length && (
  <Button onClick={() => setPage(p => p + 1)}>
    Load More
  </Button>
)}
```

---

## Related Components

- [DetailCard](/docs/components/detail-card) - For static event details
- [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) - Tabular event log
- [KanbanBoard](/docs/components/kanban-board) - Visual workflow

---

## See Also

- Audit Log Implementation - Backend setup

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# KanbanBoard

> Drag-and-drop kanban board for visual workflow management

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/kanban-board.mdx

Kanban board component with drag-and-drop support for visual workflow management and task tracking.

<Callout type='success' title='Built on dnd-kit'>
  `KanbanBoard` uses [@dnd-kit](https://dndkit.com/) for performant
  drag-and-drop (pointer/touch — a keyboard sensor is not wired up).
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
'use client'

import { KanbanBoard } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const columns = [
  {
    id: 'todo',
    title: 'To Do',
    cards: [
      { id: '1', title: 'Design homepage', description: 'Create mockups' },
      { id: '2', title: 'Setup database', description: 'PostgreSQL config' },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: 'in_progress',
    title: 'In Progress',
    cards: [
      { id: '3', title: 'Implement auth', description: 'NextAuth setup' },
    ],
  },
  {
    id: 'done',
    title: 'Done',
    cards: [
      { id: '4', title: 'Project setup', description: 'Next.js initialized' },
    ],
  },
]

export default function ProjectBoard() {
  function handleCardMove(
    cardId: string,
    fromColumn: string,
    toColumn: string
  ) {
    console.log(`Moved ${cardId} from ${fromColumn} to ${toColumn}`)
    // Update backend
  }

  return <KanbanBoard columns={columns} onCardMove={handleCardMove} />
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface KanbanBoardProps {
  columns: KanbanColumn[] // Board columns (required)
  onCardMove: (cardId: string, fromColumn: string, toColumn: string) => void
  onCardClick?: (card: KanbanCard) => void // Card click handler
  className?: string // Additional classes
}
```

<TypeTable
  type={{
    columns: { description: 'Board columns with their cards', type: 'KanbanColumn[]', required: true },
    onCardMove: {
      description: 'Called after a drop on another column — update your state here (the board does not mutate columns itself)',
      type: '(cardId: string, fromColumn: string, toColumn: string) => void',
      required: true,
    },
    onCardClick: { description: 'Called when a card is clicked (not dragged)', type: '(card: KanbanCard) => void' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

### KanbanColumn

<TypeTable
  type={{
    id: { description: 'Unique column ID', type: 'string', required: true },
    title: { description: 'Column title', type: 'string', required: true },
    cards: { description: 'Cards in the column', type: 'KanbanCard[]', required: true },
    color: { description: 'Accent dot color shown next to the title (any CSS color)', type: 'string' },
    limit: {
      description: 'WIP limit — display only ("3 / 5" in the header); it does not block moves',
      type: 'number',
    },
  }}
/>

### KanbanCard

<TypeTable
  type={{
    id: { description: 'Unique card ID', type: 'string', required: true },
    title: { description: 'Card title', type: 'string', required: true },
    description: { description: 'Card description', type: 'string' },
    assignee: { description: 'Assigned user (avatar falls back to initials)', type: '{ name: string; avatar?: string }' },
    priority: { description: 'Priority badge', type: "'low' | 'medium' | 'high'" },
    dueDate: { description: 'Due date (a Date object, not a string)', type: 'Date' },
    tags: { description: 'Tag labels', type: 'string[]' },
  }}
/>

<Callout type='warn' title='Your page owns the columns'>
  Column management and custom card rendering are up to your page; `KanbanColumn.limit` is
  display-only.
</Callout>

---

## Examples

### Basic Board

```tsx
<KanbanBoard
  columns={columns}
  onCardMove={(cardId, from, to) => {
    // Handle move
  }}
/>
```

### With Card Details

```tsx
const columns = [
  {
    id: 'backlog',
    title: 'Backlog',
    cards: [
      {
        id: '1',
        title: 'Add user authentication',
        description: 'Implement login and signup flows',
        assignee: { name: 'John Doe', avatar: '/avatars/john.jpg' },
        tags: ['feature', 'high-priority'],
        priority: 'high',
        dueDate: new Date('2026-01-25'),
      },
    ],
  },
]

<KanbanBoard columns={columns} onCardMove={handleMove} />
```

### With Column Limits

```tsx
const columns = [
  {
    id: 'in_progress',
    title: 'In Progress',
    limit: 3,  // WIP limit — shown as "1 / 3" in the header
    cards: [...],
  },
]

<KanbanBoard columns={columns} onCardMove={handleMove} />
```

The limit is informational — enforce it in your `onCardMove` handler if you
need a hard cap (skip the state update when the target column is full).

### Click Handler

```tsx
<KanbanBoard
  columns={columns}
  onCardMove={handleMove}
  onCardClick={card => {
    router.push(`/tasks/${card.id}`)
  }}
/>
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="app/projects/[id]/board/page.tsx"
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { KanbanBoard, type KanbanColumn } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useMutation } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { tasksApi } from '@/lib/api/tasks-client'

export default function ProjectBoard({
  initialData,
}: {
  initialData: KanbanColumn[]
}) {
  const [columns, setColumns] = useState(initialData)

  const moveMutation = useMutation({
    mutationFn: ({ cardId, toColumn }: { cardId: string; toColumn: string }) =>
      tasksApi.updateStatus(cardId, toColumn),
  })

  function handleCardMove(cardId: string, fromColumn: string, toColumn: string) {
    // Optimistic update
    setColumns(cols => {
      const card = cols
        .find(c => c.id === fromColumn)
        ?.cards.find(c => c.id === cardId)
      if (!card) return cols
      return cols.map(col => {
        if (col.id === fromColumn)
          return { ...col, cards: col.cards.filter(c => c.id !== cardId) }
        if (col.id === toColumn) return { ...col, cards: [...col.cards, card] }
        return col
      })
    })

    // Persist to backend
    moveMutation.mutate({ cardId, toColumn })
  }

  return (
    <div className='container py-6'>
      <div className='mb-6'>
        <h1 className='text-3xl font-bold'>Project Board</h1>
        <p className='text-muted-foreground'>
          Drag and drop tasks to update their status
        </p>
      </div>

      <KanbanBoard
        columns={columns}
        onCardMove={handleCardMove}
        onCardClick={card => console.log('open task', card.id)}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Project management** - Task tracking, sprint boards
- **Sales pipelines** - Lead stages, deal tracking
- **Hiring workflows** - Candidate pipeline
- **Support tickets** - Issue triage and resolution
- **Content production** - Editorial workflow
- **Order fulfillment** - Order status tracking

---

## State Management

**Client-side state:**

```tsx
const [columns, setColumns] = useState(initialData)
```

**With optimistic updates:**

```tsx
async function handleCardMove(cardId, from, to) {
  // 1. Update UI immediately
  setColumns(optimisticUpdate)

  // 2. Persist to backend
  try {
    await updateCard(cardId, { status: to })
  } catch (error) {
    // 3. Rollback on error
    setColumns(previousState)
    toast.error('Failed to update task')
  }
}
```

**With React Query (standard):**

```tsx
const moveMutation = useMutation({
  mutationFn: ({ cardId, toColumn }: { cardId: string; toColumn: string }) =>
    tasksApi.updateStatus(cardId, toColumn),
  onError: () => {
    setColumns(previousState)
    toast.error('Failed to update task')
  },
})
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Limit columns** - 3-6 columns for optimal UX
2. **Set WIP limits** - Prevent bottlenecks (e.g., max 5 in "In Progress")
3. **Add filters** - Filter by assignee, priority, tags
4. **Optimistic updates** - Move the card in state immediately, persist async
5. **Mobile-friendly** - Pointer sensor covers touch drag

---

## Accessibility

- Drag-and-drop uses dnd-kit's `PointerSensor` (mouse + touch) with an
  activation distance so plain clicks still fire `onCardClick`
- Keyboard-driven dragging is **not** wired up (no `KeyboardSensor`) — if
  card movement must be keyboard accessible, offer an alternative action
  (e.g. a "move to column" menu via `onCardClick`)

---

## Performance

**Optimization tips:**

- Lazy load card details (fetch them in `onCardClick`)
- Debounce backend updates
- Use optimistic updates
- Every card renders (no virtualization) — filter or paginate very large columns before passing them

---

## Related Components

- [Timeline](/docs/components/timeline) - Linear event tracking
- [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) - Tabular view
- [Calendar](/docs/components/calendar) - Time-based planning

---

## See Also

- [dnd-kit Documentation](https://docs.dndkit.com/) - Drag-and-drop library
- Kanban Best Practices - Workflow optimization

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

---

# Calendar

> Interactive calendar component for date selection and event display

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/calendar.mdx

Two calendar components: `Calendar`, a date picker grid for selecting dates, and
`CalendarWithEvents`, a month view that lays events out on their days.

<Callout type='info' title='Which one?'>
  Use `Calendar` (from `@telamonjs/ui`) to pick a date, several dates or a range. Use
  `CalendarWithEvents` (from `@telamonjs/ui` or `@telamonjs/ui/business`) for booking systems,
  event management and scheduling screens that show events per day.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { Calendar } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function DatePicker() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<Date | undefined>(new Date())

  return <Calendar mode='single' selected={selected} onSelect={setSelected} />
}
```

```tsx
'use client'

import { CalendarWithEvents, type CalendarEvent } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function TeamCalendar({ events }: { events: CalendarEvent[] }) {
  return (
    <CalendarWithEvents
      events={events}
      onDateClick={date => console.log('day', date)}
      onEventClick={event => console.log('event', event.id)}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Props

### Calendar

`Calendar` is a styled [react-day-picker](https://react-day-picker.js.org/) `DayPicker`:
`CalendarProps` is `React.ComponentProps<typeof DayPicker>`, so every DayPicker prop works.
The ones you will use most:

```typescript
// CalendarProps = React.ComponentProps<typeof DayPicker>
{
  mode?: 'single' | 'multiple' | 'range' // Selection mode (enables selected/onSelect)
  selected?: Date | Date[] | DateRange // Shape follows `mode`
  onSelect?: (selected) => void // Receives the same shape as `selected`
  defaultMonth?: Date // Initial month shown
  disabled?: Matcher | Matcher[] // Dates, ranges or { before } / { after } / { dayOfWeek }
  startMonth?: Date // Earliest month the user can navigate to
  endMonth?: Date // Latest month the user can navigate to
  weekStartsOn?: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 // 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday
  showWeekNumber?: boolean // Show week numbers
  showOutsideDays?: boolean // Days of adjacent months (default: true)
  locale?: Locale // date-fns locale object
  className?: string // Additional classes
  classNames?: Partial<ClassNames> // Merged over the built-in styles
}
```

### CalendarWithEvents

```typescript
interface CalendarWithEventsProps {
  events: CalendarEvent[] // Events to display (required)
  onDateClick?: (date: Date) => void // A day cell was clicked
  onEventClick?: (event: CalendarEvent) => void // An event chip was clicked
  defaultDate?: Date // Month shown first (default: today)
  onMonthChange?: (month: Date) => void // User navigated; gets the 1st day of the new month
  className?: string // Additional classes
}

interface CalendarEvent {
  id: string
  title: string
  date: Date // Day the event is shown on
  color?: string // CSS color for the chip (default: primary)
  allDay?: boolean
  description?: string
}
```

`CalendarWithEvents` shows one month at a time with Today / previous / next month buttons,
up to two event chips per day and a "+N more" line for the rest. There is no week or day view.

---

## Examples

### Single Date Selection

```tsx
const [date, setDate] = useState<Date>()

<Calendar
  mode="single"
  selected={date}
  onSelect={setDate}
/>
```

### Multiple Date Selection

```tsx
const [dates, setDates] = useState<Date[] | undefined>([])

<Calendar
  mode="multiple"
  selected={dates}
  onSelect={setDates}
/>
```

Select multiple individual dates.

### Date Range Selection

```tsx
import type { DateRange } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const [range, setRange] = useState<DateRange | undefined>()

<Calendar
  mode="range"
  selected={range}
  onSelect={setRange}
/>
```

Select start and end dates (e.g., booking periods).

### With Events

```tsx
const events = [
  {
    id: '1',
    title: 'Team Meeting',
    date: new Date(2024, 0, 20, 10, 0),
    color: '#3b82f6',
  },
  {
    id: '2',
    title: 'Project Deadline',
    date: new Date(2024, 0, 25),
    allDay: true,
    color: '#ef4444',
  },
]

<CalendarWithEvents
  events={events}
  defaultDate={new Date(2024, 0, 1)}
  onEventClick={(event) => console.log(event)}
/>
```

Shows events on calendar dates.

### Loading Events Per Month

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { startOfMonth } from 'date-fns'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { CalendarWithEvents } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function AgendaCalendar() {
  const [month, setMonth] = useState(() => startOfMonth(new Date()))
  const { data: events = [] } = useQuery({
    queryKey: ['agenda', month.toISOString()],
    queryFn: () => agendaApi.listByMonth(month),
  })

  return <CalendarWithEvents events={events} onMonthChange={setMonth} />
}
```

`onMonthChange` fires when the user moves to another month (previous, next, or Today while
another month is shown) with the first day of that month. It does not fire on mount — start
your state at the month you pass as `defaultDate` (today by default).

### Disabled Dates

```tsx
const disabledDates = [
  new Date(2024, 0, 15),
  new Date(2024, 0, 22),
]

<Calendar
  mode="single"
  selected={date}
  onSelect={setDate}
  disabled={disabledDates}
/>
```

Prevent selection of specific dates.

### Disable Past Dates

```tsx
<Calendar mode='single' selected={date} onSelect={setDate} disabled={{ before: new Date() }} />
```

Only allow future date selection (booking systems).

### Date Range Restrictions

```tsx
<Calendar
  mode="single"
  selected={date}
  onSelect={setDate}
  disabled={[{ before: new Date() }, { after: new Date(2024, 11, 31) }]}
  startMonth={new Date()}
  endMonth={new Date(2024, 11)}
/>
```

### First Day of Week

```tsx
// Monday as first day
<Calendar
  mode="single"
  selected={date}
  onSelect={setDate}
  weekStartsOn={1}
/>
```

`CalendarWithEvents` takes the first day of the week from the active locale.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/booking-calendar.tsx"
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { Calendar } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import {
  Card,
  CardContent,
  CardDescription,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from '@/components/ui/card'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'

interface Booking {
  id: string
  date: Date
  timeSlot: string
  customer: string
}

export default function BookingCalendar({ bookings }: { bookings: Booking[] }) {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<Date>()

  // Get booked dates to disable
  const bookedDates = bookings.map(b => b.date)

  function handleDateSelect(date: Date | undefined) {
    if (!date) return
    setSelected(date)
    // Open booking form for selected date
  }

  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader>
        <CardTitle>Appointment Booking</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>
          Select a date to view available time slots
        </CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>
        <Calendar
          mode='single'
          selected={selected}
          onSelect={handleDateSelect}
          disabled={[...bookedDates, { before: new Date() }]}
          className='mx-auto'
        />

        {selected && (
          <div className='mt-6 space-y-2'>
            <h4 className='font-semibold'>
              Available Slots for {selected.toLocaleDateString()}
            </h4>
            <div className='grid grid-cols-3 gap-2'>
              {['09:00', '10:00', '11:00', '14:00', '15:00', '16:00'].map(
                slot => (
                  <Button key={slot} variant='outline'>
                    {slot}
                  </Button>
                )
              )}
            </div>
          </div>
        )}
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Booking systems** - Appointments, reservations, rentals
- **Event management** - Conference schedules, event calendars
- **Project planning** - Deadlines, milestones, sprints
- **Availability** - Staff schedules, resource allocation
- **Date pickers** - Forms with date selection
- **Content calendar** - Publishing schedule
- **Leave management** - PTO requests, vacation tracking

---

## Best Practices

1. **Clear visual feedback** - Highlight selected dates prominently
2. **Disable unavailable dates** - Prevent invalid selections
3. **Show events** - Display bookings, holidays, important dates
4. **Mobile-friendly** - Ensure touch targets are 44×44px minimum
5. **Time zone awareness** - Handle time zones correctly
6. **Loading states** - Show skeleton when loading events
7. **Legend** - Explain color coding for events

---

## Accessibility

`Calendar` inherits react-day-picker's grid semantics and keyboard support:

- `Arrow keys` - Navigate between dates
- `Enter/Space` - Select date
- `PageUp/PageDown` - Previous/next month
- `Home/End` - First/last day of the week

`CalendarWithEvents` navigation buttons are labeled ("Previous month" / "Next month", localized),
but day cells and event chips are clickable `div`s without keyboard focus — offer another way
(a list or a form) to reach the same actions from the keyboard.

---

## Localization

`CalendarWithEvents` formats month names, weekdays and the first day of the week with the
active TelamonJS locale. `Calendar` takes react-day-picker's `locale` prop (a date-fns locale):

```tsx
import { ptBR } from 'date-fns/locale'
;<Calendar
  mode='single'
  selected={date}
  onSelect={setDate}
  locale={ptBR}
/>
```

---

## Performance

**Optimization tips:**

- Lazy load events (fetch only the visible month)
- Memoize the `events` array when it is derived from query data
- Cache formatted dates

---

## Related Components

- `DateRangePicker` - Form date range input
- [Timeline](/docs/components/timeline) - Event timeline
- [KanbanBoard](/docs/components/kanban-board) - Visual workflow

---

## See Also

- [react-day-picker](https://react-day-picker.js.org/) - Library behind `Calendar`
- Booking System Pattern - Implementation guide

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable
