# ComparisonTable

> Feature comparison table for plans or products, with check/cross cells and grouped rows

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/comparison-table.mdx

Table component for comparing plans or products feature by feature: one column per option,
one row per feature, optionally grouped by category.

<Callout type='info' title='Data Comparison'>
  `ComparisonTable` renders booleans as check/cross icons, numbers locale-formatted and strings
  as is. Import it from `@telamonjs/ui` or `@telamonjs/ui/charts`.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { ComparisonTable } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const columns = [
  { label: 'Basic', key: 'basic' },
  { label: 'Pro', key: 'pro', highlight: true, badge: 'Popular' },
  { label: 'Enterprise', key: 'enterprise' },
]

const rows = [
  { feature: 'Users', basic: 5, pro: 20, enterprise: 'Unlimited' },
  { feature: 'Storage', basic: '10 GB', pro: '100 GB', enterprise: '1 TB' },
  { feature: 'Priority support', basic: false, pro: true, enterprise: true },
]

export default function PlanComparison() {
  return <ComparisonTable columns={columns} rows={rows} />
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface ComparisonTableProps {
  columns: ComparisonColumn[] // One column per plan/product (required)
  rows: ComparisonRow[] // One row per feature (required)
  stickyHeader?: boolean // Keep the header visible while scrolling (default: true)
  className?: string // Additional classes
}

interface ComparisonColumn {
  label: string // Column header
  key: string // Field read from each row
  highlight?: boolean // Tint the whole column (e.g. the recommended plan)
  badge?: string // Small badge under the header
}

interface ComparisonRow {
  feature: string // Row label, first column (required)
  category?: string // Group rows under a category heading
  [key: string]: string | boolean | number | undefined // Value per column key
}
```

The first column's header is the localized "Feature" label. There is no `title`, `data`,
sorting or sparkline support — wrap the table in a card with your own heading if you need one.

---

## Examples

### Cell Values

```tsx
const rows = [
  { feature: 'API access', basic: false, pro: true }, // ✓ / ✗ icons
  { feature: 'Projects', basic: 3, pro: 1000 }, // locale-formatted numbers
  { feature: 'SLA', basic: undefined, pro: '99.9%' }, // missing/empty → "-"
]

<ComparisonTable
  columns={[
    { label: 'Basic', key: 'basic' },
    { label: 'Pro', key: 'pro' },
  ]}
  rows={rows}
/>
```

### Highlighted Column with Badge

```tsx
<ComparisonTable
  columns={[
    { label: 'Starter', key: 'starter' },
    { label: 'Business', key: 'business', highlight: true, badge: 'Best value' },
  ]}
  rows={rows}
/>
```

### Grouped by Category

```tsx
const rows = [
  { feature: 'Users', category: 'Limits', basic: 5, pro: 20 },
  { feature: 'Storage', category: 'Limits', basic: '10 GB', pro: '100 GB' },
  { feature: 'SSO', category: 'Security', basic: false, pro: true },
  { feature: 'Audit log', category: 'Security', basic: false, pro: true },
]

<ComparisonTable columns={columns} rows={rows} />
```

Rows are grouped by `category` in order of first appearance; rows without a category are listed
without a heading.

### Without Sticky Header

```tsx
<ComparisonTable columns={columns} rows={rows} stickyHeader={false} />
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/pricing-comparison.tsx"
'use client'

import {
  ComparisonTable,
  type ComparisonColumn,
  type ComparisonRow,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { use } from 'react'
import { getPlans } from './service'

export default function PricingComparison() {
  const plans = use(getPlans())

  const columns: ComparisonColumn[] = plans.map(plan => ({
    label: plan.name,
    key: plan.id,
    highlight: plan.recommended,
    badge: plan.recommended ? 'Recommended' : undefined,
  }))

  const rows: ComparisonRow[] = plans[0].features.map(({ name, group }) => ({
    feature: name,
    category: group,
    ...Object.fromEntries(
      plans.map(plan => [plan.id, plan.features.find(f => f.name === name)?.value])
    ),
  }))

  return (
    <div className='space-y-4'>
      <h2 className='text-xl font-semibold'>Compare plans</h2>
      <ComparisonTable columns={columns} rows={rows} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Pricing pages** - Compare subscription plans
- **Product comparisons** - Compare product features side by side
- **Vendor evaluation** - Compare suppliers or tools
- **Release notes** - What each edition includes

---

## Best Practices

1. **Highlight one column** - Point the reader to the recommended option
2. **Use booleans for yes/no features** - They render as icons
3. **Group long lists** - Use `category` once there are more than a handful of rows
4. **Keep column keys stable** - Every row must use the same keys as `columns`

---

## Accessibility

- Semantic HTML `<table>` with a header row
- Check/cross cells are icons only — when a yes/no answer matters, prefer a short string
  (`'Included'`, `'—'`) so screen readers get text

---

## Responsive Behavior

The table scrolls horizontally inside its card when the columns don't fit
(each value column has a minimum width).

---

## Related Components

- [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) - Advanced data table
- [KPICard](/docs/components/kpi-card) - Single KPI display
- [LineChart](/docs/components/line-chart) - Full-size charts

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

---

# ProgressTracker

> Visual progress indicator with multiple steps and status

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/progress-tracker.mdx

Visual progress tracking component for multi-step processes, workflows, and completion status.

<Callout type='info' title='Workflow Visualization'>
  `ProgressTracker` provides clear visual feedback for sequential processes with
  step-by-step progress indication. It is display-only: you compute each step's status.
  Import it from `@telamonjs/ui` or `@telamonjs/ui/charts`.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { ProgressTracker, type ProgressStep } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const steps: ProgressStep[] = [
  { label: 'Account Info', status: 'completed' },
  { label: 'Personal Details', status: 'current' },
  { label: 'Preferences', status: 'pending' },
  { label: 'Review', status: 'pending' },
]

export default function OnboardingProgress() {
  return <ProgressTracker steps={steps} />
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface ProgressTrackerProps {
  steps: ProgressStep[] // Steps array (required)
  variant?: 'horizontal' | 'vertical' // Layout (default: 'horizontal')
  className?: string // Additional classes
}

interface ProgressStep {
  label: string // Step label (required, also used as the React key — keep it unique)
  status: 'completed' | 'current' | 'pending' // Step status (required)
  description?: string // Text under the label
}
```

There is no click handler, custom icon, optional flag or error status — for an interactive
wizard use `Stepper` (also exported from `@telamonjs/ui`).

---

## Step Status

### Completed

```tsx
{ label: 'Account Created', status: 'completed' }
```

Shows a checkmark on a filled primary circle.

### Current

```tsx
{ label: 'Email Verification', status: 'current' }
```

Shows the step number in an outlined primary circle; the label is highlighted.

### Pending

```tsx
{ label: 'Profile Setup', status: 'pending' }
```

Shows the step number in a muted circle with a muted label.

The connector leading into a step is filled once that step is `current` or `completed`.

---

## Examples

### Basic Progress

```tsx
const steps: ProgressStep[] = [
  { label: 'Step 1', status: 'completed' },
  { label: 'Step 2', status: 'current' },
  { label: 'Step 3', status: 'pending' },
]

<ProgressTracker steps={steps} />
```

### With Descriptions

```tsx
const steps: ProgressStep[] = [
  {
    label: 'Personal Info',
    description: 'Basic information about yourself',
    status: 'completed',
  },
  {
    label: 'Address',
    description: 'Where you live',
    status: 'current',
  },
  {
    label: 'Payment',
    description: 'Payment method',
    status: 'pending',
  },
]

<ProgressTracker steps={steps} />
```

### Vertical Layout

```tsx
<ProgressTracker steps={steps} variant='vertical' />
```

Better for sidebars or narrow spaces.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/onboarding-wizard.tsx"
'use client'

import { ProgressTracker, type ProgressStep } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useState } from 'react'

const STEPS = [
  { label: 'Personal Information', description: 'Tell us about yourself' },
  { label: 'Company Details', description: 'Information about your company' },
  { label: 'Payment Method', description: 'How you want to pay' },
  { label: 'Review & Complete', description: 'Confirm your information' },
]

export default function OnboardingWizard() {
  const [currentStep, setCurrentStep] = useState(0)

  const steps: ProgressStep[] = STEPS.map((step, index) => ({
    ...step,
    status:
      index < currentStep ? 'completed' : index === currentStep ? 'current' : 'pending',
  }))

  return (
    <div className='space-y-8'>
      <ProgressTracker steps={steps} />

      <div className='bg-card rounded-lg border p-6'>
        {/* Step content */}
        {currentStep === 0 && <PersonalInfoForm />}
        {currentStep === 1 && <CompanyDetailsForm />}
        {currentStep === 2 && <PaymentMethodForm />}
        {currentStep === 3 && <ReviewStep />}

        <div className='flex justify-between mt-6'>
          <button
            onClick={() => setCurrentStep(Math.max(0, currentStep - 1))}
            disabled={currentStep === 0}
          >
            Previous
          </button>
          <button
            onClick={() => setCurrentStep(Math.min(3, currentStep + 1))}
            disabled={currentStep === 3}
          >
            Next
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Multi-step forms** - Wizards, onboarding
- **Checkout processes** - E-commerce cart → payment → confirmation
- **Workflow tracking** - Order fulfillment, approval processes
- **Onboarding** - User/employee onboarding
- **Project milestones** - Project progress visualization

---

## Best Practices

1. **Clear labels** - Concise step names (1-3 words)
2. **Linear progression** - Don't skip steps in status
3. **One current step** - Exactly one step should be `current`
4. **Allow backtracking** - Let users go back to previous steps
5. **Mobile responsive** - Prefer `variant='vertical'` on narrow screens

---

## Accessibility

- Step labels and descriptions are plain text; completed steps also show a check icon,
  so status is not conveyed by color alone
- The tracker has no ARIA step semantics — announce the current step in your own text
  (e.g. "Step 2 of 4") when it matters

---

## Responsive Behavior

**Horizontal (default):** steps share the full width; with many steps or long labels, switch
to vertical on small screens.

**Vertical:** works well on all screen sizes and in sidebars.

---

## Related Components

- [Timeline](/docs/components/timeline) - Event timeline
- `Stepper` - Interactive multi-step wizard

---

## See Also

- Multi-Step Forms - Wizard pattern
- Progress Indicators - UX best practices

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

---

# DropdownMenu

> Dropdown menu component for actions and options

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/dropdown-menu.mdx

Dropdown menu component for displaying contextual actions, options, and navigation in a floating menu.

<Callout type='info' title='Built on Radix UI'>
  `DropdownMenu` uses [Radix
  UI](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/dropdown-menu) for
  accessible, keyboard-friendly interactions.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { MoreVertical } from 'lucide-react'

export default function ActionsMenu() {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger>
        <MoreVertical className='w-4 h-4' />
      </DropdownMenuTrigger>

      <DropdownMenuContent>
        <DropdownMenuItem>Edit</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>
        <DropdownMenuItem>Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  )
}
```

---

## Components

```typescript
// Main container
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger />  // Trigger button
  <DropdownMenuContent>    // Floating menu
    <DropdownMenuItem />   // Menu item
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />  // Divider
    <DropdownMenuLabel />  // Section label
    <DropdownMenuSub />    // Submenu (with SubTrigger + SubContent)
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

<Callout type='warn' title='Root barrel exports'>
  The root barrel exports: `DropdownMenu`, `DropdownMenuTrigger`,
  `DropdownMenuContent`, `DropdownMenuItem`, `DropdownMenuLabel`,
  `DropdownMenuSeparator`, `DropdownMenuShortcut`, `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`,
  `DropdownMenuRadioGroup`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem`, `DropdownMenuSub`,
  `DropdownMenuSubTrigger`, `DropdownMenuSubContent`. There is no
  `DropdownMenuGroup` or `DropdownMenuPortal`: use labels + separators for
  grouping; `DropdownMenuContent` already renders in a portal.
</Callout>

---

## Props

All sub-components forward the props of their [Radix UI
counterparts](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/dropdown-menu).
The ones you will actually reach for:

### DropdownMenuContent

<TypeTable
  type={{
    align: {
      description: 'Alignment relative to the trigger',
      type: "'start' | 'center' | 'end'",
      default: "'center'",
    },
    side: {
      description: 'Preferred side of the trigger',
      type: "'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left'",
      default: "'bottom'",
    },
    sideOffset: { description: 'Distance from the trigger in px', type: 'number', default: '4' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

### DropdownMenuItem

<TypeTable
  type={{
    onSelect: { description: 'Called when the item is selected (also fires for keyboard selection)', type: '(event: Event) => void' },
    onClick: { description: 'Regular React click handler — also works', type: 'React.MouseEventHandler' },
    disabled: { description: 'Disable the item', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    inset: { description: 'Indent to align with items that have icons/indicators', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

### DropdownMenuCheckboxItem

<TypeTable
  type={{
    checked: { description: 'Controlled checked state', type: "boolean | 'indeterminate'" },
    onCheckedChange: { description: 'Called when the checked state changes', type: '(checked: boolean) => void' },
    disabled: { description: 'Disable the item', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
  }}
/>

### DropdownMenuRadioGroup / DropdownMenuRadioItem

<TypeTable
  type={{
    value: { description: 'Group: selected value. Item: the value this item represents', type: 'string', required: true },
    onValueChange: { description: 'Group only — called with the newly selected value', type: '(value: string) => void' },
  }}
/>

---

## Examples

### With Icons

```tsx
import { Edit, Copy, Trash2, Download } from 'lucide-react'
;<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant='outline'>Actions</Button>
  </DropdownMenuTrigger>

  <DropdownMenuContent>
    <DropdownMenuItem>
      <Edit className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
      Edit
    </DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuItem>
      <Copy className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
      Duplicate
    </DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuItem>
      <Download className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
      Download
    </DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem className='text-destructive'>
      <Trash2 className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
      Delete
    </DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

### With Shortcuts

```tsx
<DropdownMenuItem>
  <span>Edit</span>
  <span className="ml-auto text-xs text-muted-foreground">⌘E</span>
</DropdownMenuItem>
<DropdownMenuItem>
  <span>Duplicate</span>
  <span className="ml-auto text-xs text-muted-foreground">⌘D</span>
</DropdownMenuItem>
```

### With Separators and Labels

```tsx
<DropdownMenuContent>
  <DropdownMenuLabel>Account</DropdownMenuLabel>
  <DropdownMenuSeparator />
  <DropdownMenuItem>Profile</DropdownMenuItem>
  <DropdownMenuItem>Billing</DropdownMenuItem>
  <DropdownMenuItem>Settings</DropdownMenuItem>
  <DropdownMenuSeparator />
  <DropdownMenuLabel>Danger Zone</DropdownMenuLabel>
  <DropdownMenuItem className='text-destructive'>
    Delete Account
  </DropdownMenuItem>
</DropdownMenuContent>
```

### With Submenu

```tsx
import { ChevronRight } from 'lucide-react'
;<DropdownMenuContent>
  <DropdownMenuItem>Edit</DropdownMenuItem>

  <DropdownMenuSub>
    <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
      Export
      <ChevronRight className='w-4 h-4 ml-auto' />
    </DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
    <DropdownMenuSubContent>
      <DropdownMenuItem>Export as CSV</DropdownMenuItem>
      <DropdownMenuItem>Export as Excel</DropdownMenuItem>
      <DropdownMenuItem>Export as PDF</DropdownMenuItem>
    </DropdownMenuSubContent>
  </DropdownMenuSub>

  <DropdownMenuItem>Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
</DropdownMenuContent>
```

### With Checkboxes

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'

export default function ViewOptionsMenu() {
  const [showSidebar, setShowSidebar] = useState(true)
  const [showToolbar, setShowToolbar] = useState(true)

  return (
    <DropdownMenuContent>
      <DropdownMenuLabel>View Options</DropdownMenuLabel>
      <DropdownMenuSeparator />

      <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
        checked={showSidebar}
        onCheckedChange={setShowSidebar}
      >
        Show Sidebar
      </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>

      <DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
        checked={showToolbar}
        onCheckedChange={setShowToolbar}
      >
        Show Toolbar
      </DropdownMenuCheckboxItem>
    </DropdownMenuContent>
  )
}
```

### With Radio Items

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'

export default function ThemeMenu() {
  const [theme, setTheme] = useState('light')

  return (
    <DropdownMenuContent>
      <DropdownMenuLabel>Theme</DropdownMenuLabel>
      <DropdownMenuSeparator />

      <DropdownMenuRadioGroup value={theme} onValueChange={setTheme}>
        <DropdownMenuRadioItem value='light'>Light</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
        <DropdownMenuRadioItem value='dark'>Dark</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
        <DropdownMenuRadioItem value='system'>System</DropdownMenuRadioItem>
      </DropdownMenuRadioGroup>
    </DropdownMenuContent>
  )
}
```

### User Menu

```tsx
import { User, Settings, LogOut } from 'lucide-react'
;<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant='ghost' size='icon'>
      <Avatar className='h-8 w-8'>
        <AvatarFallback>JD</AvatarFallback>
      </Avatar>
    </Button>
  </DropdownMenuTrigger>

  <DropdownMenuContent align='end'>
    <DropdownMenuLabel>
      <div>John Doe</div>
      <div className='text-xs text-muted-foreground'>john@example.com</div>
    </DropdownMenuLabel>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem>
      <User className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
      Profile
    </DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuItem>
      <Settings className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
      Settings
    </DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => signOut()}>
      <LogOut className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
      Log out
    </DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/row-actions-menu.tsx"
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
  DropdownMenuSubContent,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'
import {
  MoreVertical,
  Edit,
  Copy,
  Download,
  Share2,
  Trash2,
} from 'lucide-react'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'

interface RowActionsMenuProps {
  row: { id: string }
  onEdit: (id: string) => void
  onDuplicate: (id: string) => void
  onDelete: (id: string) => void
}

export default function RowActionsMenu({
  row,
  onEdit,
  onDuplicate,
  onDelete,
}: RowActionsMenuProps) {
  return (
    <DropdownMenu>
      <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant='ghost' size='icon'>
          <MoreVertical className='w-4 h-4' />
          <span className='sr-only'>Open menu</span>
        </Button>
      </DropdownMenuTrigger>

      <DropdownMenuContent align='end'>
        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => onEdit(row.id)}>
          <Edit className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
          Edit
        </DropdownMenuItem>

        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => onDuplicate(row.id)}>
          <Copy className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
          Duplicate
        </DropdownMenuItem>

        <DropdownMenuSeparator />

        <DropdownMenuSub>
          <DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
            <Download className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
            Export
          </DropdownMenuSubTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuSubContent>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => exportAs(row.id, 'csv')}>
              Export as CSV
            </DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => exportAs(row.id, 'excel')}>
              Export as Excel
            </DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => exportAs(row.id, 'pdf')}>
              Export as PDF
            </DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuSubContent>
        </DropdownMenuSub>

        <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => shareRecord(row.id)}>
          <Share2 className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
          Share
        </DropdownMenuItem>

        <DropdownMenuSeparator />

        <DropdownMenuItem
          onClick={() => onDelete(row.id)}
          className='text-destructive focus:text-destructive'
        >
          <Trash2 className='w-4 h-4 mr-2' />
          Delete
        </DropdownMenuItem>
      </DropdownMenuContent>
    </DropdownMenu>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Row actions** - Table row operations (edit, delete, etc.)
- **User menus** - Profile, settings, logout
- **Context menus** - Right-click or click actions
- **Bulk actions** - Operations on selected items
- **Settings** - Theme, language, preferences
- **Navigation** - Quick access to pages

---

## Best Practices

1. **Group related actions** - Use separators and labels
2. **Destructive actions last** - Place delete/remove at bottom
3. **Show shortcuts** - Display keyboard shortcuts
4. **Use icons** - Improve scanability
5. **Align properly** - Use `align` prop for positioning
6. **Limit items** - 5-10 items max (use submenu for more)
7. **Disable when needed** - Show disabled state for unavailable actions

---

## Positioning

```tsx
<DropdownMenuContent
  align='start' // left-aligned
  align='center' // centered (default)
  align='end' // right-aligned
  side='top' // above trigger
  side='bottom' // below trigger (default)
  side='left' // left of trigger
  side='right' // right of trigger
/>
```

---

## Accessibility

- ✅ Keyboard navigation (Tab, Arrow keys, Enter, Esc)
- ✅ Focus management
- ✅ ARIA roles and attributes
- ✅ Screen reader announcements
- ✅ Focus trap within menu
- ✅ Escape to close

**Keyboard shortcuts:**

- `Space/Enter` - Open menu
- `↓` - Next item
- `↑` - Previous item
- `→` - Open submenu
- `←` - Close submenu
- `Esc` - Close menu
- `Home/End` - First/last item

---

**Icon button:**

```tsx
<DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
  <Button variant='ghost' size='icon'>

  </Button>
</DropdownMenuTrigger>
```

**Text button:**

```tsx

    Actions <ChevronDown className='ml-2' />
  </Button>

```

**Avatar:**

    <Avatar className='h-8 w-8'>
      <AvatarFallback>U</AvatarFallback>
    </Avatar>

# QuickActionCard / QuickActionGrid

> Shortcut cards for frequent dashboard actions

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/quick-actions.mdx

Two composable pieces: `QuickActionCard` (one shortcut) and `QuickActionGrid` (the responsive grid container).
Import them from `@telamonjs/ui` or `@telamonjs/ui/cards`.

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { QuickActionCard, QuickActionGrid } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Plus, Upload, Download, Mail } from 'lucide-react'

export default function Dashboard() {
  return (
    <QuickActionGrid columns={4}>
      <QuickActionCard title='New Order' icon={Plus} color='blue' href='/admin/orders/new' />
      <QuickActionCard title='Import Data' icon={Upload} color='green' href='/admin/import' />
      <QuickActionCard title='Export' icon={Download} color='purple' onClick={() => handleExport()} />
      <QuickActionCard title='Send Email' icon={Mail} color='orange' onClick={() => openEmailDialog()} />
    </QuickActionGrid>
  )
}
```

---

## Props

### QuickActionCard

<TypeTable
  type={{
    title: { description: 'Card label', type: 'I18nText', required: true },
    icon: { description: 'Icon — string key, LucideIcon, or component reference', type: 'string | LucideIcon | ComponentType', required: true },
    color: {
      description: 'Color variant, drives the icon gradient',
      type: "'blue' | 'green' | 'yellow' | 'red' | 'purple' | 'orange' | 'gray'",
      required: true,
    },
    href: { description: 'Navigation URL — renders as a Next.js `Link` (to `#` when omitted). Ignored when `onClick` is set.', type: 'string' },
    onClick: { description: 'Click handler — renders as a `<button>` instead of a link, and takes precedence over `href`.', type: '() => void' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

### QuickActionGrid

<TypeTable
  type={{
    children: { description: 'One or more `QuickActionCard` elements', type: 'React.ReactNode', required: true },
    columns: { description: 'Grid columns', type: '3 | 4 | 5 | 6', default: '6' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

<Callout type='warn' title='No variant/badge/shortcut/loading/permission system'>
  There is no `list`/`compact` layout variant, no `badge`, `shortcut`,
  `loading`, `disabled`, or `requiresPermission` prop on either component, and
  no single `actions` array — compose one `QuickActionCard` per shortcut
  inside `QuickActionGrid`.
</Callout>

---

## Examples

### Grid Layout

```tsx
<QuickActionGrid columns={4}>
  <QuickActionCard title='New Order' icon={Plus} color='blue' href='/admin/orders/new' />
  <QuickActionCard title='Import' icon={Upload} color='green' href='/admin/import' />
  <QuickActionCard title='Export' icon={Download} color='purple' onClick={handleExport} />
  <QuickActionCard title='Email' icon={Mail} color='orange' onClick={openEmailDialog} />
</QuickActionGrid>
```

`columns` accepts `3 | 4 | 5 | 6` — the grid is responsive (fewer columns on
smaller screens) regardless of the value passed.

### 3-Column Grid

```tsx
<QuickActionGrid columns={3}>
  <QuickActionCard title='New Order' icon={Plus} color='blue' href='/admin/orders/new' />
  <QuickActionCard title='Manage Users' icon={Users} color='gray' href='/admin/users' />
  <QuickActionCard title='Reports' icon={FileText} color='yellow' href='/admin/reports' />
</QuickActionGrid>
```

### Click Handler (no navigation)

```tsx
'use client'

import { useState } from 'react'
import { QuickActionCard, QuickActionGrid } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Download } from 'lucide-react'

export default function QuickActionsWithExport() {
  const [exporting, setExporting] = useState(false)

  async function handleExport() {
    setExporting(true)
    try {
      await exportData()
    } finally {
      setExporting(false)
    }
  }

  return (
    <QuickActionGrid columns={4}>
      <QuickActionCard
        title={exporting ? 'Exporting…' : 'Export'}
        icon={Download}
        color='purple'
        onClick={handleExport}
      />
    </QuickActionGrid>
  )
}
```

There is no built-in `loading` state on the card — reflect it in `title`/`icon`
yourself, as shown above.

### String Icon (project icon registry)

```tsx
<QuickActionCard title='New Order' icon='Plus' color='blue' href='/admin/orders/new' />
```

`icon` also accepts a string key resolved through the project's icon
registry (`setIconResolver`) — see
[Icon Resolver](/docs/patterns/provider-setup#icon-resolver-seticonresolver).

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/dashboard-quick-actions.tsx"
'use client'

import { QuickActionCard, QuickActionGrid } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Plus, Upload, Download, Mail, Users, FileText } from 'lucide-react'

export default function DashboardQuickActions() {
  return (
    <QuickActionGrid columns={3}>
      <QuickActionCard title='New Order' icon={Plus} color='blue' href='/admin/orders/new' />
      <QuickActionCard title='Import Data' icon={Upload} color='green' href='/admin/import' />
      <QuickActionCard title='Export All' icon={Download} color='purple' onClick={() => exportAllData()} />
      <QuickActionCard title='Bulk Email' icon={Mail} color='orange' onClick={() => sendBulkEmail()} />
      <QuickActionCard title='Manage Users' icon={Users} color='gray' href='/admin/users' />
      <QuickActionCard title='Reports' icon={FileText} color='yellow' href='/admin/reports' />
    </QuickActionGrid>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Dashboard shortcuts** - Frequent operations
- **Admin panels** - Common admin tasks
- **User dashboards** - User-specific actions
- **Workflow accelerators** - Reduce navigation
- **Context actions** - Page-specific shortcuts

---

## Best Practices

1. **Limit actions** - 4-8 most important shortcuts per grid
2. **Clear labels** - Descriptive, action-oriented `title`
3. **Consistent icons** - Use the same icon set (Lucide, or the project icon registry)
4. **`href` vs `onClick`** - Use `href` for navigation, `onClick` for in-page actions — not both
5. **Color coding** - Give related actions distinct `color` values
6. **Keyboard shortcuts / badges / permissions** - Not built in; wrap `QuickActionCard`
   in your own component if you need those (e.g. gate on permission before rendering)

---

## Accessibility

- `href` cards render as a Next.js `Link` (keyboard/focus native)
- `onClick` cards render as a real `<button type="button">`
- Icon-only visual weight is paired with a visible `title` label

---

## Responsive Design

`QuickActionGrid` is responsive regardless of the `columns` value:

- Desktop: up to the configured column count
- Tablet/mobile: fewer columns, wrapping automatically

---

## Related Components

- [DashboardGrid](/docs/components/dashboard-grid) - Dashboard layout
- [CommandPalette](/docs/components/command-palette) - Keyboard-driven commands

---

## See Also

- [Dashboard Patterns](/docs/patterns/dashboard) - Dashboard design

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# ExportButtons

> Export dropdown and buttons for CSV, Excel, and PDF downloads

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/export-button.mdx

Export UI for tabular data. Two complementary surfaces exist in the library:

- **`ExportButtons`** (+ `ExportPDFButton`, `ExportExcelButton`) — a dropdown
  button where **you provide the export handlers**; only the formats you pass
  a handler for appear in the menu.
- **`ExportMenu`** + **`exportToCSV` / `exportToExcel` / `exportToPDF` /
  `exportTableData`** — batteries-included export for TanStack
  `ColumnDef`-based tables (used by DataTable), generating the files
  client-side. Excel and CSV need no extra package; PDF loads the optional
  `jspdf` + `jspdf-autotable` peers on first use.

<Callout type='info' title='What is exported'>
  The exports are `ExportButtons`, `ExportPDFButton`, `ExportExcelButton`, `ExportMenu`, and the
  `exportTo*` utilities documented below. There is no JSON export built in.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { ExportButtons, type ExportColumn } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const columns: ExportColumn<User>[] = [
  { header: 'Full Name', accessorKey: 'name' },
  { header: 'Email', accessorKey: 'email' },
  { header: 'Member Since', accessorFn: u => u.createdAt.toLocaleDateString() },
]

export default function UsersToolbar({ users }: { users: User[] }) {
  return (
    <ExportButtons
      data={users}
      columns={columns}
      filename='users-export'
      onExportCSV={async (data, cols, filename) => {
        // Your export implementation (or delegate to exportToCSV — see below)
      }}
    />
  )
}
```

The dropdown renders only the entries whose handler you passed
(`onExportPDF`, `onExportExcel`, `onExportCSV`). With no handler at all, the
component renders nothing.

---

## Props

### ExportButtons

<TypeTable
  type={{
    data: { description: 'Rows to export — the button is disabled while empty', type: 'T[]', required: true },
    columns: { description: 'Column definitions passed through to your handlers', type: 'ExportColumn<T>[]', required: true },
    filename: { description: 'Base filename passed to your handlers', type: 'string', default: "'export'" },
    onExportPDF: { description: 'Adds the PDF entry — called with (data, columns, filename)', type: '(data, columns, filename) => Promise<void>' },
    onExportExcel: { description: 'Adds the Excel entry', type: '(data, columns, filename) => Promise<void>' },
    onExportCSV: { description: 'Adds the CSV entry', type: '(data, columns, filename) => Promise<void>' },
    disabled: { description: 'Force-disable the button', type: 'boolean', default: 'false' },
    labels: { description: 'Override button/menu labels: exportButton, exportPDF, exportExcel, exportCSV (default: localized)', type: 'Partial<ExportLabels>' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes on the trigger button', type: 'string' },
  }}
/>

### ExportColumn

<TypeTable
  type={{
    header: { description: 'Column header text', type: 'string', required: true },
    accessorKey: { description: 'Field key on the row (mutually exclusive with accessorFn)', type: 'keyof T & string' },
    accessorFn: { description: 'Derived/formatted value for the cell', type: '(row: T) => string | number | null | undefined' },
  }}
/>

### ExportPDFButton / ExportExcelButton

Single-format standalone buttons — same `data`/`columns`/`filename`/`disabled`/
`className` props, plus the one required handler (`onExportPDF` /
`onExportExcel`) and an optional `label`. There is no standalone CSV button —
use `ExportButtons` with only `onExportCSV`.

---

## Batteries-included: ExportMenu + exportUtils

When your columns are TanStack `ColumnDef`s (as in DataTable), skip writing
handlers — `ExportMenu` generates the files itself. `ColumnDef` is TanStack's type,
imported from `@tanstack/react-table`: `@telamonjs/ui` depends on it but does not
re-export it, so add it to the app to import the type:

```tsx
import { ExportMenu } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import type { ColumnDef } from '@tanstack/react-table'

<ExportMenu
  data={rows}
  columns={columns} // ColumnDef<T>[]
  filename='users'
  formats={['excel', 'csv', 'pdf']}
  pdfOptions={{ title: 'Users Report', orientation: 'landscape' }}
  onExportComplete={() => toast.success('Export complete')}
  onExportError={error => toast.error(error.message)}
/>
```

### ExportMenu props

<TypeTable
  type={{
    data: { description: 'All rows', type: 'T[]', required: true },
    columns: { description: 'TanStack column definitions (headers/accessors reused for the file)', type: 'ColumnDef<T>[]', required: true },
    selectedRows: { description: 'When set, offers exporting only the selection', type: 'T[]' },
    currentPageRows: { description: 'When set, offers exporting only the current page', type: 'T[]' },
    filename: { description: 'Base filename', type: 'string', default: "'export'" },
    appendDate: { description: 'Append `_YYYY-MM-DD` (local day) to the filename, once', type: 'boolean', default: 'true' },
    sheetName: { description: 'Excel sheet name (default: localized "Data")', type: 'string' },
    formats: { description: 'Formats offered in the menu', type: "Array<'excel' | 'csv' | 'pdf'>", default: "['excel', 'csv', 'pdf']" },
    pdfOptions: { description: 'PDF title, subtitle, orientation, logo (string or `{ src, width?, height? }` in mm), footer and generatedAt (`datetime` or `date`)', type: "Omit<PDFExportOptions, 'filename' | 't' | 'locale' | 'sheetName' | 'appendDate'>" },
    onExport: { description: 'Custom generator: the menu only orchestrates (loading, toast, callbacks) and skips the built-in generation', type: "(format: 'excel' | 'csv' | 'pdf', rows: T[], columns: ColumnDef<T>[]) => Promise<void> | void" },
    loadAll: { description: 'Source of the "All" scope instead of `data`, such as every page of a server query (`fetchAllPages`). A progress toast offers Cancel, which aborts `signal`; fewer `rows` than `total` shows a capped-export warning', type: '(ctx: { signal: AbortSignal; onProgress: (loaded: number, target: number) => void }) => Promise<{ rows: T[]; total: number }>' },
    allCount: { description: 'Count next to "All" when `loadAll` is set', type: 'number' },
    onServerExport: { description: 'App-side export: the menu lists the formats only (no scopes, no rows) and calls this, pending until it settles. Failures show the error toast; announcing success is up to you', type: "(format: ExportFormat) => unknown" },
    onExportStart: { description: 'Called before generating', type: '() => void' },
    onExportComplete: { description: 'Called after the download starts', type: '() => void' },
    onExportError: { description: 'Called on failure', type: '(error: Error) => void' },
    disabled: { description: 'Disable the menu', type: 'boolean' },
    className: { description: 'Additional classes', type: 'string' },
    trigger: { description: 'Custom trigger, such as a "⋯" icon button. Must forward ref/props (asChild)', type: 'ReactNode' },
    children: { description: 'Extra items above the export section, such as "Refresh"', type: 'ReactNode' },
  }}
/>

### Utility functions

```typescript
await exportToExcel(data, columns, filename, options)  // .xlsx, written in-house (bold header row)
exportToCSV(data, columns, filename, options)          // .csv, UTF-8 with BOM
await exportToPDF(data, columns, filename, options)    // .pdf via the optional jspdf + jspdf-autotable peers
await exportTableData(data, columns, format, filename, options) // dispatch by format

interface ExportOptions {
  t: ReturnType<typeof useTelamonjsT> // required: library translator
  locale: string                    // required: formats dates in cells
  includeHiddenColumns?: boolean
  filename?: string
  sheetName?: string   // Excel only
  appendDate?: boolean // default true
}

interface PDFExportOptions extends ExportOptions {
  orientation?: 'portrait' | 'landscape'
  logo?: string | { src: string; width?: number; height?: number } // size in mm
  title?: string
  subtitle?: string
  footer?: string
  generatedAt?: 'datetime' | 'date'
}
```

All take TanStack `ColumnDef<T>[]` and download client-side with a
date-stamped filename (`users_2026-08-18.csv`). `options` is required because
headers and values are localized: pass the library translator and the active locale.
`exportToExcel`, `exportToPDF` and `exportTableData` return a promise that
resolves once the download starts; await it to catch failures. Without the
`jspdf` peers, `exportToPDF` rejects with an error naming both packages
(`ExportMenu` shows it as a toast). Excel sheet names follow Excel's rules: at
most 31 characters, and `\ / ? * [ ] :` become spaces. In CSV, a text cell that
starts with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab or a carriage return gets a leading `'`, so
spreadsheets read it as text instead of running it as a formula; numbers (and numeric
strings such as `-12.50`) are written as is.

Wiring them into `ExportButtons` handlers:

```tsx
'use client'

import { useLocale } from 'next-intl'
import { ExportButtons, exportToCSV, useTelamonjsT } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function UsersExport({ users }: { users: User[] }) {
  const t = useTelamonjsT()
  const locale = useLocale()

  return (
    <ExportButtons
      data={users}
      columns={exportColumns}
      filename='users'
      onExportCSV={async data => exportToCSV(data, columnDefs, 'users', { t, locale })}
    />
  )
}
```

---

## Which one do I use?

| Situation | Use |
| --- | --- |
| DataTable/ListPage toolbar, `ColumnDef` columns | `ExportMenu` (or DataTable's built-in export) |
| Custom export pipeline (server-generated file, API call) | `ExportButtons` with your handlers |
| One format only, PDF or Excel | `ExportPDFButton` / `ExportExcelButton` |
| Programmatic export (no UI) | `exportToCSV` / `exportToExcel` / `exportToPDF` |

---

## Best Practices

1. **Limit data** - Don't export 100,000+ records client-side; generate large files on the server and download the URL
2. **Format values** - Use `accessorFn` (ExportColumn) or cell accessors (ColumnDef) for dates and currency
3. **Descriptive filenames** - The utilities append the date automatically
4. **Error handling** - `ExportButtons` logs handler errors; surface feedback via `ExportMenu`'s `onExportError` or your own toasts
5. **Permissions and audit** - Enforce who can export on the server, and log exports for compliance

---

## Accessibility

- Trigger and menu are the library's `DropdownMenu` (Radix): keyboard
  navigable, focus managed, Esc closes
- The trigger disables itself while exporting or when `data` is empty

---

## Related Components

- [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) - Table with built-in export toolbar
- [DropdownMenu](/docs/components/dropdown-menu) - The menu primitive used here

---

# BaseCard

> Foundation card component for consistent UI building blocks

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/base-card.mdx

Foundation card component with a header (title, description, icon, badge) and a built-in
loading skeleton. `KPICard` and `DetailCard` are built on it.

<Callout type='info' title='Header + loading state'>
  `BaseCard` renders the header only when `title`, `description`, `icon` or `headerBadge` is set,
  and swaps the whole card for a skeleton while `isLoading` is true.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { BaseCard } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { User } from 'lucide-react'

export default function MyCard() {
  return (
    <BaseCard title='User Information' icon={User}>
      <p>Card content here</p>
    </BaseCard>
  )
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface BaseCardProps {
  // Header
  title?: string // Card title
  description?: string // Text under the title
  icon?: LucideIcon | ReactNode | string // Component, rendered element, or Lucide icon name
  iconClassName?: string // Classes for the icon (default: 'h-4 w-4')
  headerBadge?: ReactNode // Rendered next to the icon, on the right of the header

  // Content
  children?: ReactNode // Card content

  // Loading
  isLoading?: boolean // Show the skeleton instead of the content (default: false)
  loadingSkeletons?: {
    title?: boolean // default: true
    icon?: boolean // default: true
    content?: boolean // default: true
    description?: boolean // default: true
  }

  // Styling
  className?: string // Classes on the card
  headerClassName?: string // Classes on the header
  contentClassName?: string // Classes on the content area
}
```

There is no `variant`, `padding`, `onClick`, `hoverable` or `actions` prop — style the card with
`className`/`contentClassName`, put buttons in `headerBadge`, and wrap the card in a link or
button to make it clickable.

---

## Examples

### Basic Card

```tsx
<BaseCard title='Simple Card'>
  <p>This is a basic card with just a title and content.</p>
</BaseCard>
```

### With Icon

```tsx
import { Settings } from 'lucide-react'
;<BaseCard title='Settings' icon={Settings}>
  <p>Card content</p>
</BaseCard>
```

`icon` also accepts a rendered element (`icon={<Settings className='h-5 w-5' />}`) or a Lucide
icon name (`icon='Settings'`).

### With Description

```tsx
<BaseCard
  title='User Statistics'
  description='Overview of user activity for the last 30 days'
>
  <div className='space-y-2'>
    <p>Total Users: 1,234</p>
    <p>Active Users: 892</p>
  </div>
</BaseCard>
```

### With Header Badge

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@telamonjs/ui'

<BaseCard
  title="Notifications"
  headerBadge={<Badge>5</Badge>}
>
  <p>You have 5 unread notifications</p>
</BaseCard>
```

### With Header Actions

```tsx
import { MoreVertical } from 'lucide-react'
import { Button } from '@telamonjs/ui'
;<BaseCard
  title='User Profile'
  headerBadge={
    <Button variant='ghost' size='icon' aria-label='More actions'>
      <MoreVertical className='w-4 h-4' />
    </Button>
  }
>
  <p>Card content</p>
</BaseCard>
```

### Loading State

```tsx
<BaseCard title='Revenue' icon={DollarSign} isLoading={isLoading}>
  <div className='text-2xl font-bold'>{revenue}</div>
</BaseCard>

// Only skeleton the content lines
<BaseCard title='Revenue' isLoading loadingSkeletons={{ title: false, icon: false }}>
  …
</BaseCard>
```

### Full-Width Content

```tsx
<BaseCard title='Data Table' contentClassName='p-0'>
  <DataTable columns={columns} data={data} />
</BaseCard>
```

Useful for tables and charts that need full width.

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/stats-overview-card.tsx"
'use client'

import {
  BaseCard,
  Button,
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
} from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { TrendingUp, TrendingDown, MoreVertical, type LucideIcon } from 'lucide-react'

interface StatsCardProps {
  title: string
  value: number
  previousValue: number
  icon: LucideIcon
  isLoading?: boolean
}

export default function StatsOverviewCard({
  title,
  value,
  previousValue,
  icon,
  isLoading,
}: StatsCardProps) {
  const trend = ((value - previousValue) / previousValue) * 100
  const isPositive = trend >= 0

  return (
    <BaseCard
      title={title}
      icon={icon}
      isLoading={isLoading}
      headerBadge={
        <DropdownMenu>
          <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
            <Button variant='ghost' size='icon' aria-label='More actions'>
              <MoreVertical className='w-4 h-4' />
            </Button>
          </DropdownMenuTrigger>
          <DropdownMenuContent align='end'>
            <DropdownMenuItem>View Details</DropdownMenuItem>
            <DropdownMenuItem>Export Data</DropdownMenuItem>
          </DropdownMenuContent>
        </DropdownMenu>
      }
    >
      <div className='space-y-2'>
        <div className='text-3xl font-bold'>{value.toLocaleString()}</div>
        <div
          className={`flex items-center gap-1 ${isPositive ? 'text-green-600' : 'text-red-600'}`}
        >
          {isPositive ? (
            <TrendingUp className='w-3 h-3' />
          ) : (
            <TrendingDown className='w-3 h-3' />
          )}
          <span className='text-sm font-medium'>
            {Math.abs(trend).toFixed(1)}%
          </span>
        </div>
        <p className='text-sm text-muted-foreground'>
          Previous: {previousValue.toLocaleString()}
        </p>
      </div>
    </BaseCard>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Building custom cards** - Foundation for domain-specific cards
- **Consistent styling** - Ensure all cards follow same design
- **Rapid prototyping** - Quickly build new card components
- **Loading states** - Get a matching skeleton without extra code

---

## Components Built on BaseCard

- `DetailCard` - Detail page information cards
- `KPICard` - Key performance indicator cards
- Custom domain cards in your application

**Benefit:** Consistent styling and behavior across all cards.

---

## Layout Patterns

**Grid of cards:**

```tsx
<div className='grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6'>
  <BaseCard title='Card 1'>{/* Content */}</BaseCard>
  <BaseCard title='Card 2'>{/* Content */}</BaseCard>
  <BaseCard title='Card 3'>{/* Content */}</BaseCard>
</div>
```

**Stack of cards:**

```tsx
<div className='space-y-6'>
  <BaseCard title='Section 1'>{/* Content */}</BaseCard>
  <BaseCard title='Section 2'>{/* Content */}</BaseCard>
</div>
```

---

## Best Practices

1. **Use for consistency** - Build custom cards on top of BaseCard
2. **Semantic titles** - Use clear, descriptive titles
3. **Icon usage** - Add icons for visual hierarchy
4. **Actions sparingly** - Limit header actions to 1-3
5. **Full-width content** - Use `contentClassName='p-0'` for tables and charts
6. **Loading states** - Pass `isLoading` instead of rendering your own skeleton

---

## Accessibility

- Built on the `Card` primitives (`CardHeader`, `CardTitle`, `CardDescription`, `CardContent`)
- The icon is decorative; the title carries the meaning
- Give icon-only buttons in `headerBadge` an `aria-label`

---

## Styling Customization

**Custom classes:**

```tsx
<BaseCard title='Custom Styled' className='border-blue-500 bg-blue-50'>
  Content
</BaseCard>
```

**Tailwind modifiers:**

```tsx
<BaseCard title='Hover Effect' className='hover:shadow-xl transition-shadow'>
  Content
</BaseCard>
```

- [DetailCardHeader](/docs/components/detail-card-header) - Reusable card header
- [DetailCard](/docs/components/detail-card) - Detail page cards
- [KPICard](/docs/components/kpi-card) - KPI card built on BaseCard

# LoadingSkeleton

> Unified loading skeleton with multiple shapes

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/loading-skeleton.mdx

Unified loading skeleton component with consistent pulse animation for different content shapes.

<Callout type='info' title='One component, several shapes'>
  Pick a `shape` (`card`, `table`, `text`, `stat`, `avatar`) instead of
  hand-building loading states. For a one-off block, use the lower-level
  `Skeleton` primitive.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
'use client'

import { LoadingSkeleton } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'

export default function MyPage() {
  const { data, isLoading } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['items'], queryFn: fetchItems })

  if (isLoading) {
    return <LoadingSkeleton shape='card' />
  }

  return <div>{data}</div>
}
```

---

## Props

```typescript
interface LoadingSkeletonProps {
  shape?: 'card' | 'table' | 'text' | 'stat' | 'avatar' // Skeleton type (default: 'card')
  count?: number // Cards, table rows or text lines to render (default: 1)
  columns?: number // Table columns (default: 4, 'table' only)
  className?: string // Additional classes
}
```

`count` applies to `card`, `table` and `text`; `stat` and `avatar` always render one item.

---

## Shapes

### Card Skeleton

```tsx
<LoadingSkeleton shape='card' />
```

**Use for:**

- DetailCard loading
- Dashboard widgets
- Profile cards

**Renders:**

- Card header skeleton (title + description lines)
- Three content lines
- Consistent card shape

### Multiple Cards

```tsx
<LoadingSkeleton shape='card' count={3} />
```

Shows 3 card skeletons stacked vertically.

### Table Skeleton

```tsx
<LoadingSkeleton shape='table' />
```

**Use for:**

- DataTable loading
- List pages
- Reports

**Renders:**

- Toolbar placeholders (search + button)
- Table header row
- `count` data rows × `columns` columns

### Custom Rows and Columns

```tsx
<LoadingSkeleton shape='table' count={10} columns={6} />
```

Shows a 6-column table skeleton with 10 rows.

### Text Skeleton

```tsx
<LoadingSkeleton shape='text' count={4} />
```

Renders `count` full-width text lines.

### Stat Skeleton

```tsx
<LoadingSkeleton shape='stat' />
```

A KPI card placeholder: label, icon, value and description.

### Avatar Skeleton

```tsx
<LoadingSkeleton shape='avatar' />
```

A round avatar with two text lines beside it.

---

## Examples

### In ListPage

```tsx
'use client'

import { LoadingSkeleton } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Suspense } from 'react'

export default function UsersPage() {
  return (
    <Suspense fallback={<LoadingSkeleton shape='table' count={10} />}>
      <UsersTable />
    </Suspense>
  )
}
```

### In DetailCard

```tsx
'use client'

import { LoadingSkeleton, DetailCard } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function UserCard({ userId }) {
  const { data: user, isLoading } = useUser(userId)

  if (isLoading) {
    return <LoadingSkeleton shape='card' />
  }

  return <DetailCard title='User Information'>{/* Fields */}</DetailCard>
}
```

### In Detail Page

```tsx
import { LoadingSkeleton } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Suspense } from 'react'

export default function UserDetailPage({ params }) {
  return (
    <Suspense
      fallback={
        <div className='space-y-6'>
          <LoadingSkeleton shape='avatar' />
          <LoadingSkeleton shape='card' count={3} />
        </div>
      }
    >
      <UserDetail params={params} />
    </Suspense>
  )
}
```

### In Dashboard

```tsx
<div className='grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-6'>
  <Suspense
    fallback={
      <>
        <LoadingSkeleton shape='stat' />
        <LoadingSkeleton shape='stat' />
        <LoadingSkeleton shape='stat' />
      </>
    }
  >
    <DashboardWidgets />
  </Suspense>
</div>
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="app/admin/users/page.tsx"
import { Suspense } from 'react'
import { LoadingSkeleton } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { UsersTable } from './components/users-table'
import { StatsCards } from './components/stats-cards'

export default function UsersPage() {
  return (
    <div className='space-y-6'>
      {/* Stats cards with loading skeleton */}
      <Suspense
        fallback={
          <div className='grid gap-4 md:grid-cols-4'>
            {Array.from({ length: 4 }).map((_, i) => (
              <LoadingSkeleton key={i} shape='stat' />
            ))}
          </div>
        }
      >
        <StatsCards />
      </Suspense>

      {/* Users table with loading skeleton */}
      <Suspense fallback={<LoadingSkeleton shape='table' count={15} />}>
        <UsersTable />
      </Suspense>
    </div>
  )
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Suspense fallbacks** - React Suspense loading states
- **Query loading** - TanStack Query, SWR loading
- **Page transitions** - `loading.tsx` route segments
- **Component loading** - Async component mounting

---

## Animation

**Pulse animation:**

- Consistent across all shapes
- Tailwind `animate-pulse` utility on each block (via `Skeleton`)

---

## Best Practices

1. **Match content shape** - Choose the shape matching the actual content
2. **Consistent rows** - Use the same row count as typical data
3. **Suspense boundaries** - Wrap async components
4. **Avoid nested** - Don't nest multiple skeletons

---

## Accessibility

- No interactive elements (no tab stops)
- The skeleton has no `role` or live region: if screen readers should hear a loading message, wrap it in an element with `role="status"` and visually hidden text

---

## Related Components

- [BaseCard](/docs/components/base-card) - Card with its own `isLoading` skeleton
- [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) - Table component
- [DetailLayout](/docs/components/detail-layout) - Detail page layout

---

## See Also

- Loading States - Loading patterns
- Suspense - React Suspense guide

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# StatusBadge

> Reusable status badge with typed variants (new, beta, status, trend, custom)

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/components/status-badge.mdx

Reusable badge component for "new"/"beta" tags, status labels and trend
percentages, configured per call.

<Callout type='info' title='Not the same as DetailStatus'>
  `StatusBadge` is a **base component** configured per call. `DetailStatus`
  is a separate detail-page component driven by a `statusConfig` map; it
  renders the `Badge` primitive, not `StatusBadge`.
</Callout>

---

## Basic Usage

```tsx
import { StatusBadge } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export default function MyComponent() {
  return <StatusBadge type='status' label='Active' variant='success' />
}
```

<Callout type='warn' title='There is no `status` prop'>
  The component is driven by `type` + `label` + `variant`, and `icon` takes a rendered `ReactNode`,
  not a component reference.
</Callout>

---

## Props

```typescript
type BadgeType = 'new' | 'beta' | 'custom' | 'status' | 'trend'
type BadgeVariant =
  | 'default'
  | 'secondary'
  | 'destructive'
  | 'outline'
  | 'success'
  | 'warning'

interface StatusBadgeProps {
  type?: BadgeType // Badge kind — drives default label/variant (default: 'custom')
  label?: string // Display text (overrides the type's default label)
  variant?: BadgeVariant // Color variant (overrides the type's default variant)
  value?: number // Percentage value, only used when type='trend'
  icon?: React.ReactNode // Icon element, already rendered (e.g. <Check className="h-3 w-3" />)
  size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' // Badge size (default: 'sm')
  className?: string // Additional classes
}
```

**Type → default label/variant:**

| `type`     | Default label | Default variant |
| ---------- | -------------- | ---------------- |
| `new`      | Localized "New" (`common.create`) | `secondary` |
| `beta`     | "Beta"          | `outline`         |
| `custom`   | (none — pass `label`) | `secondary` |
| `status`   | (none — pass `label`) | `default`   |
| `trend`    | (none — renders `value`%) | `secondary` |

Any of these can be overridden by passing an explicit `label`/`variant`.

<Callout type='info' title='No auto-coloring from status strings'>
  `StatusBadge` does **not** infer a color from the text of `label` (e.g. the string `"failed"` does
  not automatically turn the badge red). You always pass `variant` explicitly — build your own
  `Record<Status, variant>` mapping if you need per-status colors (see
  [Complete Example](#complete-example) below).
</Callout>

---

## Variants

### Status Badge

```tsx
<StatusBadge type='status' label='Active' variant='success' />
<StatusBadge type='status' label='Pending' variant='warning' />
<StatusBadge type='status' label='Failed' variant='destructive' />
<StatusBadge type='status' label='Draft' variant='outline' />
```

### New / Beta

```tsx
<StatusBadge type='new' />   {/* "New" (localized), secondary variant */}
<StatusBadge type='beta' />  {/* "Beta", outline variant */}
```

### Trend

```tsx
<StatusBadge type='trend' value={15.5} />   {/* Green up-arrow, "15.5%" */}
<StatusBadge type='trend' value={-4.2} />   {/* Red down-arrow, "4.2%" */}
<StatusBadge type='trend' value={0} />      {/* Muted dash, "0%" */}
```

Trend color and arrow direction are derived automatically from the sign of `value`.

### Custom

```tsx
<StatusBadge type='custom' label='VIP' variant='outline' />
```

---

## Examples

### With Icon

```tsx
import { Check, AlertCircle, X } from 'lucide-react'

<StatusBadge type='status' label='Verified' variant='success' icon={<Check className='h-3 w-3' />} />
<StatusBadge type='status' label='Warning' variant='warning' icon={<AlertCircle className='h-3 w-3' />} />
<StatusBadge type='status' label='Blocked' variant='destructive' icon={<X className='h-3 w-3' />} />
```

`icon` takes a rendered element (`ReactNode`), not a component reference.

### Different Sizes

```tsx
<StatusBadge type='status' label='Active' variant='success' size='sm' />   {/* Small (default) */}
<StatusBadge type='status' label='Active' variant='success' size='md' />   {/* Medium */}
<StatusBadge type='status' label='Active' variant='success' size='lg' />   {/* Large */}
```

### In Table

```tsx
import type { ColumnDef } from '@tanstack/react-table'

const columns: ColumnDef<User>[] = [
  {
    accessorKey: 'name',
    header: 'Name',
  },
  {
    accessorKey: 'active',
    header: 'Status',
    cell: ({ row }) => (
      <StatusBadge
        type='status'
        label={row.original.active ? 'Active' : 'Inactive'}
        variant={row.original.active ? 'success' : 'secondary'}
      />
    ),
  },
]
```

### In Card

```tsx
import { DetailCard, StatusBadge } from '@telamonjs/ui'
;<DetailCard
  title='Order Details'
  headerBadge={<StatusBadge type='status' label={order.status} variant='success' />}
>
  {/* Order details */}
</DetailCard>
```

---

## Complete Example

```tsx title="components/order-status.tsx"
import { StatusBadge } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { Check, Clock, AlertCircle, X, Package } from 'lucide-react'

type OrderStatus = 'pending' | 'processing' | 'shipped' | 'delivered' | 'cancelled'

interface OrderStatusBadgeProps {
  status: OrderStatus
}

const statusConfig: Record<
  OrderStatus,
  {
    variant: 'default' | 'secondary' | 'destructive' | 'outline' | 'success' | 'warning'
    icon: React.ReactNode
    label: string
  }
> = {
  pending: { variant: 'warning', icon: <Clock className='h-3 w-3' />, label: 'Pending' },
  processing: { variant: 'outline', icon: <Package className='h-3 w-3' />, label: 'Processing' },
  shipped: { variant: 'outline', icon: <Package className='h-3 w-3' />, label: 'Shipped' },
  delivered: { variant: 'success', icon: <Check className='h-3 w-3' />, label: 'Delivered' },
  cancelled: { variant: 'destructive', icon: <X className='h-3 w-3' />, label: 'Cancelled' },
}

export default function OrderStatusBadge({ status }: OrderStatusBadgeProps) {
  const config = statusConfig[status]

  return <StatusBadge type='status' label={config.label} variant={config.variant} icon={config.icon} />
}
```

---

## Use Cases

- **Tables** - Status columns
- **Cards** - Header badges
- **Lists** - Item status indicators
- **Forms** - Status display
- **Dashboards** - Trend/metric badges
- **Detail pages** - Entity status

---

## Best Practices

1. **Consistent mapping** - Build one `Record<Status, variant>` map and reuse it across the app (see Complete Example)
2. **Appropriate variants** - Match color to meaning (`success` = green, `destructive` = red)
3. **Icons optional** - Pass a rendered `ReactNode`, only add when it clarifies meaning
4. **Size consistency** - Use the same `size` within the same context
5. **Explicit variant** - There is no auto-coloring from label text; always pass `variant`
6. **Text clarity** - Use clear, concise labels
7. **Accessibility** - Don't rely only on color (use text + icon)

---

## StatusBadge vs DetailStatus

| Feature         | StatusBadge (Base)      | DetailStatus (Higher-level) |
| --------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| **Use case**     | General-purpose          | Detail pages specifically    |
| **Location**     | Tables, cards, anywhere  | Detail pages only            |
| **Config**       | Props per call (`type`/`label`/`variant`) | External `statusConfig` map (`status`/`statusConfig` props) |
| **Import from**  | `@telamonjs/ui`          | `@telamonjs/ui` or `@telamonjs/ui/detail` |

**Decision:**

- ✅ Use **StatusBadge** - Tables, cards, lists, forms
- ✅ Use **DetailStatus** - Detail/view pages with a shared `statusConfig` map

---

## Accessibility

- Semantic HTML (renders a `<span>`-based Badge)
- Color + text + icon (don't rely on color alone)
- Sufficient color contrast (WCAG AA)
- Screen reader friendly

---

## Customization

**Custom colors:**

```tsx
<StatusBadge
  type='custom'
  label='Custom'
  className='bg-purple-100 text-purple-700 border-purple-200'
/>
```

**Custom styling:**

```tsx
<StatusBadge
  type='custom'
  label='VIP'
  variant='outline'
  className='font-bold uppercase tracking-wider'
/>
```

---

## Related Components

- [DetailStatus](/docs/components/detail-status) - Detail page status driven by a `statusConfig` map
- Badge - Generic badge component

---

## See Also

- Status Indicators - Status design patterns
- Color System - Color usage guidelines

---

**Status:** ✅ Stable

# Hooks

> React hooks exported by the UI package, grouped by what they do

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/hooks/index.mdx

Every hook below is exported by the root barrel (`@telamonjs/ui`) unless a
different entry point is named. All of them are client-side: call them from a component or
file marked `'use client'`.

<Callout type='warn' title='Data fetching comes from React Query, not from this package'>
  `useQuery`, `useMutation` and `useQueryClient` are **not** re-exported. Import them from
  `@tanstack/react-query` directly — a second copy of React Query breaks the app's
  `QueryClient` ("No QueryClient set"). The same applies to `next-intl`.
</Callout>

---

## Table state

| Hook | Signature | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`useTableState`](/docs/hooks/use-table-state) | `(tableId: string) => TableState` | Read the whole persisted state of one `DataTable`/`ListPage` |
| `useTableSorting` | `(tableId: string) => SortingState` | Subscribe to the sorting slice only |

## URL state

| Hook | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| [`useUrlSync`](/docs/hooks/use-url-sync) | Read/write query params (`getParam`, `setParam`, `setParams`) |
| [`useTabUrlSync`](/docs/hooks/use-tab-url-sync) | Active tab kept in the URL, with validation |
| [`useUrlFilters`](/docs/hooks/use-url-filters) | `ListPage` "Filters" panel (selectors, date ranges, text) kept in the URL |

## CRUD data

These wrap React Query around a `CrudConfig`. `ListPage` already uses them — reach for them
only when you build a custom screen on top of the same config.

| Hook | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `useInfiniteListQuery` | Infinite-scroll pages from `config.query.queryFn` |
| `useCrudMutations` | Create / update / delete mutations from `config.mutations`, with cache invalidation |
| `useRecordRefresh` | Reload the record behind the nearest dialog that provides one; `null` outside it |

## Forms

| Hook | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `useForm`, `useForms`, `useFormStore` | Zustand form store used by `ZustandForm` |
| `useFormDraft` | Persist an unsaved draft and restore it |
| `useUnsavedChangesGuard` | Confirm before discarding a dirty form (`setDirty`, `guard`, `reset`, `dialog`) |
| `useWatch`, `useFormContext` | Re-exported from the same `react-hook-form` copy the forms use |

## Layout and app state

| Hook | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| [`useShellPage`](/docs/hooks/use-shell-page) | Page title/actions inside `AdminShell` |
| `useIsMobile` | Responsive breakpoint |

## Utilities

| Hook | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `toast` | Show a toast: `toast({ title, description, variant })` |
| `useDebounce` | `useDebounce(value, delay = 300)` → debounced value |
| [`useAnimatedCounter`](/docs/hooks/use-animated-counter) | Animate a number in dashboards |
| `useText`, `useFormat` | Resolve an `I18nText` slot and format dates/numbers in the active locale |

---

## Example: a selector-based store read

In a component, subscribe to the smallest slice you need; selecting the whole store re-renders on every
change. Inside a custom hook that takes the key as a parameter, do the opposite: see
[Zustand Selector Pattern](/docs/patterns/zustand-selector).

```tsx
'use client'

import { useFormStore } from '@telamonjs/ui'

// Re-renders only when this form's `name` changes
const name = useFormStore(state => state.forms['user-form']?.name)
```

## Example: toast after a mutation

```tsx
'use client'

import { useMutation } from '@tanstack/react-query'
import { toast } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function useDeleteUser() {
  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: (id: string) => usersApi.delete(id),
    onSuccess: () => toast({ title: 'User deleted' }),
    onError: () => toast({ title: 'Delete failed', variant: 'destructive' }),
  })
}
```
