- [Components](/docs/components) - UI components
- [Reference](/docs/reference) - Decision trees and reference tables

---

# useTableState

> Read the state of a DataTable or ListPage from the shared table store

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/hooks/use-table-state.mdx

Every `DataTable` and `ListPage` keeps its state (search, filters, sorting, pagination,
selection, view mode) in one shared Zustand store, keyed by a **table id**.
`useTableState(tableId)` reads the whole state of one table, so any component on the page —
a header counter, an export button, a bulk-action bar — can follow what the table shows.

```tsx
'use client'

import { useTableState } from '@telamonjs/ui'

export function UsersSelectionCount() {
  const { rowSelection, globalFilter } = useTableState('users')
  const selected = Object.values(rowSelection).filter(Boolean).length

  return (
    <span>
      {selected} selected{globalFilter ? ` matching "${globalFilter}"` : ''}
    </span>
  )
}
```

The table id is the `tableId` prop of `ListPage` (it defaults to `config.module.route`):

```tsx
<ListPage config={usersConfig} tableId='users' />
```

<Callout type='info' title='State lives in memory'>
  The store survives client-side navigation but not a full reload. To keep pagination in the
  URL, set `urlSync` on `ListPage`; for other state, use [useUrlSync](/docs/hooks/use-url-sync).
</Callout>

---

## API

```ts
useTableState(tableId: string): TableState
```

Returns the table's state, or the defaults below when the table was never initialised. The
selector is shallow-compared, so the component re-renders only when a field actually changes.

| Field | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `globalFilter` | `string` | `''` |
| `columnFilters` | `Record<string, unknown>` | `{}` |
| `sorting` | `SortField[]` (`{ field, order: 'asc' \| 'desc' }`) | `[]` |
| `page` | `number` | `1` |
| `pageSize` | `number` | `10` |
| `rowSelection` | `Record<string, boolean>` | `{}` |
| `columnVisibility` | `Record<string, boolean>` | `{}` |
| `viewMode` | `'compact' \| 'comfortable' \| 'spacious'` | `'comfortable'` |
| `currentViewMode` | `'table' \| 'cards'` | `'table'` |
| `isFullscreen` | `boolean` | `false` |
| `showFilters` | `boolean` | `false` |

---

## Reading a single field

`useTableState` only reads. When a component needs only the sorting, `useTableSorting(tableId)`
(`SortField[]`) subscribes to that slice and re-renders less.

---

## Pitfalls

- **Two lists, one table id.** Two `ListPage`s for the same `config` on one screen share their
  state, because both default to `config.module.route`. Give each a distinct `tableId`.
- **A custom list doesn't need a second pagination state.** `DataTable` already paginates from
  this store when given a `tableId`.

---

## Related

- [ListPage](/docs/components/list-page) — owns a table in the store
- [DataTable](/docs/components/data-table) — the table itself
- [useUrlSync](/docs/hooks/use-url-sync) — URL-backed state

---

# useUrlSync

> Sync state with URL query params in the Next.js App Router

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/hooks/use-url-sync.mdx

Hook to synchronize state with URL query params (Next.js App Router). Use it for state that should survive a reload or a shared link: active tab, open dialog, filters, pagination.

```tsx
'use client'

import { useUrlSync } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const { getParam, setParam } = useUrlSync()

const status = getParam('status') // string | null
setParam('status', 'active') // pushes ?status=active
setParam('status', null) // removes the param
```

---

## API

### Read

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getParam` | `(key: string) => string \| null` | Read a query param |
| `getNumberParam` | `(key: string, defaultValue?: number) => number \| undefined` | Read a numeric param with fallback |
| `hasParam` | `(key: string) => boolean` | Check if a param exists |
| `getAllParams` | `() => Record<string, string>` | All params as an object |

### Write

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `setParam` | `(key, value, options?: { replace?: boolean }) => void` | Set one param (`null`/`undefined`/`''` deletes it) |
| `setParams` | `(updates: Record<string, value>, options?: { replace?: boolean }) => void` | Atomic multi-param update in a single navigation |
| `clearParam` | `(key: string) => void` | Remove one param |
| `clearAllParams` | `() => void` | Remove all params |

All writes use `router.push(..., { scroll: false })` by default.

---

## The `replace` Option

`setParam` and `setParams` accept `{ replace: true }` to use `router.replace` instead of `push` — no browser history entry is created. This is the base of dialog deep-linking (`dialogs.*.urlParam` in [CrudConfig](/docs/getting-started/crud-config)).

```tsx
// No history entry — good for transient dialog state
setParam('view', item.id, { replace: true })

// Atomic view → edit handoff: delete ?view and set ?edit in ONE navigation,
// avoiding stale intermediate snapshots
setParams({ view: null, edit: item.id }, { replace: true })
```

---

## When to Use

- State that must survive reload / link sharing (active tab, open dialog, filters)
- Prefer [useTabUrlSync](/docs/hooks/use-tab-url-sync) for tab state — it wraps this hook with validation and history semantics
- For a `ListPage`, prefer its `urlSync` prop: it keeps page, page size, sort and search in the query params, both ways

---

## Related

- [useTabUrlSync](/docs/hooks/use-tab-url-sync) — URL-driven tab state built on this hook
- [useTableState](/docs/hooks/use-table-state) — in-memory table state

---

# useTabUrlSync

> URL-driven tab state with deep-linking and browser history

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/hooks/use-tab-url-sync.mdx

URL-driven tab state for `ShellPage`/`AdminTabs` dashboards. Encapsulates the "read `?tab` / write `?tab`" pattern that tab dashboards used to hand-roll with `URLSearchParams` + `router.replace`.

The URL is the **single source of truth**: deep-linking to `?tab=x` selects that tab on load, and changing tabs is a `router.push` by default — so the browser Back button returns to the previous tab. Other query params (`?view`, filters) are preserved via merge, so it composes with dialog deep-linking.

```tsx
'use client'

import { useTabUrlSync, AdminTabs } from '@telamonjs/ui'

const { activeTab, setTab } = useTabUrlSync({ tabs: visibleDefs.map((d) => d.value) })

<AdminTabs tabs={tabs} value={activeTab} onValueChange={setTab} />
```

---

## Options

```typescript
interface UseTabUrlSyncOptions {
  tabs: readonly string[]
  defaultTab?: string
  paramKey?: string // default 'tab'
  history?: 'push' | 'replace' // default 'push'
}
```

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tabs` | - | Valid tab values, in order. Pass the values of the **visible** tabs so a stale/hidden `?tab` falls back gracefully |
| `defaultTab` | `tabs[0]` | Fallback when the URL has no valid tab |
| `paramKey` | `'tab'` | Query param name |
| `history` | `'push'` | `'push'` creates a history entry on tab change (Back returns to the previous tab); `'replace'` keeps the URL in sync without history |

## Return

```typescript
interface UseTabUrlSyncResult {
  activeTab: string | undefined // URL is the single source of truth
  setTab: (value: string) => void // writes ?<paramKey>=<value>, merging other params
}
```

---

## When to Use

Any dashboard with tabs built on [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page) + [AdminTabs](/docs/components/admin-tabs). Replaces hand-rolled `URLSearchParams` + `router.replace` tab state.

<Callout type='info' title='Invalid tabs fall back'>
  If the URL carries a `?tab` value that is not in `tabs` (e.g. a tab hidden by
  permissions), the hook falls back to `defaultTab` instead of rendering an
  empty panel.
</Callout>

---

## Related

- [AdminTabs](/docs/components/admin-tabs) — the component this hook drives
- [useUrlSync](/docs/hooks/use-url-sync) — the underlying URL param hook

---

# useUrlFilters

> A URL-driven "Filters" panel for ListPage — selectors, date ranges and text, shareable by link

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/hooks/use-url-filters.mdx

Builds the content of the `ListPage` "Filters" popover from a list of filter definitions,
with the URL as the **single source of truth**: reloading, going Back or pasting the link keeps
the filters. It returns exactly the `ListPage` props of the [toolbar levels](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern#toolbar-levels)
plus the active `values` for your query.

```tsx
'use client'

import { useMemo } from 'react'
import { ListPage, useUrlFilters, type PaginationParams, type UrlFilterDef } from '@telamonjs/ui'
import { ordersConfig } from './config'

// Module level (or memoized): the hook keys its memo on this array
const FILTERS: UrlFilterDef[] = [
  {
    kind: 'options',
    param: 'status',
    label: 'Status',
    defaultValue: 'OPEN',
    noDefaultValue: 'ALL',
    options: [
      { value: 'ALL', label: 'All' },
      { value: 'OPEN', label: 'Open' },
      { value: 'PAID', label: 'Paid' },
    ],
  },
  {
    kind: 'options',
    param: 'customer',
    apiKey: 'customerId',
    label: 'Customer',
    queryKey: ['customers', 'options'],
    load: (search, { selected, signal }) => customersApi.options({ search, include: selected, signal }),
  },
  { kind: 'dateRange', param: 'due', label: 'Due date' },
  { kind: 'text', param: 'doc', apiKey: 'document', label: 'Document', placeholder: 'Number' },
]

export function OrdersPage() {
  const { values, filtersPanel, activeFilters, onClearFilters } = useUrlFilters(FILTERS)
  const config = useMemo(
    () => ({
      ...ordersConfig,
      query: {
        ...ordersConfig.query,
        queryKey: [...ordersConfig.query.queryKey, values],
        queryFn: (params: PaginationParams) =>
          ordersConfig.query.queryFn({ ...params, filters: { ...params.filters, ...values } }),
      },
    }),
    [values]
  )
  return (
    <ListPage
      config={config}
      filtersPanel={filtersPanel}
      activeFilters={activeFilters}
      onClearFilters={onClearFilters}
    />
  )
}
```

<Callout type='warn' title='Do not list these params in `urlFilters`'>
  `ListPage`'s `urlSync` treats the keys listed in `urlFilters` as its own: it sends them to
  `queryFn` as filters and writes them back to the URL with the list's state. The hook owns its
  params, and `ListPage` ignores a change to any param it does not own; its `values` reach the data through
  `config.query`, as above. `urlSync` itself (page, search, sort) can stay on.
</Callout>

---

## Signature

```typescript
function useUrlFilters(
  defs: readonly UrlFilterDef[],
  options?: UseUrlFiltersOptions
): UseUrlFiltersResult

interface UseUrlFiltersOptions {
  omit?: readonly string[] // apiKeys a scope already fixes: those filters leave the panel
  fixed?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> // parent values when the parent is not in the URL, keyed by param
}

interface UseUrlFiltersResult {
  values: Record<string, string> // { apiKey: value } of the active filters; same object until a value changes
  filtersPanel: ReactNode
  activeFilters: ActiveFilterChip[]
  onClearFilters: () => void // one URL write with every param removed
  params: string[] // every URL key of the panel
}
```

It needs the `QueryClient` that `AppProviders` provides (remote labels are queries), and
writes with `router.replace`: changing a filter adds no history entry.

## Filter definitions

Every definition has `param` (the URL key — unique on the page), `apiKey` (the key in
`values`, default `param`) and `label` (`I18nText`). The `kind` picks the control.

### `'options'` — a searchable selector

Rendered with [`RichSelector`](/docs/components/rich-selector). Give it either a fixed list or a
server search:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `options` | Fixed `{ value, label }[]`, searched in the browser. A URL value outside it is ignored |
| `load`, `queryKey` | `load(search, { parent, selected, signal })` returns `RichSelectorItem[]`. Return the `selected` items too, so their labels show. A URL value is always kept; its chip label comes from `load('', { selected: [value] })`, cached for 5 minutes |
| `dependsOn` | `param` of the parent filter. Changing or removing the parent clears this one, and its own dependents, in the same write. `load` receives the parent value |
| `requireParent`, `parentPlaceholder` | Without a parent value the selector is disabled and shows `parentPlaceholder` |
| `defaultValue` | Value when the param is absent. It shows as a chip — an invisible default would make the list look complete |
| `noDefaultValue` | Written when the default's chip is removed (a value such as `ALL` that the API ignores). Without it, the default cannot be cleared |
| `allLabel`, `searchPlaceholder`, `emptyLabel`, `icon`, `renderItem` | Selector texts and looks |
| `chipLabel` | `(item) => string`: shorter chip text for a remote value (default: the item's `label`) |

### `'dateRange'` — a calendar range

| Field | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fromParam`, `toParam` | `${param}From`, `${param}To` | URL keys. Set them to keep links that already exist |
| `apiFrom`, `apiTo` | `${apiKey}From`, `${apiKey}To` | Keys in `values` |

Dates travel as `YYYY-MM-DD`; anything else in the URL is ignored. Either end may be missing:
the chip then reads "since …" or "until …". With no dates the control shows "Any date".

### `'text'` — free text

`placeholder` is optional. The value is written on Enter or when the field loses focus — not on
every key, which would refetch the list on every key.

---

## Behavior

- **One write per action.** Changing a parent clears its dependents in the same `replace`;
  "Clear filters" removes every param in one call (two writes in a row overwrite each other).
- **Other params are kept** (`tab`, `view`, a second list's filters).
- **The panel never grows past the popover**: a one-column `minmax(0, 1fr)` grid, so a long
  option truncates inside its selector, with the full text on hover.
- **The popover stays open while you work in it**: typing in a field, or a selector or calendar
  opened from it with the focus inside. A plain hover and leave still closes it.

## Lists inside a scope (`omit` / `fixed`)

A list rendered inside a portal that already fixes some filters (one project's tasks) passes
those keys to `omit`, and their values to `fixed` so dependent filters still get their parent:

```tsx
const { values, ...panel } = useUrlFilters(TASK_FILTERS, {
  omit: Object.keys(scope.filters), // e.g. ['projectId']
  fixed: scope.filters, // the goal selector loads the goals of this project
})
```

To clear the panel together with a param of your own, use `params`:

```tsx
onClearFilters={() => setParams(Object.fromEntries([...params, 'community'].map(p => [p, null])), { replace: true })}
```

---

## Related

- [ListPage pattern — filters in the URL](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern#filters-in-the-url)
- [useUrlSync](/docs/hooks/use-url-sync) — the underlying URL param hook
- [RichSelector](/docs/components/rich-selector) — the selector of `'options'` filters

# useShellPage

> Access ShellPage fullscreen context from any descendant

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/hooks/use-shell-page.mdx

Access the [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page) context — fullscreen state and toggle — from any descendant component. Returns `null` when used outside of a `ShellPage`.

```tsx
'use client'

import { useShellPage } from '@telamonjs/ui'

function CustomFullscreenButton() {
  const shell = useShellPage()
  if (!shell) return null // not inside a ShellPage

  return (
    <button onClick={shell.toggleFullscreen}>
      {shell.isFullscreen ? 'Exit fullscreen' : 'Fullscreen'}
    </button>
  )
}
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
function useShellPage(): ShellPageContextValue | null

interface ShellPageContextValue {
  isFullscreen: boolean
  toggleFullscreen: () => void
}
```

---

## Notes

- [AdminHeader](/docs/components/admin-header) consumes this hook automatically to render its fullscreen button — you only need `useShellPage` for custom controls (e.g. a `TabToolbar.Fullscreen` inside a tab panel).
- The `null` return is deliberate: components can render both inside and outside a `ShellPage` and degrade gracefully.

```tsx
// Wiring TabToolbar.Fullscreen to the shell
const shell = useShellPage()

<TabToolbar.Fullscreen
  isFullscreen={shell?.isFullscreen ?? false}
  onToggle={shell?.toggleFullscreen ?? (() => {})}
/>
```

---

## Related

- [ShellPage](/docs/components/shell-page) — the provider
- [AdminHeader](/docs/components/admin-header) — built-in consumer
- [TabToolbar](/docs/components/tab-toolbar) — toolbar with a fullscreen sub-component

# useAnimatedCounter

> Animate number transitions with easing at 60 FPS

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/hooks/use-animated-counter.mdx

Animate a number from its previous value to a new target using `requestAnimationFrame` with ease-out easing (starts fast, decelerates at the end). Powers `StatCard`'s `animate` prop.

```tsx
'use client'

import { useAnimatedCounter } from '@telamonjs/ui'

function AssetCount({ total }: { total: number }) {
  const animated = useAnimatedCounter(total, 500)
  return <span>{Math.round(animated)}</span>
}
```

---

## Signature

```typescript
function useAnimatedCounter(
  target: number,
  duration?: number // ms, default: 500
): number
```

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `number` | - | Value to animate to |
| `duration` | `number` | `500` | Animation duration in milliseconds |

**Returns:** the current animated value (integer, rounded each frame).

---

## Behavior

- Animates **from the previous value** to the new target — subsequent updates transition smoothly instead of restarting from zero.
- A new target cancels the in-flight animation and starts a new one from the current position.
- Automatic cleanup: pending animation frames are cancelled on unmount.

## When to Use

- Numeric stat values that change on refresh (counters, totals)
- Page-load effect (initial value → target)

Avoid for string values or performance-critical mobile dashboards — pass the raw value instead.

---

## Related

- [Dashboard Pattern](/docs/patterns/dashboard) — stat cards and dashboard composition
- [StatCard](/docs/components/stats-card) — `animate` uses this hook

---

# Data

> The server half of a list — the ListPage wire contract, sort and paging sanitizers, a Prisma adapter with scope-safe where and paginated services, and NestJS plumbing

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/packages/data.mdx

`@telamonjs/data` (current version: <PkgVersion pkg='data' />) is what an endpoint runs on what a
[`ListPage`](/docs/patterns/listpage-pattern) sends: page, page size, search, sort and filters.
It has no dependencies and imports neither React, Next nor Prisma, so a NestJS or plain Node API
installs it alone. A NestJS API also gets the [Prisma exception filter, health
endpoint and audit interceptor](#nestjs) every API repeats.

```bash
pnpm add @telamonjs/data
```

| Entry | What it has | Needs an ORM? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@telamonjs/data` | The wire contract (`PaginationParams`, `PaginatedResponse`, `SortField`, `createPaginatedResponse`), `sanitizePaginationParams`, `resolveSort`, `resolveSortPath`; the audit helpers `computeDiff`, `redactPayload`, `DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS` | No |
| `@telamonjs/data/prisma` | `buildPrismaOrderBy`, `buildPrismaOrderByMulti`, `buildSearchConditions`, `buildFilterConditions`, `buildWhereClause`, `createPaginationContext` | Builds Prisma's object shape; never imports `@prisma/client` |
| `@telamonjs/data/nest` | `PrismaExceptionFilter`, `HealthModule`, `createAuditInterceptor`, `SkipAudit`, `isPrismaKnownRequestError`, `isPrismaValidationError` | Needs `@nestjs/common` and `rxjs` (optional peers); never imports `@prisma/client` |

## Sort

A list sends the sort field as the column's data path (`customer.name`, with
`list.sortParam: 'path'`) or as the TanStack column id (`customer_name`, the default). Both resolve
to the same path, and `_count.<relation>` orders by a relation count:

```ts
import { resolveSortPath } from '@telamonjs/data'
import { buildPrismaOrderBy } from '@telamonjs/data/prisma'

resolveSortPath('customer_name')                          // 'customer.name'
buildPrismaOrderBy('customer_name', 'asc')                // { customer: { name: 'asc' } }
buildPrismaOrderBy('_count.items', 'desc')                // { items: { _count: 'desc' } }
buildPrismaOrderBy('created_at', 'asc', ['created_at'])   // { created_at: 'asc' }
```

<Callout type='warn'>
  Pass the endpoint's `sortableFields`. A listed snake_case field (`created_at`) then stays a
  scalar instead of being read as `created.at`, and `resolveSort` rejects any field that is not
  listed, falling back to the default sort.
</Callout>

```ts
import { resolveSort } from '@telamonjs/data'

const sort = resolveSort(query.sortBy ?? 'name', query.sortOrder, {
  defaultOrderBy: 'name',
  defaultOrderDirection: 'asc',
  sortableFields: ['name', 'customer.name', 'created_at'],
})
```

With another ORM or plain SQL, `resolveSort` and `resolveSortPath` are all you need to build your
own `ORDER BY`.

## Where

`buildWhereClause` combines search and filters with the endpoint's `baseWhere` and the user's
visibility rule using `AND`. None of them can overwrite another, even when they share a key or
use `OR`:

```ts
import { buildSearchConditions, buildWhereClause } from '@telamonjs/data/prisma'

const where = buildWhereClause(
  buildSearchConditions(query.search, ['name', 'customer.name']),
  [],
  { deletedAt: null },
  { OR: [{ ownerId: user.id }, { public: true }] }
)
```

## Paginated services

`createPaginationContext` builds a `list` (and `getFilterOptions`) per model from a declarative
config: search fields, typed filters, `sortableFields`, visibility, relation counts and hooks.

```ts
import { createPaginationContext } from '@telamonjs/data/prisma'

export const { createPaginatedService } = createPaginationContext({
  prisma,
  auth, // () => Promise<{ user } | null>
  filterLabels: () => ({ yes: 'Sim', no: 'Não', active: 'Ativo', inactive: 'Inativo' }),
})

export const customers = createPaginatedService({
  model: 'customer',
  searchFields: ['name', 'email'],
  filters: { active: 'boolean', state: 'string' },
  sortableFields: ['name', 'created_at', '_count.orders'],
})
```

`filterLabels` receives the `locale` passed to `getFilterOptions` and returns the labels of
boolean filter options; without it they are in English. Configuration warnings go to
`onWarning` (default `console.warn`).

`createCachedPaginatedService` takes the same config and caches through `cache.cacheEntity` of
the context. Entries are keyed by the service config and, with `visibility`, by the user and the
clause the rule returns for them, so that clause must be deterministic for a given user:
`{ publishedAt: { lte: new Date() } }` changes on every call, so nothing is reused and each call
stores one more entry. A service with `beforeQuery`, `afterQuery`, `customFilterOptions` or a
filter `transform` is returned uncached, with an `onWarning` message.

## NestJS

`@telamonjs/data/nest` needs `@nestjs/common` and `rxjs`, optional peers that only this entry
imports (every Nest app already has both):

<PeerDeps pkg='data' />

### Prisma errors as HTTP statuses

`PrismaExceptionFilter` answers Prisma errors with a status instead of a 500. It matches
Prisma's known-request and validation errors by shape (`code` + `name`/`clientVersion`), so it
works with any `@prisma/client` copy, and it never claims other errors: your own filters and
Nest's default handling still get them.

```ts
import { PrismaExceptionFilter } from '@telamonjs/data/nest'

app.useGlobalFilters(new PrismaExceptionFilter())
```

| Prisma | HTTP |
| --- | --- |
| `P2002` unique | 409, `field` = first `target` field |
| `P2003` foreign key | 400, `field` = constraint |
| `P2025` not found | 404 |
| `P2011`, `P2012`, `P2014`, `PrismaClientValidationError` | 400 |
| `P1000`–`P1003` connection | 503 |
| any other code | 500, logged with Nest's `Logger` |

The body is `{ statusCode, message, error, field?, timestamp, path }`, written with Express's
`res.status().json()`. Outside HTTP (RPC, WebSocket, GraphQL) the error is rethrown. Messages are
English; replace them (in your app's language, say) per code, `validation` or `default`, with a
string or a function of the reported fields:

```ts
new PrismaExceptionFilter({
  messages: {
    P2025: 'Nothing here',
    P2002: (fields) => `${fields.join(', ')} is already taken`,
  },
})
```

To change one case (say, `P2003` on a `DELETE` as 409), subclass it, handle that case in `catch`
and call `super.catch(exception, host)` for the rest.

### Health endpoint

`HealthModule.forRoot()` serves `GET /health`. It runs the checks in parallel and answers 200, or
503 with `status: 'error'` when any check is down, so Docker and load balancers can read the
status code (`downStatus: 200` keeps 200 for setups that read only the body):

```ts
import { Public } from '@telamonjs/auth/nest'
import { HealthModule } from '@telamonjs/data/nest'

HealthModule.forRoot({
  decorators: [Public()],             // class decorators for the controller
  inject: [PrismaService, REDIS],
  checks: (prisma: PrismaService, redis: Redis) => ({
    database: () => prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT 1`,
    redis: () => redis.ping(),
  }),
})
// GET /health → { status: 'ok', timestamp, uptime, database: 'connected', redis: 'connected' }
```

A check is down when it throws, rejects or resolves `false`. `path` changes the route (default
`'health'`); `imports` brings in the modules of the `inject` tokens when they are not global.
The package imports no auth: pass the auth package's [`@Public()`](/docs/packages/auth#nestjs-setup)
in `decorators` when a global guard protects every route.

### Audit trail

`createAuditInterceptor()` returns an interceptor class that turns every successful,
authenticated `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` into an `AuditEntry` and hands it to your `write`.
The package owns no table: you persist the entry wherever you keep audit rows.

```ts
import { APP_INTERCEPTOR } from '@nestjs/core'
import { createAuditInterceptor } from '@telamonjs/data/nest'

export const AuditInterceptor = createAuditInterceptor({
  inject: [PrismaService],
  write: (entry, _context, prisma: PrismaService) => prisma.auditLog.create({ data: entry }),
})

// app.module.ts
providers: [{ provide: APP_INTERCEPTOR, useClass: AuditInterceptor }]
```

A Prisma model that takes the entry as it is:

```prisma
model AuditLog {
  id             String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId         String
  impersonatedBy String?
  action         String   // CREATE | UPDATE | DELETE
  entityType     String
  entityId       String?
  changes        Json?
  ipAddress      String?
  userAgent      String?
  method         String
  path           String
  statusCode     Int
  createdAt      DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([entityType, entityId])
  @@index([userId, createdAt])
}
```

| Entry field | Comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `userId`, `impersonatedBy` | `request.user.id` and `request.user.originalUser.id`, the `@telamonjs/auth` user; without one, an API-key caller's `request.servicePrincipal` as `service:<id or name>` (`user` option to read another shape) |
| `action` | `POST` → `CREATE`, `PUT`/`PATCH` → `UPDATE`, `DELETE` → `DELETE`; any other audited method as is |
| `entityType`, `entityId` | The first static segment of the matched route that is not `api` or a version (`/v1/orders/:id` → `orders`, however the client spelled the URL), and the `:id` param as sent or the response body's `id`; a numeric pipe's `42` for `/v1/orders/042` is used only when the handler returns the record, so numeric-id mutations should return it (`resolveEntity` option to change both) |
| `changes` | The request body through `redactPayload`; absent when the body is empty |
| `ipAddress`, `userAgent` | `request.ip` (set Express's `trust proxy` behind a proxy) and the `User-Agent` header |
| `method`, `path`, `statusCode` | The request, without the query string or an absolute-form `scheme://host`, and the status Nest answered with |

Nothing is written when the handler throws, when there is neither a user nor an API-key
principal (logins, public sign-ups) or outside HTTP. The response does not wait for `write` (`await: true` makes it wait), and a
`write` that throws or rejects goes to `onError` (default: Nest's `Logger`) and never fails the
request.

```ts
createAuditInterceptor({
  write,
  methods: ['POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],     // the default
  ignore: (ctx) => ctx.switchToHttp().getRequest().path.startsWith('/v1/webhooks'),
  redact: ['ssn'],                                 // added to DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS
  resolveEntity: (ctx, body) => ({ type: ctx.getClass().name, id: (body as { id?: string })?.id }),
  onError: (error, entry) => logger.warn({ error, entry }, 'audit write failed'),
})
```

`@SkipAudit()` on a handler or a controller skips it, the same as `ignore`.

### Audit helpers

The root entry has the two pure helpers the interceptor and hand-written audit calls share.
`redactPayload(value, keys = DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS)` returns a deep copy with the value of every
secret key replaced by `'[REDACTED]'`. A key is secret when, lowercased and without `-`/`_`, it
contains one of `keys`: `password` catches `newPassword`, `senha` catches `novaSenha`, `token` catches
`REFRESH_TOKEN`, `apikey` catches `api-key`. Spread `DEFAULT_REDACT_KEYS` to add your own.

`computeDiff(before, after)` returns the fields of `after` that changed, as `{ key: { old, new } }`.
It reads only the keys of `after`, so a partial DTO works; `null` equals `undefined`, dates compare
by instant, a Decimal or numeric string compares as a number, and nested objects and arrays compare
as JSON. `createdAt` and `updatedAt` are skipped (`{ ignore }` replaces that list). Use it where you
already load the record, for an `UPDATE` row with before and after:

```ts
import { computeDiff } from '@telamonjs/data'

const before = await prisma.order.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id } })
await prisma.order.update({ where: { id }, data: dto })
const changes = computeDiff(before, dto)   // { status: { old: 'OPEN', new: 'PAID' } }; {} when nothing changed
```

---

# Auth

> Auth bridge NextAuth v5 ↔ NestJS — shared session-token contract, Nest guard, Next callbacks

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/packages/auth.mdx

`@telamonjs/auth` (current version: <PkgVersion pkg='auth' />) is the
**auth bridge between a Next.js app using NextAuth v5 and a NestJS API**. Both
sides share one session token: the app issues it at login, the API decodes it
per request — no second login, no token exchange.

The package owns the **token contract**, not the login flow:

- **Isomorphic core** — the `JwtPayload` / `AuthUser` types plus
  `encodeSessionToken` / `decodeSessionToken` / `payloadToAuthUser`,
  `createImpersonationToken` and the session-freshness helpers
  `stampSessionTimes` / `sessionState`, and `generateApiKey` / `hashApiKey`
- **`/next` subpath** — `createAuthCallbacks()` with the canonical claim-copy
  for the NextAuth `jwt`/`session` callbacks
- **`/nest` subpath** — `createJwtAuthGuard()`, the `@Public()` decorator and
  the API-key guard for [service-to-service calls](#service-to-service-api-keys)

```bash
pnpm add @telamonjs/auth
```

Ships dual ESM+CJS builds (NestJS apps on CJS work out of the box). Peer:
`@auth/core`; the `/nest` subpath additionally expects `@nestjs/common` and
`@nestjs/core`.

---

## Token Architecture

The session token is the **NextAuth v5 JWE** produced by `@auth/core/jwt` —
an encrypted JWT, not a signed one. Decryption requires two inputs that MUST
be identical on both sides:

1. **Secret** — `AUTH_SECRET` (fallback `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`), same value in the
   Next app and the Nest API.
2. **Salt** — used in the key derivation. NextAuth uses the session cookie
   name as the salt, so the default is `'authjs.session-token'` (v5). Apps
   still serving the legacy v4 cookie use `'next-auth.session-token'`.

```ts
import { encodeSessionToken, decodeSessionToken } from '@telamonjs/auth'

// Emit a session token outside the browser flow (server-side login, tests,
// impersonation):
const token = await encodeSessionToken(payload, { maxAge: 60 * 60 })

// Decode (returns null for invalid/expired tokens):
const payload = await decodeSessionToken(token)
```

`TokenConfig` (`secret`, `salt`, `maxAge`) is accepted by every function and
by the Nest guard; secret defaults to the env vars, salt to the v5 default.
`maxAge` is the lifetime of an encoded token (default 24h). When decoding
(`decodeSessionToken`, the guard), a `maxAge` you pass also rejects a token
issued longer ago than that; without one, the token's own `exp` is the only
limit. The guard also accepts `secret` as a function resolved per
request (see [Secret resolved per request](#secret-resolved-per-request)).

### Known trap: which salt does your project use?

<Callout type='error' title='Wrong salt = every token “invalid”'>
  The salt feeds the JWE key derivation. If the app encodes with one salt and
  the API decodes with another, decryption fails silently and every request is
  a 401 — with valid cookies and the correct secret.
</Callout>

| Project                              | Cookie generation      | Salt to configure               |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| New apps (CLI template)              | NextAuth v5            | `'authjs.session-token'` (default — configure nothing) |
| Any app migrated from NextAuth v4 that kept its cookie config | Legacy v4 | `'next-auth.session-token'` |

A related knob on the guard: `cookieNames` controls **where the guard looks
for the cookie**, independent of the salt. Default:
`['__Secure-' + salt, salt]`. A project that decodes with one salt but serves
a differently-named cookie passes both explicitly (see below).

Only a secure origin can set a `__Secure-` cookie, while any plain-HTTP
response or non-secure sibling subdomain can plant the plain one. So while the
`__Secure-` cookie is present (even expired), the guard never falls back to
the plain one. An API served only over HTTPS should pass
`cookieNames: ['__Secure-authjs.session-token']`, so a planted plain cookie is
not read even when the user has no session.

### The payload contract

`JwtPayload` is the shared shape both sides agree on:

```ts
import type { JwtPayload } from '@telamonjs/auth'

interface JwtPayload {
  id: string
  pessoaId?: string
  name?: string
  email: string
  role: RoleInfo            // { id, name, code }
  roles?: RoleInfo[]        // multi-role
  permissions: string[]     // materialized RBAC — see the Permissions package

  clienteIds?: string[]     // optional data-scope claim (app domain)

  sid?: string              // stable per login; copied from `user.sid` by the jwt callback
  authTime?: number         // login time (epoch ms), stamped by the jwt callback
  accessAt?: number         // when role/roles/permissions were computed (epoch ms)

  // NextAuth claims: sub, iat, exp, jti

  // Impersonation block
  impersonatedUserId?: string
  originalUserId?: string
  // ... originalUserName / Email / Role / Roles / Permissions
}
```

`payloadToAuthUser(payload)` maps it to the `AuthUser` the guard attaches to
`request.user`, normalizing `roles` (falls back to `[role]`) and expanding the
impersonation block into `isImpersonating` + `originalUser`.

`AuthUser.sessionId` is `sid ?? jti`. NextAuth changes the `jti` on every cookie renewal, so return
a `sid` from `authorize()` when you need to end a specific session: it stays in the token across
renewals.

---

## Next.js Setup

The package provides the **callbacks**, the app provides **`authorize()`**:
how users are verified (password hash, external API, SSO) is app domain. The
contract is only that `authorize()` returns the canonical claims
(`SessionClaims`): `id`, `email`, `role`, `roles`, `permissions`, plus
optionals like `pessoaId` and `accessToken`.

```ts title="auth.ts"
import NextAuth from 'next-auth'
import Credentials from 'next-auth/providers/credentials'
import { createAuthCallbacks } from '@telamonjs/auth/next'

const base = createAuthCallbacks()

export const { handlers, auth, signIn, signOut } = NextAuth({
  session: { strategy: 'jwt' },
  providers: [
    Credentials({
      async authorize(credentials) {
        // App domain: verify the user, then return SessionClaims
        const user = await verifyLogin(credentials)
        if (!user) return null
        return {
          id: user.id,
          email: user.email,
          name: user.name,
          role: user.role,                          // { id, name, code }
          permissions: await getPermissionsForJWT(user), // materialized RBAC
        }
      },
    }),
  ],
  callbacks: base, // jwt + session with the canonical claim-copy
})
```

`createAuthCallbacks()` returns `{ jwt, session }`:

- **`jwt`** copies the claims from `user` into the token on login (id, role,
  roles, permissions, accessToken/refreshToken) and stamps `authTime` /
  `accessAt` (see [Session freshness & revocation](#session-freshness--revocation)).
- **`session`** projects the token back into `session.user` and exposes
  `isImpersonating` / `originalUser` at the session root.

Apps with extra token logic (sliding window, impersonation cookies) compose on
top instead of replacing:

```ts
const base = createAuthCallbacks()

callbacks: {
  jwt: async (args) => {
    const token = await base.jwt(args)
    // app-specific claims here
    return token
  },
  session: base.session,
}
```

---

## NestJS Setup

`createJwtAuthGuard()` builds the guard class; register it globally and opt
out per route with `@Public()`:

```ts title="src/common/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts"
import { createJwtAuthGuard } from '@telamonjs/auth/nest'

export const JwtAuthGuard = createJwtAuthGuard()

// Legacy v4 cookie project (see the salt table):
// export const JwtAuthGuard = createJwtAuthGuard({
//   salt: 'next-auth.session-token',
//   cookieNames: ['next-auth.session-token', '__Secure-next-auth.session-token'],
// })
```

```ts title="src/app.module.ts"
import { APP_GUARD } from '@nestjs/core'
import { JwtAuthGuard } from './common/guards/jwt-auth.guard'

@Module({
  providers: [{ provide: APP_GUARD, useClass: JwtAuthGuard }],
})
export class AppModule {}
```

```ts
import { Public } from '@telamonjs/auth/nest'

@Public()          // guard lets this route through without a token
@Post('login')
login() {}
```

### Token extraction order

The guard looks for the session token in three places, in priority order:

1. **`Authorization: Bearer <token>`** — the API-client pattern; the Next app
   forwards its own session JWE as a bearer token.
2. **`?token=` query param** — for SSE: `EventSource` cannot send custom
   headers, so streams pass the token in the URL.
3. **NextAuth cookies** — `cookieNames` (default `['__Secure-' + salt, salt]`),
   for same-domain requests with `credentials: 'include'`.

On success the guard attaches the decoded `AuthUser` to `request.user`; any
failure is a single `UnauthorizedException('Invalid or expired token')`.

To keep session tokens out of URLs (and access logs) outside your SSE routes,
subclass the guard and override `allowQueryToken(request)` — `request.path` /
`request.url` are available; return `false` and `?token=` is ignored.

### Secret resolved per request

`createJwtAuthGuard()` runs when its module is imported, before Nest DI and
before your env is loaded. Instead of a static string, `secret` takes a
function (sync or async) that the guard calls on every request:

```ts
export const JwtAuthGuard = createJwtAuthGuard({
  secret: () => process.env.AUTH_SECRET,
})
```

Returning `undefined` falls back to `AUTH_SECRET` / `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, as with
a static value. Subclasses inherit it unchanged.

### Throwing the host's exceptions (`createException`)

`createException?: (status: 401 | 403, message: string) => Error` builds every
401 the guard throws (this guard only passes 401). Leave it out and the guard
throws `UnauthorizedException` from the package's `@nestjs/common`; set it when
the package is linked and that copy is not the host's — see
[NestJS guard exceptions across package instances](/docs/troubleshooting#nestjs-guard-exceptions-across-package-instances).
It has the same signature as the option of `createPermissionsGuard`, so one
function serves both guards.

Downstream, pair it with the permissions guard from
[@telamonjs/permissions](/docs/packages/permissions), which reads
`request.user.permissions`.

---

## Impersonation

Impersonation is encoded **in the token**: when an admin impersonates a user,
the app re-issues the session token with the target user's claims plus the
original user's identity preserved in dedicated claims
(`impersonatedUserId`, `originalUserId`, `originalUserName`,
`originalUserEmail`, `originalUserRole`, `originalUserRoles`,
`originalPermissions`).

- `createImpersonationToken({ target, actor, logId })` mints that token
  server-side: `target` becomes the subject, `actor` fills the `original*`
  claims, and `logId` is the id of the app's audit record. It expires after
  1h by default (`DEFAULT_IMPERSONATION_MAX_AGE`). `encodeSessionToken`
  remains the lower-level primitive.
- `payloadToAuthUser` surfaces it as `user.isImpersonating = true` and
  `user.originalUser` — so API audit logs can attribute actions to the real
  operator while authorization applies the impersonated user's permissions.
- `createAuthCallbacks().session` exposes the same flags to the Next app
  (`session.isImpersonating`, `session.originalUser`) for the UI banner and
  the "stop impersonating" action.

Who may impersonate whom is app policy (typically superadmin-only, and never
impersonating another superadmin) — the package only carries the state.

---

## Session freshness & revocation

Roles and permissions live **in the token**, which keeps every check a lookup
— but a role change in the database only reaches the token at the next login,
and there is no way to end every session of a user. The package gives you the
building blocks; the app keeps the state:

- The `jwt` callback stamps two claims at login: `authTime` (login time) and
  `accessAt` (when roles/permissions were computed), both epoch ms. `iat` can't
  serve: NextAuth re-signs the token on every renewal, so `iat` keeps moving.
  `encodeSessionToken` stamps both on a payload without `authTime`, so tokens
  issued on the API (server-side login, impersonation) carry them too.
- `sessionState(token, { revokedAt, accessChangedAt })` compares them with two
  per-user marks and returns `'revoked'` (revocation newer than the login),
  `'stale'` (access changed after the claims were computed) or `'fresh'`.
  Revoked wins; a missing claim counts as 0, so tokens issued before you
  adopted this are caught by the next mark; `null` marks mean nothing changed.

<Steps>
<Step>

**Two per-user columns, stamped by the app.** For example `accessChangedAt`
and `sessionsRevokedAt` on the user table. Set `accessChangedAt = now()` when
the user's roles change, or the permissions of a role they hold change (for
every holder of that role); set `sessionsRevokedAt = now()` when an admin
revokes the user's sessions (or on password change).

</Step>
<Step>

**Nest: one lookup by primary key per request.** Subclass the guard and
override `resolveUser` — its return value becomes `request.user`, `null` is a
401. It runs after the token is decoded and the impersonation check passed.

```ts title="src/common/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts"
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'
import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core'
import { payloadToAuthUser, sessionState } from '@telamonjs/auth'
import { createJwtAuthGuard, type MfJwtPayload } from '@telamonjs/auth/nest'

@Injectable()
export class JwtAuthGuard extends createJwtAuthGuard() {
  constructor(
    reflector: Reflector,
    private readonly prisma: PrismaService
  ) {
    super(reflector)
  }

  protected override async resolveUser(payload: MfJwtPayload) {
    const marks = await this.prisma.user.findUnique({
      where: { id: payload.id },
      select: { accessChangedAt: true, sessionsRevokedAt: true },
    })
    if (!marks) return null
    const user = payloadToAuthUser(payload)
    switch (
      sessionState(payload, {
        revokedAt: marks.sessionsRevokedAt,
        accessChangedAt: marks.accessChangedAt,
      })
    ) {
      case 'revoked':
        return null
      case 'stale': // recompute role/roles/permissions for this request only
        return { ...user, ...(await loadAccess(this.prisma, payload.id)) }
      default:
        return user
    }
  }
}
```

Errors thrown inside `resolveUser` propagate unchanged: a database outage is
a 500, not a misleading 401. With a custom user type, pass it as
`createJwtAuthGuard<MyUser>()` and return it from `resolveUser`.

The base class (`JwtAuthGuardBase`), the constructor type (`JwtAuthGuardClass`)
and `RequestLike` (the `allowQueryToken` parameter) are exported from
`@telamonjs/auth/nest`, so `export class … extends createJwtAuthGuard()` also
compiles in projects with `declaration: true`.

</Step>
<Step>

**Next: refresh the token on renewal.** Compose over `createAuthCallbacks()`;
on non-login calls read the marks, sign out a revoked session by returning
`null`, and rewrite the claims (plus `accessAt`) of a stale one. `auth()` runs
the `jwt` callback on every call, so wrap the lookup in a per-request cache
such as React `cache` to avoid repeating it within one render.

```ts title="auth.ts"
import { cache } from 'react'
import { sessionState } from '@telamonjs/auth'
import { createAuthCallbacks } from '@telamonjs/auth/next'

const base = createAuthCallbacks()
const loadMarks = cache((userId: string) =>
  prisma.user.findUnique({
    where: { id: userId },
    select: { accessChangedAt: true, sessionsRevokedAt: true },
  })
)

callbacks: {
  jwt: async args => {
    const token = await base.jwt(args)
    if (args.user) {
      // fresh login: authorize() read the claims before this clock, so count
      // them as older than any mark (a change committing meanwhile stays stale)
      token.accessAt = 0
      return token
    }
    const marks = await loadMarks(token.id as string)
    if (!marks) return null
    const state = sessionState(token, {
      revokedAt: marks.sessionsRevokedAt,
      accessChangedAt: marks.accessChangedAt,
    })
    if (state === 'revoked') return null // signs the user out
    if (state === 'stale') {
      // role, roles, permissions — same source as authorize(); `accessAt` is
      // the mark read above, never the clock, so a change that commits while
      // loadAccess runs leaves the token stale
      Object.assign(token, await loadAccess(token.id as string), {
        accessAt: marks.accessChangedAt?.getTime() ?? 0,
      })
    }
    return token
  },
  session: base.session,
}
```

</Step>
</Steps>

<Callout title='Impersonation'>
  While impersonating, `id` is the target's. Decide which user's marks apply —
  typically the actor's (`originalUserId`) for revocation — and skip the stale
  refresh: the impersonation token carries the target's claims.
</Callout>

### Cached yes/no checks (`validateUser`)

`resolveUser` builds `request.user`, so it runs on every request. When the
user comes from the token and you only need a yes/no answer (user still
active, account not suspended, this session not ended), override
`validateUser` instead and cache its verdict with `validateUserCacheTtlMs`:

```ts title="src/common/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts"
import { Injectable } from '@nestjs/common'
import { Reflector } from '@nestjs/core'
import { createJwtAuthGuard, type AuthUser } from '@telamonjs/auth/nest'

@Injectable()
export class JwtAuthGuard extends createJwtAuthGuard({ validateUserCacheTtlMs: 30_000 }) {
  constructor(
    reflector: Reflector,
    private readonly prisma: PrismaService
  ) {
    super(reflector)
  }

  protected override async validateUser(user: AuthUser) {
    // While impersonating, the actor losing access ends the session too
    const ids = [user.id, user.originalUser?.id].filter((id): id is string => !!id)
    const active = await this.prisma.user.count({
      where: { id: { in: ids }, active: true, deletedAt: null },
    })
    if (active !== ids.length) return 'user inactive or deleted'
    if (user.sessionId && (await this.prisma.sessionLog.count({
      where: { sessionId: user.sessionId, endedAt: { not: null } },
    }))) {
      return 'session ended'
    }
    return true
  }
}
```

- It runs after `resolveUser`, only when that returned a user, and receives
  `(user, payload, context)`.
- `true` passes. `false` or a reason string is a 401 with the generic
  'Session is no longer valid'; the reason goes to the guard's Nest `Logger`,
  never to the client. A thrown error propagates (a 5xx), like `resolveUser`'s:
  a database outage must not look like an expired session and sign every user
  out. When the client must see a specific error (e.g. a suspended account),
  throw it from `resolveUser`.
- The cache is in memory, per process, keyed by the session token (a new
  login does not inherit an old `false`) and bounded to 1000 tokens. A thrown
  error is never cached. A database change takes up to the TTL to apply, so
  keep it short; with the cache on, the verdict must not depend on the
  request. Without `validateUserCacheTtlMs`, it runs on every request.

---

## Service-to-service (API keys)

Jobs, CI pipelines, other APIs and external integrations call the API with a
key instead of a session. The `/nest` subpath checks the key; the core
generates and hashes it.

### A route that only takes a key

`createApiKeyGuard(options)` builds a guard class. `verify(key, request)`
returns the principal the key belongs to, or `null` to reject; sync or async,
so a shared env secret and a database lookup both fit:

```ts title="src/common/guards/internal-key.guard.ts"
import { createApiKeyGuard, staticApiKey } from '@telamonjs/auth/nest'

export const InternalKeyGuard = createApiKeyGuard({
  header: 'x-internal-token', // default 'x-api-key'
  bearer: true,               // also read Authorization: Bearer <key>
  verify: staticApiKey(() => process.env.INTERNAL_API_TOKEN, 'jobs'),
})
```

```ts
@Public()                    // skip the global session guard...
@UseGuards(InternalKeyGuard) // ...the key guard protects the route
@Post('emit')
emit(@Req() req: { servicePrincipal: ServicePrincipal }) {}
```

- The key is read from `header` (any case; `false` reads none), then from
  `Authorization: Bearer` when `bearer: true`. A repeated header is not a key.
- A valid key attaches the principal to `request.servicePrincipal`;
  `request.user` is left untouched, so code that expects a user never mistakes
  a service for one.
- Anything else is a 401 'Invalid or missing API key', built by
  `createException` when you pass it (same option as `createJwtAuthGuard`).
  The guard logs nothing, so no key reaches the logs.
- A thrown verifier error propagates as-is: a database outage is not an
  invalid key. To send a specific 401/403 body (e.g. a suspended client),
  throw your own exception from `verify`.
- The guard does not read `@Public()`; that is how it composes with a global
  session guard.

`staticApiKey(expected, name = 'service')` checks one shared secret: it
hashes both sides with sha256 and compares them with `timingSafeEqual`, so
neither the content nor the length leaks through timing, and it resolves to
`{ name }` (`ServicePrincipal`). An unset or empty expected key rejects every
request, never "open when unconfigured". Pass a function: the guard is built
at import, before your env loads, and the function is called per request.

### A route that takes a session or a key

Give the session guard an `apiKey` option and mark the route
`@AllowServiceToken()`:

```ts title="src/common/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts"
import { createJwtAuthGuard, staticApiKey } from '@telamonjs/auth/nest'

export const JwtAuthGuard = createJwtAuthGuard({
  apiKey: { verify: staticApiKey(() => process.env.INTERNAL_API_KEY) },
})
```

```ts
import { AllowServiceToken } from '@telamonjs/auth/nest'

@AllowServiceToken() // a valid key passes; otherwise the normal session check
@Post('send')
send() {}
```

On a marked route, a valid key passes and sets `request.servicePrincipal`; no
key or a rejected one falls through to the session check, so the route is
never open (unlike `@Public()`). Unmarked routes never read the key. With
`bearer: true`, a session JWE sent as Bearer simply misses the key check and
authenticates as a session.

The option lives on the session guard rather than in a second guard because a
global guard is the one that has to let the key through: a second guard after
it would never run for a request without a session.

A service request has no `request.user`, so a `PermissionsGuard` after the
session guard answers 401 on a route with `@Permissions`. When a route takes
both, decide in your own guard what a service may do (e.g. skip the
permission check when `request.servicePrincipal` is set).

### Keys stored in the database

For many keys (one per client integration), store only a hash:

```ts
import { generateApiKey, hashApiKey } from '@telamonjs/auth'

const key = generateApiKey('svc_')  // 32 random bytes, base64url, after the prefix
await prisma.integration.create({
  data: { keyHash: await hashApiKey(key), keyStart: key.slice(0, 12) },
})
// show `key` once; it cannot be recovered
```

```ts
export const IntegrationKeyGuard = createApiKeyGuard({
  verify: async key => {
    const row = await prisma.integration.findUnique({
      where: { keyHash: await hashApiKey(key) },
    })
    return row?.active ? { clientId: row.clientId } : null
  },
})
```

`hashApiKey` is the hex sha256 of the key, the same digest as
`createHash('sha256').update(key).digest('hex')`, so hashes stored that way
keep working. A random 32-byte key needs no salt or slow hash. Both helpers use
Web Crypto, so the core entry stays isomorphic.

Scopes, rotation (several valid keys at once), rate limits and audit logging
stay in your app: put them in `verify` or in the principal it returns.

---

## Troubleshooting

### Every API request returns 401 with a valid session

Almost always the **salt mismatch** from the table above: the app encodes with
the legacy v4 salt while the guard decodes with the v5 default (or
vice-versa). Confirm which cookie name the browser actually stores and pass
that as `salt` (and `cookieNames`) to `createJwtAuthGuard`.

Second suspect: **different `AUTH_SECRET`** between the Next app and the API —
they must load the same value.

### 401 only on SSE endpoints

`EventSource` sends no custom headers and, cross-origin, no cookies either.
Append the session token as `?token=` — extraction priority 2 exists for
exactly this.

### 401 only in production

Production serves the `__Secure-` cookie prefix over HTTPS. The default
`cookieNames` covers `__Secure-${salt}`, but if you passed custom
`cookieNames` remember to include both variants.

### Guard works but `request.user.permissions` is empty

The claims were never copied into the token: `authorize()` didn't return
`permissions`, or the app replaced the callbacks instead of composing over
`createAuthCallbacks()`. Log the decoded payload — if `permissions` is missing
there, the problem is at login time, not in the guard.

### 500 instead of 401 in development

The package is linked instead of installed, so the guard throws an
`UnauthorizedException` from a second copy of `@nestjs/common`. Pass
`createException` so it throws the host's class; see
[NestJS guard exceptions across package instances](/docs/troubleshooting#nestjs-guard-exceptions-across-package-instances).

---

- [Permissions](/docs/packages/permissions) — the RBAC that fills `permissions[]`

- [Troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting) — two copies of a peer dependency

# Permissions

> RBAC materialized in the JWT — pure checkers, role helpers, Nest guard, Prisma tables and catalog sync

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/packages/permissions.mdx

`@telamonjs/permissions` (current version:
<PkgVersion pkg='permissions' />) is the authorization system of the TelamonJS
ecosystem: **RBAC materialized in the JWT**.

Permissions are resolved from the database **once, at login**, and carried in
the session token as a flat `permissions: string[]`. Every check after that is
a pure function over the token claims — **no query per request, no cache to
invalidate, client-safe by construction**.

- **Core (isomorphic)** — `createPermissionChecker` (`can` / `canAny` /
  `canAll` / `hasBypassRole`) and role helpers
- **`/nest` subpath** — `@Permissions()` decorator + `createPermissionsGuard()`
- **Prisma RBAC tables** — `Role`, `Permission`, `RolePermission`,
  `UserRole` to copy into your app, plus `diffPermissionCatalog` to keep the
  `Permission` table in step with the catalog defined in code

```bash
pnpm add @telamonjs/permissions
```

Dual ESM+CJS build; the `/nest` subpath expects `@nestjs/common` and
`@nestjs/core` in the host.

---

## Data Model (Prisma)

These are the tables the admin kit generates. Copy the fragment shipped with
the package (exported at `@telamonjs/permissions/prisma/schema.prisma`) into
your `schema.prisma` and migrate — it is a template, not a managed migration:

```prisma title="prisma/schema.prisma"
model Role {
  id          String  @id @default(cuid())
  name        String
  code        String  @unique // "superadmin", "admin", "readonly", ...
  description String?
  system      Boolean @default(false) // built-in role: the app must not delete it

  permissions RolePermission[]
  users       UserRole[]
}

model Permission {
  id          String  @id @default(cuid())
  code        String  @unique // "module.action", e.g. "users.read"
  module      String
  action      String  // "read" | "write" | "execute" | "approve"
  category    String?
  description String?

  roles RolePermission[]

  @@index([module, action])
}

model RolePermission {
  roleId       String
  permissionId String

  role       Role       @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  permission Permission @relation(fields: [permissionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([roleId, permissionId])
  @@index([permissionId])
}

model UserRole {
  userId String
  roleId String

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  role Role @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([userId, roleId])
  @@index([roleId])
}
```

Your app owns the `User` model: add the back-relation `roles UserRole[]` to it,
and keep `UserRole.userId` the same type as `User.id`. `action` is a `String`
holding the suffix of the code, not an enum — a new action needs no migration.
Rename the models or map the tables freely; the checker only reads the
`permissions[]` claim.

Effective permissions for a user = **the union of all their roles'
permissions**.

### Syncing the catalog

The permission catalog is defined in code; the `Permission` table follows it.
`diffPermissionCatalog(catalog, rows)` compares the two by `code` and returns
what to change — it never touches the database or its inputs:

| Field       | Holds                                                         |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `toCreate`  | Codes in the catalog, not in the table — every column resolved, ready for `createMany` |
| `toUpdate`  | Codes in both whose `description` or `category` changed — the row's `id` plus the catalog's values |
| `toDelete`  | Rows whose code is no longer in the catalog                   |
| `unchanged` | Rows with nothing to change                                   |

`module`/`action` default to the two halves of `code` (split at the last dot,
so `reports.sales.export` → `reports.sales` + `export`) and are not compared: a
row stored as `READ` for `users.read` is left alone. `null` and a missing value
are equal. A duplicate code in the catalog, or a code without a dot and no
explicit `module`/`action`, throws.

Apply it in one transaction, at deploy, in a seed or when the API boots:

```ts title="permissions/sync.ts"
import { diffPermissionCatalog, type PermissionDefinition } from '@telamonjs/permissions'
import type { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'

export const PERMISSIONS: PermissionDefinition[] = [
  { code: 'users.read', category: 'Records', description: 'View users' },
  { code: 'users.write', category: 'Records', description: 'Create, edit and remove users' },
  { code: 'roles.read', category: 'Access', description: 'View roles' },
  { code: 'roles.write', category: 'Access', description: 'Edit roles and the permission matrix' },
]

export async function syncPermissions(prisma: PrismaClient) {
  const rows = await prisma.permission.findMany()
  const { toCreate, toUpdate, toDelete } = diffPermissionCatalog(PERMISSIONS, rows)

  await prisma.$transaction([
    prisma.permission.createMany({ data: toCreate }),
    ...toUpdate.map(({ id, category, description }) =>
      prisma.permission.update({ where: { id }, data: { category, description } }),
    ),
    // RolePermission rows go with them (onDelete: Cascade)
    prisma.permission.deleteMany({ where: { id: { in: toDelete.map((row) => row.id) } } }),
  ])

  return { created: toCreate.length, updated: toUpdate.length, deleted: toDelete.length }
}
```

Leave out the `deleteMany` to keep permissions that are no longer in code
(an upsert-only sync). Assigning permissions to a role is a separate step:
replace the role's `RolePermission` rows (`deleteMany` + `createMany` in a
transaction).

---

## The Flow: Resolve at Login, Check from the Token

<Steps>
<Step>

### Resolve permissions in `authorize()`

At login, the app materializes the user's effective permission codes and puts
them in the session claims. The convention is a `getPermissionsForJWT` helper
that takes the union of the user's roles' permissions over the tables above:

```ts title="auth.ts (authorize)"
async authorize(credentials) {
  const user = await verifyLogin(credentials)
  if (!user) return null

  return {
    id: user.id,
    email: user.email,
    role: user.roles[0],                 // { id, name, code }
    roles: user.roles,                   // multi-role via UserRole
    permissions: await getPermissionsForJWT(user.id),
    // → ['users.read', 'users.write', 'roles.read', ...]
  }
}
```

```ts title="getPermissionsForJWT"
async function getPermissionsForJWT(userId: string): Promise<string[]> {
  const links = await prisma.rolePermission.findMany({
    where: { role: { users: { some: { userId } } } },
    select: { permission: { select: { code: true } } },
  })
  return [...new Set(links.map((l) => l.permission.code))]
}
```

The [Auth package](/docs/packages/auth)'s `createAuthCallbacks()` copies
`permissions` into the JWT and back into the session — both the Next app and
the Nest API see the same array.

<Callout type='info' title='Trade-off'>
  Changes to a user's roles/permissions take effect on the **next login** (or
  forced token refresh) — the token is the snapshot. In exchange, checks cost
  zero queries and work identically on client, server and API.
</Callout>

</Step>
<Step>

### Create the app's checker (once)

```ts title="lib/permissions.ts"
import { createPermissionChecker } from '@telamonjs/permissions'

const checker = createPermissionChecker({
  bypassRoles: ['superadmin'], // app domain — these roles pass every check
})

export const { can, canAny, canAll, hasBypassRole } = checker
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Check anywhere

```tsx
import { can, canAny } from '@/lib/permissions'

// Client Component — session.user satisfies UserWithPermissions by shape
{can(session?.user, 'clientes.create') && <CreateButton />}

// Server Action
export async function deleteCliente(id: string) {
  const session = await auth()
  if (!can(session?.user, 'clientes.delete')) {
    throw new Error('Unauthorized: clientes.delete')
  }
  // ...
}
```

| Function                | Semantics                                          |
| ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `can(user, p)`          | User has permission `p` (or a bypass role)         |
| `canAny(user, ps)`      | Has **at least one** (OR)                          |
| `canAll(user, ps)`      | Has **all** (AND)                                  |
| `hasBypassRole(user)`   | Has any configured bypass role                     |

All are pure and null-safe (`user` may be `null`/`undefined` → `false`). An
empty list (`canAny(user, [])`, `canAll(user, [])`) is `false` too, bypass roles
included: an empty requirement is a bug, not "nothing required". The
`UserWithPermissions` type is structural on purpose: the `AuthUser` from the
auth package satisfies it by shape, with no dependency between the packages.

Two optional settings cover apps that keep (part of) the table in code:

```ts
createPermissionChecker({
  bypassRoles: [],
  // granted by role code, merged with the user's own permissions[]
  rolePermissions: {
    teacher: ['classes.read', 'grades.write'],
    student: ['portal.access'],
  },
  wildcard: '*', // holding '*' (in the token or through rolePermissions) grants everything
})
```

`rolePermissions` reads every role in `roles[]` (the singular `role` is the fallback, as for
`bypassRoles`). With `wildcard`, a user holding that code passes every check; an empty
requirement list still denies. Without the options, `'*'` is an ordinary code. Give
`createPermissionsGuard` the same `rolePermissions`/`wildcard` so the server agrees with the
client.

A `CrudConfig` takes the same checker: `permissions: { can: p => can(session?.user, p), create:
'clientes.create', … }` gates the list's "New" button, row actions and dialogs (see
[Permissions](/docs/getting-started/crud-config#permissions)). To give it once for every list
and the `AdminShell` menu, wrap the shell in `<PermissionsProvider can={…}>`.

</Step>
</Steps>

---

## Role Helpers

Two distinct questions, two distinct helpers — do not mix them:

```ts
import {
  isAdminRole,
  isSuperAdminRole,
  hasGlobalDataVisibility,
  getPrimaryRole,
} from '@telamonjs/permissions'
```

| Helper                       | Question it answers                                | Use for |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `isSuperAdminRole(role, roles)` | "Is this a superadmin?"                         | **Privilege gates**: system roles management, impersonating admins, dangerous maintenance |
| `hasGlobalDataVisibility(role, roles)` | "Can they see all records?" (admin **or** superadmin) | **Data scoping**: skip the per-user visibility filter |
| `isAdminRole(role, roles)`   | admin or superadmin                                | Building block of the above |
| `getPrimaryRole(role, roles)` | First role of the list (or the singular role)     | Display  |

All helpers check `roles[]` first (multi-role) and fall back to the singular
`role`.

---

## NestJS: Decorator + Guard

### `@Permissions` — clause semantics

```ts
import { Permissions, RequirePermission } from '@telamonjs/permissions/nest'

// string clauses = OR: needs ONE of the two
@Permissions('relatorios.read', 'relatorios.export')

// array clause = AND: needs BOTH
@Permissions(['clientes.update', 'clientes.approve'])

// mixed: (a AND b) OR c
@Permissions(['clientes.update', 'clientes.approve'], 'admin.override')
```

`RequirePermission` is an alias of `Permissions` for projects that use that
naming convention. Routes without the decorator are **not** restricted by the
guard, unless it is created with `failClosed: true` (see below).

`@Permissions()` with no clause, or with an empty `[]` clause, throws when the
decorator is applied. The guard denies (403) any route whose permission metadata
is an empty list — whoever the user is — instead of treating it as "no decorator".

### `createPermissionsGuard`

```ts title="src/common/guards/permissions.guard.ts"
import { createPermissionsGuard } from '@telamonjs/permissions/nest'

export const PermissionsGuard = createPermissionsGuard()
// options: createPermissionsGuard({ bypassRoles: ['superadmin', 'admin'], failClosed: true })
// defaults: bypassRoles ['superadmin'], failClosed false
// rolePermissions / wildcard: as in createPermissionChecker
```

```ts
@Get('admin')
@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, PermissionsGuard) // order matters
@Permissions('admin.read')
getAdminData() {}
```

The guard runs **after** the auth guard from
[@telamonjs/auth](/docs/packages/auth): it reads
`request.user.permissions` (the array materialized in the JWT), applies the
clause semantics, and throws `ForbiddenException` (403) with the generic message
`Insufficient permissions` — the required codes are never sent to the client. A
request without `request.user` gets `UnauthorizedException` (401). Bypass roles
short-circuit to allow. It can also be registered globally via `APP_GUARD` after
the auth guard.

### `failClosed` — deny by default

With `failClosed: true`, a route that carries no `@Permissions` is denied (403)
unless it is marked `@Public()`. That turns a forgotten decorator into a denial
instead of an open endpoint — useful with a global `APP_GUARD`.

```ts
import { createPermissionsGuard, Public } from '@telamonjs/permissions/nest'

export const PermissionsGuard = createPermissionsGuard({ failClosed: true })

@Public()
@Get('health')
health() {}
```

`Public()` uses the metadata key `'isPublic'`, the same as `Public()` from
`@telamonjs/auth/nest`, so either decorator marks a route public for both
guards. Default: `false` — routes without the decorator stay open.

### `onDenied` — observe denials

`onDenied` is called right before every 403 with
`{ user, required, request }`: the route's clauses (`[]` on a `failClosed`
denial, where `user` may be `undefined`) and the raw HTTP request. The client
still gets the generic `Insufficient permissions`.

```ts
export const PermissionsGuard = createPermissionsGuard({
  onDenied: ({ user, required }) =>
    logger.warn('permission denied', { userId: user?.id, required }),
})
```

It runs synchronously: a returned promise is not awaited, and an error thrown
inside it replaces the 403. It is not called on a 401.

### `createException` — throw the host's exceptions

`createException?: (status: 401 | 403, message: string) => Error` builds the
401 and 403 the guard throws. Leave it out and the guard throws
`UnauthorizedException`/`ForbiddenException` from the package's
`@nestjs/common`; set it when the package is linked and that copy is not the
host's — see
[NestJS guard exceptions across package instances](/docs/troubleshooting#nestjs-guard-exceptions-across-package-instances).
The JWT guard of [@telamonjs/auth](/docs/packages/auth) takes the same option,
so one function serves both.

---

## Troubleshooting

### `can()` returns false for a permission the user clearly has

The token predates the grant — permissions are materialized at login. Have the
user log out/in, or implement token refresh. Verify by logging
`session.user.permissions`.

### Guard throws "User not authenticated" (401)

`PermissionsGuard` ran without `JwtAuthGuard` before it — nothing attached
`request.user`. Check guard order.

### Every check passes for some users

They hold a bypass role. `bypassRoles` is configured per app in
`createPermissionChecker` / `createPermissionsGuard` — make sure the list is
what you intend (default for the guard: `['superadmin']`).

### `permissions` is empty in the token

The login path never called the resolution helper, or the auth callbacks
dropped the claim — see the
[auth troubleshooting](/docs/packages/auth#troubleshooting).

---

- [Auth](/docs/packages/auth) — the token that carries `permissions[]`
- [Admin Module Structure](/docs/patterns/admin-module-structure) — module conventions that name the permission codes
