# Error Handling

> Structured error classes with categorized codes, context data and classification utilities

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/queue/error-handling.mdx

All errors in the queue system extend the base `QueueError` class, which provides:

- **Structured error codes** — categorized by domain (`QUEUE_1xxx`–`QUEUE_9xxx`)
- **Context data** — extra information for debugging and logging
- **Operational flag** — recoverable vs. critical errors
- **Timestamp** and **JSON serialization** (`toJSON()`) for structured logging

```typescript
class QueueError extends Error {
  code: ErrorCode
  context: Record<string, any>
  timestamp: Date
  isOperational: boolean
  toJSON(): Record<string, any>
}
```

<Callout type='info' title='Import paths'>
  The full error hierarchy, `ErrorCode` enum and utilities are exported from
  `@telamonjs/queue/utils`. The most common classes (`QueueError`,
  `JobNotFoundError`, `JobAlreadyRegisteredError`, `RedisConnectionError`,
  `WorkerError`, `QueueOperationError`, `JobValidationError`, `JobTimeoutError`)
  are also re-exported from the package root.
</Callout>

## Error code categories

| Range | Domain        | Base class            |
| ----- | ------------- | --------------------- |
| 1xxx  | Configuration | `ConfigurationError`  |
| 2xxx  | Job           | `JobError`            |
| 3xxx  | Worker        | `WorkerError`         |
| 4xxx  | Queue         | `QueueOperationError` |
| 5xxx  | Redis         | `RedisError`          |
| 6xxx  | Flow          | `FlowError`           |
| 7xxx  | Registry      | `RegistryError`       |
| 9xxx  | Generic       | `QueueError`          |

## Error reference

| Error class                 | Code       | Operational | Use case                       |
| --------------------------- | ---------- | ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| `InvalidRedisConfigError`   | QUEUE_1001 | No          | Invalid Redis configuration    |
| `InvalidWorkerConfigError`  | QUEUE_1002 | No          | Invalid worker configuration   |
| `InvalidJobOptionsError`    | QUEUE_1003 | No          | Invalid job options            |
| `InvalidJobNameError`       | QUEUE_1004 | No          | Invalid job name format        |
| `InvalidCronScheduleError`  | QUEUE_1005 | No          | Invalid cron schedule          |
| `JobNotFoundError`          | QUEUE_2000 | Yes         | Job not registered             |
| `JobAlreadyRegisteredError` | QUEUE_2001 | Yes         | Duplicate job registration     |
| `JobValidationError`        | QUEUE_2002 | Yes         | Job data validation failed     |
| `JobTimeoutError`           | QUEUE_2003 | Yes         | Job execution timeout          |
| `JobExecutionError`         | QUEUE_2004 | Yes         | Job execution failed           |
| `JobTransformError`         | QUEUE_2005 | Yes         | Job data transformation failed |
| `JobStalledError`           | QUEUE_2006 | Yes         | Job stalled                    |
| `WorkerNotFoundError`       | QUEUE_3001 | Yes         | Worker not found               |
| `WorkerAlreadyExistsError`  | QUEUE_3002 | Yes         | Worker already exists          |
| `WorkerStartError`          | QUEUE_3003 | No          | Worker failed to start         |
| `WorkerStopError`           | QUEUE_3004 | No          | Worker failed to stop          |
| `QueueNotFoundError`        | QUEUE_4001 | Yes         | Queue not found                |
| `QueueAddError`             | QUEUE_4002 | Yes         | Failed to add job to queue     |
| `QueueRemoveError`          | QUEUE_4003 | Yes         | Failed to remove job           |
| `QueuePauseError`           | QUEUE_4004 | Yes         | Failed to pause queue          |
| `QueueResumeError`          | QUEUE_4005 | Yes         | Failed to resume queue         |
| `RedisConnectionError`      | QUEUE_5000 | No          | Redis connection failed        |
| `RedisHealthCheckError`     | QUEUE_5002 | Yes         | Redis health check failed      |
| `FlowInvalidStructureError` | QUEUE_6001 | No          | Invalid flow structure         |
| `FlowExecutionError`        | QUEUE_6002 | Yes         | Flow execution failed          |
| `RegistryValidationError`   | QUEUE_7001 | No          | Registry validation failed     |

## Using custom errors

```typescript
import {
  QueueError,
  ErrorCode,
  JobNotFoundError,
  InvalidJobOptionsError,
} from '@telamonjs/queue/utils'

// Specific error
throw new JobNotFoundError('send-email')

// With context for debugging
throw new InvalidJobOptionsError('send-email', 'attempts must be >= 1', {
  attempts: 0,
})

// Base error with a custom code
throw new QueueError('Custom error message', ErrorCode.INTERNAL_ERROR, {
  customData: 'value',
})
```

### Serialization for structured logging

```typescript
try {
  await job.process(data)
} catch (error) {
  const jobError = new JobExecutionError('send-email', 'job-123', error)
  logger.error('Job failed', jobError.toJSON())
  // { name, message, code: 'QUEUE_2004', context, timestamp, isOperational, stack }
}
```

## Utilities

```typescript
import {
  isQueueError,
  isOperationalError,
  getErrorCode,
  formatError,
  ErrorCode,
} from '@telamonjs/queue/utils'

try {
  await queueManager.add(SendEmailJob, data)
} catch (error) {
  // Type guard
  if (isQueueError(error)) {
    logger.error('Queue operation failed', error.toJSON())
  } else {
    logger.error('Unexpected error', formatError(error))
  }

  // Extract code from any error
  if (getErrorCode(error) === ErrorCode.JOB_NOT_FOUND) {
    // job not registered
  }

  // Operational vs critical
  if (isOperationalError(error)) {
    await retry() // recoverable — retry / notify
  } else {
    await gracefulShutdown() // critical — shut down
    process.exit(1)
  }
}
```

## Failures inside a job

The classes above describe failures of the queue system itself. A job reports its
own failure by **throwing** from `process()` (or `validate()`/`transform()`):

1. The `onFailed(error)` hook runs. It runs after **every** failed attempt, not only
   the last one, so keep it idempotent (log, count, alert).
2. BullMQ retries the job according to `attempts` and `backoff`. The `Job` defaults
   are 3 attempts with exponential backoff starting at 1 second.
3. After the last attempt the job stays in the queue's failed set (the newest 500
   by default, `removeOnFail`) and is copied to the
   [Dead Letter Queue](/docs/queue/dead-letter-queue).

```typescript
import { Job } from '@telamonjs/queue'

export class ChargeOrderJob extends Job<ChargeData, ChargeResult> {
  name = 'charge-order' as const

  options = {
    attempts: 3,
    backoff: { type: 'exponential', delay: 5000 },
  }

  async process(data: ChargeData): Promise<ChargeResult> {
    try {
      return await primaryGateway.charge(data, { idempotencyKey: `order-${data.orderId}` })
    } catch (error) {
      // Degrade instead of failing when a fallback exists
      if (isRateLimited(error)) return secondaryGateway.charge(data)
      throw error // retried by BullMQ
    }
  }

  async onFailed(error: Error): Promise<void> {
    await alerts.notify(`charge-order attempt failed: ${error.message}`)
  }
}
```

**Make every job idempotent.** A retry runs `process()` again from the start, and a
worker that crashes mid-job (a *stalled* job) gets its job re-run by BullMQ. Check
for work already done (an existing row, a sent flag), pass idempotency keys to
external APIs, and give enqueue calls a stable `jobId` when the same logical job
must not be added twice:

```typescript
await queueManager.add(SendInvoiceJob, { invoiceId }, { jobId: `invoice-${invoiceId}` })
```

**Don't retry what can't succeed.** When an error is permanent (bad input, a 4xx
from an external API), retrying only delays the DLQ. Validate data before `add()`,
set `attempts: 1` on jobs that must never run twice (imports, payments without an
idempotency key), or catch the error and return a result that records the failure.

## Best practices

1. **Use the most specific error class** — `new JobNotFoundError('send-email')`,
   not `new Error('Job not found: send-email')`.
2. **Provide context data** — include the invalid values, limits, IDs.
3. **Catch specific error types** — `instanceof JobNotFoundError` branches instead
   of a generic catch-all.
4. **Log with `toJSON()`** — keeps logs structured and queryable.
5. **Split handling by `isOperational`** — recover from operational errors, shut
   down on non-operational ones.

## Related

- [Logging](/docs/queue/logging)
- [Validation](/docs/queue/validation)
- [Dead Letter Queue](/docs/queue/dead-letter-queue)

---

# Logging

> Structured logging via ILogger injection from @telamonjs/logger

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/queue/logging.mdx

`@telamonjs/queue` does not ship its own logger.
All logging goes through the **`ILogger`** interface from
[`@telamonjs/logger`](/docs/packages/logger), injected via the `logger`
config option.

## Logger resolution

The `QueueManager` resolves its logger in this order:

1. **`config.logger`** — the `ILogger` you inject (recommended). Pass
   `new NoOpLogger()` from `@telamonjs/logger` for a silent manager
   (useful in tests).
2. **Default** — `createLogger({ context: { service: 'telamonjs-queue' } })` from
   `@telamonjs/logger` (environment auto-detection)

The same logger instance is propagated to the job registry, workers, the DLQ and
the flow producer.

## Injecting a logger

```typescript
import { QueueManager } from '@telamonjs/queue'
import { createLogger, LogLevel } from '@telamonjs/logger'

const logger = createLogger({
  level: LogLevel.INFO,
  context: { service: 'my-queue-service' },
})

const queueManager = new QueueManager({
  redis: { host: 'localhost', port: 6379 },
  logger,
})
```

Worker-oriented logging with scoped context:

```typescript
import { createWorkerLogger } from '@telamonjs/logger'

const queueManager = new QueueManager({
  redis: { host: 'localhost', port: 6379 },
  logger: createWorkerLogger({ context: { service: 'queue-worker' } }),
})
```

## Silent logging (tests)

```typescript
import { NoOpLogger } from '@telamonjs/logger'

const queueManager = new QueueManager({
  redis: { host: 'localhost', port: 6379 },
  logger: new NoOpLogger(),
})
```

## What gets logged

All queue logs carry structured metadata:

| Event             | Level | Example message            | Metadata                          |
| ----------------- | ----- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| QueueManager init | info  | `QueueManager initialized` | `prefix`, `redisHost`, `redisPort`|
| Job registration  | debug | `Job registered`           | `jobName`                         |
| Job added         | debug | `Job added to queue`       | `jobName`, `jobId`                |
| Job completed     | debug | `Job completed`            | `jobId`, `jobName`                |
| Job failed        | error | `Job failed`               | `jobId`, `error`, `attemptsMade`  |
| Bulk add          | debug | `Bulk jobs added to queue` | `jobName`, `count`                |
| Bulk remove/retry | info  | `Bulk jobs removed` / `Bulk jobs retried` | counts             |
| Queue actions     | info  | `Queue cleaned` / `Queue drained` / `Queues paused` | queue names, counts |
| Cron scheduled    | info  | `SchedulerReconciler scheduled job` | `jobName`, `cronPattern`, `timezone` |

## Correlation IDs

Use the logger's own context management:

```typescript
import { logger } from '@telamonjs/logger'

const requestLogger = logger.withRequestId(req.headers['x-request-id'])

const queueManager = new QueueManager({
  redis: { host: 'localhost', port: 6379 },
  logger: requestLogger,
})
```

Or scope per-job context inside `process()`:

```typescript
import { createWorkerLogger } from '@telamonjs/logger'

export class SendEmailJob extends Job<EmailData, void> {
  name = 'send-email' as const

  async process(data: EmailData): Promise<void> {
    const log = createWorkerLogger({ context: { jobName: this.name } })
    log.info('Job started', { to: data.to })
    await sendEmail(data)
    log.success('Email sent')
  }
}
```

## Custom sinks (Sentry, Datadog, …)

Any object implementing `ILogger` works. The shortest adapter extends one of the package's
loggers and overrides the levels it cares about:

```typescript
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/node'
import { ConsoleLogger, type LogContext } from '@telamonjs/logger'

class SentryLogger extends ConsoleLogger {
  override error(message: string, context?: LogContext): void {
    super.error(message, context)
    Sentry.captureException(new Error(message), { extra: context })
  }
}

const queueManager = new QueueManager({
  redis: { host: 'localhost', port: 6379 },
  logger: new SentryLogger({ context: { service: 'queue' } }),
})
```

## Best practices

- **Structured context** — put IDs and counts in the context object, not in the message, so
  they stay searchable.
- **Appropriate levels** — `debug` for development detail, `info` for normal
  operations, `warn` for recoverable issues, `error` for failures.
- **No PII in log context** — log IDs, never emails/passwords/tokens.

## Related

- [Logger package](/docs/packages/logger) — adapters, factories and the full `ILogger` API
- [Error Handling](/docs/queue/error-handling) — `toJSON()` for structured error logs

# Metrics

> Prometheus metrics with caching, batching and sampling for high-throughput queues

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/queue/metrics.mdx

`@telamonjs/queue/metrics` exports two Prometheus collectors:

- **`QueueMetrics`** — the standard collector, fine for most workloads
  (&lt; 100 jobs/sec)
- **`OptimizedQueueMetrics`** — a drop-in replacement adding caching, batching,
  sampling and lazy updates for high-throughput environments, with fewer Redis
  calls and less CPU per event

Import them from `@telamonjs/queue/metrics`. `prom-client` is a dependency of
the package, nothing to install. `@telamonjs/queue/monitoring` also exports both, next to the health
checks; the root entry still re-exports them for compatibility, marked
`@deprecated`.

## Exposed metrics

```text
# Job counters
queue_jobs_processed_total{queue="send-email",status="completed"}
queue_jobs_completed_total{queue="send-email"}
queue_jobs_failed_total{queue="send-email"}

# Job duration quantiles
queue_job_duration_seconds{queue="send-email",quantile="0.5"}
queue_job_duration_seconds{queue="send-email",quantile="0.95"}
queue_job_duration_seconds{queue="send-email",quantile="0.99"}

# Queue sizes
queue_size{queue="send-email",state="waiting"}
queue_size{queue="send-email",state="active"}
queue_size{queue="send-email",state="failed"}

# Workers
queue_active_workers{queue="send-email"}

# Optimized-only: cache/batch performance
queue_metrics_cache_hits_total
queue_metrics_cache_misses_total
queue_metrics_batch_size
```

## Quick start

```typescript
import { OptimizedQueueMetrics } from '@telamonjs/queue/metrics'
import express from 'express'

const metrics = new OptimizedQueueMetrics(queueManager)
metrics.startCollection()

const app = express()
app.get('/metrics', async (req, res) => {
  res.set('Content-Type', metrics.getRegistry().contentType)
  res.end(await metrics.getMetrics())
})
```

## Optimization features

| Feature      | What it does                                            | Trade-off                        |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| **Caching**  | Caches queue stats with TTL (default 5s)                | Stats stale up to `cacheTTL`     |
| **Batching** | Groups metric updates, flushes every `batchInterval`    | Metrics delayed by ~1–2s         |
| **Sampling** | Records only a fraction of events (e.g. 10%)            | Approximate counts               |
| **Lazy**     | Fetches stats only on `getMetrics()` (Prometheus scrape)| —                                |

## Configuration

```typescript
interface MetricsConfig {
  cacheTTL?: number // default 5000 ms
  enableBatching?: boolean // default true
  batchInterval?: number // default 1000 ms
  enableSampling?: boolean // default false
  sampleRate?: number // 0.0–1.0, default 0.1
  collectionInterval?: number // default 10000 ms
}
```

### Recommended presets

```typescript
// Low throughput (< 100 jobs/sec): standard collector
import { QueueMetrics } from '@telamonjs/queue/metrics'
const metrics = new QueueMetrics(queueManager)

// Medium (100–1000 jobs/sec)
new OptimizedQueueMetrics(queueManager, {
  cacheTTL: 5000,
  enableBatching: true,
  batchInterval: 1000,
})

// High (1000–10,000 jobs/sec)
new OptimizedQueueMetrics(queueManager, {
  cacheTTL: 10000,
  enableBatching: true,
  batchInterval: 2000,
})

// Very high (> 10,000 jobs/sec): add sampling
new OptimizedQueueMetrics(queueManager, {
  cacheTTL: 15000,
  enableBatching: true,
  batchInterval: 5000,
  enableSampling: true,
  sampleRate: 0.1,
})
```

<Callout type='info' title='Tuning cacheTTL'>
  Set `cacheTTL` to 50–75% of your Prometheus scrape interval (e.g. scraping
  every 15s → `cacheTTL: 10000`), and target a cache hit rate above 70%
  (`cache_hits / (cache_hits + cache_misses)`).
</Callout>

## API

`OptimizedQueueMetrics` shares the `QueueMetrics` API:

```typescript
metrics.incrementProcessed(queueName, jobName)
metrics.incrementCompleted(queueName, jobName)
metrics.incrementFailed(queueName, jobName, errorType)
metrics.recordDuration(queueName, jobName, seconds)
metrics.updateQueueSizes()
metrics.updateActiveWorkers(queueName, count)
await metrics.getMetrics()
metrics.getRegistry()
metrics.startCollection(interval)
metrics.stopCollection()
```

Plus optimized-only methods:

```typescript
metrics.invalidateCache() // force fresh stats on next scrape
metrics.getCacheStats() // cache hit rate
metrics.getConfig() // current config
```

Invalidate the cache after manual queue operations (`pauseAll()`, bulk cleans) so
the next scrape reflects reality.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                        | Fix                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Metrics are stale              | Reduce `cacheTTL`                                      |
| Inaccurate low-volume metrics  | Disable sampling or raise `sampleRate`                 |
| Low cache hit rate             | Raise `cacheTTL` toward the Prometheus scrape interval |
| High memory from batching      | Reduce `batchInterval` (more frequent flushes)         |

## Related

- [Logging](/docs/queue/logging)
- [Error Handling](/docs/queue/error-handling)
- [Dead Letter Queue](/docs/queue/dead-letter-queue)

# Priorities

> Semantic job priority levels and utilities for ordering queue processing

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/queue/priorities.mdx

BullMQ uses numeric priorities from 1 to 10 where **lower number = higher priority**.
`@telamonjs/queue` wraps them in a semantic `JobPriority` enum so intent
is clear and consistent across the application:

```typescript
export enum JobPriority {
  CRITICAL = 1, // processed immediately
  HIGH = 3, // processed before normal jobs
  NORMAL = 5, // default
  LOW = 8, // processed when system has capacity
  DEFERRED = 10, // lowest priority
}
```

| Level      | Use for                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `CRITICAL` | Security alerts, password resets, expiring tokens — true emergencies     |
| `HIGH`     | User-facing operations the user is actively waiting for (uploads, forms) |
| `NORMAL`   | Regular background jobs (default behavior when omitted)                  |
| `LOW`      | Cleanup, analytics, non-urgent reports                                   |
| `DEFERRED` | Batch processing, large reports, migrations                              |

## Usage

```typescript
import { QueueManager, JobPriority } from '@telamonjs/queue'

await queueManager.add(SendSecurityAlertJob, alertData, {
  priority: JobPriority.CRITICAL,
})

await queueManager.add(ProcessUploadJob, uploadData, {
  priority: JobPriority.HIGH,
})

// Omitting priority = NORMAL behavior
await queueManager.add(ProcessDataJob, data)
```

<Callout type='warn' title='Reserve CRITICAL for true emergencies'>
  If everything is CRITICAL, nothing is. Newsletters and marketing belong in
  `LOW`/`DEFERRED`; security alerts belong in `CRITICAL`.
</Callout>

## Utilities

```typescript
import {
  getPriorityName,
  getPriorityDescription,
  isHigherPriority,
  getHighestPriority,
  getLowestPriority,
  isValidPriority,
  clampPriority,
  sortByPriority,
  groupByPriority,
  getPriorityDistribution,
  suggestPriority,
} from '@telamonjs/queue'

getPriorityName(JobPriority.CRITICAL) // 'Critical'
getPriorityDescription(JobPriority.HIGH) // human-readable description

isHigherPriority(JobPriority.CRITICAL, JobPriority.NORMAL) // true
getHighestPriority([5, 1, 8, 3]) // 1
getLowestPriority([5, 1, 8, 3]) // 8

isValidPriority(11) // false
clampPriority(15) // 10 (clamped to 1–10)

sortByPriority(jobs) // highest priority first
groupByPriority(jobs) // Record<number, T[]>
```

### suggestPriority — dynamic decisions

```typescript
// User-facing operation with a tight timeout
suggestPriority({ userFacing: true, timeoutMs: 3000 }) // JobPriority.CRITICAL

// Batch operation
suggestPriority({ batch: true }) // JobPriority.LOW

// Full characteristics
suggestPriority({
  userFacing: job.requiresUserInteraction,
  critical: job.affectsSystemHealth,
  timeoutMs: job.maxWaitTime,
  batch: job.isBatchOperation,
  cleanup: job.isCleanup,
})
```

### Distribution analysis

```typescript
const jobs = (await queueManager.getQueue('my-queue')?.getJobs(['waiting', 'active'])) ?? []
const distribution = getPriorityDistribution(jobs)
// { total, byLevel: { 1: { count, percentage }, ... }, averagePriority }

if (distribution.byLevel[JobPriority.CRITICAL]?.percentage > 10) {
  logger.warn('Too many CRITICAL jobs — review priority assignments')
}
```

## Example: e-commerce order processing

```typescript
// Customer just placed an order — user-facing
await queueManager.add(ProcessOrderJob, orderData, { priority: JobPriority.HIGH })

// Payment failed — notify immediately
await queueManager.add(SendPaymentFailedEmailJob, emailData, {
  priority: JobPriority.CRITICAL,
})

// Inventory update — regular background work
await queueManager.add(UpdateInventoryJob, inventoryData, {
  priority: JobPriority.NORMAL,
})

// Analytics — when there is capacity
await queueManager.add(UpdateAnalyticsJob, analyticsData, {
  priority: JobPriority.LOW,
})

// Daily sales report — can wait
await queueManager.add(GenerateDailySalesReportJob, reportData, {
  priority: JobPriority.DEFERRED,
})
```

## Troubleshooting

**High-priority jobs are not processed first?**

1. With high worker concurrency, everything runs simultaneously — lower
   `concurrency` to observe priority ordering.
2. Verify the `priority` option is actually being set on `add()`.
3. Inspect the waiting jobs: `sortByPriority(await queue.getJobs(['waiting']))`, with
   `queue = queueManager.getQueue('my-queue')`.

## Related

- [Bulk Operations](/docs/queue/bulk-operations) — per-job priority overrides in `addBulk`
- [Scheduling](/docs/queue/scheduling)

# Scheduling

> Cron scheduling with human-readable helpers, timezone support and pattern validation

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/queue/scheduling.mdx

Recurring jobs use standard cron expressions
(`minute hour day month dayOfWeek [year]`), but the package provides
human-readable helpers so you rarely write raw cron:

```typescript
import { dailyAt, Timezones } from '@telamonjs/queue'

// Instead of: schedule = '0 9 * * *'
const schedule = dailyAt(9, 0, Timezones.AMERICA_NEW_YORK)
// { pattern: '0 9 * * *', tz: 'America/New_York' }
```

## Declaring a scheduled job

A job class declares its default cron in `configDefaults`. That value seeds a
`JobConfigStore` (Redis), and a `SchedulerReconciler` keeps BullMQ job schedulers in
sync with the store, so the cron can be toggled or edited from the
[Jobs Dashboard](/docs/queue/dashboard) without a redeploy:

```typescript
import { Job, QueueRegistry, dailyAt, Timezones, type JobConstructor } from '@telamonjs/queue'
import { JobConfigStore, setupFromConfig } from '@telamonjs/queue/job-config'
import { SchedulerReconciler } from '@telamonjs/queue/scheduler'

export class DailyReportJob extends Job<void, void> {
  name = 'daily-report' as const
  configDefaults = {
    cronPattern: dailyAt(9, 0).pattern, // '0 9 * * *'
    timezone: Timezones.AMERICA_SAO_PAULO,
    enabled: true, // without it the job is seeded disabled
  }

  async process(): Promise<void> {
    const report = await generateDailyReport()
    await sendReport(report)
  }
}

const redis = { host: 'localhost', port: 6379 }
const jobs = new Map<string, JobConstructor>([['daily-report', DailyReportJob]])
const store = new JobConfigStore({ redis, prefix: 'myapp' }) // same prefix as the queues

// Seeds the store from Job.configDefaults and registers the enabled jobs
await setupFromConfig(queueManager, store, jobs)

// Adds/removes/updates BullMQ job schedulers to match the store, every minute
const reconciler = new SchedulerReconciler(new QueueRegistry({ redis, prefix: 'myapp' }), store, jobs)
await reconciler.start()
```

The store keeps its configs under `${prefix}:config:`. Give it the same `prefix`
as the queues (and give `JobEventPublisher`/`createSSEBroadcaster` the same one
for events): apps sharing one Redis with the default `telamonjs` share one
config index, so each app's bootstrap disables the other's jobs. An existing
app moving off the default can pass `keyPrefix: 'telamonjs:config:'` to keep its
stored configs.

The reconciler writes one BullMQ **job scheduler** per job (`upsertJobScheduler`,
id = job name), so a cron, timezone or priority edit updates it in place. It
removes the scheduler when the job is disabled or loses its cron.

<Callout type='info' title='Upgrading from repeatable jobs'>
  Earlier versions scheduled through BullMQ's deprecated repeatable API
  (`add(..., { repeat })`), and those repeatables are still in Redis after an
  upgrade. On its first reconcile the reconciler finds every repeatable of a job
  it manages, removes it together with its pending run, then upserts the
  scheduler — the two never coexist, so no job runs twice. A repeatable of a job
  that is no longer enabled is simply removed. During a rolling deploy, a
  repeatable re-created by an instance still on the old version is cleaned up on
  the next cycle.
</Callout>

`enabled` seeds as `false` when omitted: without `enabled: true` the job starts
disabled (not registered, no schedule) until it is turned on from the
dashboard. `configDefaults` only seeds — a value already in Redis wins.

`configDefaults` takes the same fields as `JobConfigInput` from
`@telamonjs/queue/job-config`: `description`, `enabled`, `cronPattern`,
`timezone`, `priority`, `concurrency` and `timeout`. `setupFromConfig` also
accepts per-job `defaults` in its options, merged over the class's
`configDefaults` field by field, to override a seed without touching the class.

<Callout type='warn' title='The cron lives in configDefaults'>
  A job class has no `schedule` field. A class that declares one makes
  `QueueManager.register()` and the `SchedulerReconciler` constructor throw, so a
  job can never be silently left unscheduled.
</Callout>

### What `setupFromConfig` does

1. **Bootstrap** (`store.bootstrap()`) reconciles the jobs in code with the
   configs in Redis. A job missing from Redis is created from its defaults. A
   field present in the defaults but empty in Redis is backfilled; a value
   already set in Redis (an edit made from the dashboard) is never overwritten.
   A config whose job no longer exists in code is marked `orphan` and disabled;
   if the job comes back, the orphan flag is cleared but the job is **not**
   re-enabled. Running it twice changes nothing.
2. **Registration** registers on the `QueueManager` only the jobs that are
   `enabled` and not `orphan`.
3. **Fallback.** If Redis is unreachable, every job is registered
   unconditionally and the result reports `mode: 'fallback'`, so a config
   outage never takes the workers down with it.

The result lists `registered`, `skipped` (disabled, orphan or without a
config) and `missing` (enabled in Redis with no class in code) job names.

## SchedulePatterns

Pre-defined constants for common scenarios:

```typescript
import { SchedulePatterns } from '@telamonjs/queue'

SchedulePatterns.EVERY_MINUTE // '* * * * *'
SchedulePatterns.EVERY_5_MINUTES // '*/5 * * * *'
SchedulePatterns.EVERY_15_MINUTES // '*/15 * * * *'
SchedulePatterns.EVERY_30_MINUTES // '*/30 * * * *'
SchedulePatterns.EVERY_HOUR // '0 * * * *'
SchedulePatterns.EVERY_6_HOURS // '0 */6 * * *'
SchedulePatterns.EVERY_12_HOURS // '0 */12 * * *'
SchedulePatterns.DAILY_AT_MIDNIGHT // '0 0 * * *'
SchedulePatterns.DAILY_AT_NOON // '0 12 * * *'
SchedulePatterns.WEEKLY_MONDAY // '0 0 * * 1'
SchedulePatterns.WEEKLY_SUNDAY // '0 0 * * 0'
SchedulePatterns.MONTHLY_FIRST // '0 0 1 * *'
SchedulePatterns.MONTHLY_LAST // '0 0 L * *'
SchedulePatterns.YEARLY // '0 0 1 1 *'
```

## Schedule helpers

All helpers return `{ pattern, tz? }` and validate their inputs (throwing on
out-of-range values):

| Helper                                    | Example                                | Result pattern        |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `everyMinutes(n, tz?)` (1–59)             | `everyMinutes(5)`                      | `*/5 * * * *`         |
| `everyHours(n, tz?)` (1–23)               | `everyHours(6)`                        | `0 */6 * * *`         |
| `dailyAt(hour, minute?, tz?)`             | `dailyAt(9, 30)`                       | `30 9 * * *`          |
| `weeklyOn(days, hour?, minute?, tz?)`     | `weeklyOn([1, 3, 5], 9, 0)`            | `0 9 * * 1,3,5`       |
| `monthlyOn(day \| 'L', hour?, minute?, tz?)` | `monthlyOn('L', 23, 59)`            | `59 23 L * *`         |
| `yearlyOn(month, day, hour?, minute?, tz?)` | `yearlyOn(12, 25, 9, 0)`             | `0 9 25 12 *`         |
| `weekdays(hour?, minute?, tz?)`           | `weekdays(9, 0)`                       | `0 9 * * 1,2,3,4,5`   |
| `weekends(hour?, minute?, tz?)`           | `weekends(10, 0)`                      | `0 10 * * 0,6`        |

Day-of-week values: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday.

## Timezones

The `Timezones` constant covers common IANA zones (`UTC`,
`AMERICA_SAO_PAULO`, `AMERICA_NEW_YORK`, `EUROPE_LONDON`, `ASIA_TOKYO`, …), and any
valid IANA string is accepted:

```typescript
import { dailyAt, Timezones } from '@telamonjs/queue'

dailyAt(9, 0, Timezones.AMERICA_SAO_PAULO)
dailyAt(9, 0, 'America/Mexico_City') // custom IANA zone
```

## Validation and parsing

```typescript
import {
  isValidCronPattern,
  parseSchedule,
  formatCronPattern,
} from '@telamonjs/queue'

// Validate (5 or 6 fields, supports * / - , L W)
isValidCronPattern('0 9 * * *') // true
isValidCronPattern('60 25 * * *') // false

// Parse human-readable strings → cron
parseSchedule('every 5 minutes') // '*/5 * * * *'
parseSchedule('daily at 9:30am') // '30 9 * * *'
parseSchedule('daily at 12am') // '0 0 * * *' (midnight)
parseSchedule('weekdays at 9am') // '0 9 * * 1-5'
parseSchedule('hourly') // '0 * * * *'
parseSchedule('monthly') // '0 0 1 * *'

// Format cron → human-readable (unknown patterns returned as-is)
formatCronPattern('*/5 * * * *') // 'Every 5 minutes'
formatCronPattern('30 14 * * *') // 'Daily at 2:30 PM'
formatCronPattern('0 9 * * 1-5') // 'Weekdays at 9:00 AM'
```

## Dynamic scheduling

`QueueManager.add()` deliberately leaves out BullMQ's `repeat` option. For a
one-off schedule outside the `JobConfigStore`, upsert a job scheduler on the raw
queue; the fixed id makes it idempotent, so a restart does not register it twice:

```typescript
import { everyMinutes } from '@telamonjs/queue'

const schedule = everyMinutes(5)

await queueManager
  .getQueue('monitor')
  ?.getRawQueue()
  .upsertJobScheduler(
    'monitor-every-5-minutes',
    { pattern: schedule.pattern, tz: schedule.tz },
    { name: 'monitor', data: {} }
  )
```

Keep such a job out of the `SchedulerReconciler`'s job map: the reconciler
removes any schedule of a job it manages other than its own.

<Callout type='info'>
  In the [Jobs Dashboard](/docs/queue/dashboard) configuration tab, cron patterns
  of registered jobs can be inspected and edited at runtime per job.
</Callout>

## Related

- [Priorities](/docs/queue/priorities)
- [Validation](/docs/queue/validation)

# Validation

> Automatic Zod validation of queue configuration, job options, names and job data

Source: apps/docs/content/docs/queue/validation.mdx

All queue configuration is validated automatically with **Zod**. Invalid input
throws a structured error (a `QueueError` subclass with a `QUEUE_1xxx` code, see
[Error Handling](/docs/queue/error-handling)) with a readable message, instead of
failing later inside BullMQ.

| What | Checked by | Throws |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `QueueManager` config | `new QueueManager()` | `ConfigurationError` |
| Job name | `register()` | `InvalidJobNameError` |
| Job options (merged) | `add()` / `addBulk()` / `FlowProducer.add()` | `InvalidJobOptionsError` |
| Worker config | `createWorkers()` | `InvalidWorkerConfigError` |

## What gets validated

### QueueManager configuration

```typescript
import { QueueManager } from '@telamonjs/queue'
import { ConfigurationError } from '@telamonjs/queue/utils'

try {
  const queueManager = new QueueManager({
    redis: {
      host: 'localhost', // default 'localhost'
      port: 6379, // 1–65535, default 6379
      db: 0, // 0–15, default 0
    },
    prefix: 'my-queue', // 1–50 chars, default 'telamonjs'
  })
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ConfigurationError) {
    console.error(error.message, error.context)
  }
}
```

<Callout type='info' title='Extra Redis options pass through'>
  The Redis config schema uses `.passthrough()` — valid ioredis options
  beyond the validated core fields (e.g. `maxRetriesPerRequest`,
  `enableReadyCheck`, TLS settings) are preserved instead of being silently
  discarded.
</Callout>

### Job names

Pattern `/^[a-z0-9-_]+$/`, 1–100 characters: lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens
and underscores only. `SendEmail`, `send email`, `send.email` are all rejected at
registration.

### Job options

```typescript
await queueManager.add(MyJob, data, {
  attempts: 5, // 1–100
  priority: 1, // 1–10 (lower = higher)
  timeout: 30000, // positive ms
  delay: 5000, // non-negative ms
  backoff: { type: 'exponential', delay: 1000 }, // or fixed / plain number
  removeOnComplete: 10, // boolean or positive number
  removeOnFail: 50,
  jobId: 'unique-id', // non-empty string
})
```

### Worker configuration

```typescript
await queueManager.createWorkers({
  concurrency: 10, // 1–100
  autoRun: true,
  limiter: { max: 100, duration: 1000 }, // positive integers
})
```

## Job data validation (custom)

Validate payloads with the `validate()` hook and your own Zod schema:

```typescript
import { z } from 'zod'
import { Job } from '@telamonjs/queue'

const EmailSchema = z.object({
  to: z.string().email(),
  subject: z.string().min(1).max(200),
  body: z.string().min(1),
})

type EmailData = z.infer<typeof EmailSchema>

export class SendEmailJob extends Job<EmailData, void> {
  name = 'send-email' as const

  async validate(data: unknown): Promise<void> {
    EmailSchema.parse(data) // throws ZodError if invalid
  }

  async process(data: EmailData): Promise<void> {
    await sendEmail(data.to, data.subject, data.body)
  }
}
```

`validate()` runs **in the worker**, right before `process()` (and before the
optional `transform()` hook), not when the job is added. A throw fails that
attempt like any other error: it is retried according to `attempts`, and lands in
the [Dead Letter Queue](/docs/queue/dead-letter-queue) after the last one. Data
that can never become valid should be rejected before `add()`, at the API
boundary.

## Manual validation

`@telamonjs/queue/utils` exports `validateJobOptions` (throws a `ZodError`, returns
the validated options, typed as `ValidatedJobOptions`) for checking options before enqueueing —
see the API-boundary example below. The other validators run inside `QueueManager` and are not
exported.

## Handling validation errors

```typescript
import { InvalidJobOptionsError, JobNotFoundError } from '@telamonjs/queue/utils'

try {
  await queueManager.add(MyJob, data, options)
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof InvalidJobOptionsError) {
    logger.error('Invalid job options', error.toJSON())
  } else if (error instanceof JobNotFoundError) {
    logger.error('Job not registered', error.toJSON())
  } else {
    throw error
  }
}
```

Validating user input at API boundaries before enqueueing:

```typescript
import { ZodError } from 'zod'
import { validateJobOptions } from '@telamonjs/queue/utils'

app.post('/jobs', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const options = validateJobOptions(req.body.options)
    await queueManager.add(MyJob, req.body.data, options)
    res.json({ success: true })
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ZodError) {
      res.status(400).json({ error: error.message })
      return
    }
    throw error
  }
})
```
